articleTitle: Directivity Enhancehment of Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna using Broadband Metasurface Lens
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, radiation performance of an antipodal Vivaldi antenna is enhanced using a broadband metasurface lens structure in 1-6 GHz bandwidth. Radiation pattern for the new antenna is more directive due to electromagnetic properties of the metasurface lens. In order to create such a lens, electrically responsive unit cells with high effective permittivity values are utilized. Unit cell dimensions are adjusted to display no resonant behaviour in the designated bandwidth. Overall lens structure is etched over the same substrate containing the antipodal Vivaldi antenna resulting in a compact and low profile design. Far-field radiation patterns indicate a more directive beam is radiated from the modified antenna with metasurface lens. Measurement and simulation results show that directivity is increased considerably without affecting the efficiency characteristics of the antenna due to the inclusion of the metasurface lens.

articleTitle: Transient Analysis of Electromagnetic Scattering by Penetrable Objects Based on Time-Domain PMCHWT Equations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Transient analysis of electromagnetic (EM) scattering by penetrable objects is formulated by time-domain Poggio-Miller-Chang-Harrington-Wu-Tsai (TD-PMCHWT) equations. Traditionally, the equations are solved by discretizing the space domain with the method of moments (MoM) and discretizing the time domain with a march-on-in-time (MoT) scheme. The MoM may be very inconvenient in the time-domain environment and the MoT scheme will give rise to a late-time instability. We propose a different approach to solve the TD-PMCHWT equations by incorporating the Nyström method of discretizing the space domain and Galerkin's scheme with Laguerre function for discretizing the time domain. The approach can overcome the drawbacks of traditional approach and a numerical example is provided to demonstrate its performance.

articleTitle: An Experimental Procedure and Initial Results of RF Propagation in Human Subjects
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we designed a procedure for in vivo RF propagation measurements and presented initial results performed on human subjects. More specifically, two wooden frames with holes are manufactured to fix two broadband horn antennas. Then, a human subject is positioned between the prepared fixture and a vector network analyzer is used to measure the RF propagation at multiple distances. The experiments were performed in an anechoic chamber under an approved protocol. Initial experimental results showed that for a 3 ft distance between horn to horn with human subjects standing in between, 70% of power is lost in the human body and 30% is received by the second horn antenna at 900 MHz. However, the RF power loss increased up to 100% over a frequency range from 900 MHz-18 GHz when the horn antennas are in direct contact with the human subject.

articleTitle: Broadband dispersion engineering of CRLH Transmission Lines for low signal distortion in backward regime
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design method for the broadband compensation of the intrinsic dispersion of a Composite Right/Left-Handed (CRLH) transmission line is presented. The design is based on Cauer’s method that is typically used for the design of microwave networks that must exhibit a specific input impedance profile over an arbitrary frequency band. Here, we consider a conventional microstrip CRLH-TL and the method is applied. The compensating network has been designed for linearizing the dispersion relation, keeping the left-handed propagation regime unaltered. The network consists of a series and shunt connections of inductors and capacitors, some of which exhibit negative value, meaning that a Non-Foster elements are required. When the compensating network is connected to CRLH-TL, a significant reduction of dispersion of broad band signal propagating through the line is achieved.

articleTitle: Adaptive modulation for MU-MIMO-OFDM systems in Underlay Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a modified rate quantization algorithm for multi-user multiple-input-multiple-output-orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MU-MIMO-OFDM) cognitive architectures is proposed. Targeting to fulfill the requirements of 5G communications systems and beyond, while keeping a low complexity degree, we first adapt the sub-channel transmit power and spectral efficiency in the spatial and temporal domains under transmit power and instantaneous bit error rate (BER) constraints. We then use a stochastic algorithm to maximize the rate and transmit power of each secondary user (SU) over the spatial eigen-channels of the corresponding subcarrier MIMO channel, under the constraints of average power budget and probability of interference. It is shown that the proposed scheme outperforms the extended rounding-off (SR) alternative, for the entire SNR range.

articleTitle: A Compact and High Gain Dielectric-Loaded 60GHz Multi-Stepped Waveguide Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a wideband high-gain 2 × 2-element subarray is presented for 60 GHz applications. The antenna is fed with waveguide-fed cavity backed configuration and designed entirely via simple rectangular apertures. To improve radiation pattern characteristics and reduce the antenna size, stepped-radiating apertures loaded with a solid dielectric material. A standard WR-15 rectangular waveguide is designed to excite the antenna at the input port over the operation frequency. The most significant advantage of using this design is its efficient radiation patterns, ability to decrease complexity and cost of fabrication. Simulated results demonstrate a maximum gain of about 19.5 dB, and the sidelobe level (SLL) of the antenna is less than -19 dB in E- and H-planes radiation patterns over the frequency range from 57.5 to 62.5 GHz. In contrast to previous works, the proposed antenna is much more simple to use in antenna array applications. Reduction in the number of radiating apertures and compact feeding networks will lower significantly the size and complexity of a large array with higher gain.

articleTitle: Polarization Reconfigurable Patch Antenna With a Continuously Rotatable Polarization Plane
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a polarization reconfigurable patch antenna with an arbitrary polarization plane of a linearly polarized (LP) wave. To generate an LP wave with a continuously reconfigurable polarization plane, left-handed circularly polarized (LHCP) and right-handed circularly polarized (RHCP) waves radiated from a dual circularly polarized (CP) patch are combined. The polarization plane is continuously controlled by changing the phase difference between the LHCP and RHCP waves using variable phase shifters in a feeding network. The simulated tilt angle of the polarization plane changes continuously from -97° to 97° at 5.2 GHz with a cross-polarization discrimination (XPD) kept better than 20 dB.

articleTitle: Full Wave Solutions of Multiple Scattering Using 3D Vector Cylindrical Wave Expansions In Foldy-Lax Equations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we develop a method for full wave simulations of vegetation/forests based on the scattered field formulation of Foldy-Lax multiple scattering equation (FL). The novelty of this method is that the 3D vector cylindrical wave expansions are used in FL, because the trees are compactly enclosed by the infinite cylindrical surfaces without overlap. For cylindrical scatterers such as tree trunks, infinite cylinder approximation is used to calculate the T matrix. Vector translation addition theorem of 3D vector cylindrical waves is used, and the FL is solved iteratively. Solving FL is equivalent to solving Maxwell equations and all the interactions and multiple scatterings among the scatterers are considered. The correctness of the method is verified by HFSS. This method has been implemented on parallel computing for large problems such as full wave simulations of forests.

articleTitle: Electromagnetically Induced Transparency in Metamaterials Using Theory of Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: High sensitivity in sensors, large group delays for filters and slow light can be achieved by engineering electromagnetically induced transparency within a narrow electromagnetic spectrum. The induced transparency is due to the elimination of the effect of a medium caused by interaction between two resonant states often referred to as the bright and dark modes. Induced transparency are often attained by breaking the structural symmetry of metamaterials as this allows interaction between the two modes. In a case of a given excitation, there is a need to understand the behaviour of the various modes thus making the application of theory of characteristic modes relevant to this work. This paper presents an approach to obtain electromagnetically induced transparency for a given excitation using the theory of characteristic modes. It presents how electromagnetically induced transparency in a structure can be systematically engineered by determining which modes are responsible for its occurrence and how to excite these modes. In our example, EIT occurred at 36 GHz where there was an interaction between the bright and dark modes. This provides an insightful way for designing structures for electromagnetically induced transparency applications.

articleTitle: FDTD Modeling of a Dipole Antenna above Metasurface Using Surface Impedance Boundary Condition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a FDTD modeling method for calculating characteristics of an antenna above a metasurface is presented. A surface impedance boundary condition (SIBC) is introduced into the FDTD method to reduce computational time and resources. The validity of the proposed method is numerically confirmed by calculating an input impedance and a radiation pattern of a horizontal dipole antenna located above the metasurface.

articleTitle: Dual Polarized Omni Cell Antenna with Cylindrical Loop Slot
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper discusses a slant ±45° dual polarized omnidirectional antenna to operate as omni cell antenna covering the IMT frequency band from 1920 MHz to 2170 MHz. The antenna is used to cover low reception areas between sector antennas with directivity in horizontal plane. Good antenna performances are achieved where measurement results agree well with simulation results, with the gain of more than 4 dBi and a gain difference of less than 1.5 dB.

articleTitle: mmWave Double Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna featuring Electrically Small and Low-Profile
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes a mmWave double cavity-backed slot antenna (CBSA) for mmWave frequencies. The proposed antenna achieves dual resonance at 28GHz and 38GHz. The finalized 1 × 4 antenna array features 5.64 dBi and 8.84 dBi gain at 28GHz and 38GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Optimization of microwave hyperthermia array applicators using field interpolation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Phased array applicators for deep microwave hyperthermia struggle to reach satisfying target-to-remaining power absorption ratios in the brain area. In our opinion, this is partly because their design is meant for an overall body region rather than a particular tumor. A paradigm shift in the antenna arrangement design is thus necessary: from regional applicator arrays to target-specific ones. Exploring all the possible array configurations and simulate them, however, is computationally unfeasible. This conference contribution presents an approximated method for determining the field distribution generated by an antenna at any desired location across the surface of the so-called water bolus. This approximated field can be effectively used within an array optimization algorithm, and initial results suggest that the optimal antenna arrangement for treating a child brain tumor differs substantially from that of a regular array.

articleTitle: Finite Metal Wall Effects of W-Band Circular Polarized Horn Antenna with Inbuilt Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The performance of finite metal wall thickness of a novel W-band left-hand circular polarized (LHCP) cylindrical waveguide feed horn antenna is investigated. Two different modified designs of the horn antenna with the additional metal thickness are studied. The modified design with a circular skirt at the aperture helps to reduce the undesired diffraction current and ripples in the radiation pattern. The final modified design has a superior axial ratio performance over a wide angle and also shows symmetric radiation pattern over different planes. The measurement of the prototyped feed horn antenna validates the analysis and simulation results.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Wideband Feeding Network for Polarization Diverse Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an active 8-port feeding network that achieves a full range 360° phase coverage. The network is designed to only require a phase shift tuning of 180°. The performance of the proposed feeding network along its various active components can be achieved by necessitating less than 4 V of biasing voltage requirements. The feeding network is tested on an array of eight circularly polarized helical antenna elements where polarization reconfiguration in the radiated fields is achieved. The control of the phase shift between the feeding network ports allows the overall antenna array to change its polarization across the entire frequency band of interest between 1.7 GHz and 2.3 GHz.

articleTitle: Parallelization Efficiency of Multi-GPU In-Core LU-Decomposition of Dense Matrices
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Acceleration of in-core LU decomposition of a dense MoM matrix by using multiple GPUs in parallel, is presented in this paper. Results for nonsymmetrical and symmetrical matrices are shown. Limitations for further increasing the parallelization efficiency and the ways for overcoming these limitations are discussed. The achieved acceleration efficiency is high (about 65%), but remains limited by the speed of data transfers between CPU RAM and GPUs VRAM.

articleTitle: A Multilayer Dielectric Filled Radial Substrate Integrated Waveguide Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A narrow slot antenna is excited by designing a radial substrate integrated waveguide (R-SIW) having TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> mode. The length of the narrow slot antenna is increased to achieve wide impedance bandwidth and is found to be 10.61%, after simulation. In order to further increase the performance of the narrow slot antenna, in terms of gain and the shape of the principal E-plane radiation pattern; an engineered layer consisting of metal strips and EBG are constructed on top of the R-SIW. The simulated results for the realized gain and the principal radiation patterns are presented, and are compared with the presence and absence of an engineered layer. A peak realized gain of 11.5 dB at 30 GHz and impedance bandwidth of 10.5% are observed from frequency range 28.6 - 32 GHz, for the narrow slot antenna including the engineered layer.

articleTitle: How to Phase Antenna Arrays and Metasurfaces of Arbitrarily Oriented and Polarized Elements?
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose an analytical method to phase any arrays of antennas or any metasurfaces made of elements with any arbitrary orientations or arbitrary polarizations. We are unaware of such an analytical phasing technique in the literature. The method can pave the way for phasing arrays with more complicated configurations, and also, for real-time beam steering.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Radiation Characteristics for Balanced- and Unbalanced-Feed Grid Array Antennas Composed of Rectangular Loop Cells
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A grid array antenna composed of rectangular loop cells printed on a dielectric substrate (RecL-PGAA) is analyzed using the method of moments. The RecL-PGAA is fed from the antenna center (balanced feed) or in the vicinity of the antenna center (unbalanced feed). The radiation characteristics for the balanced feed RecL-PGAA are compared with those for the unbalanced feed RecL-PGAA.

articleTitle: Predicting Instability in Transient Simulations, using Complex Numerical Impulse Response
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a method for detecting instability of transient simulation of the SPICE equivalent circuit models is presented. The proposed algorithm, uses the behavior of the real/imaginary part of the impulse response obtained from Inverse Laplace Transform (ILT) of the transfer function in pole-zero form, to decide whether the transient simulation will run and converge, or fail.

articleTitle: Corrosion-Related Magnetostatic Field Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A surface integral equation method for computing the corrosion-related magnetostatic field is presented. An integral equation is solved for the corrosion-related electrostatic field in a homogeneous electrolyte from which the corrosion-related magnetostatic field is determined. The surface integral equation is discretized using the locally-corrected Nyström method. The field analysis is validated through comparison to analytical and published results.

articleTitle: A Quasi-optical Testbed for Terahertz On-Wafer Device and Circuit Characterization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a novel quasi-optical vector network analyzer (VNA) topology for terahertz (THz) on-wafer measurement and characterization. We combine a frequency-independent quasi-optical topology and on-wafer antenna probes to enable a non-contact, ultra-wideband THz on-wafer testing system. Additionally, the use of optical components allows the use of photonics-based THz emitters and detectors, which also support ultra-wide bandwidths of operation. A proof-of-concept testing setup is built and evaluated in the 300-340 GHz band using on-wafer measurements. The characterization of a passive device shows good agreement with simulation results and verifies the feasibility of the proposed VNA topology.

articleTitle: Excitation of Circularly Polarized Wave In Substrate Integrated E-Plane Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: a novel SMA Adaptor is proposed to excite circularly polarized wave in the substrate integrated E-plane waveguide (SIEW). The adaptor is built by binding two printed circuit board parts, which allows the insertion of copper strips into the middle layer of the structure. A piece of `T' shape copper strip is inserted at the middle layer to excite the horizontal component of electric field. A small plated through hole is used to excite the vertical component of electric field. The two orthogonal field components propagate in the SIEW with different propagation constants. A 90 degree phase difference between the two orthogonal components can be obtained after the wave propagates a certain distance in the SIEW. Consequently, circularly polarized wave is excited at that location.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Electromagnetic Time Reversal Spatial Focusing (EMTR-SF)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present two evaluation approaches of the electromagnetic time reversal technique spatial focusing (EMTR-SF). The first approach is based on measuring the spatial correlation function. This yields the diameter of the circle the power is focused on. Our experiments for a given reverberation chamber result in a 0.75λ focusing diameter. The second approach is based on the energy enhancement ratio (EER). This gives a physical insight into the amount of energy enhancement offered by EMTR. It also helps to determine the optimum pulse width for EMTR in a given environment. A maximum EER of 2.5× is measured for an optimum pulse width of 2 ns. Both evaluation approaches should be considered in order to properly asses and establish an efficient EMTR scheme.

articleTitle: Reflection Behavior of Metasurface Using Full-wave and Characteristic Mode Analyses
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The reflection phase of HIS structure is usually captured using full-wave simulations. To accomplish this, full- wave solver is used to model HIS as finite and infinite structures. In this paper, another technique, namely the characteristic mode analysis (CMA), will be considered to acquire the reflection phase. The results of the two analyses will be discussed, compared and verified by placing a dipole above a HIS.

articleTitle: The Use of Singular Basis Functions for Precise EM Analysis of Axially Symmetric Metallic Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Implementation of singular basis functions is proposed in a method for EM analysis of axially symmetric metallic structures, which is based on the exact kernel of electric field integral equation in combination with Galerkin testing. By the use of a proper analytic form of these basis functions the edge effect is taken into account. The benefits of using singular basis functions are illustrated on biconical antennas with arm length from 0.5λ up to 10λ.

articleTitle: Sparse-Regular Array Design for SKA Mid Frequency Aperture Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Current research in the development of a sparse-regular aperture array concept is presented for use in the Square Kilometre Array's (SKA) Mid Frequency Aperture Array (MFAA). Advantages offered by the sparse array regime are explored, while considering methods to overcome its inherent problems. In particular, the prevalence of grating lobes in visible space poses a significant design challenge, which is carefully considered and addressed. The work is a collaborative effort between South African and Dutch institutions affiliated with MFAA, and involves parallel investigations of both the overall system and the antenna element design. First-stage solutions are presented, providing a foundation on which a more complete system prototype may be developed.

articleTitle: Role of the Parkes Radiotelescope in the First Moon Landing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Parkes radiotelescope and Honeysuckle Creek stations in Australia received the telemetry from the Lunar Module "Eagle", including the first television pictures from the first moonwalk for distribution to millions of people on Earth. Parkes' TV picture quality was superior to those received at the other ground stations, therefore NASA used Parkes as the TV source for all but the first nine minutes of the over 5 hours of the TV broadcast. The Parkes radiotelescope is historically important for its contribution to the first Moon landing as well as its design and for the corrugated feed horn first used at Parkes.

articleTitle: Complex Transformation Optics and Generalized Double Negative Layers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The conventional Veselago-Pendry (VP) lens with ε = μ = -1 can be derived via real-valued transformation optics (TO) technique. We extend such approach to complex coordinates to study generalized Veselago-Pendry (GVP) lenses. The derived material properties are doubly anisotropic and impedance matched to free space for all angles of incident. In addition, because the loss is incorporated into the coordinate transformation through an imaginary part of the coordinate transformation, its performance is, in a certain sense, immune to losses. We study different transformation profiles for the imaginary part of the coordinate transformation, i.e, non-symmetric, mirror-symmetric (PT symmetry), resulting in a loss, gain, and balanced loss/gain media.

articleTitle: Nonreciprocal Metasurfaces through Biasing with Circularly Polarized Waves
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Spatiotemporal modulation (STM) has emerged as a promising paradigm for the development of magnetless nonreciprocal devices, but it poses significant practical challenges when sought to be implemented over structures with a large number of modulated components, such as metasurfaces. Here it is shown that this problem may be overcome in metasurfaces biased with circular-polarized waves. In particular, it is shown that this type of biasing can create modulation equivalent to angular-momentum modulation, without any complicated modulation network. Different forms of CP modulation are discussed and shown how they can lead to different nonreciprocal functionalities, including Faraday rotation, nonreciprocal amplification and isolation.

articleTitle: A Meta-Surface Antenna Array Decoupling (MAAD) Method for Two Linear Polarized Compact Antenna Elements at 3.5GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new type of metasurface consisting of double layer short wire for decoupling has been proposed which can solve the decoupling problem of antennas arranged along the H-plane. The |S21| of the antenna arranged along the H-plane can be reduced from about -10 dB to below -25 dB at a frequency band of 3.3 GHz to 3.7 GHz while |S11| can be kept below -15 dB by adding a metasurface. Not only that, cross polarization has also been improved well.

articleTitle: Temporal HF Noise Cross-Correlation Trends in San Diego Waters
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: High-frequency (HF) noise measurements are analyzed to investigate temporal noise characteristics measured over an eleven-day period off the coast of Southern California. The investigation employs cross-correlation techniques to distinguish unique signature properties of hourly noise. Correlation techniques provide the ability to accurately identify and characterize normal and temporal noise characteristics.

articleTitle: Novel Integral Equation Formulation for the Analysis of Capacitive Step Discontinuities
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, a novel integral equation formulation is used for the electromagnetic analysis of rectangular waveguide capacitive discontinuities. The proposed integral equation, solved by the Method of Moments (MoM), accurately models the coupling between the step discontinuity and a given number of arbitrarily shaped metallic posts in its vicinity. The kernel of the Integral Equation is written in terms of parallel plate Green's Functions in the spatial-spectral frequency domain taking into account the capacitive symmetry and thus reducing a 3D problem to a simpler 2.5D one. The computational technique has been validated through the analysis of a practical lowpass filter, that uses one capacitive step as an impedance inverter. The results are in very good agreement with respect of full-wave software tools while exhibiting higher computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Turntable ISAR Imaging of a Circular Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Turntable inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) has a rich history with many significant connections recognized in antenna theory, Fourier analysis, sampling theory, remote sensing inverse problems, medical tomography, imaging, synthetic apertures, radar signals, range and doppler and signal processing. In fact, most ISAR and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) theory has been derived from perspectives of approximations imposed upon the signal models. Consequently, most literature focuses upon overcoming these artificial limitations that are inherently due to imposed approximations. Our work analyzes these approximations differently with the use of statistical characterization. In doing so we create expected patterns of the ISAR data.

articleTitle: Distributed NUMA Implementation of a Direct Solver for DDM Preconditioning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a scalable, and memory and time efficient parallel blockwise-sparse LU decomposition for distributed NUMA architectures suitable for global domain decomposition preconditioning. A static task scheduling heuristic is used to spatial and temporary allocate computational tasks on distributed NUMA systems. Asynchronous communication aided by manual progression techniques are used to maximize communication and computation overlap. Comparisons with state of the art sparse direct solvers on various electrically large problems suggest up to 2 times less memory and up to 4 times faster time while having better parallel efficiency.

articleTitle: A Dual-band Strain Sensor Based On Pop-up Half Wavelength Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Here we present a pop-up half wavelength dipole antenna with dual band operation for strain sensing applications. The proposed antenna is lightweight, low cost and easy to fabricate with a simple design based on a compressive buckling technique. This flexible strain sensor can measure 0 to 30% uniaxial strain with the frequency shift in the range of 2.45 GHz to 2.9 GHz in the first band and 5.5 GHz to 6.3 GHz in the second band. A prototype of the proposed structure was fabricated and tested. Measured results show a good correlation with the Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulation.

articleTitle: Wideband Multilayer 45-Degree Polarizer (2 - 6GHz)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a wideband multilayer 45-Degree polarizer design is described in detail. The design consists of five layers of strip-lines oriented progressively from 0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> to 45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>. A semi-analytical method, developed in a previous work is used to optimize the structure over the bandwidth 2 to 6 GHz. To validate the approach, patch antennas resonating at different frequencies are stacked with the polarizer. The results of the full structures are discussed over the complete bandwidth.

articleTitle: Simplified Synthetic Electrode Strategy for Electrical Capacitance Volume Tomography
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Electrical capacitance volume tomography (ECVT) has been used for imaging of flow media in various industrial applications. An ECVT sensor operates in the Laplacian (quasi-static) regime, which exacerbates the ill-conditioning of the associated inverse problem and the imaging resolution. In this paper, we propose a new strategy to increase image resolution through the use of a higher electrode density sensor, which enables electronic scanning by means of synthetic electrodes. We validate the proposed strategy through various simulations.

articleTitle: Effect of Antenna Coupling on the SNR Improvement of Mm-Wave Massive MIMO for 5G
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, it is shown that an optimum coupling between massive MIMO elements improves the SNR for each user in 5G downlink mode. It is assumed that a massive MIMO base station with 64 compact antennas with sub-wavelength spacing (0.37λ) serves 8 user equipments. With proper design of antennas couplings, the mean received SNR of users improves from 4 to 7 dB. Different coupling values are implemented for a sample patch antenna at 28 GHz with a slot on substrate between adjacent patch elements to control the element coupling. The whole system is simulated in MATLAB, with 5G millimeter-wave channel characteristics and OFDM modulation.

articleTitle: A Fabrication Compatible On-chip Linear Tapered Slot Antenna with CPW Feed
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An on-chip linear tapered slot antenna is designed in this paper for 60 GHz communications in 0.18 µm RF CMOS process with maximum dimensions of 3 mm × 1.25 mm. A uniplanar broadband CPW to slot line transition with stepped impedance transformation network is used as the feed for the antenna. The traditional exponential flaring used in tapered slot antennas is replaced by staircase flaring to follow the fabrication process design kit rules. The simulated impedance bandwidth is 22.3 GHz. Corrugations on the outer metal edges of the antenna enable a front-to-back ratio of more than 13 dB. The maximum gain obtained at 60 GHz is -1.5 dBi in the end fire direction.

articleTitle: Dual Polarizations Single-feed Cross-Dipole Energy Harvesting Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a single-feed energy harvesting surface (EHS) designed for electromagnetic energy harvesting. The EHS unit cell of the proposed harvester comprises two cross-dipoles with one feeding port that enables capturing the energy at multiple polarizations of the incident field at an operating frequency of 3.2 GHz. The simulation results yielded radiation to ac efficiency of 92% at two polarizations. A critical designing feature for the proposed single-feed cross-dipole EHS is that it minimizes the number of the rectifying elements (diodes) to half. The single-feed EHS also allows a direct matching to a rectifying circuitry at the cross-dipole plane.

articleTitle: Ultra-Deep Sub-Wavelength Mode Confinement in Graphene Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a nano-structured device is designed using two adjacent graphene-based waveguides which is capable of confining an incident light-wave at the deep nano-scale. The Fermi energy of graphene in both waveguides are tuned by electrostatic gating, providing an active control on the working frequency of the device.

articleTitle: A Novel Scheme for Evaluating Hypersingular Volume Integrals over Tetrahedral Elements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Volume integral equations (VIEs) are indispensable to solve electromagnetic (EM) problems with inhomogeneous or anisotropic penetrable objects. In the numerical solution of VIEs, one has to evaluate hypersingular volume integrals over tetrahedral elements in the diagonal matrix entries. In this paper, we develop a novel scheme to evaluate such integrals by transforming the volume integrals into boundary integrals based on the Green-Gauss theorem so that the formulations can be simplified. A numerical example is presented to illustrate the scheme.

articleTitle: Disc-Loaded, Vertical Top-Hat Monopole Antenna at 225 GHz for On-Chip Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The challenges of intra- and inter-chip wireless communication arise from the very small electrical thickness of the silicon dioxide and from the direction of the main beam of the antenna. In most of these cases the antennas are placed horizontally on the substrate with the radiation orthogonal to the plane of the chip which results in low transmission in the plane of the chip. A vertical monopole has the desired radiation pattern but becomes electrically small which, in turn, makes the input impedance highly capacitive. Furthermore the silicon substrate reduces the radiation resistance. To address these issues, the present work presents a vertical top-hat monopole placed in silicon dioxide (SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) as the wireless interconnect. It has a ground plane in the shape of a disc to improve the radiation resistance. Matching is achieved by the top-hat that provides a capacitance and a shorting post connecting the top-hat to the grounded disc which provides an inductance. The results for impedance matching and the radiation pattern obtained through simulations are encouraging. To increase the radiation efficiency, it is design trade-off with the silicon dioxide substrate thickness.

articleTitle: UWB Rotation Scanning System for Breast Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: UWB microwave imaging has been demonstrated to have clinical potentials for breast screening. However, existing imaging system either incorporate commercial VNA or simplify the system by sacrificing bandwidth or ADC accuracy. We proposed a system that equips a rotation mechanism to reduce antenna elements and a line laser for skin surface estimation. We demonstrated the feasibility of the system through silica gel based breast phantom.

articleTitle: An Improved Model for Static Field Micro-Particle Components on a Printed Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Amongst existing RF switching methods, a directly connected biasing circuitry is not required for Static Field Micro-Particle Components (SFM-PCs); therefore, not only power consumption is lowered but also these particle-based switches can be used in complex geometries. In this paper, an improved model for SFM-PC was presented and the effects of its physical characteristics on the performance of a microstrip TL was investigated. HFSS simulations and measurements reveal that the frequency bandwidth of both ON and OFF states varies with its physical characteristics; this mandates a careful design to meet the requirements of different wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Microwave Imaging of Strong Scatterers through a Multi-Resolution Contraction Integral Equation Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work deals with the solution of highly nonlinear inverse scattering (IS) problems. Towards this end, an innovative microwave imaging (MI) method based on the integration of the Contraction Integral Equation for Inversion (CIE-I) method with the iterative multi-scaling approach (IMSA) is proposed. Accordingly, robust multi-resolution MI of large and/or strong scatterers is achieved thanks to the effective combination of the capabilities of the CIE-I to alleviate multiple scattering contributions with those of the IMSA, which mitigates the non-linearity of the IS problem by keeping as low as possible the ratio between unknowns and informative data. A numerical benchmark is shown to assess the proposed method and to compare it against a state-of-the-art single-resolution technique.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Antenna Array based on Orbital Angular Momentum
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, an antenna array able to generate orbital angular momentum (OAM) electromagnetic waves with ultra-wideband (UWB) characteristics is proposed. In particular the proposed array antenna is based on cavity back UWB antennas. In particular each array element is backed with a surface impedance waveguide SIW to improve the performances and reduce the single element dimensions. The array elements are a circularly arranged and the correct phase shift, mandatory to obtain a suitable OAM wave, have been obtained with reconfigurable reflection type phase shifters based on two quadrature hybrids and commercial pin diodes. The phase shifters are driven by mean of a suitable micro-controller. A proof of concept prototype has been designed fabricated and experimentally assessed. The obtained results were quite promising.

articleTitle: Optimal Synthesis of Wideband Beamforming Weights for Monopulse Tracking Radar - The Linear Array Case
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An innovative and effective strategy for the synthesis of fixed-geometry linear arrays generating sum and difference patterns for monopulse radar applications operating at maximum bandwidth is presented. The problem is formulated to obtain a sum pattern and a difference pattern with maximum directivity and slope along the boresight, respectively, while both satisfying mask-power constraints on the sidelobes. Moreover, the two beams share the same amplifiers to reduce the beamforming network complexity. An iterative convex programming strategy is used to find the common amplitude coefficients satisfying the requirements on the radiation patterns over the possible largest bandwidth. A numerical result is reported to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Fast Method for First-Principles-Based Parasitic Extraction of Integrated Circuit Layout
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we develop an accurate yet fast method to perform parasitic extraction of integrated circuit layout. Starting from coupled full-wave Maxwell's equations, we decompose the layout response rigorously into R-, C-, L- and full-wave components. We show how to obtain the RC-component based on first principles, which captures complicated 3-D and distributed effects that cannot be captured by prevailing heuristic RC-extraction. Fast algorithms are also developed to efficiently obtain the layout model. Numerical results and comparisons with measurements have validated the proposed method for layout extraction.

articleTitle: A Glass-Integrated Ferrite FM Antenna for Vehicle Telematics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a miniaturized glass-integrated ferrite symmetric dipole antenna to enable frequency modulation (FM) communication in automotive applications. The geometry and dimensions of the dipole are optimized to obtain the desired antenna performance. The radiating element of the antenna is placed between two layers of glass substrates (ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> =5.5,μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> =1). A layer of ferrite substrate (ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 20, μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> =1000) is introduced at the bottom to minimize the antenna size. The number of shorting pins and their positions were optimized to increase the realized gain. The resonant frequency of the designed antenna was decreased by 80 %, indicating antenna miniaturization, and the antenna showed the maximum realized gain of -13.7 dBi with an omnidirectional radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Planar Frequency-Tunable Quad-Band Antenna with Independently Controllable Bands
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low-profile quad-band loaded-slot antenna with independently controllable frequency bands is presented in this paper. Four slots are carefully designed to generate four separate frequency resonances, which were independently tuned by employing varactor diodes in each slot. The proposed concept was simulated using a full-wave solver and validated through measurements. The results show that each of the four bands can be independently controlled by altering the bias voltage of the respective varactor diode. Overall, the measured frequency tuning of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th bands were 450-750 MHz, 600-1200 MHz, 1200-2100 MHz and 2100-2700 MHz, respectively. The proposed antenna has good potential for applications in the concurrently tunable multiband radio systems, including 5G.

articleTitle: A K/Ka Shared-Aperture DRA Array with High Isolation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band antenna array designed using the aperture sharing concept. The proposed sub array unit consists of a K-band antenna element interlaced within a 2 × 2 Ka-band antenna elements. Aperture coupled dielectric resonator antenna elements are used for both frequency bands. The simulated results show that the interlaced configuration of dielectric resonators provides an isolation of ≥25 dB between the two bands, and a cross polarization of ≥50 dB in both the E- and H-plane, at both frequency bands while maintaining a low profile.

articleTitle: Multiple Wedges Diffraction in Propagation Problems using the Generalized Wiener-Hopf Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, in order to accurately predict diffraction phenomena in propagation problems, we introduce the analysis of the scattering of multiple wedges using the semianalytical method known as Generalized Wiener-Hopf Technique. The analysis is of interest to correctly model path-loss in real-life scenarios for wireless communications.

articleTitle: A Generalized Technique to Accurately Predict Conformal Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The purpose of this paper is model the array performance of an array of open waveguide antennas. In order to improve the prediction of the array pattern, a new equation with four coefficients was used to model each single element H-plane pattern. The four coefficients were related to known characteristics of each array fixture characterized used in the measurements in order to create four, stand alone equations. These equations are applied to the modified H-plane model and used to predict the performance of a conformal array H-plane pattern.

articleTitle: Single-coil Dual-band Transmitting Antenna Design for Wireless Capsule Endoscopic Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Multi-band communication is a viable method to realize a higher antenna transmission speed for MHz band wireless capsule endoscopic (WCE) communication. However, due to the strict size limitations of capsules, it is difficult to design compact multi-band transmitting antennas. In this paper, a single-coil dual-band transmitting antenna is proposed. By optimizing the matching circuit of the antenna, two resonant frequencies can be generated from one coil, thereby reducing the size of the antenna. The simulated reflection coefficient shows that the two resonant frequencies of the antenna are 38.5 and 57.6 MHz, respectively. The simulated transmission coefficient indicates that the antenna can be used for WCE communication in the MHz band.

articleTitle: Design of Multilayered Meta-Lenses for Image Resolution Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Multilayered meta-lenses composed of Silver, PMMA and photoresist with different thicknesses are investigated in order to increase the amplification of evanescent waves traveling through the lenses, aiming to enhance image resolution.

articleTitle: A Novel Diagnostics Method for Determining the Unknown Permittivity Profile of 3D Printed Lenses
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel diagnostics technique that can reconstruct through reverse engineering the permittivity profile of an inhomogeneous dielectric lens which was misprinted due to either voxelization method errors and/or printer tolerances. The technique can be classified as an inverse scattering tool. It is based on a novel combination of Curved Ray Geometrical Optics (GO) for inhomogeneous media and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The lens inhomogeneous permittivity profile is synthesized to reconstruct the known measured near fields when illuminated by the also known feed radiation pattern. Once the true permittivity profile is known, a new optimization can be ran to determine a new optimal focal point to illuminate the lens from in order to restore the performance of the lens back to original designs expectation. An example of a fabricated 3D printed 18cm lens misprinted to both voxelization errors and printing tolerance errors is given. The actual permittivity is found through the diagnostics technique and a new focal point is found through optimization which restores the pattern performance of the lens back to the theoretical values.

articleTitle: Accuracy Investigation of Single-Cut Near-Field Far-Field Transformation Technique Based on 2D Plane-Wave Expansion
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The accuracy of a single-cut near-field far-field transformation technique is studied. The technique is based on the two-dimensional (2D) plane-wave expansion and the approximation that the antenna under test (AUT) is low enough along the direction vertical to the cut-plane under observation. We employ an AUT high enough to break condition for the approximation and observe accuracy of the transformation technique.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Localization of Multiple Targets Using TDOA and Wideband Frequency Modulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a distributed radar is presented that can perform both ranging and time difference of arrival (TDOA), resulting in two-dimensional location estimation without beam-scanning. The transmitter emits a linear frequency modulated (LFM) signal, ranging from 37 to 40 GHz. The receiver is composed of two antennas separated by 80 cm (102.7λ). By performing matched filtering with the transmitted LFM signal on each individual receive element, the range information of multiple targets can be obtained using the signal leakage from the transmit signal. By comparing the two waveforms, their angles are calculated from the TDOA between them. The theory behind the technique is explained and experimental measurements of two reflecting targets are shown.

articleTitle: Wideband 3D Printed Conformal Dielectric Antenna with End-fire Radiation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a conformal 3D-printed endfire dielectric antenna with wideband performance is proposed. The device contains a multi-section dielectric block that is designed with stepped permittivities to attain a wide bandwidth. Through altering the infill percentage during 3D printing, the effective relative permittivity of dielectric segments can be precisely controlled in the range of 8.5 to 2.5. The antenna can be printed to be conformal to a curved metal ground plane to obtain an end-fire radiation beam with a reduced tilt angle. Measured results confirm a wide impedance bandwidth of 67.4% from 6.2 to 12.5 GHz, a stable end-fire beam and a realized gain above 7 dBi over the whole operation band.

articleTitle: General Design Equations For 3-Way Unequal-Split Bagley Power Dividers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We systematically derive general design equations for 3-way unequal-split Bagley power dividers (BPD). The proposed design procedure allows for obtaining power dividers with the same split ratio but with different parameters. Conditions are firstly derived to achieve perfect input port matching. Then, these conditions are taken into consideration to divide the power unequally between the output ports with a desired split ratio.

articleTitle: Error Sensitivity in Reconfigurable OTA Chamber Field Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Prior analysis of the reconfigurable over-the-air chamber - a chamber designed for over-the-air testing of wireless devices - has not incorporated error in the currents when synthesizing fields incident on the device under test. This work incorporates these errors into the model relating currents to the synthesized fields and uses the analysis to quantify the impact of errors on the system performance. The analysis reveals that the signal-to-noise ratio required to achieve a certain level of error in the synthesized field increases with the number of antennas used for synthesis, with the observations suggesting that such chambers must be carefully designed to achieve the correct performance/complexity balance.

articleTitle: Tight Bounds on the Bandwidth of Small Multiresonant Electric Dipole Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Fano matching limitations are applied to the analysis of small multi-resonant electric dipole antennas. It is assumed that the achievable Q-factor of the fundamental resonant mode of the antenna is known for a given frequency. The results can then be combined with known lower bounds on Q for arbitrary geometries. In this manner, tight bounds can be derived on the achievable bandwidth for many practical antennas.

articleTitle: Range and Capacity Optimization of a 10GBps Access Point Employing 12 MIMO Chains
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We outline the design and testing of a highly optimized antenna system for 10Gbit/s performance WLAN access point suitable. The product is the first wireless home gateway to realize these speeds.

articleTitle: Evaluation on Pseudo-Doppler Antenna Array using Software-Defined-Radio
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We investigated the effects of adjacent monopole spacing of pseudo-doppler antenna arrays (PDAAs) on detecting the angle-of-arrival (AoA) in both indoor and outdoor environments above 2 GHz. A software-defined-radio technology was adopted to realize the capability of PDAA. Among three adjacent monopole spacing (0.1414λ, 0.2λ, and 0.25λ, where λ is the wavelength of the frequency), the adjacent monopole spacing of 0.2λ showed the lowest angle difference between desired and actual angle in both environments above 2 GHz.

articleTitle: On Scattering of a Vector Cylindrical Wave by an Axisymmetric Semitransparent Reflector
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Semitransparent surfaces are used in antenna reflectors to obtain the required shape of the radiation pattern. The task of transparency optimization can be simplified with analytical formulae. In this paper, we investigate the scattering of a vector cylindrical wave by a semitransparent half-plane and axisymmetric reflector. The profile of the reflector can be concave, convex, or concavo-convex. We derive some asymptotic formulae for the radiation pattern of the scattering task. In this paper, we present the numerical results calculated through the asymptotic formulae. These results have also been verified through the method of moments.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of the Shadow Projection Algorithm for Near-Field Microwave Imaging of Buried Objects in Layered Media
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A shadow projection algorithm for near-field microwave imaging has been introduced to distinguish the size of objects hidden in the layered structure. For an external source, the radiated energy is focused into the normal direction due to the lensing effect caused by refraction at the boundary between free space and the first layer. The lensing effect is utilized to form the shadow of the buried objects on the rear interface, which provides more accurate object size and shape than a conventional image. The efficacy of the shadow projection approach is validated with measurements of multiple objects embedded in stratified media.

articleTitle: Extremely Wideband Imaging Antenna with Unifrom Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The presented work details the design of extremely wideband antenna and balun. The antenna front-end is designed to operate from 10 GHz to 40 GHz with linear polarization. An extremely wideband balun is also designed and integrated to the radiating element. The structure is optimized to achieve uniform radiation patterns for the complete operating frequency band. The simulated and measured results show the feasibility of the structure for wideband imaging applications.

articleTitle: Forward Transmission Matrix Analysis of Lorentz Sensor For High Permittivity Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Forward Transmission Matrix Analysis (FTM) is a powerful analysis technique which employs a systematic approach to solve complicated microwave circuits. In this paper, we apply FTM to analyze a Lorentz sensor and demonstrate its application for detection of high permittivity liquid samples. The permittivity is calibrated using the resonance signature of the phase spectrum rather than the traditional use of amplitude spectrum. We anticipate that the proposed detector can be potentially applied in biomedical applications such as blood glucose estimation.

articleTitle: Error Prediction in Electromagnetic Simulations Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a novel approach of using deep convolutional neural networks (CNN) to predict electromagnetic scattering errors in iterative solutions of electrically large three-dimensional objects. Deep CNN models are constructed and trained by using surface current images to predict far-zone scattering errors. Numerical experiments demonstrate successful predictions with more than 95% accuracy. The constructed models can be useful to quickly assess the accuracy of candidate solutions of current distributions via their images.

articleTitle: Estimating The Number of Modes in Underground Mine tunnel
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This letter explores the relation between the number of modes in a lossy waveguide environment and Multiple Input Multiple Output antenna array size. We estimated the number of modes in the underground mine tunnel theoretically by using a ray tracing model. The presented formula can be used for determining the number of modes which can act as a propagating channel for MIMO in a straight mine tunnel.

articleTitle: Compact Comparator for 2-D Monopulse Array Based on Novel Eight-Port Coupler
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact comparator is proposed for two-dimensional (2-D) monopulse beamforming. A novel eight-port coupler is adopted as the fundamental component to generate the sum/difference ports for differential beams in two orthogonal planes. The proposed comparator has a double-layer microstrip configuration and without using T-junctions, vias, and steps on each layer. An example of 2 × 2 planar monopulse arrays working at 5.8GHz is built and simulated to verify and demonstrate the performance of 2-D sum/difference beamforming. Satisfying properties at matching, isolation, power division and phase distribution can be achieved in 10% fractional bandwidth.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Modeling of Crosstalk Effect in Graphene-Encapsulated Cu Nano-Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Graphene-encapsulated Cu (CuG) interconnects are promising alternative interconnect solutions for the development of future integrated circuit technology. However, their crosstalk effect, which is of great importance in modern circuit design, has not been thoroughly studied. In this paper, we propose a method to evaluate the crosstalk effect of CuG nano-interconnects by co-simulating, in time domain, Maxwell's equations, Boltzmann equation, and the dispersion of graphene. We also develop an unconditionally stable time marching scheme to remove the dependence of time step on space step, as the space step required for time-domain stability is extremely small in nano-interconnects. The resulting numerical simulations show that CuG nano-interconnects exhibit a much increased crosstalk effect as compared to the bare Cu counterparts.

articleTitle: Center-Fed Circularly Polarized Omnidirectional Open-Helical Element Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Circularly Polarized Omnidirectional Open-Helical Antenna element was designed and optimized. This element consists of 2 dipoles wrapped in a helical shape to force circular polarization. The element was first modeled in ANSYS HFSS and optimized by running parametric simulations to determine the proper angle, trace width, and scaling factor. The element was then etched onto a flex circuit and a circular PCB was used to feed it from the center of the helix. This element had a center frequency of 907 MHz, a bandwidth of 55 MHz, a minimum cross polarization rejection of 11.93 dB, and a total gain of 1.45 dBi. Right and left-hand circular elements can be combined to transmit and receive a signal having any possible polarization on the Poincaré Sphere.

articleTitle: Simultaneous High Data Rate Communication and Highly Efficient Wireless Power Transfer Through a Coplanar Link
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A coplanar link consisting of a Conformal Strongly Coupled Magnetic Resonant (CSCMR) system for a unified wireless power transfer (WPT) and high data rate communication is proposed in this paper. The proposed system has the ability to simultaneously transmit power with high efficiency (i.e., 75% efficiency) and high data rate (i.e., 3 Mbps). Different parameters that affect the resonant frequency of CSCMR are investigated and reported. The proposed topology is designed to operate at 120 MHz, with an achieved bandwidth of 7 MHz.

articleTitle: A Frequency-Reconfigurable Magnetic Monopole Antenna Based on Quarter-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A frequency-reconfigurable magnetic monopole antenna is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna is based on a single-layer quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide (QMSIW). A narrow QMSIW is used to produce monopole-like radiation pattern and an ellipse-shape slot and two varactors are used to realize the reconfigurability. This antenna is designed and optimized by using full-wave simulation software and is continuously reconfigurable over a frequency range of 380 MHz which is from 2.33 GHz to 2.71 GHz. Also, the vertically-polarized monopole-like radiation pattern is kept within the frequency range.

articleTitle: Accuracy of the approximation of Dyadic Green’s Function for Multilayered Uniaxial Anisotropic Medium
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Accuracy of the approximation of the dyadic Green’s functions both in the spectral domain and spatial domain for the planar multilayered uniaxial anisotropic media is verified in this paper. The kDB coordinate system and the wave iterative technique are exploited in the derivation of the spectral-domain Green’s function. The presented algorithm relies on the accurate expressions of unbounded dyadic Green’s function and scattered Green’s function, which are classified into the ordinary and extraordinary waves. Then, the accuracy of spectral-domain Green’s function is proved through the comparison of results between it in the EFIE and it in the MPIE. The effectiveness of the spatial domain Green’s function calculated by the modfied fast Hankel transform method for the planar multilayered uniaxial anisotropic media is verified by the comparison with the results from the Finite Element Method.

articleTitle: Tunable Multiband Devices Based on ON/OFF Switches in Metamaterials SOR for WIFI Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new design of stopband filters, based on a coplanar waveguide loaded with resonator elements, is presented. The structure is composed of four split octagonal resonators (SOR), with three cases according to the angular position of the gaps created by ON/OFF switches in the inner and outer resonators. The design is based on the use of a metamaterial to create notch filters for microwave applications. From the simulation results, the filters exhibit high frequency selectivity via the presence of transmission zeros. To confirm the generation of the rejection bands, an ultra-wideband (UWB) circular monopole antenna is added to the filter. The extracted data are also compared with filter simulation results, revealing good agreement.

articleTitle: Parallel Direct Domain Decomposition Methods (D3M) for Finite Elements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A parallel direct solution approach based on domain decomposition method (DDM) and directed acyclic graph (DAG) scheduling is outlined. Computations are represented as a sequence of small tasks that operate on domains of DDM or dense matrix blocks of a reduced matrix. These tasks can be statically scheduled for parallel execution using their DAG dependencies and weights that depend on estimates of computation and communication costs. Performance comparison with MUMPS 5.1.2 on electrically large problems suggest up to 20% better parallel efficiency, 30% less memory and slightly faster in runtime, while maintaining the same accuracy.

articleTitle: A stable sub-gridding with time and spatial refinements for the FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a stable spatial sub-gridding algorithm for the FDTD method based on electromagnetic energy conservation and a variational formulation of the problem. In addition, a temporal refinement dissociated from spatial refinement is also proposed. The refinement factors in space and time are equal to two.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of Square-Ring Antenna Using Surface Waves on Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Low-profile antennas operating in the resonant mode have a narrow matching bandwidth. Various methods have been proposed to improve the bandwidth. In the present design, the excitation of surface waves is employed to enhance the bandwidth and the radiation performance of a square-ring radiating element. Different configurations to excite surface waves are proposed, and the performance of all configurations are investigated.

articleTitle: FDTD Simulations Of The Impedance Of A Dipole Antenna in A Plasma
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The impedance of a dipole antenna in the earth's ionospheric plasma is dependent on the ambient plasma properties such as electron density and electron neutral collision frequency. Depending on the length of the dipole, it is possible to not only measure the plasma properties, but in addition, receive plasma waves that are found propagating in the ionosphere. Here we report on some FDTD simulations of a dipole antenna in a cold plasma, and present some approximate expressions that can be used to analyze this behavior. When the dipole antenna resonant wavelength λ/4 and associated frequency is far from the upper hybrid, cyclotron and plasma frequencies of the local plasma, the expressions work fairly well. However, when the length of the antenna is such that it's resonant wavelength coincides or is close to the plasma resonances, the expressions fail, and a full- wave FDTD simulation has to be performed to extract meaningful plasma data.

articleTitle: Two-Element Compact Antenna Arrays using Decoupling Networks and Phase Shifters for Four-Branch Switching Diversity
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel method of realizing four-branch switching diversity by a compact two-element antenna array is proposed. The proposed antenna consists of a two-element antenna array, a decoupling network composed of four susceptances, and two phase shifters. This antenna has a simpler circuit configuration compared with conventional one, then the circuit loss can be decreased. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed antenna, we simulate a small two-element inverted-F antenna array. Then, we confirm that the correlation coefficients between any two branches are less than 0.50, and the reflections and coupling can be decreased.

articleTitle: Optimization of Rural Cellular Coverage on the Islands of Hawaii
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this communication genetic programming (GP) is applied to optimize the coverage of wireless networks in rural areas. Three locations in the Hawaiian Islands were studied: Kohala area on Hawaii, the North Shore on Oahu, and the populated area on Maui between West Maui Mountains and Haleakala. Omnidirectional and directional base station scenarios were optimized and simulated. For all three locations studied directional base stations provided better coverage than omnidirectional base stations. For the Maui and Oahu locations directional base stations provided significantly more coverage.

articleTitle: Ridge Gap Array Antenna with Inter-Element Spacing of a Wavelength
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A high-gain ridge gap array antenna, consists of an array of 2×8 monopole antennas with inter-element spacing equals to a wavelength, is proposed and investigated as a promising state-of-the-art grating lobe suppressed high-gain array for millimeter-wave frequency-bands. Increasing the inter-element spacing is a technique for enhancing the directivity; however, it would bring the grating lobe into the visible zone and deteriorate the antenna radiation efficiency. The proposed technique using a supplementary sub-array would suppress the grating lobe in the visible zone. On the other hand, the feeding network is designed with ridge gap waveguide technology in which the waveguide width is about a wavelength making the design of an array antenna with lower inter-element spacing more challenging.

articleTitle: Reducing the Number of Phase Shifters in Circular Arrays of Circular Subarrays for a Wide-Scanning Pattern
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a design of circular arrays of circular subarrays for reducing the number of phase shifters (PSs) considering a wide-scanning pattern using the rotational symmetry properties of the array geometry. The array design model includes the optimization of the amplitude and phase excitations for each subarray with minimum side lobe level SLL and maximum directivity.

articleTitle: Binormalized Factorizations for Magnetostatic Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Localization-based sparse direct solvers provide a general framework for preconditioning sparse representations of integral equation formulations of magnetostatic field problems. However, problems involving complex meshes and geometries often lead to poorly conditioned system matrices. In some cases, localization-based preconditioners fail to yield convergent iterative solutions for these matrices. In this presentation it is shown that incorporating a multilevel matrix binormalization significantly increases the effectiveness of localization-based preconditioners.

articleTitle: Gain Optimization of a Seven Element ESPAR Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we have proposed an algorithm for gain optimization of electronically steerable parasitic array radiator (ESPAR) antennas. Typically, ESPAR antennas have a circular array of parasitic elements around a central active (driven) element. Parasitic element are loaded with the variable reactances such that the antenna beam can be steered by varying the reactance set. We have optimized gain of the ESPAR antenna by using the trust region reflective algorithm. After optimization, peak directivity of the antenna is 10.01 dBi (φ=0° ). Prior to the optimization, peak directivity of the antenna was 8.04 dBi (φ=0° ). A gain increment of 1.97 dB is achieved.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Uniform/Periodic Dual-Mode Dielectric Grating Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: As two categories of the leaky-wave antennas (LWAs), the uniform and periodic LWAs are widely studied individually in the last decades. Here, a hybrid uniform/periodic dual-mode dielectric grating LWA is proposed to combine the uniform and periodic leaky-wave modes together in a simple strategy. The uniform leaky-wave mode is achieved by the inherent leaky property of a dielectric waveguide, while the periodic leaky-wave mode is realized by the periodic load of the dielectric gratings. With the elaborate combination of these two leaky-wave modes, the beam-scanning ability can be enhanced with a supplement in near end-fire direction to eliminate the end-fire scanning blindness of conventional LWAs.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Force and Hidden Momentum for a Perfectly Conducting Sphere
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The exact time-domain force is found for the dipoles induced on an electrically small perfectly conducting sphere by an incident plane wave in order to confirm a recently obtained result that the magnetic dipoles of electrically small perfectly conducting scatterers of arbitrary shape contain a hidden-momentum force that makes the expression for the force on the Amperian magnetic dipoles identical to the expression for the force on magnetic-charge magnetic dipoles.

articleTitle: 1D Array Antennas In Tandem for a Large Gain and Moving the Direction of the End-Fire Beam
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an antenna is designed to generate an end-fire radiated beam of a very large gain for a PCB structure and steer the beam at an ISM-band.
