Via-holes are arranged to reduce the insertion loss due to the leakage power between parallel plates in dielectric substrate. However, the transition obtained quite narrow frequency bandwidth in the millimeter-wave band. Therefore, a design technique of via-hole locations at both sides of the microstrip line is proposed for bandwidth extension of planar microstrip-to-waveguide transition used at a frequency of 76.5 GHz. The double-resonant frequency is formed by controlling the via-hole locations at both sides of the microstrip line. The broadband of 10.6 GHz (13.8%) is obtained where the reflection level is lower than -15 dB. Characteristics of broadband planar microstrip-to-waveguide transition depending on via-hole positions are investigated in this study.

articleTitle: Virtual Drive Testing based on Automotive Antenna Measurements for Evaluation of Vehicle-to-X Communication Performances
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we present a new Virtual Drive Test (VDT) technique which allows to evaluate the Vehicle-to-X (V2X) communications performances taking into account the measured characteristics of transmit and receive antennas installed on vehicles. The proposed VDT technique is a multistage process where the radiation characteristics of the vehicle mounted antennas are first measured in free-space conditions in a controlled and repeatable laboratory environment. The Vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) or Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) are then evaluated with a coupling equation (or transmission formula) where variable ground conditions can also be considered. The proposed technique is presented taking into account measurements of a representative scaled automotive scenario.

articleTitle: Origami Multimode Ring Antenna Based on Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact ring shaped Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna operating in two high order modes is implemented on an origami waterbomb structure. Operation in two modes allows the single element to act as a MIMO while the foldable waterbomb structure offers frequency and radiation pattern reconfigurability. Characteristic mode analysis is performed to determine the two most desirable modes of operation. The realized gain as well as the reconfigurable nature of the antenna as it is folded is presented.

articleTitle: A Novel UWB Antenna For Wireless Communication Systems Using Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel UWB antenna design using Genetic Algorithms (GA). The new design is based on circular pixels to provide larger band response. In every iteration, the GA optimizes the surface of the patch by cutting away a random number of circular pixels, while maintaining the same compactness of the antenna. The proposed antenna operates in the frequency range of 3.2 GHz to 12.9 GHz and shows good results in terms of matching performance and gain.

articleTitle: Novel SIE Formulations for Accurate and Stable Analysis of Near-Zero-Index Materials
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present surface-integral-equation formulations for accurate and stable solutions of electromagnetic problems involving near-zero-index materials with arbitrarily small permittivity and/or permeability values. The formulations are developed for conventional discretizations, while they can be implemented by using interaction routines of existing solvers. Initial results on canonical objects clearly demonstrate the superiority of the developed formulations in comparison to the conventional ones.

articleTitle: Array of Antennas for a GPR system onboard a UAV
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, the prototype of an array of antennas to be used in a GPR mounted in a UAV is presented. The array, while light enough to be mounted in the UAV, allows for faster scanning of large areas and to create high resolution radar images using Synthetic Aperture Radar algorithms. Preliminary calibration results show the good imaging capabilities of the system.

articleTitle: Spread Spectrum Techniques for Interference Mitigation in Large Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Communication links are vulnerable to signal fratricide and intentional interference. Therefore, there is a strong interest for interference resistant links to enable secure communication protocols. One way to achieve interference immunity is by exploiting Spread Spectrum (SS) coding techniques with significant coding gain. With access to large bandwidth, it is now possible to spread the signal below the noise floor and secure reliable communication. The focus of this paper is to present a Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum - Binary Phase Shift Keying (DSSS-BPSK) modulation link with over 1 GHz signal bandwidth, in presence of collocated multiple high power interferers. It is observed that DSSS results in better bit error rate (BER) performance. This improvement was in presence of an interferer-signal (I/S) ratio of 34.34 dB.

articleTitle: Predicting MRI RF Exposure for Complex-shaped Medical Implants Using Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a fast prediction method using a 3-layer feed-forward artificial neural network (ANN) based on complex shape descriptors was proposed to estimate the radio-frequency (RF) exposure for complex-shaped implantable devices under magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The inputs of the ANN consist of 20 parameters based on dimensions and surface-based features of the complex-shaped devices, and the output is the peak MRI RF exposure, in terms of 1-gram averaged specific absorption rate (SAR1g), for the device. This method is implemented and validated with 408 complex-shaped trauma implantable devices. These accurate 3D CAD models are used to numerically calculate the peak SAR1g of the devices by using a full-wave electromagnetic solver based on finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. Among the 408 devices, 326 were used to train the neural network, while 82 were utilized to examine the validity of the SAR1g values predicted by the ANN. The results have shown that the correlation between the estimation and the target values was larger than 0.993, and the root mean square error was less than 6.21 W/kg.

articleTitle: A Wearable Reconfigurable Electromagnetic Metamaterial Absorber using Artificial Magnetic Inclusions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable textile electromagnetic absorber is proposed for wearable applications. The textile absorber is composed of a modified version of the well-known, artificial magnetic inclusion, the Split-Ring Resonator (SRR). The designed electromagnetic absorber provides extra freedom in ease of placement of either rectified load or a biasing circuitry for reconfigurability of the absorber or even both. Numerical studies are carried out in order to investigate the absorption strength from the proposed metamaterial absorber. Furthermore, the reconfigurability was achieved using a biasing varactor circuitry. Based on the numerical full-wave simulations, the proposed absorber structure exhibits an absorption of 99% at a frequency of 4.9 GHz under normal incidence when absorber is in ON state, while the peak absorptivity was shifted to higher frequency of 5.06 GHz when absorber is in OFF state with slight reduction in absorption level.

articleTitle: Mechanically-Rotating Electret ULF/VLF Antenna Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Given that Ultra-Low-Frequency (ULF)/Very-Low-Frequency (VLF) communication systems are lower power consumption than traditional transmitters, more and more researchers focus on the development of the ULF/VLF transmitter. In this paper, an innovative design of ULF/VLF transmitter is introduced based on mechanically-rotating electret, and is validated using both theoretical analysis and finite element simulations. This work is intended to lay the foundation for future tests involving the implementation of efficient, small form-factor, mechanically-actuated antennas.

articleTitle: MM-Wave Beam-Steering Slot Antenna using Gradient Relative-Permittivity FSS Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel beam-steering technique for planar antennas with gain enhancement utilizing gradient relative-permittivity of frequency selective surface (FSS) unit-cells for fifth-generation (5G) applications. A dual- used at the above a slot antenna. The slot antenna using the ridge gap waveguide (RGW) technology, which is composed of printed parallel-plate waveguide surrounded by the mushrooms unit cells, is used to excite an FSS superstrate. Simulated results show that the proposed beam-steering antenna has a wide impedance bandwidth (S11 <; -10 dB) from 31 to 35.8 GHz (14 %). A maximum gain of 11.8 dB is achieved by adding FSS.

articleTitle: A Comparison Between Grey Wolf and Invasive Weed Optimizations Applied to Microstrip Filters
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Two relatively novel optimization algorithms, the invasive weed optimization and the grey wolf optimizer are here applied to the design of a lowpass microstrip filter to compare their relative performances on an electromagnetic problem.Insight over the different characteristics of the two techniques is given.

articleTitle: Broadband Linear to Circular Reflection Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband linear to circular polarization converting surface is presented. The polarization reflector consists of a dogbone-shaped FSS separated from the metallic ground plane by a Teflon dielectric slab of thickness equal to 3.95 mm. The polarization converter is composed by a periodic arrangement of metallic particles, positioned in a square lattice with a periodicity D = 5 mm. The surface provides an efficient conversion from linear to circular polarization in the frequency band spanning from 9.45 GHz to 21.1 GHz thus obtaining a relative bandwidth of 76.2 %.

articleTitle: Retro-directive Array Antenna With Parabolic Shape Structure for Short-range Microwave Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Demands for wireless power transmission(WPT) technologies have been increasing recently with a significant increase in IoT(Internet of Things) and mobile devices. While these microwave power transmission(MPT) technologies want to be generally used within 10 m, conventional studies have assumed that transmission distance is very long. A retro-directive array structure can be used for microwave power transmission in the Fresnel region. The parabolic shape structure is proposed for higher efficiency of microwave power transmission. The parabolic shape structure is arranged to have the same phase from the receiver. The efficiency of microwave power transmission in the receiver is higher than that of the equi-phased array and retro-directive array of linear structure. In addition, the power distribution analysis is performed with regard to the location of the equi-phased array, the retro-directive array, and the retro-directive array with a parabolic shape structure.

articleTitle: 3D Printed 2.45 GHz Yagi-Uda Loop Antenna Utilizing Microfluidic Channels and Liquid Metal
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 3D printed deployable Yagi-Uda loop antenna designed to operate at the Ultra High Frequency (UHF) Industrial, Scientific and Medical (ISM) band is presented. Utilizing high resolution Stereolithography (SLA) 3D printing, microfluidic channels are incorporated into a 3D structure that enables utilization of liquid metal conductors for deployable antenna, with multiple spiral parallel dielectric structures interconnecting the loops together in a manner that enables a flattened design under compression.

articleTitle: Microwave Imaging Technology for In-line Food Contamination Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Foreign body contamination in food is one of the major sources of complaints against food manufacturers, and it can lead to injury, loss of brand loyalty and large recall expenses. Different technologies, such as X-ray or infrared techniques, are currently applied to detection systems used for food inspection, but physical contamination, with e.g. wood, plastic, metal and glass fragments, is still present in food. For this reason, there is the interest to develop new technologies able to address the still unmet needs of food industry. In this paper, we report about preliminary investigations of the use of the microwave imaging technology for food contamination monitoring. Numerical results show the feasibility of the proposed approach. The realization of prototype measurement system is under development.

articleTitle: Design of High Gain Low Cost Beam-Steering Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Design of a low cost and high gain reflectarray antenna is presented in this paper. A 28 × 28 element reflectarray surface has been designed for beam steering between -40° and +40° from the broadside. Unit cell of the reflectarray surface consists of a circular ring and a double square. The characteristics of the reflecting elements are selected such that a progressive phase shift is achieved. Beam steering can be achieved by switching between multiple feed antennas. Antenna shows a peak gain of 29.77 dBi at 18 GHz. In Comparison to the conventional beam steering antennas, the proposed antenna has higher gain and the design is cost effective to implement.

articleTitle: Bending and Twisting Tests for RF Performances of Textile Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The RF performances of smart textiles upon bending and twisting are considered in this work. Two textile-based transmission lines (TTLs) were fabricated on denim and organza, and loss-performance comparison was made based on two mechanical deformations such as bending and twisting. The measurements suggested that organza-based TTLs exhibited the least loss (0.6 dB/cm) for frequency up to 10 GHz when considered parameters like embroidery patterns, stitching density and tension, as well as microstructure of the substrates. The validation of the proof-of-concept was realized by fabricating a patch antenna, which measurements have very close agreement with simulation. These results can be used as guidelines for future textile fabrication for wearable applications.

articleTitle: Dual Polarized Plane Wave Generator Design for Direct Far-Field Testing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Plane Wave Generator (PWG) is an array of elements with suitably optimized complex coefficients, generating an approximate plane wave over a finite testing volume called the Quiet Zone (QZ). The PWG enables direct measurements of far-field performance of the Antenna Under Test (AUT) in a controlled indoor environment as an alternative to Compact Antenna Test Range (CATR). In this paper we present our sub-array-based approach to minimize the number of parallel transceiver modules controlling the complex excitations of the elements of the PWG.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Proximity Feed Patch Antenna for FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a broad band circularly polarized antenna is presented which can operate over 300MHz bandwidth. Investigation for the design parameter is performed and improvement in axial ratio for the proposed design is also shown. The fabricated antenna is tested and measured results are given for comparison. The prototype is used as a transmitter and receiver antenna in a FMCW radar system. Also the range profile for a moving target is recorded and presented with experimental setup.

articleTitle: Spread-Spectrum Camouflaging based on Time-Modulated Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a metasurface that is temporally modulated so as to perform camouflaging. This metasurface consists of a two-dimensional array of patches, each loaded by a grounding stub equipped by a diode switch controlled by an external broadband random signal. This random signal spreads out the spectrum of interrogating radar waves so as to transform them into a noisy signals with undetectably low intensity. As a result, no back-scattering is measurable, and the object is concealed to the radar. Simulation shows that the metasurface scatters a monochromatic incident wave into a reflected wave of 50 MHz spread spectrum with power level reduced by 35 dB, with further level reduction obtainable using random signal of larger bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Origami FSS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-band origami FSS design and its performance analysis for the case of normal incident wave is presented in this work. As an origami structure, a Miura-Ori geometry is chosen for the implementation of a rhombic loop FSS. This FSS shows a dual frequency band stop characteristic at its flat state. Exploiting the ability of the origami pattern to fold/unfold, the two frequency bands are appropriately adjusted for both TE and TM polarizations.

articleTitle: High Gain Ridge Gap Dielectric Resonator Antenna using FSS Superstrates
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents design and simulation of a high gain ridge gap dielectric resonator antenna (RGDRA) for 5G applications. The proposed antenna shows an impedance bandwidth of 26.6 GHz to 29.1 GHz with a maximum gain of 5.1 dBi at 28 GHz. Moreover, by loading three layers of frequency selective surfaces (FSS) horizontally in front of the RGDRA in the H-plane, 4.2 dBi gain enhancement is reached compare to the unloaded antenna at 28 GHz. Each FSS layer consists of 2×3 array of FSS unit cells. The proposed unit cell holds a size of 0.46λ × 0.46λ (at 28 GHz) and composed of a slotted square patch at the top and a square strip at the bottom side of Rogers 4003C substrate.

articleTitle: Theory of Electromagnetic-Based Communication within Bacterial Communities
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel model referred to as electromagnetically-coupled system of mechanical oscillators is presented in this paper to unravel the concept of possible electromagnetic-based communication between bacterial cells within bacterial communities (biofilms). This study is motivated by desire to decipher the information transferred between the cells and through such signaling try to control physiological activities of biofilms for treating related diseases efficiently. The Lagrangian technique which is the resultant of Hamilton's principle is applied to solve the coupled system of electromechanical oscillators representing the structure of a biofilm. Through this formulations, it is shown how individual cells can radiate electromagnetic waves and at which frequency bands. In addition, synchronization phenomena between the cells within biofilm samples through EM coupling is predicted. Our modeling results indicate presence of EM communication between bacteria within kilohertz to gigahertz ranges.

articleTitle: Generalization Capabilities of Deep Learning Schemes in Solving Inverse Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Inverse scattering problem (ISP) is devoted to retrieving permittivities of dielectric scatterers from the knowledge of measured scattering data, which is highly nonlinear due to multiple scattering that exists in the exact scattering model. Iterative algorithms with regularization are usually used to solve such problems, but they are often time consuming. Recently, deep learning schemes have been proposed to solve full-wave ISP, in which contrasts are directly trained and then estimated with the convolutional neural network (CNN). It was found that even for the tests well out of the range of the training databases, these learning schemes are able to obtain satisfying results since the training of network is conducted on natural pixel bases. In this paper, we compare the generalization capabilities, i.e., the ability to reconstruct unseen data, for different deep learning schemes. Further, methods to improve the generalization capabilities have also been discussed and verified by numerical examples.

articleTitle: Impacts of MRI frequency on RF-induced Heating for External Fixation with Insulating Material
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper investigates the impacts of MRI operating frequency on the RF-induced heating for external fixation with insulating material. It is found that the trend of RF-induced heating varied with the dielectric constant of the insulating material is different at 1.5 T and 3 T. This fact is due to the resonance resulted from the inductance produced by the external fixation and the capacitance introduced by the insulating material.

articleTitle: Micro-Doppler Based Detection of Hovering UAVs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a method for detecting hovering UAVs in ground clutter background. The proposed method is based on both Range-Doppler (RD) map and micro-Doppler signatures, aiming to distinguish the hovering UAV from ground clutter. Frequency modulation characteristic induced by rotating blades is extracted as a unique micro-Doppler signature to discriminate between the hovering UAV and ground clutter. Simulation data is used to verify the performance of the proposed method and results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Application of Sparse Representation to Beamforming for Direction of Arrival Estimation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new technique for high-resolution direction of arrival estimation is presented. The method utilizes the traditional beamforming approach and sparse representation to locate signals in single and multiple emitter scenarios. An example is provided where two emitters are spaced 60 degrees apart and then brought closer together, with the performance of the beamforming approach and new approach compared.

articleTitle: Development of High Gain Virtual-Element Arrays with Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A high gain array using virtual-element Fabry Perot-Cavity Antenna (VE-FPCA) with near field split-beam that emulates a two-element slot array is presented. A novel frequency selective surface (FSS) design is used to split the source antenna beam into two in the near field. Each beam is circular and generated by a square aperture of horizontal slots within the FSS. Comparison of electric field magnitude, phase and beam separation is made between the FPCA system and two-element slot array in the near field. Feedline loss is also compared between both systems. The FPCA has a 5dB far-field gain improvement over the two-element array. It has a constant E-field phase in the E-plane, which is the result of an increased aperture efficiency.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Wideband Connected Dipole Array with Compact Balun and Power Divider
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Microstrip patch antennas are typically used in low- profile array designs. Nevertheless, the bandwidth is usually less than 10% unless special loading and/or feed coupling techniques are used. In this paper, we propose a low-profile (0.09 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</sub>), wideband connected dipole array, operating at a center frequency of 200 MHz. The array consists of 10 × 20 electrically short (0.08 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</sub>) dipole elements, forming a 2.3 m × 2.3 m aperture. The dipole elements are fed in pair using a combination of a tapered microstrip balun and a power divider. Within a small area, the 50 Ω unbalanced coaxial input is matched to two 200 Ω broadside coupled strip lines. The design reduces the profile and avoids the use of narrow 200 Ω microstrip lines. Simulation results show that the antenna array has a 32% bandwidth. As a comparison, a center-fed patch array with the same profile using air substrate would only have a bandwidth of less than 20%.

articleTitle: An Octa-Band Antenna for LTE Mobile Handsets without Ground Clearance
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An octa-band antenna for LTE mobile handsets without ground clearance is proposed and studied. The total size of the mobile phone is 141mm×79mm×7.5mm. The proposed antenna consists of two monopole branches, a match circuit and two open slots. With the help of the match circuit, the two monopole branches are used to produce the main working modes at the lower band (698-960MHz) and the higher band (1710-2690MHz). One of the slots is used to produce a new resonant frequency at the higher band, and the other slot is used to make the lower band matched. The simulated -5 dB impedance bandwidth at the lower band is 268MHz (695-963MHz) and the simulated -6dB impedance bandwidth at the higher band is 1300MHz (1700-3000MHz). The LTE700, GSM850, GSM900, DCS, PCS, UMTS, LTE2300, and LTE2500 bands are covered. The simulated efficiencies are 50-76% and 63-91% at the lower and higher bands, respectively.

articleTitle: On the Location of Transverse Electric Surface Wave Poles for Electrically Thick Substrates
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the transverse electric (TE) surface wave (SW) poles for a grounded single dielectric layer are determined using Mittag-Leffler (ML) expansion method. The poles located using ML expansion method are then compared against existing methods in terms of convergence to final root. This paper shows the effectiveness of ML expansion method by locating SW poles for lossless and lossy dielectric substrates. This method also possess the capability of obtaining more than one SW pole for electrically thick substrates.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Optimization of Meta-atoms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metasurfaces are thin structures that can control electromagnetic propagation in a variety of ways. This is done by designing discrete elements (meta-atoms) with desired properties that form the building blocks of the metasurface. In the past, these meta-atoms have often been comprised of simple shapes (e.g., rectangles, ellipses, split-rings). However, greater throughput and multiple functionalities can be achieved by more complex shapes. In the present work, a single method to represent most shapes is demonstrated. By combining this shape generation method with a multi-objective optimizer, the best meta-atom designs can be found that achieve good performance for multiple objectives. This method is demonstrated by designing a polarization-selective, beam steering application where transmitted electromagnetic radiation deflects into the +1 or -1 diffraction order depending on the incident wave polarization.

articleTitle: Folded 1-bit Transmitarray with Reduced Height
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a low profile folded transmitarray (TA) antenna in Ku-band. The folded TA antenna consisted of a polarization selected transmitting array, a polarization twisting reflector and a microstrip feed antenna. The proposed unit-cell of transmitting surface is based on a pair of identical slot loaded rectangular microstrip patches printed on both the top and the bottom layers. The patches are connected by metallized via holes located at the center. The 1-bit phase shift is realized by physical rotation of the patches. The initial folded TA antenna already shows promising results in terms of directivity and thickness reduction.

articleTitle: Design And Analysis Of FengYun3 Microwave Humidity Sounder(FY3MHS) Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: FY3 microwave humidity sounder (MHS) antenna has the specialties: high gain, low noise, high beam efficiency, high frequency. Offset parabolic apertures with conical corrugated horns are selected for these antennas. The working frequencies of the antenna are 89,118,166GHz and 183GHz separately. Separation of the frequency is carried out by polarization grids. Great challenges are brought about with the stringent demand for the FY3MHS antenna. The analysis and design of this antenna need intercross knowledge of the electromagnetic theory, mechanics, measurements, thermal, orbit knowledge etal.

articleTitle: Wrist-Worn RFID Antenna Printed on Additive Manufactured Flexible Substrate
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We assess the feasibility of fabricating a flexible RFID wrist-worn antenna printed on a substrate manufactured using 3D-printing technology, as to enable full customization of the bracelet at low cost. Numerical results show adequate power transmission to the RFID chip. Also, the fabricated prototype shows enough flexibility to be bent around the wrist.

articleTitle: Space-time modulated cloaks for breaking reciprocity of antenna radiation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In telecommunications, antennas are one of the key elements of the entire system, without which the wireless communication is impossible. It is well-known that antennas are reciprocal devices and exhibit the same properties in transmission and in reception. However, recently breaking the reciprocity of antennas without using ferromagnetic materials is feasible thanks to modulated metamaterials. In this contribution, we show that a properly designed space-time modulated metamaterial cloak can be used to significantly change the realized gain exhibited by an antenna in its transmission and reception mode.

articleTitle: How the Lualualei VLF Antenna was Designed : At the Dawn of the Computer Era
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The beginning of the modern era of computer aided design is traced here in the design of the US Navy's high power VLF transmitting antenna at Lualualei, Hawaii. The roles played by the use of physical scale models and by computer simulation are reviewed and their relative merits are discussed. Rules derived from the fundamental limitations on electrically small antennas are shown to remain valid to guide the designer even with computer methods.

articleTitle: Compact Microstrip Patch Antennas on 3-D Printed Substrates with Dielectric Loading
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, dielectric loading with a high dielectric constant material is investigated for the design of a compact, inset-fed patch antenna using a hybrid 3-D printing approach. Two loading patterns are presented that allow the reduction of the antenna's resonant frequency without increasing its size. Using the substrate loading configurations developed, a resonant frequency identical to that of a purely high dielectric substrate (42% drop from 2.44 GHz to 1.39 GHz) is realized, with a 2 to 4 dB improvement in gain compared to that of the purely high dielectric substrate. Moreover, when compared to the conventional approach to increasing antenna size in order to achieve the same 42% drop in frequency, this design offers a 66% reduction in surface area. The low cost and ease of manufacture furthermore renders these patterns useful to realize compact patch antennas while maintaining good RF performance, thereby offering increased design flexibility.

articleTitle: A Compact Radome Mounted Monopulse Antenna for Direction-Finding Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a compact monopulse antenna which can be fitted inside of a small diameter radome. The monopulse antenna is composed of four antenna elements and each antenna consists of a square open-ended waveguide(OEWG), a stepped impedance matching structure, and a conformal aperture. Because of the compactness and the conformal aperture of the element that can be mounted on the inner surface of the radome, the center space of the radome can be secured, which can provide a space for other sensors or devices. To verify the monopulse performance of the designed antenna, its sum (Σ) and difference (Δ) patterns are calculated. The Σ pattern gains of the antenna are 15.3 dB, 15.1 dB, and 15.4 dB for f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</sub> GHz, f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> GHz, and f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</sub> GHz, respectively. The normalized null depths of the Δ patterns are under -40 dB within the operational frequency.

articleTitle: Grounded Coplanar Waveguide-Fed Millimeter Wave Volumetric Pyramidal Horn on LTCC
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: There is a strong interest to implement antenna-in-package (AiP) systems for a variety of applications such as imaging, beamforming, integrated transceivers, and radars. Substrate integrated horn antennas are valuable AiP candidates due to their small form factor, ease of integration, and high gain. Alternatively, a volumetric packaging approach can significantly reduce the antenna's form factor and enhance the gain. For the first time, in this paper, we present a 94GHz low temperature cofired ceramic (LTCC) integrated volumetric pyramidal horn antenna. Using a vertical LTCC approach, a GCPW-fed single horn antenna was designed. Results show that the antenna operates from 91.6GHz to 95.6GHz for S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> <; 10dB, with a realized gain of 8.7dBi.

articleTitle: A CSRR and SRR Based Ultrawideband MIMO Antenna with Band-Notched Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An ultra-wideband(UWB) multiple input and multiple output(MIMO) antenna consisting of complementary split-ring resonator(CSRR) to improve mutual coupling and split-ring resonator(SRR) is proposed in this paper for automotive communications. The UWB MIMO antenna has a compact size of 54×33mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including two parallel monopoles. The isolation of less than -15db is achieved from 3.1 to 10.6GHz by the SRR located between the two grounds. Moreover, to reject the interference from existing frequencies, the antenna exhibits dual band-notched characteristics at 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> generation band of 3.3-3.6GHz and 4.8-5GHz by applying CSRRs structures on the patch.

articleTitle: Design of Miniaturized ESPAR Antenna for Next Generation Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a miniaturized dual-band electronically steerable parasitic array radiator (ESPAR) antenna with conformal radiation pattern. The designed antenna operates in the bands from 2.3 GHz to 2.53 GHz and from 2.8 GHz to 3.7 GHz. Antenna is capable of 360° beam steering in steps of 60°. The antenna design consists of six folded monopoles and a conical center element. Folded monopoles are used to reduce the antenna size by reducing the height of parasitic monopoles to λ/12. Thus, the designed antenna is three times smaller than the conventional ESPAR antennas. The active element is made conical in shape in order to improve the antenna bandwidth. The proposed design is not only smaller than its conventional counterparts but it also supports dual band operations. In-spite of the compact design peak antenna gain is 6.3 dBi, this gain is equivalent to the conventional ESPAR antenna gain.

articleTitle: A Method for the Measurement of RF Absorber using Spectral Domain Transformations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Indoor antenna ranges must have the walls, floor and ceiling treated with RF absorber. Pyramidal absorber is shaped to create an impedance transform from free space to that of the absorbing material. The pyramidal shape provides this very effectively for normal incidence, but performance typically gets worse as the angle of incidence deviates from normal. Unfortunately, it is difficult to measure reflectivity at large oblique angles because of difficulty differentiating the reflected signal from that of the direct path. In this paper, a novel approach for performing such measurements is introduced. Preliminary measurements are compared to RF simulations. The comparison appears to indicate that this approach is a valid way to perform RF absorber measurements at wide angles.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave Automotive Radar Characterization and Target Simulator Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A millimeter-wave radar characterization setup for retrieving automotive radar profiles is described. Then, an automotive radar target simulator system based on the retrieved radar profile is proposed, implemented, and tested.

articleTitle: A Triple-band Millimeter Wave SIW Antenna with Dual-Sense Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A single-feed single-layer triple-band substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) antenna operating in millimeter wave (mmWave) band with dual-sense circular polarization is presented. The polarization states at three bands are right-hand circular polarization(RHCP), vertical polarization and left-hand circular polarization(LHCP) respectively. The proposed antenna consists of circular patch radiator, annular-ring slot radiator and SIW transmission line. The lower band (28 GHz) and middle band (33 GHz) are generated by the circular patch that at the center of the antenna. The annular-ring slot radiator generats upper band (38 GHz). The proposed antenna has characteristics of low-profile and simple structure.

articleTitle: Scan Properties of Slot-Fed Dielectric Resonator Antenna Arrays for 5G Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An 8×8 array antenna based on dielectric resonator antennas (DRA) fed by a slot antennas is proposed as a base-station antenna for millimeter-wave 5G wireless communications. The total radiation efficiency is modeled as a function of frequency and beam steering. It turns out that the total radiation efficiency is higher than 80% over the frequency band from 26 GHz to 34 GHz and for scan angles up to 60 degrees along the H-plane. The DRA can perform beam steering over wide bandwidth with a scan-loss comparable to the array factor of an ideal source. In addition, The DRA array is 20% smaller in size compared to conventional half-spaced antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Slot-Excited Wideband Horn Antenna with Microstrip Line Feeding for Ka-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An exponentially tapered horn antenna for symmetrical radiation patterns in E/H-planes is presented. The horn antenna is incorporated with the planar feeding network. The antenna is excited through a slot engraved in the ground plane that is transverse to the packaged microstrip feed line (MSL). The single antenna element provides 46% (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub><; -10 dB) bandwidth in the Ka-band with a gain value of 10.3 dBi. An array of 2×2 elements with an MSL corporate-feeding network achieves the gain of 15.7 dBi. The antenna/array shows an excellent radiation performance across the frequency band of 25~40 GHz.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Inverted-F Antenna and Temperature Sensor using Microfluidics Technologies
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel wireless and passive temperature sensor that utilizes 3D printed inverted-F antenna (IFA) microfluidic and liquid metal technologies for the temperature sensor is introduced in this paper. The thermal volume expansion of liquid metal to progressively increase the length of the arm of IFA which will effectively increase or decrease with respect to temperature. In this way, the sensed temperature value can be accurately quantified by the change in its resonant frequency. Simulation result shows the sensitivity of temperature is 2.54 MHz/°C.

articleTitle: New Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna with 4 U-Slots for MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: New compact and low profile pattern reconfigurable antenna with four U-slots is proposed. The size of the antenna is 42 mm * 40 mm * 0.72 mm, and the used substrate is FR-4 with a dielectric constant of 4.4 and a loss tangent of 0.02. The antenna has four pattern configurations which are directed (in HFSS simulation) to phi = 85, 120, 245 and 285 degrees, with simulated peak gains ranging between - 0.11 dB to 2.7 dB at theta = 90 degrees, and with a simulated overlapped 10-dB bandwidth from 3.65 GHz to 3.752 GHz (Overlapped bandwidth is 102 MHz). The simulated efficiencies for all configurations are ranging from 50% to 59%.

articleTitle: Research on Polarization-Reconfigurable Holographic Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the potential of using holographic metasurfaces to realize high directivity radiation with polarization diversity performance is investigated. With the aid of reconfigurable antenna technique, a holographic metasurface antenna with high gain and linear polarization (LP), right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) and left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) diversity is achieved. The antenna consists of a polarization-insensitive holographic metasurface as the radiating structure and an embedded polarization reconfigurable feeding launcher.

articleTitle: A Total-Variation Compressive Processing Approach to Two-Dimensional Field Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An innovative approach based on a total variation (TV) version of the compressive sensing (CS) technique is proposed for the two-dimensional far field reconstruction from a limited number of measurement points. The reconstruction problem is formulated as the minimization of an augmented Lagrangian function. A set of numerical experiments results is provided to assess the potentialities and features of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Integrated Multilayer Yagi Antenna for 5G
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: 5G is announced for 2020 and to fulfil its expectations there will be a great demand for lower latency, higher data rates and better energy efficiency. Taking advantage of the larger bandwidth available, the migration to higher frequencies has been extensively studied in recent years. Thus, the work made to obtain a multilayer Yagi-Uda antenna, operating at 24 GHz, is presented. It has more than 25% bandwidth and almost 11 dBi of gain. This antenna can integrate simple sensors or larger antenna arrays.

articleTitle: New Receiver Technology for Radio Astronomy : A Technology Update from CSIRO and FAST
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Radio astronomy receiver development is focusing on increasing the field of view and bandwidth in tandem with the exponential increase in data volumes permitted by signal processing. We present recent receiver and signal processing developments from CSIRO and FAST.

articleTitle: Characterization of Oils and Oil Mixtures using Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (TDS) transmission analysis as applied to oils typically involves multi-layer sample holders of differing materials. Here we investigate the THz transmission through multilayer systems using a simplified holder design consisting of a milled delrin ring and two thin low-density polyethylene (LDPE) windows. This configuration reduces the complexity of the analysis and increases the accuracy of terahertz time-domain measurements on oil-based samples. We analyze the refractive index and absorption coefficient for different oils. This analysis offers a new approach in monitoring oil quality during manufacturing and degradation with use of oils in food industry. The use of oils that are largely transparent in the THz regime also serves as a medium in which to dissolve chemicals for THz spectroscopic analysis.

articleTitle: Design of A Metamaterial Absorber With Ultra-Wide Angle Incidence
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wide angular metamaterial absorber is proposed through the design of a resistor-loaded planar dipole with artificial magnetic conductor ground. With application of antenna reciprocity, a wide-beam antenna element is designed based on image theory for its ability to receive electromagnetic waves in a wide range of angle and configured as a wide angular absorber. Simulated results show that the metamaterial absorber has achieved 90% absorptivity in the range from −70° to +70°. Besides, the designed absorber can achieve 85% absorptivity under ±80° incident angles. In addition, the thickness of the absorber is only 0.093λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>.

articleTitle: Nonreciprocal Transmission through Locally Time-Modulated Bianisotropic Metafilms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Materials with space-time modulated electromagnetic properties provide a promising route for breaking Lorentz reciprocity as an alternative to conventional platforms based on bulky magnets. In this paper, we demonstrate that nonreciprocal wave propagation can be achieved in thin metasurfaces at normal incidence using solely temporal modulations. The transmission symmetry is lifted due to the asymmetric polarization response of the metasurface expressed in its bianisotropic nature.

articleTitle: Fully Inkjet-printed Tunable Hybrid n-Ripple Miura (n-RiM) Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A first-of-its-kind fully inkjet-printed tunable hybrid n-ripple Miura (n-RiM) frequency selective surface (FSS) is presented that combines the advantages of n-RiM FSS structures (i.e. ultra wideband frequency & bandwidth tunability) and traditional Miura-FSS (i.e. ability to form multilayer FSS structures without mechanical support). They also feature high angle of incidence rejection, making them suitable for wide range of terrestrial and outer-space wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: Bi-Static Simultaneous Transmit And Receive (STAR) Antenna Array System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Bi-static, dual-polarized antenna array subsystem with high isolation between transmitting (TX) and receiving (RX) ports is proposed. Each array consists of eight active patch antenna elements built on a single layer substrate. Microstrip and substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) feed networks are used to excite broadside and scanned beams. It is shown that > 10 dB improvement in isolation can be achieved by employing SIW over microstrip. Each array has realized gain > 11.9 dBi and > 6.1 dBi for broadside and scanned beam (@ θ = 55° and φ=0°), respectively. Measured isolation > 50 dB is achieved between the TX and RX arrays fed by SIW.

articleTitle: Efficient and Misalignment-Robust PT-Symmetric Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We theoretically investigate and experimentally demonstrate a new non-radiative wireless power transfer technique based on the concept of parity-time (PT-) symmetry. Our results show the higher-order PT-symmetric power transfer system has a nearly perfect and constant efficiency in different operating conditions. The proposed technique may solve the main challenge in the conventional wireless powering system which has a fluctuating transfer efficiency in the weak coupling regime. The PT-symmetric non-radiative wireless power transfer will pave the way towards robust and efficient wireless powering of stationary electric vehicles, mobiles, wireless sensors, and implantable medical devices.

articleTitle: Design Guidelines for a Novel Tunable Aperture-Coupled Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the design and analysis of a novel electronically tunable aperture-coupled microstrip patch antenna are presented. The design procedures are illustrated with the help of an example. The measured tuning range of the antenna is 875 MHz (1.395-2.27GHz) for a minimum return loss of 10dB. The paper includes, for the first time, detailed design guidelines as well as important results and insights from simulations and measurements.

articleTitle: ADMM based Consensus and Sectioning Norm-1 Regularized Algorithm for Imaging with a CRA
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A norm-1 regularized, distributed technique based on the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) is presented in this paper. This method divides the sensing matrix of the problem in both rows and columns, leading to the so-called consensus and sectioning-based ADMM, which incorporates the convergence properties of the consensus-based ADMM with the communication efficiency of the sectioning-based ADMM. A Compressive Reflector Antenna (CRA) has been recently proposed as a hardware to increase the sensing capacity of the imaging systems. The combination of the consensus and sectioning-based ADMM with a CRA allows a quasi real-time imaging with high communication efficiency.

articleTitle: Design of Frequency Selective Surfaces for Wide Frequency and Angular Responses
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: For many applications, it is highly desired to have Frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) that have wide frequency (3:1) and angular responses (up to 65<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> for both TE and TM polarizations) along with small ripples in the passband (~1 dB), better than 10 dB attenuation in the specified stopband, and sharp roll-offs at the skirts of the transition regions. To the best of our knowledge, none the existing designs are able to achieve these highly challenging goals, and the objective of this paper to is to propose a new design which is able to meet all of these requirements.

articleTitle: A compact dual band ring antenna with embedding grounded patches
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact nested ring patch antenna with grounded vias is proposed in this paper. The outer ring and the meandered inner ring of the proposed antenna are nested in a single radiation layer for miniaturization. The antenna size is further reduced through embedding four small patches with grounded vias in the meandered inner ring. The side length of the inner square ring is only .16 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub> (guided wavelength), while the side length of the outer square ring is 0.25λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Application in a Circular Microstrip Antenna Developed for the Detection of Partial Discharges
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, the evaluation of the metamaterial application in the gain improvement of a circular microfita antenna developed for the detection of partial discharges is presented. For this, a rectangular Split Ring Resonator was combined with Capacitive Load Strip for the development of the proposed metamaterial unit cell. The designed metamaterial was individually simulated for the evaluation of its double negativity features (ε <; 0, μ <; 0). After the individual simulation, the metamaterial was applied as a superstrate for the evaluation of the impact on the circular reference microstrip antenna gain. From the obtained results, it was possible to verify that the application of the superstrate composed by metamaterial resulted in the increase of 1.15 dB in the reference antenna average gain.

articleTitle: Fast prediction of MRI RF-induced heating for a generic stent with arbitrary orientation using ANN
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a three-layer feed forward artificial neural network (ANN) is proposed to fast predict the radio frequency (RF)-induced heating for a generic stent with arbitrary posture under 1.5T MRI. The stent is studied of its RF-induced heating in various parameters, e.g. stent length, diameter and orientation, and the specific absorption rate (SAR) is adopted to characterize the heating level. 336 stent models are created and simulated based on the feasible stent parameters, 70% of which are utilized to train the ANN and the other 30% are utilized to test the performance of the ANN. It is shown that the simulated results and the predicted results are in good consistency. The maximum error between the target and the output is less than 7.6 W/kg. The correlation coefficient between the target and the output is larger than 0.998 for the testing data and 0.999 for all data.

articleTitle: Arbitrary High Order Discontinuous Galerkin Transient Analysis of Periodic Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An arbitrary high order discontinuous Galerkin time domain method is proposed for periodic structure analysis. Periodic boundary conditions are implemented to efficiently truncate the computational domain by using a transformed field variable approach. An arbitrary high order scheme is presented for the time integration of the transformed semi-discrete discontinuous Galerkin system. The accuracy and capability of the proposed method are demonstrated by analyzing the electromagnetic scattering from an infinite dielectric slab under both normal and oblique incidence illumination.

articleTitle: Metagrating-Inspired Approach for Suppressing Reflections in H-Plane Waveguide Bends
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a semianalytical technique for achieving perfect transmission of power across H-plane bends in rectangular single-mode waveguides. Inspired by recent work on metagratings, we utilize a single polarizable element in conjunction with modal analysis to eliminate spurious scattering. This simple concept, verified via full-wave simulations, forms an attractive alternative to the cumbersome waveguide deformations commonly used to implement this functionality to date.

articleTitle: Time-modulated reflective metasurface for the control of the reflected signal frequency
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, we present a time-modulated full-reflective metasurface able to realize a frequency shift of the illuminating electromagnetic wave. The metasurface consists of an array of metallic patches printed on a grounded electrically thin dielectric substrate. The patches are loaded by a set of varactors controlled by a low-frequency time-varying voltage signal. The varactors change in real-time the response of the metasurface realizing the required reflection response for achieving the frequency shift. We report here our preliminary results, showing the ability of the metasurface to reflect a frequency-shifted signal according to the modulation imparted by the varactors. The proposed metasurface is a bi-dimensional version of the recently proposed Doppler cloak, a spatiotemporally modulated metamaterial cover to be placed in front or wrapped around a moving object to restore locally the source illumination frequency, as if it were not in motion.

articleTitle: Effects of Large Angle of Incidence in Offset-Fed Reflectarray Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the effects of large angle of incidence in offset-fed reflectarray antennas using the single-layer ring is presented. When the incidence angle becomes large, the reflection phase of the ring becomes highly frequency dispersive. As a result, the normal-incidence reflection phase curve is no longer valid for designing the element to compensate the spatial phase delay. The phase error will shift the reflected beam direction and reduce the antenna gain.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of a Dual-Band Impedance Transformer Based on an Embedded MTM-EBG
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a dual-band impedance transformer using an embedded metamaterial-based electromagnetic bandgap structure (MTM-EBG). The MTM- EBG has a controllable bandgap with dispersive passbands on either side, which possess points of identical phase at arbirtary and designable frequencies. In this work, a MTM-EBG was designed to appear as a quarter wavelength 70.7 Ω microstrip transmission line to convert 50 Ω to 100 Ω at two frequencies: 2.4 GHz and 5.0 GHz, by using these points of equal phase. The resulting structure was then fabricated and tested, with experimental results demonstrating excellent agreement with the simulated data.

articleTitle: A High Performance Terahertz Metalens
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a high performance terahertz (THz) metalens with attractive features such as high numerical aperture and high transmission efficiency, which has not been reported in the literature. A metalens prototype operating at 1.56 THz has been designed, fabricated and characterized. The measured results agree well with theoretical predictions, validating the performance of the proposed THz metalens.

articleTitle: Measuring GPS Transmit Antenna Pattern Using On-Orbit Receivers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel method to calibrate the transmit antenna pattern of the GPS satellites, using the zenith antenna mounted on each of the 8 small satellites of the NASA CYGNSS mission. The zenith measurements are calibrated using an end-to-end calibration. The pattern of the zenith antenna is calibrated using the multiple published GPS transmit antenna patterns. A weighted spherical harmonic fitting algorithm is used to minimize the impacts by the measurement noise. The weighted RMSD of two independently calibrated patterns using GPS PRN 21 and 28 is only 0.31 dB. The 8 calibrated CYGNSS zenith patterns are used to accurately and precisely calibrate the GPS transmit antenna pattern over the full terrestrial service volume for all 32 GPS satellites. The calibrated patterns have 0.5 × 0.5 degree resolution while the published patterns have a 2 × 10 degree resolution. The calibrated patterns are significant to resolve many open challenges in Earth remote sensing using the reflected GPS signal and accurate on-orbit calibration of antenna pattern for small satellites and CubeSats. The research is useful to the system design, engineering calibration and science investigation for future small satellite missions using Signals of Opportunity (SoOP).

articleTitle: Comparative study of Four Path Loss Models for UWB off-body Propagation Channel Inside a Mine
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this study, four path loss (PL) models are generated to describe the UWB off-body propagation inside a mine. Frequency domain measurements campaigns allow extracting the frequency responses at different distances from the transmitter. Residuals are greatly minimized for the optimal PL model with an RMSE value of 0.4 dB. The scattering-rich mine environment causes an abundance of multipath components (as denoted by the impulse responses results) and frequency selective fading (as observed in the frequency responses). The PL exponent is considerably lower than that of free space due to wave guiding effect of the mine tunnel.

articleTitle: Wideband Printed Antenna Arrays for 5G Mobile Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present two novel edge-located, wideband phased array designs for 5G mobile applications. Using the edge of the smart device as reference, one of the arrays is parallel- polarized, while the other is perpendicularly-polarized. Both arrays are stripline-fed, and their geometries are realized using Duroid 5880 laminates. The array elements generally consists of an integrated balun, a ground plane formed using via walls and dipole radiator elements that are capacitively-coupled with adjacent elements to form a tightly-coupled array topology. By balancing the mutual capacitance between the elements, the inductance from the ground plane and the length (parallel) or impedance (perpendicular) of the balun, compact arrays (λ/5 and λ/8 for parallel- and perpendicular polarizations, respectively) are achieved, having continuous bandwidth coverage from 24 GHz to 86 GHz with VSWR <; 2 and broadside and VSWR <; 3 when scanned to at least ±40° in both E- and H-plane. A finite 4 x 4 array with a 4-to-1 combiner (in E-plane) is designed for fabrication and measurement, with appropriate terminations added to the edge elements to compensate for the reduced mutual capacitance. The two finite array designs achieve VSWR <; 2.2 throughout the entire 5G frequency bands, with realized gain of ≥ 8 dB above 50 GHz.

articleTitle: RCS of Complex Targets via Compressive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Compressive Sensing (CS) is a novel signal processing paradigm that allows sampling of compressible signals at lower than Nyquist rate. In this paper, CS is combined with an accelerated iterative thresholding algorithm to successfully improve the efficiency of commercial electromagnetic simulation software in solving the Radar Cross Section (RCS) of complex conducting targets at L-band. The proposed method is particularly effective in solving high angular resolution RCS by enforcing signal compressibility while considering target complexity and frequency. The simulated RCS results of a KingAir aircraft at L-band frequencies demonstrated the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Modeling and Measurement of Ducted EM Propagation over the Gulf Stream
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The study of atmospheric refractive conditions is essential in the shipboard radars and radio communication conditions in the maritime environment. Especially at low altitudes, as radio refractivity can vary considerably with both height and range, characterizing marine atmospheric boundary layer properties, ducting in particular, is thus crucial for air-sea interaction research. The numerical weather prediction model Navy Atmospheric Vertical Surface Layer Model (NAVSLaM) is used to estimate the refractive structure of the evaporation duct as a function of height and range using the environmental conditions in the region of the Gulf Stream, and the refractive profiles are used as input to Advanced Propagation Model (APM) for predicting the EM propagation across the Gulf Stream boundary. The data measured during the CASPER-East at-sea experimental campaign, which was conducted off the coast of Duck, NC, during October-November of 2015, are compared with the simulated propagation loss based on the range-dependent profile predicted from NAVSLaM.

articleTitle: Wideband printed ridge gap waveguide differential feeding aperture antenna for millimeter wave applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Millimeter wave has gained great attention for 5G communications and imaging systems. Building a high gain antenna is essential to such systems. In this paper, the design of a high gain differential feeding aperture antenna in the printed ridge gap waveguide technology is presented. It has a fractional bandwidth of 16.1% at 30 GHz with S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> <; -10 dB and peak gain of 12.8 dBi. The aperture efficiency is 52% and the radiation pattern is stable over the operating frequency range. The 3-dB gain bandwidth is 15.4% dBi.

articleTitle: A Multi-Resolution Evolutionary Programming Technique For GPR Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An efficient inverse scattering multi-step technique is proposed for dealing with large-scale high-contrast buried scenarios. This method is based on evolutionary programming (EP) stochastic optimizer that ensure a reliable inversion in high-contrast problems. Moreover, an iterative multi-resolution approach (IMRA) is integrated with EP, to guarantee the convergence of large-scale problems. This algorithm starts with using large meshes in lower frequencies, and then, step by step, tighten the borders of search domain to the estimated target location to increase the resolution, without increasing the number of unknown parameters. This method is assessed by implementing it to a large-scale high-contrast GPR scenario. The presented results show that this technique can be considered as an efficient and reliable inversion technique for such applications. Moreover, comparing IMRA-EP results with IMRA-PSO, indicates that the proposed method significantly outperforms the latter.

articleTitle: A Log-Periodic based Broadband Reject Filter for Dielectric Constant Characterization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a broadband reject filter for dielectric constant characterization is presented. Four complementary open loop resonators (OLRs), which follow a modified log-periodic distribution, are etched beneath a tapered feed line to achieve a broadband rejection response for the proposed filter. The configuration of the embedded log-periodic resonators is designed to attain high sensitivity to lossy material over the 1.25-2.25 GHz frequency span. A prototype of the proposed filter is fabricated and tested to validate its sensitivity and performance in terms of differentiating among various dielectric constant levels for a material under test (MUT). An average sensitivity of 0. 42 dB/ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> and 3. 65°/ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> is achieved at f = 2. 25 GHz.

articleTitle: A Defected Ground Structure for Circularly Polarized (CP) Microstrip Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a single-feed circularly polarized (CP) microstrip antenna achieved by defected ground structure. With the proposed DGS, a new resonant mode is added, which is orthogonal to the original resonant mode. These two modes will have the same magnitude and the 90° time-phase difference by adjusting the DGS dimensions, which contributes to achieve the CP radiation. Both the simulated and measured 10-dB impedance bandwidth of the CP microstrip antenna are 30 MHz, while the 3-dB axial-ratio bandwidth is 6 MHz. The CP gain across the 3-dB AR band ranges from 4.6 to 5.0 dBic.

articleTitle: Adaptive Equalization Super-Resolution Time Delay Estimation with High Accuracy and Low Complexity
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An adaptive multipath equalization time delay estimation (METDE) algorithm is presented to estimate the time delays of received signals through a multipath channel with high accuracy and resolution. The proposed approach is developed utilizing a sequential minimization of a square error function that is updated according to the difference of received data and pre-known model at each moment. The METDE algorithm is uniquely established through a multi-tap equalizer structure and without using any complex optimization or matrix inversion operation. Thus, it will have lower complexity and better compatibility with practical hardware implementation in the real-time systems. The mathematical formulation and the accuracy analyses of the METDE algorithm are derived in the paper through numerical simulations and experimental tests. Providing 95% improved resolution compared to the Fourier limit, the proposed approach is a good candidate in low-frequency applications to mitigate the Fourier limit on the range resolution and achieve higher penetration in lossy environments.

articleTitle: Design of High Gain Single Layer Reflectarray Antenna using Ring and Double Square Elements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A center feed reflectarray antenna is presented in this paper. Reflectarray antenna surface consists of the single layer unit cells. Each unit cell has a circular ring and a double square. Dimensions of the unit cells are selected such that a progressive phase shift is achieved at each unit cell. The Proposed reflectarray antenna has a gain of 30.86 dBi at 18 GHz. The designed antenna shows good performance in terms of gain and phase range. This makes our antenna design simple, cost-effective and lightweight as compared to other single layer reflectarray antennas.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Positioning Calibration Technology Based on Kriging Interpolation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The electromagnetic positioning system is a system that uses the spatial magnetic field strength to obtain the position and direction angle of the receiving sensor in real time, and is widely used in virtual reality and medical navigation. Due to its inherent characteristics, the electromagnetic positioning system receiving sensor is easy to lost the accuracy and stability of its positioning and tracking results due to external interference, resulting in a large positioning error, so the calibration work is very important for it. In this paper, the spatial sampling points are divided into tetrahedrons by Delaunay triangulation to interpolate and the Kriging interpolation algorithm is used to compensate the accuracy. Through experiment and simulation, the position and direction angle accuracy is significantly improved, and it is shown that the performance of proposed method is better than traditional polynomial fitting and traditional interpolation algorithms.

articleTitle: Dual-band Printed Monopole Antenna for Indoor MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-band printed multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is presented. The antenna has a modified rectangular ground plane for improving isolation between radiating ports and two monopole radiators. The antenna provides two operating bands centered at 1.5 and 2.35 GHz, covering GPS, WLAN, and LTE2300 bands. The isolation between the antenna elements is better than 10 dB across 1.5 GHz-band and 21.5 dB across 2.35 GHz-band where an isolation structure is employed between elements. The proposed MIMO antenna shows good radiation characteristics and diversity performance. Measured and simulated results are generally in good agreement.

articleTitle: Extrapolation of Antenna Near-Field Measurements Using the Iterative Greedy Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: There are often missing gaps in the antenna near-field measurements, due to various physical limitations. However, the missing data are indispensable if we want to accurately evaluate the complete far-field pattern by the near-field to far-field transformations. To address this problem, a fast extrapolation method based on the iterative greedy algorithm is proposed to reconstruct the missing part of antenna near-field measurements in this paper. The near-field data is approximated by sparse signals with the Fourier basis, which is recoverable by the greedy pursuits. As the near-field data in this paper is obtained on the spherical measurement surface, the far field of the antenna is calculated by the spherical near-field to far-field transformation with the extrapolated data. Some numerical results are given to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed scheme in extrapolating antenna near-field measurements.

articleTitle: Beam Reconfiguration Using Imaging Reflector Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Beam reconfiguration of antenna payloads is becoming an essential requirement for future satellite systems used for commercial and military communications. This paper presents an imaging reflector antenna system that achieves beam reconfiguration using a cost-effective method.

articleTitle: Multiple-Polarized UHF RFID System for UAV Wireless Item Management
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Multiple-polarized ultra-high frequency (UHF) radio frequency identification (RFID) system for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) wireless item management is presented in this paper. The system has the RF sensing part on UAV and data acquisition part on the server. A sensing part consists of the polarization selective antenna, UHF RFID reader module, and zigbee module for transmitting data to the server.
