For minimizing the polarization loss, the proposed sensing part perform the sensing by changing the quadruple-polarization modes such as two linear polarizations and two circular polarizations. The server is able to transfer the command for operating RF sensing system and receive the RFID tag information. These two parts of the system communicate airborne UAV to server. To demonstrate wireless item management, the proposed system is implemented and verified by the two differential experiments.

articleTitle: Low-Cost and High-Gain W-Band Circularly Polarized SIW Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel circularly polarized (CP) SIW cavity backed slot antenna is proposed for W-band operation. It is composed of SIW cavity, an aperture coupling slot, two radiation slots and a lower metallic WR-10. CP operation is achieved by embedding two perturbation stubs around the two opposite corners of the radiation slots. A low-loss WR-10 waveguide is adopted to excite TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">220</sub> cavity mode through an aperture coupled slot for the proposed antenna, and the radiation loss as well as substrate loss of the feed line are significantly decreased. Results show that the antenna exhibits an impedance bandwidth (IBW) with |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <; -10 dB from 89.9 to 96.8 GHz (7.43%), and a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) from 90.3 to 95 GHz (5.08%) with the peak gain of the antenna is 10.5 dBi. Results of full-wave simulation by virtue of HFSS demonstrate the design.

articleTitle: A Wideband Top-Hat Loaded Monocone Antenna Using Shorting Strips
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband top-loaded monocone antenna with shorting strips is proposed. By loading the shorting strips and the top-hat with two slots, the miniaturization of an antenna is achieved. The shorting strips from the monocone-hat to the ground plane are mounted to improve the antenna bandwidth at the low frequency band and the slots inside the top-hat is inserted to improve the impedance matching characteristic in the mid frequency band. From the simulation results, the -10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidth of the proposed antenna is ranging from 1.05 GHz to 10.4 GHz.

articleTitle: 77 GHz Screen Printed, Flexible, Beam-Switching Antenna Array for Wearable Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: mm-Wave radars are widely used in the automotive industry, but the concept is rather new for wearable applications, such as detection of obstacles for visually impaired people. Beam-switching techniques for radar antennas, typically, are either complicated or bulky, whereas for wearable applications, simpler methods are desirable. In this paper, we present a high gain antenna array with a low profile and a simple beam-switching design. The concepts of parasitic antenna array and partially reflective surface have been combined to simultaneously achieve a narrow beam (higher gain) as well as beam-switching. Additive manufacturing (screen printing) has been utilized which ensures flexibility (essential for wearable applications) and a lower cost. A ±30° beam switching and 11-13 dB realized gain has been achieved, which is deemed suitable for the given application.

articleTitle: UHF Rectenna for Implanted and Free Space Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a UHF rectenna that is able to communicate with an RFID reader at a distance of 50 cm when it is implanted in human muscle phantom, and at a distance of 6 m when in free space, is described. The antenna has a size of 38 mm by 12.7 mm. An experimental prototype of the rectenna was fabricated on a Rogers R3010 substrate that is optimized to operate with a commercial RFID tag IC. The optimal rectenna was tested in a liquid phantom mimicking the properties of muscle. Experiments showed successful detection when the designed tag was submerged by 5 cm of liquid phantom at a detection distance of 50 cm.

articleTitle: A new Gradient Descent Positioning Method in Wireless Sensor Network Based on Received Signal Strength
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this article, we propose a new localization technique in a wireless sensor network (WSN), using the gradient descent optimization algorithm, combined with the Received Signal Strength (RSS) method. In this work, a new objective function is represented as the sum of the difference between the real and estimated power. By applying gradient descent technique on this objective function, the positions of unknown nodes are estimated. Simulation results have shown the efficiency of our proposed method in accurately localizing numerous unknow nodes, using an RSS- based technique.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Metasurface Lens Thin Antenna with 3-State Unit Cells in 28-GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This article presents a metasurface lens thin antenna in 28-GHz band for continuously beam scanning. It comprises a 20×20 array of 3-state unit cells and a slot source as first radiator. In unit cell design, PIN diodes are used to obtain phase states switching. The cascaded structure achieves 360° phase shift coverage with 0°/100°/200° phase states. The antenna aperture size is 100mm×100mm with 40mm height. In full wave simulation, a maximum gain of 23.2dBi and ±40° beam steering angle with over 20.0dBi gain are obtained.

articleTitle: Modeling of Power Delay Profile in the Desktop Size Metal Cavity at 300 GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a two-dimensional (2D) geometrical propagation model for line-of-sight (LoS) communication in the desktop size metal cavity environment at 300 GHz. Based on the developed geometrical model, a parameter reference model and power delay profile (PDP) have been derived. The simulated PDPs have been compared with measured PDPs and good agreement has been observed.

articleTitle: Beamforming Optimization based on Kalman Filter for Vehicle in Constrained Route
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: By analyzing a simplified model for vehicles in a constrained route like High Speed Railway (HSR), it is found that when the distance between transmitter and route is short, the Direction of Arrival (DOA) changing speed is not a negligible effect. A Kalman Filter based solution is then proposed to fuse the vehicle speed sensor and DOA estimation. By using the filtered angle from Kalman filter, power loss due to angle mismatch could be reduced by more than 4dB for 4 elements antenna beamformer in the simulated scenario.

articleTitle: Omega-bianisotropic Wire-Loop Huygens’ Metasurface for Wide-Angle Refraction
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Huygens' metasurfaces allow the arbitrary control of electromagnetic waves by utilizing both electric and magnetic currents. These electrically thin structures interact with incident electromagnetic waves on a sub-wavelength scale to produce desired wave effects. To realize Huygens' metasurfaces, different unit cell topologies such as the wire-loop or the stacked-layer configurations can be utilized. In recent years, Omega-bianisotropic Huygens' metasurfaces have been demonstrated utilizing asymmetric stacked-layer unit cells, allowing the realization of reflectionless transformations. However, an Omega-bianisotropic version of the wire-loop unit cell has yet to be demonstrated for modulated Huygens' metasurfaces. In this paper, the design and fullwave simulation results of Omega-bianisotropic Huygens' wire-loop metasurfaces for reflectionless wide-angle refraction from normal incidence to 71.8° for both transverse-electric and transverse-magnetic polarizations centered at 20GHz are presented.

articleTitle: Approximate Inverse of the Rao-Wilton-Glisson Basis Functions Gram Matrix via Monopolar Representation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Starting from the monopolar representation of the Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) functions, an approximate inverse (AI) of the RWG Gram matrix is constructed, where only 3x3 matrices for all individual triangles have to be inverted. The inversion of the Gram matrix is, however, only approximate, since it results as the inverse of a product of singular matrices, which is not easily obtained. The AI is shown to be an effective preconditioner for the RWG Gram matrix and is in particular useful for ill-conditioned Gram matrics on distorted meshes.

articleTitle: Improved Reconstruction Method Based on k-Means by Finding Peak Density Automatically in Microwave Induced Thermoacoustic Tomography
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Microwave induced thermoacoustic tomography is a developing non-destructive method combining microwave imaging and ultrasound imaging which has potential for biomedical imaging, especially for early breast tumor detection. In real breast tumor detection, tissues to be detected are usually acoustic heterogeneous which will result in distortions. In our previous research, k-means has been used for clustering different tissues in the process of inversion instead of iterative method which can save computational resources and time. But image quality is largely determined by the initial choice of the cluster centers and the number of tissue types should be pre-set. In this paper, an improved reconstruction method according to human breast anatomical structure is proposed to improve the quality of image. The proposed method uses decision graphs to find the number of tissue types automatically and ensure that the cluster centers are characterized by a higher density than other points around them. Simulations of real breast anatomical model demonstrate that image reconstructed based on the updated inhomogeneous acoustic property is better than that based on homogeneous one and the proposed method also shows better robustness with respect to model error compared with k-means only based method.

articleTitle: A PSK Modulation Scheme for Sensor Integrated RFIDs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a PSK based modulation scheme is proposed in the RFID framework for transmitting at high bit rates from the tag. The PSK modulation circuit is compatible with the existing passive RFID tag RF front end circuit. The modulation scheme is useful for high speed sensor integrated with RFID applications. The PSK modulation and demodulation circuits are fabricated on PCB and the measurement results are reported.

articleTitle: Hardware Realization and Performance Measurement of an Anti-Jam GPS Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A four-port anti-jam GPS antenna array is used to electronically steer pattern nulls in the direction of incoming RF interference. Null-steering weights are applied using physical hardware and reception pattern measurements are made in an anechoic chamber for multiple jammer angles-of-arrival. Jammer suppression and null misalignment for two null steering reference element cases are compared.

articleTitle: Parallel-Plate Waveguides Formed by Arbitrary Impedance Sheets
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we introduce and study parallel-plate-waveguide structures that are formed by two penetrable metasurfaces having arbitrary sheet impedances. We investigate the guided modes which can propagate in such structures and derive the corresponding dispersion relations. Different scenarios including series- and parallel-resonant impedance sheets are considered. The obtained theoretical formulas are applied to predict the dispersion properties for different separations between the two symmetric or asymmetric metasurfaces.

articleTitle: A V2X Communication System Test on Sea
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Maritime radio communication is modernizing day by day to avoid collision among ships and reduce traffic congestion. The emerging vehicular communication technologies like V2X can overcome these challenges on land and possibly applied on sea.In this paper, the possibility of using the V2X communication systems at sea is examined. The challenges faced in maintaining a reliable communication link over the sea surface is discussed. The results and discussion in this paper will help in the understanding of the variations in received signal strength from land to over the sea surfaces. Severe blockages due to large vessels crossing the link and their effects on link reliability is examined. The measured signal strength is compared with the existing empirical models. The maximum range of this V2X communication system over the unique sea channel is examined.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Sub-Gridded FDTD for Efficient Time Reversal Simulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Based on the sub-gridding scheme, in this paper, a hybrid method including explicit finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) and implicit Crank-Nicolson (CN) FDTD is proposed for efficient time reversal (TR) simulation in an indoor environment. The whole computational program can be run with a common time step determined by the coarse grid in a stable fashion since CN-FDTD is unconditionally stable and its time step can be set to a large value. A numerical example of TR wave propagation in an electrically large environment is included to validate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Array Optimization for Maximum Realized Gain in Terahertz Antenna with Lens
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The main shortcoming of the photoconducting terahertz sources is their low output power. Traditionally the antenna beam is focused using a dielectric lens to achieve high directivity but, since the radiated power of an antenna is in the order of micro watt, the power which comes out of the lens is very low. One way to increase the output power is to use an array of antennas to feed the lens. Here we investigate the effect of the antenna size and the array pitch on the realized gain of the system which consists of the antenna array and a lens. Simulation results for different antenna sizes and different pitch values of the antenna array are provided. Based on the simulation results, increasing number of array elements, increases total output power but directivity of the systems decreases. At lower frequencies the array with larger elements has higher realized gain but, the array element size does not have any effect at higher frequencies.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Planar Microwaves Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a sensor design concept for enhancing the electromagnetic energy stored in the sensing volume is presented. The design concept is based on using a three-dimensional capacitor to enhance the stored electric energy in the sensing volume that is exposed to the material under test. For validation, a resonator based on a split-ring resonator (SRR) was utilized to design a sensor. The concept was tested using numerical simulation to characterize dielectric materials.

articleTitle: 2-D Pattern Reconfigurable Array Antenna with Excitation Phase Difference Circuit
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a sparse array antenna using two-dimensional pattern reconfigurable antenna. In order to cut down the manufacturing cost of active phased array antenna, the number of T/R modules is drastically reduced. The proposed antenna composes of four patch antenna elements as subarrays, and subarray spacing increases in size. The radiation pattern of the subarray can be changed by varying the excitation phase of each element with simple feed circuit. Thus, to avoid the degradation of antenna performances due to arising grating lobes, the proposed antenna improves the gain of the main lobe direction and can reduce the gain in the direction at which the grating lobe arise. The effectiveness of the proposed antenna is verified through the numerical simulation.

articleTitle: A Planar Ultrawideband Wide-angle Scanning Tightly Coupled Array Loaded With Metal Strips
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A planar ultrawideband wide-angle scanning tightly coupled array based on capacitance coupled slot antenna is proposed in this paper. The element consists of tightly coupled slot antenna, microstrip-to-coaxial transition and wide angle impedance matching layer. A series capacitance is introduced in the feeding line to improve the low-frequency performance. Periodic metal strips loaded above the antenna serve as wide angle impedance matching layer to improve the scanning performance of the array. The proposed array achieves a bandwidth of 3.87:1 with voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) VSWR<; 3 when scanning up to 60° in both E and H plane. The cross polarization is lower than -9dB when scanning to 60° in D plane.

articleTitle: A Massive MIMO Array Antenna Incorporating Filtering Sub-Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes the design and realization of a Massive MIMO array antenna which incorporates 16 filtering sub-arrays (i.e., array of 1-by-2 elements). The sub-arrays operates at 3.55 GHz which is an allocated frequency with in the CBRS (Citizen Broadband Radio Service) band to cover a bandwidth of approximately 100 MHz. Two stacked microstrip patch antennas connected by two highly isolated feed networks enable a sub-array to provide slanted +/-45-deg. polarization, with the port-to-port coupling of less than -23 dB. The feed networks, which are slightly different in structure, overcome the traces crossover issue by employing a combination of series and corporate feeding scheme. The embedded gain of the sub-array on average is nearly 11.5 dB where the cross-polarization rejection ratio is 20 dB in broadside direction. The initial performance evaluation of the fabricated filtering array, including the matching condition and frequency selectivity testing, demonstrated an acceptable agreement with numerical predictions.

articleTitle: Gain Optimization of a Yagi-Uda Antenna using the Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 5.8-GHz Yagi antenna consisting of a reflector and one director is optimized for high gain using the classic method and then optimized even more using the Genetic Algorithms. The approach was to divide the director into pixels and then to cut away a random number of randomly placed pixels, then to find the best antenna performances in terms of gain and return loss. The proposed configuration achieved a 0.33 dB improvement in realized gain and is suitable for wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Liquid Metal Broadband Monopole for Stretchable Electronics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a broadband monopole antenna made out of smart materials for stretchable electronics. The antenna consists of a liquid conductor and a thermoplastic - Galinstan (gallium indium and tin) for the radiating element and SEBS (styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene) for the antenna substrate. The antenna is simulated with a full-wave solver and is compared to measurement. The simulated result is in a good agreement with the measured. The reflection coefficients show broadband characteristics from 1.4 GHz to 6 GHz.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Deep Learning Technology for Radar Target Identification
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a new electromagnetic deep learning technology to radar target identification implemented via a novel spatial singularity expansion method (S-SEM). The proposed approach utilizes a recently-found radiation function that holds the spatial parameters of targets defined as the surface current and the geometrical details. Through EM machine learning, an estimation of these parameters is performed in a form of inverse problems for a single wire system. The estimated parameters, which are the S-SEM data, length and orientation, are validated and compared with numerical results obtained from the EM solver where an excellent agreement is achieved.

articleTitle: Covariance Matrix Evaluation of a Diversity Slot Antenna for Vehicular Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-port slot antenna is proposed for vehicular communications. The antenna works at 5.9 GHz in intelligent transportation system (ITS) band. The diversity performance of the design is evaluated using a novel covariance matrix methodology based on reciprocity theorem. The performance evaluation at the early design stage is explained for the first time by relating the radiation pattern of the designed antenna to the effective length matrix. The antenna offers -21 dB of isolation and a minimum gain of 6.5 dB before mounting on the vehicle roof. The evaluated effective diversity gain is 8.6 db.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Wideband Circularly Polarized Antenna Array Using SIW-Fed S-Dipole Elements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a millimeter-wave (mm-wave) wideband circularly polarized (CP) antenna array which is composed of novel SIW-fed S-dipole elements. Each array element consists of two rotational symmetric curved arms which form an "S" shaped geometry. By exciting the element differentially through aperture coupling, the S-shaped element can radiate CP wave within a wide frequency range. A 4 × 4 array is fabricated by cost-effective PCB technology to investigate the performance of the proposed design. Good agreements between the simulation and measurement results are observed and it is noticed that the proposed array achieves a wide impedance bandwidth from 25 GHz to 32.7 GHz (26.7%), a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth from 24.1 GHz to 34.6 GHz (35.8%) and a 3-dB gain bandwidth from 24.8 GHz to 33.5 GHz (30%). With its planar structure and excellent performance, this antenna is suitable for various mm-wave applications.

articleTitle: An Efficient Design Approach for Wideband Tightly Coupled Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a design method based on equivalent circuit model (ECM) to efficiently construct the antenna structure for the tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) with assigned impedance matching performance. It is noted that this method can be even applied to the TCDA with the dipoles using non-standard shape. To discuss the scalability of this method, two antenna structures using difform dipoles are respectively optimized by the ECM setting different goals. The HFSS simulation results of the two optimized antenna structures are respectively in accordance with their ECM results, while this phenomenon indicates that the proposed method has good scalability and accuracy. In addition, the parametric analysis of the two antenna structure is proceeded to show that the ECM can basically maintain the accuracy when the variables are changed.

articleTitle: Pattern Reconfigurable Dielectric Resonator Antenna Actuated by Shorted Parasitic Elements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel pattern reconfigurable cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna is presented. It is based on mode excited by the probe located at the center of dielectric resonator. Centrosymmetric parasitic elements on the lateral wall of cylindrical dielectric resonator and the corresponding diodes between them and ground plane are used for actuating different radiation pattern. It has omnidirectional state and beam-steering capacity. When 16 parasitic elements are adopted, 16 maximum beam directions states are equally distributed with interval of 30° in the azimuth plane under diodes ON in proper order.

articleTitle: A New Millimeter Wave FMCW Radar Target Simulator Based on Frequency Synchronization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new frequency-modulated continuous-wave radar target simulator based on frequency estimation is proposed. This cost-effective platform has a target range simulation accuracy less than 4 cm in frequency band 76~81 GHz.

articleTitle: Radar Cross Section Reduction of A Foldable Microstrip Patch Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Radar Cross Section (RCS) reduction of a foldable microstrip patch array is studied in this work. The proposed array is initially designed with a novel hinge that allows the array to fold approximately 360<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>. By replacing the ground plane with an appropriately designed Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) an RCS reduction of 10 dB, for both TE and TM polarizations, is achieved in the band where the FSS acts as a passband filter.

articleTitle: MoM Analysis of Conducting Surface-to-Wire Structures in Multilayered Uniaxial Media
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a method of moments (MoM) analysis for conducting bodies composed of surfaces connected to thin wires in multilayered uniaxial anisotropic media, such as often occurs in modeling geophysical problems. Wire, wire-to-surface junction, and RWG bases are used to model electric currents on the thin wire, junction, and conducting surfaces, respectively. Based on the transverse equivalent network (TEN) analogy with transmission lines, the dyadic Green's function for multilayered uniaxial media is efficiently evaluated using Kummer's method to accelerate the spectral integral contributions by extracting their asymptotic spectral forms, which are later restored in spatial forms derived from the Sommerfeld identity; this also reduces the spatial singularities of the spectral integrals such that they may be efficiently interpolated using a simplex interpolation scheme. A major contribution of this work is to model surface-to-wire junctions for structures penetrating layer boundaries in a multilayered uniaxial medium. In addition, a proper numerical scheme for modeling thin wire structures in multilayered uniaxial media is proposed.

articleTitle: Characterization of Biological Tissues Using a Suspended Microstrip Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a simple ex-vivo method to characterize the dielectric properties of biological tissues is demonstrated using a proximity-fed suspended microstrip ring resonator. Samples of porcine tissue are placed between the microstrip feed lines and the ring resonator. Using typical porcine bio-material data, the layout of the loaded resonator and feeds are optimized by full-wave simulations to obtain a discernable resonance signature in insertion loss profile. Measurements of the fabricated prototype with porcine fat samples closely follow the simulated S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> plots and yield relative permittivity of 5.35 and loss tangent of 0.059 at resonance. This set up is also used to extract permittivity of porcine skeletal muscle tissues and experimentally demonstrate its anisotropic nature.

articleTitle: A modified test fixture using parallel strips for measuring attenuation of the dielectric rod
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A modified test fixture using parallel strips line for measuring the attenuation of the dielectric rod is introduced. The hyperbolical tapered lines on the top and bottom of the substrate to realize an approximate impedance matching. In the center of the parallel strips, there is an arc tapered line to reduce the mismatching from the sample hole. The dielectric rod is inserted into a sample hole with 1.2mm in diameter and passed through the substrate to test along the rod. The test fixture exhibits a desired insertion loss of less than 3dB and return loss of more than 10dB (about 23dB maximum) over whole frequencies.

articleTitle: Graphene metasurface based tunable double split-ring resonator for far infrared frequency region
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: we propose graphene metasurface based actively tunable far infrared double split-ring resonator structure. Transmittance, reflectance and absorption parameter is investigated for metasurface structure. Metasurface can be controlled by the different value of the chemical potential of the graphene sheet. Proposed structure can be used as a basic building block of several infrared devices.

articleTitle: A Fast Method to Estimate Peak Local SAR under MRI With RF Shimming
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Radio frequency (RF) shimming is widely used in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to improve the imaging quality by optimizing excitations of RF coil. However, the changes of RF excitations can significantly change the specific absorption rate (SAR) distribution, and thereby, the peak local SAR inside human bodies under MRI. It is important to estimate the peak local SAR for patients under MRI with RF shimming techniques in real time. In this study, a fast method is proposed to estimate the maximum local SAR under RF shimming. Numerical simulations were performed to model the SAR under different excitations of RF shimming, then space averaging filters were designed to estimate the local SAR. Results are compared with IEC standard method, as results suggested, this method is capable of estimating both location and value of mass averaged SAR under different excitation modes.

articleTitle: Printed 5G Reconfigurable Wireless Modules Using Additive Manufacturing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The overview of recent advances in additive manufacturing techniques such as different metallization methods is introduced. A fully printed 5G reconfigurable antenna is proposed. The fabrication process using 3D and inkjet printer is characterized. The flexible 3D printed material is used as the base substrate and the inkjet printed silver traces are used as the conductive traces. The operational frequency range of the proposed antenna can be changed by applying pressure on the flexible to change the shape of the structure. Thus, reconfigurability can be achieved. The center of the operational frequency can be adjusted between 26 GHz to 28.9 GHz. The adjusting rate is 11 %.

articleTitle: Scattering at Interluminal Interface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Interest for spacetime structures has recently been revived, following developments in metamaterials and ultrafast optics. Such structures essentially consist of successions of space-time interfaces for which the theory is still incomplete, in particular in the regime where the interface velocity lies between the wave velocities in the two media involved. This paper addresses this "interluminal" regime, providing exact scattering solutions for both approaching and receding interfaces. The solutions are verified to be consistent with the transmission matrix perspective and to be continuous at the limits of the subluminal and superluminal regimes.

articleTitle: Development of X-Band Metamaterial-Inspired Sensors for Dielectric Constant Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A metamaterial-inspired patch antenna sensor design is proposed for sensing applications to detect and classify different dielectric testing materials in the X-band regime using reflection coefficients. A multi-negative-refractive-index band MTM placed over a patch antenna is specifically designed to enhance the differentiation between several testing dielectric substrates with permittivity varying from 2.5 to 3.2.

articleTitle: Reduction of the Number of Phase Shifters in Linear Phased Antenna Arrays by using Evolutionary Multi-Objective Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An evolutionary multi-objective optimization approach for the design of linear phased antenna arrays based on non-uniform subarrays and reduction of phase shifters is presented. The global optimum solution resulted from an exhaustive search and the candidate solution from an approximated Pareto front (APF) obtained by an evolutionary multi-objective algorithm SMPSO are compared. A sequence from the APF reported a SLL value of -15.93 dB outperforming the optimum solution from exhaustive search by 2.57 dB. This result is possible by sampling a search space 484 times bigger than the one explored by the exhaustive approach.

articleTitle: All-Frequency Stable Potential-Based Formulation for Electromagnetic Modeling and Simulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: While the numerical solution of the vector wave equation breaks down at very low frequencies, the use of quasistatic formulations results in an incomplete physical description. It is highly desirable that a single formulation can work directly from zero frequency to microwave frequencies. This can be achieved by formulating electromagnetic problems with the magnetic vector and the electric scalar potentials and by enforcing Gauss's and charge conservation laws explicitly. In this paper, two potential-based formulations are presented and compared, both theoretically and numerically. A simple circuit has been simulated at different frequencies using the two formulations to demonstrate their numerical performances.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Planar Marchand Balun Design for the Pyramidal Sinuous Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This article presents the design of an ultra-wideband planar Marchand balun for the pyramidal sinuous antenna. Ground plane slots, placed beneath the coupled-line sections, increase the coupling factor of the coupled-line sections and ensure tight coupling. This results in wider bandwidths compared to standard implementations and relaxes the requirements on the trace width and gap spacing. The balanced output lines are placed on the same side of the substrate to facilitate straightforward integration with the antenna. The designed balun showcases a simulated return loss better than 10 dB, and an insertion loss better than 0.84 dB across the band from 2-6 GHz. The simulated amplitude and phase balance are better than 0.8 dB and −12° respectively. Manufactured performance corresponds well with simulated predictions with minor differences being attributed to manufacturing tolerances.

articleTitle: SNO and mBBO Optimization Methods for beam scanning Reflectarray Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In these years high gain antennas have become very interesting from an application point of view, in particular the possibility to use a Reflectarray Antenna as a new technology of reflector has been studied by researchers. One of the most alluring features of RA is that modifying the phase of its re-radiating element is possible to obtain the desired pattern in the desired direction. In this work the possibility to obtain a scanning beam RA has been studied applying two evolutionary algorithms: the SNO and the mBBO.

articleTitle: A Compact Broadband Phase-Inverter-Based TwoSection Forward Coupler for Sub-6-GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact broadband phase-inverter-based two-section forward coupler is realized in double-sided parallel stripline technology for work on the sub-6-GHz band. Compactness is mostly achieved by exploiting the parasitic inductance of the phase inverters while the coupler's forwardness results from two backward coupler topologies compensating each other. An excellent matching of the phase inverters is ensured by interdigital capacitors. The proposed coupler is 45% the size of a conventional two-section branchline coupler on the same technology, but the performances are similar. The simulated fractional bandwidth of 42.4% is limited by the 1 dB amplitude imbalance and guarantees at least 20 dB return loss and isolation as well as phase imbalance smaller than 5°.

articleTitle: On Broadband Active Cloaking
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Although great progress has been made in the theory and realization of invisibility devices, the issue of narrow-bandwidth operation remains unsolved. In particular, physical bounds have been recently derived, based on Bode-Fano theory, that quantify the inherent difficulty in broadening the bandwidth of any linear, causal, and passive cloak. If we remove the passivity restriction, introducing active media into the system, it is then relevant to ask the following questions: 1. Can we overcome the Bode-Fano limit, at least theoretically, and to what extent? 2. Can we guarantee the unconditional stability of the active cloak? In this paper, we discuss some steps toward answering these general questions. We first offer an intuitive discussion of why a passive cloak cannot be broadband, while an active cloak might. Then, we use a 1-D example to show, for the first time, that active cloaks have indeed the potential to operate beyond the Bode-Fano bandwidth limit. Finally, we design a simple 3-D active cloak that exhibits a much broader bandwidth than any traditional passive plasmonic cloak. All our design examples of active cloaks are stable, and we discuss some useful conditions to ensure unconditional stability.

articleTitle: Antenna Phase Center Analysis for the LOFAR Radio Telescope
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Knowledge of the phase centers of the constituting antennas is important to obtain an accurate array response. This contribution shows an analysis of the antenna phase centers for a station of the Low Frequency Array (LOFAR) radio telescope. Based on simulated patterns, the positions of the phase centers for 46 antennas have been computed at 32 MHz showing considerable deviations from their physical positions due to mutual coupling. The flatness of the phase patterns significantly improves when the phase center is considered.

articleTitle: Analysis of a 200-GHz OAM Radio Link Using a Generalized Friis Transmission Equation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Transmission characteristics of a 200-GHz OAM radio link is investigated using a generalized Friis transmission equation. The OAM radio link is composed of high gain Cassegrain helicoidal parabolic reflector antennas using split surfaces for both Tx and Rx. The limitations and antenna requirements of an OAM radio link are discussed in terms of a decomposed near-and-far-field convolution integral (NFCI).

articleTitle: Mimicking Antenna Near-Field Measurements using Full Wave Solvers For Error Characterization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The advent of modern CAD simulation suites enable full-wave solutions of many complex antenna designs. Apart from aiding the design of advanced antennas, it can also enable engineers to characterize errors that occur during antenna measurements, which is the focus of this work. A planar-near field measurement process is mimicked in FEKO by modeling an antenna under test (AUT) and a probe, and recording the S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> between them at various points on the scan plane. Data corresponding to both the copolarized and cross polarized directions of the probe are recorded and Fourier transformed to get the far-fields. As a representative example of using full wave solvers to characterize near-field measurement errors, we assess the impact of probe radiation pattern on the measured far-fields of the AUT, which is a critical aspect for measurements.

articleTitle: Optimization of A Wideband Planar Sparse Array Based on Danzer Aperiodic Tiling
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents our study on the effect of perturbing variables and array size in optimizing a planar sparse array based on Danzer aperiodic tiling. A side lobe level below -12 dB has been achieved within a wide bandwidth from f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> to 10 f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> in a circular disk with radius of 5λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, while below -14.2 dB in a circular disk with radius of 10λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. It is also demonstrated that covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) has outperformed other evolutionary algorithms, i.e. genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimization (PSO).

articleTitle: Phoenix cells reduced database construction for efficient reflectarray synthesis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Reflectarray antennas are becoming a popular technology, in particular for what concerns space applications. In this paper a technique for the synthesis of low profile reflectarray for space application is proposed and demonstrated in the context of an S-band design. It consists of the construction of a reduced bijective database, obtained by selecting a very limited set of Phoenix cells with minimal frequency dispersion. The geometrical continuity requirement between cells presenting close phase shifts has to be ensured as well. This kind of database is particularly applicable to narrowband applications, which would include reflectors for scientific space missions.

articleTitle: A Microwave Tomography System Using Time-Reversal Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 16-antenna-element microwave tomographic imaging system using a fast switching matrix is presented. This system uses frequency domain sampling and time-reversal image processing to image its environment. The use of time-reversal provides a more efficient computational method than traditional inverse techniques, creating a faster processing time. This introduces a potential for near-real-time image processing. To reduce the need for precise time-domain equipment, the short pulses required for time-reversal simulations are synthesized using frequency domain sampling over a broad bandwidth. A 1-5 GHz system using 16 planar antennas controlled by a switch matrix is presented. Measured results and reconstructed images are presented for both a PEC and dielectric cylinder as well as a wood sample and compared to their optical images.

articleTitle: Potential-Based TDIEs for Dielectric Regions Using Magnetic Currents
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new potential-based TDIE formulation for dielectric regions is proposed that directly uses magnetic current densities as unknowns. This new formulation avoids the use of inconvenient integral operators that complicate the discretization, while also providing simpler computation of far-field results due to direct access to the magnetic current density. Appropriate marching-on-in-time discretization schemes are discussed so that stable results can be achieved at middle frequencies. Overall, this results in the improved performance of these new equations compared to previous formulations. The accuracy and stability of this new formulation is demonstrated through numerical results.

articleTitle: The SKA Aperture Array Verification System: Measured Digitally-Beam-Formed Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Aperture Array Verification System stimulated extensive test activities towards the development of the low-frequency instrument (50-350 MHz) of the Square Kilometer Array. This paper discusses radiation patterns measurements carried out on a 16-element array prototype with full digital beam-forming. A micro Unmanned Aerial Vehicle was adopted as the automatic positioner for the test source.

articleTitle: Broadband Dual Linear Polarized (DLP) Antenna Array for Energy Harvesting System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband linear polarized antenna is designed for radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting. The antenna covers the frequency range from 1.35 GHz up to 6 GHz with relative impedance bandwidth of 126% at -6 dB reflection coefficient |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| and extended from 1.1 GHz to 3.3 GHz. A 2×2 dual linear polarized (DLP) antenna array is designed based on the antenna element by using equal phase and Wilkinson equal power divider. The dual linear polarized antenna array covers the frequency band from 1.8 to 2.9 GHz. This frequency band covers a wide range of modern wireless communication standards, including GSM 1800, UMTS 2100, Wi-Fi 2.4, and most of LTE bands. The developed array prototype was then used to experimentally validate the simulation results. The horizontally polarized and vertically polarized gain of the designed array were found to be quite similar across the 1.8 to 2.9 frequency band with an average gain value of 5.5 dBi.

articleTitle: On Changing the Impedance of a Reactive Surface Using Magneto-static Responsive Particles
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Leaky wave antennas can be designed in many ways. One design parameter is the surface impedance which can be controlled by varying the transmission line in order to leak energy and radiate by creating varying gaps in the line. Controlling the surface impedance can also be achieved by changes in the dielectric substrate of the antenna. The work presented in this paper demonstrates a new way to change the surface impedance by embedding conductive micron-sized particles in the substrate. More specifically, the conductive micron-sized particles can be moved using external magneto-static fields, thus changing the overall effective permittivity of the substrate. Simulation results at 10 GHz show that a change in surface impedance can be achieved by manipulating the microparticles in the substrate, rather than changing the gaps in the transmission line. Finally, the simulation results are validated with a comparison to published literature.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave SIW Cavity-Backed Dual-Band Self-Complementary Log-Periodic Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this is paper, a millimeter-wave dual-band self-complementary log-periodic SIW Cavity Backed Antenna for 5G applications is proposed. The antenna is designed on a substrate integrated waveguide cavity with a 2-arms log-periodic toothed bow tie shaped slot. This antenna is designed to operate for the next generation fifth generation wireless communication systems. The proposed antenna is printed on a cavity backed planar substrate integrated waveguide technology. The proposed antenna shows a good performance in terms of return loss and efficiency.

articleTitle: 4x4 Circularly Polarized Antenna Array for Ambient RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a planar circularly polarized (CP) 4x4 antenna array for RF energy harvesting applications. The single element is a coplanar waveguide (CPW) slot antenna. A sequentially rotated feed network is introduced for generating CP 2×2 array and achieved a phase excitation of 0°, 89.39°, 178.6°, and 271°. This 2×2 planar antenna array is repeated three times to produce CP 4×4 antenna array that equally feeds the four groups of 2×2 arrays. A microstrip to CPW transition by via holes is used for connecting the Wilkinson microstrip lines to CPW antenna elements. Four lobes at +45°, +135°, -45°, and -135°, respectively can be noticed and other interlaced beams with lower magnitudes are evolved. The array ARBW (for AR <; 3 dB) is extended from 1.3 GHz to 2.83 GHz (with bandwidth of 1.53 GHz).

articleTitle: Transmitarray based Metasurface Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A transmitarray metasurface design is proposed to function as an integrated lens antenna within the frequency range of 11.6 GHz to 13.25 GHz. A finite periodic array of three-layer metallo-dielectric discrete unit cells is used to form the transmitarray lens. The transmitarray is used in front of an open-ended waveguide to obtain more directive radiation. The transmitarray lens is shown to provide at least 3.75 dB higher gain than a comparable standard horn antenna whilst occupying about half of the physical space.

articleTitle: Metal-only modulated metasurface antenna for Cubesat platforms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a 19 cm diameter metal-only modulated metasurface (MTS) antenna with right-handed circular polarization (RHCP) at Ka-band, more precisely, in the down-link DSN frequency band. The proposed antenna topology may provide high-gains and can be easily integrated on a CubeSat's chassis. The modulated MTS consists of several thousands of sub-wavelength metallic cylinders, with elliptical cross-sections and different heights and orientations across the aperture. This type of antenna can be easily fabricated by metal additive manufacturing and avoids the problems sometimes encountered by dielectrics in space.

articleTitle: Design Considerations in a Graded Index Flat Dielectric Lens for an Impulse Radiating Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a flat dielectric graded refractive index lens is presented as an interesting and easy-to-build alternative to implementing an Impulse Radiating Antenna (IRA), in order to replace the conventional parabolic metal dish. The equal-time approach is applied in the lens' design stage to obtain the desired plane wavefront, required in IRA applications. Time-domain, full-wave simulation results of the complete antenna system are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Compact Comparator for Dual-Polarized Monopulse Array Based on Novel Eight-Port Coupler
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact planar comparator is proposed for a dually-polarized monopulse beamforming. A novel eight-port coupler is employed as the central part to produce the sum- and difference- beams for two orthogonal polarizations, independently and simultaneously. The proposed comparator has a double-layer microstrip configuration smaller than the area of 0.75λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub> × 0.2λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>, and without using T-junctions, vias, closed loops, or steps on each layer. An example of a dual linearly-polarized monopulse array composed of two elements working at 5.8 GHz is built and simulated to verify and demonstrate the performance of the compact comparator. Satisfying properties of sum- and difference-beams for two orthogonal polarizations can be observed, and good matching, isolation, and power division can be achieved in a 10% fractional bandwidth.

articleTitle: A 24 GHz ISM Band Doppler Radar System for Moving Target Sensing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 24 GHz ISM band Doppler radar system for moving target sensing is presented. The system is comprised of a Doppler radar antenna, transceiver module and display software. High isolation characteristic of the proposed antenna is achieved by inserting a decoupling structure. The simulated -10 dB bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 510 MHz and the simulated isolation between Tx and Rx ports is higher than 36.7 dB over the 24 GHz ISM band. Movement information of an object can be detected by using base-band signals from phase- modulated received wave with proper filtering and decision processing. The proposed system can be a good candidate for contact-free heart rate and respiration rate monitoring in health care applications.

articleTitle: A Novel 3D and Inkjet Printed Pressure-sensing Button-shaped Resonator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel 3D and inkjet printed pressure-sensing button-shaped resonator is proposed. The button is fabricated using fast, cost-effective, flexible and environment friendly stereolithography (SLA) 3D printing and inkjet printing techniques. The resonant frequency of the button can be tuned from 2.7 GHz, for idle status, to 1.6 GHz, for a hard press. This design can be used for applications such as gesture detection for Internet of Things (IoT) devices and wireless pressure monitoring for buildings and constructions.

articleTitle: Design methodology of a passive reflectarray for main beam collimation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a design methodology of a planar passive reflectarray, which is able to focus indoor arbitrary energy within a particular direction range. A typical circular patch is considered as the unit cell of the structure, while phase tuning (intrinsic and structural excitation phase shifts) between cells is realized with delay lines, in order to collimate the main beam. Theoretical results compare well with full-wave simulations for a specified main beam collimation objective. The proposed formulation can be implemented within an optimization algorithm for `quick' design purposes.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Slot Antennas By Using Combined Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes two methods to design wideband slot antennas. With the analysis of the combined characteristic modes, it is found that by loading two slot stubs or introducing a parasitic ring slot, a new mode can be generated, and hence, the bandwidth of the ring slot antenna can be enhanced owing to dual mode radiation.

articleTitle: Triangular and Rectangular SIW Microstrip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper reports the cavity model analysis of the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) microstrip antennas based on rectangular and triangular geometries. From these canonical geometries, a diversity of antennas combining magnetic and electric walls are proposed. The electric field distribution inside the antennas and the resonant frequencies are summarized for ten different radiators. In order to validate the proposed geometries, simulations were carried out in the HFSS software and two prototypes were manufactured, presenting good agreement with theoretical prediction.

articleTitle: On the Phase-Error Tolerance of Virtual Antenna Arrays in MIMO Radars
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present that the MIMO radar arrays, in addition to better resolution, can also have improved phase error tolerance as compared to phased-array radars for a certain maximum required side-lobe level. We perform statistical simulations and the results highlight the phase error tolerance of MIMO virtual arrays for both uniform and non-uniform configuration.

articleTitle: On Propagation Losses due to In-Vivo Electromagnetic Nanoscale Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In-vivo nano-biosensing has been attracting a lot of interest within the academic research community recently since it plays a major role in the development of personalized nano-medicine technologies and solutions. The implementation of new nano-biosensing systems inside the human body faces the major challenge of modeling the in-vivo communication channel. Several efforts have been reported recently to investigate the main factors that define the characteristics of the in-vivo communication channel. This paper outlines and discusses the factors that contribute to the path loss encountered by an EM wave in-vivo. These include spreading loss of the propagating wave, the loss due to molecular absorption by biological tissue, and the scattering from the body particles.

articleTitle: Channel Characterization for mmWave V2I Communication in Urban Scenario
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS), vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communication is one of the most important modes. Both ultra-reliable low latency and high-data rate communication are required in the V2I network. In this paper, extensive ray-tracing (RT) simulations are conducted to characterize the channel for mmWave V2I communication in typical urban scenarios in 22-23.6 GHz. Based on the RT results, the path loss, root-mean-square (RMS) delay spread, and the Rician K-factor of the channel are characterized, which guide the design and deployment of V2I communication systems.

articleTitle: Design of a Reconfigurable Metal-Plasma L-Band Transmit-Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a feasibility study of a simple and realistic reconfigurable metal-plasma transmit-array antenna that operates at 1.55 GHz. The antenna consists of a ground plane, an active dipole and a set of realistic plasma tubes placed in front of it. It is shown that the radiation pattern of the array can be reconfigured by switching on/off the plasma tubes. Moreover, a particle swarm optimization algorithm is adopted to find the best geometrical parameters of the antenna in order to enhance the directivity in the broadside direction when the plasma tubes are energized.

articleTitle: Electroless Silver Plating of Additive Manufactured Trough Waveguide Mode Transducer and Antenna Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Three-dimensional printing and metal plating of trough waveguide structure operating in the ISM band ranging from 57-64 GHz is discussed. Addition of commercially available filter in the currently available circulatory electroless silver plating system is discussed and the improvement in insertion coefficient measurement is highlighted. Potential application of short length trough waveguide as TRU calibration standard for measuring longer length trough waveguide section is also discussed.

Author Keywords: Electroless plating and trough waveguide section

articleTitle: A Switchable Reflection-Type Linear/Circular Polarizers Based on Active Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a switchable reflection-type linear/circular polarizer has been proposed which can covert the linear incident wave to the cross-polarization or circular polarization. As a linear polarizer, More than 90% cross-polarization conversion efficiency is observed over the frequency range of 10.6-20.6 GHz. As a circular polarizer, the two orthogonal linear polarizations are equal in magnitude and, at same time, the phase shift is 90°. The bandwidth of the axial ratio less 3 dB is from 10 to 21.4 GHz.

articleTitle: High Gain Wideband Air Strip-Line Fed Antenna For High Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a high power and wideband antenna in L band microwave frequencies. In the antenna configuration, an air suspended stripline (SSL) is used as dielectric medium to have maximum power handling capability. The proposed antenna is inspired from a fork like monopole shape The antenna structure is made from aluminum sheets to have the advantage of low cost. The antenna structure and the excitation transition from coaxial cable to SSL were designed. The antenna functionality was validated using 3D simulation. The results indicate that the antenna is a wideband antenna with good matching properties, omnidirectional pattern, and high radiation efficiency over the frequency band (1.4 GHz to 5 GHz).

articleTitle: A Well-Conditioned Differential Surface Admittance Formulation for Modeling Penetrable Media
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A single-source surface integral equation formulation for modeling penetrable media is proposed. The differential surface admittance operator is enhanced with Buffa-Christiansen basis functions to obtain a well-conditioned system of equations, which can be solved iteratively with fast convergence. Superior convergence of the proposed formulation is demonstrated for a large on-chip interconnect network.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Coupling from Radiating Slots in a Double-Layered Radial Line Slot Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper investigates power coupling out of radiating slots in a double-layered circularly polarised radial line slot array (RLSA) antenna. The antenna is composed of three plates which form a folded radial waveguide and supports inward-travelling waves. Top plate of the antenna has radiating slots. The slots are designed to intercept the currents on the radial waveguide and produce a circularly polarised broadside beam. The slot length is varied using coupling factor in order to achieve a uniform aperture distribution. The simulation results show that the antenna has fairly uniform phase distribution in its near field. The far-field result indicates a peak directivity of 26.4 dBic at 20 GHz with a good pattern quality and a side lobe level of -21.8 dB.

articleTitle: A SIW Uniform Circular Antenna Array for 5G Applications Fed By a Radially-symmetric Eight-way SIW Power Divider
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An eight-element uniform circular antenna array based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology is presented for 5G applications. Cylindrical SIW cavity-backed slot antennas are utilized as array antenna elements. An axially symmetric eight-way SIW power divider is also presented to feed the eight antennas in a circular configuration. The experimental results show an axially symmetric radiation pattern with a peak realized gain of 6.61 dBi, and radiation efficiency of ~ 75%.

articleTitle: A Compact Metasurface Based Cross Polarization Converter for X Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This article reports on a compact, single layer polarizer having angular independent metasurface. The proposed design can efficiently convert cross polarization to co-polarization and vice versa for X - band applications. The unit cell consists of a stretched 8 shaped element printed diagonally on an FR4 substrate having 1.6 mm thickness backed by ground plane. The proposed design converts a linearly polarized incident wave into its orthogonal counterpart after getting reflected from the metasurface polarizer provided that the incident wave is polarized in x or y axis. Two distinct polarization conversion peaks are obtained at 9.9 GHz and 11.2 GHz with overall bandwidth more than 2 GHz. The design also exhibits stable frequency response at oblique angles of incidence up-to 45°. A finite prototype with overall dimensions of 210 × 290 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> containing 21 × 15 unit cells is fabricated and tested. A good agreement between the measured and simulated results showed that the proposed design can be employed for linear polarization conversion applications in X band.

articleTitle: Highly Miniaturized Mircrostrip Antenna with Slots and a Superstrate for RFID Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: RFID Tags, typically, require ultra-small antennas and at 900 MHz most of the designs end up being meandered line wire antennas. These may not be suitable because such antennas are heavily influenced by the object on which they are placed. An antenna with a ground plane, such as a microstrip antenna, is a more suitable candidate in that scenario, however, typically micrsotrip patch antennas are large in size. In this paper, we introduce a highly miniaturized microstrip antenna with multiple slots and a superstrate with high-permittivity material. The size of the microstrip antenna at 900MHz is reduced by 87.5% as compared to a conventional rectangular microstrip patch antenna at 900MHz. The gain of the miniaturized antenna is 0.36dBi, achieving 40% efficiency, which is decent enough for short to medium range RFID applications.

articleTitle: Cancer Classification of Freshly Excised Murine Tumors with Ordered Orthogonal Projection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a low dimension feature extraction method for cancer classification with terahertz (THz) images of freshly excised murine tumors. In THz imaging, the properties of various tissue regions, such as cancer, fat, and muscle, are embedded in the shape of reflected THz pulses. We propose to extract such information by projecting the frequency domain THz waveforms onto a series of ordered orthogonal basis. Experiment results demonstrated that the proposed algorithm can achieve reasonably accurate detection results for fresh tissues with three regions.

articleTitle: Dual-Linear or Dual-Circular Polarized Slot Excited ME-Dipole Antenna with Single-Layer Feeding
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A magnetoelectric (ME) dipole antenna with a single-layer microstrip line feeding network is proposed for either dual-linear or dual-circular-polarizations. To achieve better isolation, a hook and fork-shaped feedlines are designed to excite dual linear polarizations, which are combined with a quadratic hybrid to provide dual-circular polarizations. Furthermore, in the proposed feeding configuration, the isolation level is tuned properly according to the requirements. The operational bandwidth of the antenna (impedance bandwidth <; -10 dB, Isolation > 30 dB (linear) and > 20 dB (circular), and Axial Ration <; 3 dB) is 23% at 30 GHz. The average radiation efficiency and maximum gain of the antenna are calculated to be 95% and 9.2 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Influence of 3T MRI coil modeling on EM exposure estimation using a human model
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We evaluated the influence of 3T magnetic resonance imaging whole body birdcage coil modeling on electromagnetic exposure estimation using a human model. Simplification of coil geometry, realistic tuning and capacitor losses had a relevant impact on the estimated electric distributions. Variety of the generated electric field has to be carefully considered for reliable RF safety assessment of a patient with a passive or active implant undergoing magnetic resonance imaging.

articleTitle: Development of a Rear Glass Antenna System for a Hatchback Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a rear glass antenna system for a hatchback vehicle equipped with tailgate. The proposed rear glass antenna system consists of passive glass pattern, LNA module, HSC and GSC, which operate in the AM/FM radio frequency band. The suggested antenna is designed and analyzed by using an EM simulation tool, and its simulated results are well matched with the measured results. Moreover, we verified the function of HSC and GSC through RF noise interference test. Therefore, the proposed antenna and its design procedure can be applied to develop a rear glass antenna system for a hatchback vehicle as well as a sedan.

articleTitle: Quantitative Evaluation on Memory Characteristics of High-Speed Railway Fading Channel
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Evaluating the influence of vehicular speed on the memory characteristics of fading channels in high-speed railway communications is a key issue for transmission scheme and protocol design of vehicular communications. In this paper, we propose a quantitative method based on Markov chain order estimation to evaluate the effect of vehicular speed on the memory characteristics of fading channel. The influence of different methods of channel state partition on estimating the Markov order is also considered. The Bayesian information criterion is adopted to determine the order of the Markov chain.

articleTitle: UWB Antenna Printing on Glass Substrate Through Cost-Effective Copper Foils
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A UWB antenna printing on glass substrate using copper foil is reported which is extremely cost-effective fabrication process as compared to that of inkjet or screen printing. In particular, a 50 Ω CPW fed circular UWB antenna on a glass substrate with ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 4.3 and 2 mm thickness having a size of 43 × 49 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is first designed in a simulator and then realized for the validation of the proposed cost-effective fabrication procedure. The fabrication procedure involves the lamination of adhesive copper foils on a glass substrate followed by the chemical etching for drawing conductive patterns instead of using expensive copper or silver nano-particle inks that employ costly screen or inkjet printing. The comparison of the simulated and measured results showed that proposed process can be used to produce other types of antennas on various kind of substrates such as glass, paper, plastic, etc.

articleTitle: Frequency Independent Method for RCS Reduction of Dihedral Corners Using Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Using orthogonality principles and array theory, a frequency independent method for reducing the Radar Cross Section (RCS) in the entire concave region of dihedral corners is developed and validated. The proposed technique can further be applied for broadband RCS reduction of complex corners and open-ended cavities where fields undergo multiple bounces.

articleTitle: A Patch Antenna with Liquid Crystal Elastomer Switching for Passive RFID Temperature Sensing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The antenna design presented here supports a new generation of battery-free RFID sensing technology in which the antenna element dynamically conforms to the changing environment in a controlled manner. Specifically, we propose a sensing antenna that reversibly and repeatedly switches operating frequencies from 905MHz to 923.5 MHz based on a temperature threshold crossing. The developed antenna is a patch antenna matched to an RFID IC and integrated with a customized slot. The antenna shifts its operating frequency by using a novel thermal responsive polymer or Liquid Crystal Elastomer (LCE) which is programmable and operates reversibly. Furthermore, 4D printed LCE structures are to be coupled with an Ultra Subminiature Mechanical Switch (USMS) which shorts the slot when the LCE is activated. Finally, as the thermal excitation is removed, the switch returns to the open state. The short and open states of the switch will enable the frequency shift of the antenna structure. In this paper, the methodology of the frequency shift in the patch antenna and the novel LCE switch mechanism are described through simulation and measurements.

articleTitle: Numerical Investigation on Graphene Based Mantle Cloaking of a PEC Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A specific coating for the achievement of the mantle cloaking of a metallic cylinder in the Terahertz frequencies is investigated. The coat is realized starting from a dielectric layer covering the cylinder, over which a certain number of modulated strips of graphene are laid. Properly set the values of the available parameters (chemical potential of graphene μ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, dielectric constant, dielectric thickness h, number of modulated strips n and variation of width of each strip w(z)), a combination of the values that allows to reach the cloaking of the object is obtained. In order to quantify the cloaking at the desired frequency f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, the Maximum Radar Cross Section is computed and compared to the various structures.

articleTitle: An Ultra-thin Wideband 3-D Frequency Selective Rasorber based on Ferrite Absorber and Slow Wave Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-thin wideband 3-D frequency selective rasorber (FSR) based on ferrite absorber and slow-wave structure. The thickness is reduced by using a slow wave structure, which also produces a pass-band within the absorption band provided by ferrite absorber. With the help of a series LC circuit in front of the ferrite absorber, the losses from the ferrite absorber can be by-passed in the pass-band, resulting transmission window with very low insertion loss. The thickness of this FSR is less than λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">C</sub>/11 at the center resonant frequency. This present structure is suitable for applications below 1 GHz, thought it may be scaled to other frequency bands.

articleTitle: A Higher-order Explicit Marching-on-in-time for Analysis of Transient Acoustic Scattering from Rigid Objects
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
