abstract: An explicit marching-on-in-time (MOT) scheme for solving the time domain Kirchhoff (surface) integral equation (TDKIE) to analyze acoustic scattering from a rigid scatterer is presented. The unknown velocity potential induced on the scatterer surface is approximated using nodal interpolation functions in space and shifted Lagrange polynomials in time. Inserting this expansion into the TDKIE and testing the resulting equation at the interpolation points (i.e., Nyström method in space) yield a system of ordinary differential equations (ODEs). This ODE system is integrated in time using a PE(CE)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>-type linear multistep scheme to yield unknown expansion coefficients. Numerical results demonstrate that the explicit MOT scheme uses the same time step as its implicit counterpart without sacrificing from accuracy or stability and is faster under low frequency excitation (i.e., for large time step).

articleTitle: Focused CW Mm-Wave Characterization of Lossy Penetrable Dielectric Slab Affixed to Human Body
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Building on a previously developed virtual-source model for loss-less dielectric slabs attached to metallic planes, we present a fast focused raster scanned spot continuous-wave (CW) method to find the thickness, dielectric permittivity, and loss-tangent of lossy dielectric slabs that could potentially be explosive threats. A library of reflection responses for objects with different sizes and electric properties is precomputed, and an inversion algorithm incorporates the measured data to predict the object features. It is shown that this characterization is possible even using only a single working frequency. The method is validated empirically by comparing to the synthetic reflection of the millimeter-wave imaging radar.

articleTitle: Investigation of Channel Correlation in Indoor Wideband Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This study investigates the channel correlation and the power delay profile (PDP) of the propagation channels in wideband massive MIMO networks through measurements on prototypes under certain circumstance. To this purpose, an antenna array for the base station (BS) and the single directional antenna for the user equipments (UE) are designed and fabricated. In the setting up for the measurement, the UEs are located at different locations in an office in order to produce various realistic channel propagation scenarios. The results show that the channel correlation is heavily related to the locations of the UEs and the propagation environment, for example, closely located UEs in line-of-sight (LOS) have strong channel correlations. On the other hand, when the UEs are far away or being in a non-line-of-sight (NLOS) situation, a low-level channel correlations are observed even with closely placed antenna elements at the BS array.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of Anisotropic Dielectric Objects Based on Integral Equation Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Anisotropic dielectric objects are reconstructed by an integral equation method. Since the objects are anisotropic and imaging domain is inhomogeneous, volume integral equations (VIEs) must be employed to describe the problem. Traditionally, the VIEs are solved by the method of moments (MoM) with the Schaubert-Wilton-Glisson (SWG) basis function in the forward scattering VIEs (FSVIEs). We use a Nyström method to solve the FSVIEs and it may be more suitable than the MoM due to the anisotropy. For the inverse scattering VIEs (ISVIEs), we use a Gauss-Newton method (GNM) to solve it. A numerical example is presented to illustrate the approach and its good performance has been validated.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Time-modulated Array in Digital Communication System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a simple time-modulated array (TMA) whose elements are excited sequentially is studied in multiuser and physical layer secure wireless communication system. On a theoretical level, some significant details are discussed. For multiuser wireless communication, in order to avoid aliasing of the spectrum, the time modulation frequency must be greater than the bandwidth of baseband signal. However, take advantage of the aliasing of the spectrum, TMA can be used in secure wireless communication. Some numerical results are given to verify the feasibility of TMA from time domain.

articleTitle: Design of an Interstitial Microwave Applicator for 3D Printing Antennas in the Body
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: 3D printing in the body is an emerging technology with a host of biomedical applications, including wireless telemetry. An EM heating applicator can be used to "print" structures in the body using a biocompatible polymer material. This paper evaluates an applicator that could be used to produce focused heating for this purpose. This applicator is a sleeved-slot antenna operating at 2450 MHz. Simulations in brain tissue showed the applicator was capable of heating 3.3°C in 3 s.

articleTitle: Effects of MWT Radiation on Sidelobe Levels in mm-Wave Microstrip Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The effects of unwanted radiation from microstrip-to-waveguide transition (MWT) on a millimeter-wave microstrip array antenna was investigated. Spurious radiation was observed when an MWT was used to feed the array antenna. The unwanted MWT radiation was shown to be coupled to the array antenna elements causing the spurious radiation. The spurious radiation was shown to decrease by blocking the direct radiation from the MWT toward the array antenna.

articleTitle: Dual-Band High-Gain Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna Design Using Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel compact dual band circularly polarized (CP) antenna for WiMAX and WLAN applications is presented in this paper. With a conventional metasurface (MS) placed atop a patch radiator two operating frequency bands are obtained. Further, by modifying the unit cell of the MS layer, both the bands at 3.52 GHz and 5.5 GHz give rise to CP radiations. Axial ratio bandwidths (ARBWs) are 2% and 3.63% at the lower and upper frequency bands respectively. The designed structure is low profile and has a gain better than 6 dBi at both the resonant frequencies.

articleTitle: Modified EBG Design Circuit Model for Isolation Improvement Between Monopole Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A combined antenna plus EBG circuit model is proposed to predict the isolation versus frequency response of monopole antennas with a single column Mushroom EBG (M- EBG) in between them. The existing circuit model for M-EBG structures is modified to include a new capacitance called plate capacitance. The new circuit model can predict the EBG stopband frequency more accurately than the existing model. The new circuit model is then combined with an existing monopole antenna circuit model to obtain the isolation versus frequency response.

articleTitle: A Retro-reflective Scheme for Wireless Power transmission in Fully Enclosed Environments
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a retro-reflective scheme of wireless power transmission in fully enclosed environments. In this scheme, the power transfer system consists of a single transmitter and a reconfigurable reflecting array with each element loaded with a switchable reactive element. The power receiver first broadcasts a pilot signal and the power transmitter records the power level of the received pilot signal while reconfiguring the reactive loads through all possible combinations. The optimal load combination is determined to be the one with the maximum transmission efficiency. Then the power is transmitted with the reflecting array configured with the optimal load combination. Simulation and measurement results are provided showing that the proposed scheme improves the power transmission efficiency significantly.

articleTitle: Broadband WAIM Metasurface Structure for Electronically Beam Scanning Holographic Antenna for Ku-Band Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel, low-profile, broadband, wide-angle impedance matching (WAIM) metasurace structure for significant gain improvement of liquid crystal (LC)-based, holographic beam scanning, radial aperture antennas. The WAIM provides up to 5 dB and 3 dB gain improvement over Rx and Tx satellite Ku-band frequencies, respectively, at all scan angles (0 to 60 deg), and for both horizontal and vertical polarizations.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Edge-Fed Octagonal Four-Arm Archimedean Spiral Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an octagonal dual polarized four-arm Archimedean spiral antenna integrated with edge-fed impedance transformers covering mm-Wave frequencies. Compared to a conventional center-fed antenna with coaxial feed, this compact planar proof-of-concept design mimics an on-chip implementation and demonstrates edge-feeding and a geometry that is amenable to multi-feed on-antenna power combining, while maintaining desired spiral antenna characteristics such as broad bandwidth and dual polarization. The simulated results of the proposed antenna show return loss > 10dB, isolation > 60dB, and half power beamwidth (HPBW) > 45°, covering nearly 7:1 bandwidth ratio from 11-75GHz.

articleTitle: Truncating Matrx-free Time-Domain Method with PML for Solving 3-D Open Region Problems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we develop a formulation to truncate the matrix-free time-domain (MFTD) method in unstructured meshes with PML. Utilizing the strength of the MFTD method in handling arbitrarily shaped elements, we employ an orthogonal-grid based discretization in the PML, while keeping the unstructured meshes in the solution domain. The proposed formulation in PML is conformal to the original MFTD method in unstructured meshes, and hence can be readily employed to truncate MFTD for simulating open-region problems. Numerical results have validated the proposed method.

articleTitle: On the Placement of Particle Containing Cylindrical Cavities in a Grounded Dielectric Substrate to Change the Impedance of a Printed Reactive Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Real time control of the surface impedance of a printed conducting layer is of interest for the design of frequency selective surfaces and leaky wave antennas. Currently, the surface impedance is defined by changing the layout of printed conductors on a grounded dielectric substrate with fixed dielectric properties. However, the surface impedance can also be tailored by fixing the conductor layout and changing the dielectric substrate properties. In this paper, we present such a method where cylindrical air cavities containing micron-sized conducting particles embedded in a grounded substrate are used to change its dielectric properties. Results are presented to demonstrate the effect of cavity placement on the impedance of a fixed printed reactive surface at 10 GHz. The results are shown to compare well with published literature for validation.

articleTitle: High Gain Dual Polarized Omni Antenna for four channel MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Here we present a four channel omni-directional antenna that covers the 4.9-6.4GHz frequency band. It employs a combination of dipole and patch coupled slot antennas. It uses a parallel feed network to avoid beam squint. We optimized the patterns for 4x2 MIMO. The antennas are widely deployed in fixed wireless and outdoor Wi-Fi applications.

articleTitle: Transparent Microstrip Antennas for CubeSats
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Transparent microstrip antennas are explored for use on CubeSats. A review of methods for making transparent antennas is given, including the use of transparent metal, the use of meshed surfaces, and the creation of holey structures that have a periodic array of holes drilled through the structure.

articleTitle: Relation between Complex Propagation Constant and Complex Eigenmodes in Lossy Traveling-Wave Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A simple procedure to extract the attenuation constant of a lossy traveling-wave structure using eigenmode simulations is presented. For lossy structures, the eigenmode analysis outputs complex eigenvalues which mathematically results in complex frequencies, Ω. Using the proposed relations, these complex frequencies are mapped to the complex propagation constant γ and the corresponding attenuation constant α through the group velocity of the mode. Taking a standard rectangular waveguide as an example, complex eigenmodes are extracted through full-wave simulations, which are then used to correctly predict the the per-unit length attenuation constant under low- loss conditions.

articleTitle: On the Bandwidth of Loop Antennas using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Characteristic Mode Analysis of various loop antennas will be performed in order to show how the bandwidth of these antennas can be enlarged. A thin loop, a loop with some height and a loop with larger width and no height will be analyzed in terms of characteristic modes, showing interesting results.

articleTitle: Polarization-Diversity Conformal VHF Antenna with Near-Perfect Radiation Efficiency for Small UAVs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The integration of wide-band high efficiency antennas into conducting airframes especially at low frequencies is very difficult for two reasons: (1) Such antenna need to be large and cannot be protruding out of the airframe, (2) because most airframes are electrically conductive (aluminum or carbon fiber), conformal antenna printed on such surfaces have narrow bandwidth and low efficiency. A method is presented for realizing dipoles and monopoles with near-perfect efficiencies formed using airframe sections resulting in no additional RCS and requiring minimal wiring. Multiple realizations with varying polarizations are possible for small-size UAVs with conducting airframes.

articleTitle: Bistatic RCS of a One-Dimensional Metasurface Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper examines the bistatic radar cross section (RCS) of a sinusoidally-modulated metasurface leaky-wave antenna (LWA) under normal incidence. The RCS performance is characterized by modeling the antenna as a linear array, with each sinusoidal period as a sub-element of the array. The analytically determined bistatic RCS patterns are compared to simulations, and the model is shown to predict accurately the directions of maxima.

articleTitle: A Novel Bio-Inspired Quasi-Yagi Helical Antenna with Beam Direction and Beamwidth Switching Capability using Origami DNA
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a bio-inspired origami quasi-Yagi helical antenna having beam direction and beamwidth switching capability is presented. The structure of the antenna is based on the transformable origami DNA which is inspired from DNA of living cell. The length of a living cell DNA is few microns in the folded state and can be transformed to 2 m by unfolding. In this study, three origami DNA geometries named as DNA #1, DNA #2 and DNA #3, are applied to design quasi-Yagi helical antenna. DNA #2 serves as a driven element and DNA #1 and DNA #3 serve as parasitic elements. The beam direction and beamwidth of the antenna can be controlled by folding and unfolding the parasitic elements. The presented antenna provides four beam steering states having first three states with narrow beamwidth and fourth state with wide beamwidth at the fixed resonant frequency of 1.9 GHz. For example, the beam direction of the antenna for the states 1, 2, 3, and 4 can be steered to -30°, 0°, +30°, and -40° respectively. The presented antenna provides wider 3 dB beamwidth of 104° in the fourth state, while beamwidth of the first three states are narrower than 64°.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Metallic Bull’s–Eye Antenna with Wideband Broadside Radiation Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a low-profile metallic Bull's-Eye antenna with high broadside gain and a wide bandwidth. The antenna was designed for a center frequency of 37.5 GHz and showcases 6 periodic corrugations plus a soft electromagnetic surface at its outer edge with 5 corrugations. Simulation results reveal a broadside gain greater than 15 dBi over a 6.5 GHz bandwidth (17.3%). The antenna has a peak gain of 18.9 dBi at 36.1 GHz with a return loss below -15 dB throughout its operational bandwidth. An input-matching bandwidth greater than 10 GHz (26.7%) was achieved using a tapered waveguide feeding structure. The soft electromagnetic surface is used to achieve a sidelobe level of -12 dB at 36.1 GHz and better than -9.5 dB throughout the bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Wide Band Meta- Surface Enhancement of Mutual Coupling in SatCom / 5G Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a wideband mutual coupling reduction between two aperture coupled microstrip (ACMS) antennas, is introduced. The antennas are functioning from 17 - 31 GHz which is in the region of the Ka-band for the satellite communication (SatCom) applications. The mutual coupling has been reduced by using a periodic meta-surface structure (J-cross) unit to achieve wideband isolation in the Ka (uplink) band of 17-31 GHz. Reduction of the mutual coupling has been proven efficient on employing it in array or MIMO antenna applications.

Author Keywords: aperture coupled microstrip antenna (ACMS) antenna array

articleTitle: Approximation of Reflectarray Cross-Polarization Response Using A Hybrid FEM-PO Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a scheme to approximate the cross-polarization response of a reflectarray antenna using a simple, hybrid finite element-physical optics (FEM-PO) method. Surface currents are solved on a unit cell with periodic boundary conditions using FEM for a single case and applied throughout the aperture surface. These currents are used in a PO calculation to obtain the cross-polarization far fields of the antenna.

articleTitle: Compact and High Gain half-sphere Dielectric Antenna Using 3D printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a 77 GHz half-sphere dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) based on a coplanar-waveguide (CPW) fed for millimeter-wave application. The antenna offer low-cost compact and high-efficiency performance in the W-band using ABS material that is compatible with the 3D printing technology. The compact-size and low profile of the half-sphere make it great candidate for short-range wireless communication and high-resolution imaging. The antenna works in the W-band with an achieved gain of 6.89 dB at 77 GHz and with a radiation efficiency of 96.7%.

articleTitle: C-Band Multi-Beam Planar Lens Antenna Based on Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a multi-beam planar lens antenna based on frequency selective surface (FSS)operating at 6GHz. The proposed C-band multi-beam planar lens antenna exhibits the advantages of low profile and ease of manufacture, with good transmission characteristics at 6 GHz. A rectangular waveguide of 40.386mm×20.193mm is used as the feed. The gain of designed C-band multi-beam planar lens antenna reaches 14.4dBi, which shows an increment of 7.9dBi compared with the gain of rectangular waveguide. The simulation results confirm the wide-angle scanning properties of the proposed C-band multi-beam planar lens antenna in the ±30° range with gain scanning loss less than 0.6dBi.

articleTitle: The Bifocal Microwave Microscope
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Millimeter-wave imaging radar is becoming increasingly popular for sensing and security applications. Usually full phased arrays, synthetic apertures, or focusing reflect-arrays are employed to sense a given image space. One new approach is to generate an axially-scanning focal spot using an axial nearfield bifocal dual reflector. The bifocal has two perfect foci on the symmetry axis, each corresponding to the two perfect feed points on the axis, made possible when two degrees of freedom - two reflectors - are employed. With two perfect foci, the optical aberrations for other image points between them must be of even order, which leads to a reasonable focal region bounded by the perfect foci. It is envisioned that a small feed moving along the axis might interrogate the image region, with better precision and speed, and less force than the full focusing stage. Alternatively, an electronically selective line source could scan the image space at nanosecond rates using only one dimension of sensing hardware. The concept is referred to as a microscope, because it maps rays diverging from the image space to rays converging at the observation points much like an optical microscope.

articleTitle: Two Element Series Fed Origami Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Origami inspired antennas have been investigated for their potential as lightweight and efficient multi-purpose reconfigurable antennas for a variety of radio frequency applications. Being able to change antenna frequency, bandwidth and gain simply by folding the antenna structure is certainly attractive, however, challenges must be overcome for real-world applications. Providing sufficient gain is a challenge for small antennas and this issue can be compounded by impedance matching problems resulting from folding the antenna feedlines. Providing sufficient structural strength along with a reliable means to physically fold the antenna can also be a challenge. In this paper a novel origami inspired two-element hexagonal antenna array is investigated for its potential to provide a simple and stable physical structure that demonstrates consistent gain and impedance matching for multiple configurations.

articleTitle: An Unified Equation for Active Reflection Coefficient in 4D Antenna Arrays including Mutual Coupling Effect
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A unified time- and frequency-domain equation in terms of the active reflection coefficient (ARC) in four-dimensional (4D) antenna arrays including mutual coupling effect is presented. The "instantaneous" active reflection coefficient (ARC) as a function of time and the "averaged" active reflection coefficient as a function of frequency are introduced to evaluate the port matching and the mutual coupling in 4D arrays, respectively. The two analysis approaches from different viewpoints are demonstrated to be unified and complementary through Fourier transform. The results of a 16-element 4D linear array with tightly coupled elements are used to validate the unified equation.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Multi-Antenna Structure for Simultaneous Transmission of Wireless Information and Power
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a dual-polarized multi-antenna structure is designed at 2.45 GHz with the goal of allowing simultaneous transmission of wireless information and power. Differential feeding was used to minimize the mutual coupling due to radiation leakage in addition to a mushroom-type EBG structure for suppressing the surface waves. Simulation results for the proposed structure show a mutual coupling level lower than -40 dB between the information transmitting antenna and the power transmitting antennas for both polarizations. The isolation level between the antennas is improved by at least 22 dB and 14 dB for the E-plane and H-plane coupling, respectively.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Simulation of CMOS On-Chip Spiral Inductors in 5 GHz band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) circuits became applicable to radio frequency (RF) bands in the advanced CMOS process technology. On-chip spiral inductors are key component to obtain high performance RF circuits. Electromagnetic simulation of the on-chip spiral inductors is very important for systematic design and improving performance. Electromagnetic simulation of a 2 nH spiral inductor in 5 GHz band is performed. Modeling of the CMOS substrate was key issue for proper simulation. The agreement between measurement and simulation was very good.

articleTitle: Recording Critical Epilepsy Indicators using a Fully-Passive Wireless System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Implantable sensors for recording neural activity are often used for a variety of applications, including epilepsy studies. Current versions of these recorders are highly-invasive impractical implants and undesirable in daily life. To address this, for the first time we present a novel fully- implantable and passive system for recording characteristic epileptic activity. In this paper, we focus on recording interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs), known indicators of clinical significance. IEDs can serve to identify the location of seizure onset zones. Notably, in the case of temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE). Here, we present IED signals recorded using neural probes previously tested with our system and demonstrated to be capable of sensing signals as low as 15 μVpp in amplitude. These recordings refer to actual animal experiments and are indicative of the broad spectrum of neural signals that can be recorded.

articleTitle: Retrieval of Subsurface Properties of Layered Dielectric Structures Using Hybrid Global and Local Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present an inversion scheme to retrieve subsurface properties of layered dielectric structures with random slightly rough interfaces. We use the small perturbation method in the forward model. To solve the inverse-scattering problem, we utilize a novel global optimization technique, which takes advantage of the speed of local optimization while ensuring convergence to a global minimum. More specifically, by modifying the perturbation scheme in the simulated annealing method using a non-linear simplex search algorithm, we enhance the performance of global search by choosing effective perturbation directions. We have demonstrated the strength of the method in solving the inverse-scatting problems by some numerical results.

articleTitle: Point-to-Point Dielectric-Horn Integrated Resonator Antenna with Reduced Side-Lobe Level
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel dielectric resonator antenna (DRA), working at 28 GHz with a peak gain of 12.4 dBi over a fractional bandwidth of 12.6%, is presented. The novel design achieves side-lobe levels below -10 dB for both the E and H-planes so to meet the requirements of the new generation 5G wireless communications systems.

articleTitle: A 3D Printed Fragmented Aperture Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This document describes a method of generating, optimizing, and fabricating a three-dimensional (3D) fragmented aperture antenna. The 3D design was able to achieve right-hand circular polarization with a single unbalanced feed. Measured results are shown to confirm the designed performance.

articleTitle: Multi-Broadband Microstrip Antenna for LTE Smartphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new compact design of multi-broad band microstrip antenna, used in smartphone is presented. It supports 40-LTE bands including LTE 700, LTE2300, LTE2500, LTE42, LTE43 and LTE46 bands. Also, it covers WLAN 2.4GHz, WiMAX 2.5GHz and WiMAX 3.5GHz applications. The proposed antenna composed of four different monopole antennas connected together at the input feed. Three monopole antennas have the same width while the fourth one is wider than others in order to improve the matching of the reflection coefficient. The antenna occupies a compact size of 17 × 60 × 0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> which makes it appropriate for operating in slim smartphone devices. There is a good agreement between the simulated and the measured results.

articleTitle: A Compact Electrically Tunable VHF Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An electrically small dipole antenna that can be tuned from 35 MHz to 90 MHz is reported. The proposed design is low profile and lightweight, and is integrated on the landing gear of a compact UAV. The antenna operates as an inductively loaded, folded dipole to efficiently utilize the available space. The antenna is tuned with both RF switches and varactor diodes. The RF switches short out different sections of the inductive coil enabling discrete frequency tuning. The varactor diodes in parallel with the coil allow for continuous frequency adjustments. Full wave simulation results show that the antenna can be tuned from 35 to 90 MHz. The instantaneous bandwidth and gain at 42 MHz are 1% and -8 dB, respectively. The gain and bandwidth increase when the antenna is tuned to the higher end of the frequency band of interest.

articleTitle: A Stable 3-D FDTD Method with Multiple Embedded Reduced-Order Models
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method has been widely used for its versatility in solving electromagnetic problems. However, the computational efficiency of FDTD can be significantly reduced in subgridding schemes, where a locally refined grid is adopted in the spatial domain. An emerging approach to accelerate FDTD subgridding is model order reduction (MOR), which can be used to compress the update equations of the refined regions. However, reduced-order models can easily introduce instability when embedded into an FDTD grid. In this paper, we propose a systematic strategy to couple multiple reduced models to a 3-D FDTD grid with guaranteed stability under the Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) limit of the fine grid. Furthermore, the CFL limit of the entire scheme can be extended with a perturbation of the reduced model coefficients, which can further improve computational efficiency. A numerical example with two reduced-order models indicates the potential of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A Fast and Accurate Transfer Function Validation Strategy Using Rotational Invariant Lead Trajectories
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper demonstrates a novel strategy to validate the transfer function, which is used to predict the radiofrequency (RF) induced heating near the distal end of active implantable metallic device (AIMD) with long metallic leads under magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanning. The strategy uses a rotatable circular plate on which the AIMD is fixed. The rotational invariant lead trajectories in ASTM phantom are determined by rotating the circular mounting plate. The tangential components of incident electric fields along the different lead trajectories are highly orthogonal. Numerical simulations and measurement results are used to demonstrate the advantages of this method. This strategy is an efficient and accurate validation procedure compared to current validation strategies.

articleTitle: A Dual-band Electromagnetic Energy Harvesting Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a dual-band electromagnetic energy harvesting surface that is designed for absorbing electromagnetic energy in the GSM-1800 and Wi-Fi bands. The unit cell of the periodic structure incorporates two bow-tie dipoles and a resistive load demonstrating excellent absorption characteristics with minimal dielectric losses. We also demonstrate how the proposed surface can increase the rectenna phsyical area and the collected power per rectifier, leading to viable energy harvesting applications in low power density environments.

articleTitle: Compact UWB Slotted Pentagonal Patch Antenna for Radar and Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a microstrip patch antenna that have an ultra-wideband (UWB) characteristics. The proposed antenna design is a slotted non-uniform pentagonal microstrip patch antenna with 1.6mm thickness of FR-4 as the substrate. Its small size of 30mm × 33mm achieved the miniaturization characteristics to fit on the surface of CubeSat. The antenna is simulated to resonate at 6.33GHz and operates at the range of frequency from 2.56GHz to 19.89GHz with bandwidth enhancement of 273.78%, while the fabricated antenna is measured to resonate between 3.10GHz to 12.74GHz and is optimum at 3.9GHz with bandwidth enhancement of 247.18%. This range covers most commonly frequencies for wide usage of radar and communication application such as earth observation, space weather forecasting, mobile communication etc. It manages to attain VSWR≤2 at the optimum frequency and have relatively good gain of 3.67dBi. The antenna is designed and simulated using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Microwave Studio.

articleTitle: On the Surface Roughness and Smoothing in the 3D Printed THz Reflectors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the effect of surface roughness on the performance of the 3D printed near field focused THz Cassegrain antenna configuration. It is found that the roughness affects the focal plane parameters. The nearfield directivity is reduced by ~ 3.5 dB for 60 μm rough surface, there is only a small effect on the focus spot width. A smoothing process, which reduces the conductive coating surface roughness to 4 μm, is also described. The roughness loss is less than 0.1 dB at 300GHz.

articleTitle: Uniplanar Rectenna Designs Matched with either Active or Passive DC-to-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Two rectenna designs consisting of a patch antenna and a voltage doubler operating at 5.6 GHz are presented. Rectenna-1 is matched with a varying input impedance active DC-to-DC booster based on Texas Instruments charge pump IC TPS60300. Depending on the biasing conditions the ohmic impedance varies significantly between 4.2-6.7 KΩ which consists of a design challenge for the rectifier matching. Rectenna-2 is optimized to be terminated with a passive ultra-low-voltage self-powered converter with relatively constant 3.9 KΩ input impedance. The passive converter can only be used if the required rectified power is sufficiently small.

articleTitle: A DGTD-Based Multiscale Simulator for Electromagnetic Multiphysics Problems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Most multiphysics problems are multiscale problems due to the mutual couplings between physics of different natures. To perform an accurate multiphysics simulation, these multiscale couplings and interactions must be accounted for carefully. In this paper, a multiscale simulator for multiphysics problems based on the discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method is described. An adaptive technique that allows a dynamic adjustment of the polynomial orders in the simulation domain is used to provide different spatial resolutions for the multiscale couplings. To achieve a high simulation efficiency, a multirate time integration method is adopted to permit different temporal resolutions in different simulation regions. An electromagnetics-plasma interaction process is presented to demonstrate the effort towards this high-performance multiscale simulator.

articleTitle: A Stepped-Ring Fabry Perot Cavity Antenna for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a Fabry Perot Cavity (FPC) antenna with wide bandwidh and high gain characteristics at millimeter wave (MMW) band. By using a quasi-curve plane which consists of five metallic stepped rings, the antenna operating at 60 GHz achieves 38% impedance bandwidth and 32% 3-dB gain bandwidth. Its peak gain is 21.5 dBi. This antenna technology finds a potential application in millimeter-wave communications such as 5G applications.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Microwave Tomography Algorithm Using the DDA as a Fast Forward Solver
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The forward model directly impacts the computation time of an iterative image reconstruction algorithm for microwave tomography. Therefore, there is a need to decrease the computation time without sacrificing accuracy. To accomplish this, the discrete dipole approximation (DDA) is used to improve time efficiency. Although the DDA is an accurate and efficient forward solver, the optimization of its implementation can have a significant impact on its time efficiency. We propose a possible forward solution set-up to benefit in computation time efficiency. Optimizing the DDA implementation can decrease the computation time for a microwave tomography algorithm significantly, and thus produces images closer to real time.

articleTitle: A Dual Band Circular Polarized Antenna Array based on the Sequential Arrangement of Non-identical Disc Patches
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a circular polarized antenna array based on the sequential rotation architecture applied to a set of nonidentical antenna elements. Exploiting the recursive application of sequential rotation architecture, the entire set of elements is excited with the opportune phase progression, despite the different resonant frequencies. The resulting structure is an irregular array, suitable for operation at two independent frequencies.Simulation shows a gain exceeding 11.0 dB at 5.3 GHz and 12.5 dB at 6.9 GHz. Return loss better than 18 dB is observed, as well as, polarization ratios exceeding 22 dB. Adequate bandwidths around the operation frequencies are observed as well.

articleTitle: A Simple High-Performance First-Order P-Band Probe for Spherical Near-Field Antenna Measurements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A shorted annular air-substrate patch antenna is proposed as a first-order P-band probe for spherical near-field antenna measurements. This antenna is simple to design and manufacture; yet, it has a superior performance in terms of bandwidth, directivity, and gain compared to other types of P-band probes. This work discusses the electrical and mechanical properties of the antenna and presents simulation results.

articleTitle: Peel-off and Stick Antennas for Small Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Antennas on changing platforms without hindering the device performance is a fairly novel concept in antenna technologies. Reconfigurability in terms of the real estate can open new avenues for antenna designs that haven't been explored before. This paper investigates a `peel off' antenna which can be mounted on any desirable surface and can be made operational. The suggested antenna is reusable and can be made to stick on multiple surfaces based on the operational requirements at a certain point in time. This research is primarily focused on antennas for small unmanned aircraft vehicles (sUAV) and hence both conformal and planar designs are investigated.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Reconfigurable Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A radiation pattern reconfigurable horn antenna (RHA) capable of steering its main beam in three directions in the semi-sphere space corresponding to θ ∈ {-25°, 0°, 25°}, is presented. The RHA consists of a driven X-band (10 GHz-11.5 GHz) horn antenna, a reconfigurable parasitic layer and a dielectric loaded truncated pyramid (DLTP). The surface of the parasitic layer has two metallic strips and a grid of 4x4 square metallic pixels, which are interconnected by PIN diode switches, thereby enable configuring the surface geometry. The simulated results indicate that from 10 GHz to 11.5 GHz realized gain of ~ 14 dB is achieved in all modes of operation.

articleTitle: Hybrid Solver Via Equivalence Principle Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The challenges of predicting wireless device performance may be addressed by constructing hybrid solutions with rigorous models around sensitive regions and approximate methods over electrically-large smooth structures. The surface equivalence principle supports constructing multiple scattering problems with per-domain scattering algorithms, but discretization over electrically large surfaces is prohibitively expensive. A Schur complement applied to the equations expresses a generalized hybrid method with clear physical interpretation. An example case with results is presented.

articleTitle: Study of 3D printed HoneyComb Microwave Absorbers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this study, we propose to apply a 3D printing technology to the realization of honeycomb microwave absorbers. At first, printability of simple honeycomb structures was demonstrated and validated by microwave measurements between 2 and 18 GHz. Then, we designed and manufactured multi-scale honeycomb absorbers. These complex absorbers that cannot be manufactured by a standard process, make it possible to increase absorption level at high frequencies, and thus bandwidth. This new shaping technique of microwave absorbers paves the way for the design and fabrication of complex high-performance topologies that cannot be reached by conventional materials and processes.

articleTitle: Parallel Subdomain Level DGTD Method with Load Balancing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a parallel subdomain level discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method is achieved via Message Passing Interface (MPI) library based on upwind flux and Runge-Kutta explicit time integration. A load balancing scheme is proposed for subdomains with multiple kinds of elements in different orders. Numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme and good speedup is achieved.

articleTitle: Bow-Spiral Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The paper presents the bow-spiral antenna, a hydride design which integrates the geometry structure of an exponential bow-tie into an Archimedean spiral antenna in order to reduce its high input impedance.

articleTitle: Metasurface from Hyperuniform Disordered Distribution
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metasurface with different reflection phases have promised great possibilities in realizing diffusion-like backward scattering. In this paper, metasurface with unit cells based on hyperuniform disordered structure is presented. It is proven to be able to reduce Radar Cross Sections(RCS) in comparison with its counterpart design based on metasurfaces from periodic distribution. V-shape antenna is used as unit cell and '1' bit coding metasurfaces based on hyperuniform disordered structure and periodic structure are designed respectively. Numerical results show that metasurface with hyperuniform disordered structure generate more diffusion, which demonstrate larger bandwidth and higher RCS reduction compared with the corresponding metasurface based on periodic distribution.

articleTitle: A Novel OAM Generator with Third Order meta-FSS
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper propose a novel third order meta-frequency selective surfaces (meta-FSS) to generate transmitted orbital angular momentum (OAM) waves at X-band. The meta-FSS consists of three metal layers separated by two substrate layers. A phase difference of 180º is introduced between two orthogonal directional by changing the size of the structure. Based on element rotation theory, the meta-FSS array is arranged with different rotation angles. A panel including 13×13 elements is designed and simulated to produce +1 and -2 mode OAM waves.

articleTitle: Circular Polarization Conversion Reflectarray Suppressing Beam Shift
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes arbitrary shaped elements for a linear-to-circular polarization reflectarray suppressing beam shift depending on frequencies. To make aperture phase distribution uniform even at different frequencies, each element achieves specified different frequency properties. So we optimize the elements with orthogonal two axial symmetries by the genetic algorithm (GA). Furthermore, linearly polarized orthogonal waves will be transformed into a circularly polarized one by making reflection-phase difference between TE/TM incidences 90 degrees.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Model for Reconfigurable Far-Infrared Filter Employing Vanadium Dioxide
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose equivalent circuit models for a reconfigurable multi-band bandstop filter in the far-infrared region of 8 -17 μm (36-18 THz) utilizing Vanadium Dioxide (VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>). Implementation of VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> allows the resonant frequencies of the filter to be reconfigured. Two circuit models are proposed to characterize the metal and insulator phases of VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>.

articleTitle: Modeling of circularly-polarized CTS arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an efficient numerical tool for the analysis of circularly-polarized continuous transverse stub (CTS) arrays. The proposed structure comprises oversized open-ended parallel-plate waveguides (PPWs), radiating in free space. The operation of the antenna relies on the simulataneous excitation of two orthogonally-polarized modes in the PPWs, i.e. the fundamental TEM and the first higher order TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> mode. The developed numerical model provides the active reflection coefficient of the radiating slots and the radiated fields. The axial-ratio (AR) is computed as well. Results are in excellent agreement with full-wave simulations. Guidelines are then provided to help the design of the antenna. A design example is presented. It attains an axial ratio of less than 1.5 dB and an input reflection coeffcient lower than -10 dB over a relative bandwidth of 43.9%.

articleTitle: Additively Manufactured Circular-Linear Polarization Converter using Circular Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper details the design of a novel circular-linear polarization converter using circular waveguide with elliptical corrugations to be constructed using additive manufacturing, making use of the technique's ability to create otherwise difficult geometries and rapid prototyping capabilities. The designed converter has under 1 dB of insertion loss and below 20 dB cross-polarization in its operating band.

articleTitle: Design of an Ultra Low Frequency CubeSat Antenna Payload for Radio Astronomy in Space: State of the Art
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a brief overview of the state of the art for the design of an ultra low frequency antenna (80 kHz-30 MHz) as a payload for a CubeSat used for radio astronomy in space. Current ultra low frequency radio astronomy antenna designs are shown along with a discussion about the basis for future research. One of the designs, the spiral antenna is discussed in more detail.

articleTitle: Extraction of Lung Water Content from Computerized Tomography Scans
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An automatic procedure is developed to extract the water content in lungs based on the computerized tomography (CT) scans of the human torso. Image processing techniques such as watershed segmentation are used to isolate the lungs from rest of the organs in the torso. The water contents of 60 sets (patients) of CT scans are calculated with a mean values similar to the values in the literature.

articleTitle: A Novel Numerical Technique for Analyzing Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a novel technique for efficient numerical modeling of electromagnetic scattering from metasurfaces comprising of truncated periodic or locally-varying quasi-periodic surfaces. The proposed technique hybridizes the periodic Finite Element Method (FEM) with the Method of Moments (MoM) to develop an algorithm far more efficient than conventional numerical methods for electromagnetic scattering from arbitrary objects. The key feature of the proposed algorithm is that it takes advantage of the quasi-periodic nature of metasurfaces to derive high-level Macro Basis Functions (MBFs) derived by using the FEM, and subsequently used to derive a reduced MoM matrix for the unknown coefficients of the MBFs. Numerical results are derived and validated by comparing them with those obtained from commercial softwares.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Azimuth-Only Amplitude-Comparison DF System in Operational Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a performance analysis of an azimuth-only amplitude-comparison direction finding (DF) system in operational scenarios. The DF system is composed of two-squinted cavity-backed spiral antennas and it can move while in operation. Initially, the DF system is calibrated by using the spirals embedded element patterns, being the resulting calibration residual errors evaluated at frequencies in the range from 1 to 18 GHz. Errors obtained are lower than 1° rms. The azimuth angular errors are then computed considering sources not polarization matched to the spiral antennas and the system moving on paths whose heights may change with time. Full-wave simulations are run to estimate the radiation data needed for evaluation.

articleTitle: Wideband Anisotropic Unit Cell Design for Perfect Cross-Polarization Conversion
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the design of a wideband cross polarization converter is presented. The surface is composed by anisotropic unit cells have three resonances at 17.9, 32.8, and 48.4 GHz. The unit cell has 100% cross polarization conversion efficiency from 15 to 52GHz. Furthermore, the same unit cell is further used to compose a cheeseboard-like metasurface for monostatic radar cross section reduction. The proposed design has been fabricated and measurement is currently being carried out.

articleTitle: A Broadband Array with Unbalanced Feeds : Elements and Power Combiners Based on the Fragmented Aperture Principle
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A fully combined, fixed-beam, ultra-wideband array with unbalanced feeds is described. Both the array elements and power combiners are based on the fragmented aperture principle. Each was designed separately using a genetic algorithm, then combined to form an integrated version of the array. Measured results are reported including realized gain, and beamwidths in the principal planes.

articleTitle: Path loss compensated pattern diversity antennas for mmWave 5G indoor base stations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A tapered slot antenna integrated with metamaterial unit cells and dielectric loading is proposed in this paper. The impedance bandwidth is 27-29 GHz (7.2%) with a forward gain of 12 dBi and a high aperture efficiency of 75%. In order to achieve uniform received power on the ground, antenna elements with 3 dB higher gain are necessary for beams oriented at ±45°, hence a compact co-polarized topology of pattern diversity is proposed to achieve a wide angle coverage of ±65° with path loss compensation. Detailed simulation and measurement results are presented.

articleTitle: Identification of Suspicious Mass in Biological Tissues Using Resonance Parameters Extracted from Late Time Response
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Singularity expansion method (SEM) has been used for a long time to directly extract residues and poles of a target from its transient response. It is well known that the complex natural resonances (CNRs) extracted from the transient response are aspect independent, while they are only function in the geometry and electrical properties of the target. In this paper, a new approach applying generalized pencil of function method (GPOF) has been presented for detection and characterization of suspicious mass in biological tissues.

articleTitle: A novel structure for VHF band dipole antenna miniaturization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A miniaturized VHF band single dipole antenna based on a novel structure is presented. Compared to the original single dipole antenna or simple spring structure, proposed antenna has a better merit in miniaturization by introducing a slow-wave structure inserted the spiral. As a result, the frequency is drifting down, without sacrificing the return loss and gain, which means the possibility of decreasing the size. The antenna is designed for a VHF sensor, whose operate frequency is 220MHz. Because of a quarter of its wavelength is about 340mm, which is too long to fit into a small device. The proposed antenna is designed with a physical dimension of φ10×62.5mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, which is only about 18.2% of normal dipole antenna length. The proposed antenna was simulated by HFSS, and the results show that the antenna can provide a max gain with 1.72dBi. A prototype was fabricated and teste, and the results show the operate frequency is drifting down about 45MHz.

articleTitle: Pulse Generation using a Degenerate Band Edge Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a pulse generation scheme based on a fourth-order degeneracy in the dispersion relation. We take advantage of the loaded quality factor enhancement and the ultra-sensitivity to external perturbations due to the high order degeneracy in such a structure. The proposed scheme is able to produce a train of nanosecond pulses with several watts of output power. Such a design offers a flexibility that allows to conceive either high output power pulses or high frequency train of pulses.

articleTitle: E-shaped Nano-antenna with Asymmetric Integrated Dielectric-plasmonic Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel design of end-fire nano-antenna is introduced with higher directivity compared with previous works. To feed the designed nano-antenna by low loss dielectric waveguide, integrated dielectric-plasmonic waveguide is designed and by directional nano-particles inside the waveguide, directivity of the nano-antenna increases.

articleTitle: Aggressive Space Mapping Technique for Reconfigurable Hexagonal Patch Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, aggressive space mapping (ASM) combined with finite element method (FEM) is applied to a frequency reconfigurable patch antenna design. This technique provides an efficient approach in reducing the computational time for the determination of the RF, DC bias capacitor and DC bias inductor values. The efficiency of aggressive space mapping in the frequency reconfigurable antenna design is very high.

articleTitle: A Capacitive Loaded CRLH in Reversal Triple band MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a compact and high isolated multiband two elements MIMO antenna. The single antenna is based on new capacitor loading of composite right/left handed (C-CRLH) unit cell configuration. A resonant one cell antenna is designed for having triple band at 1.95 GHz, 3.6 GHz and 6.5 GHz. The MIMO configuration has been designed in opposite mirror configuration to have high isolation between the elements without the need of using additional mutual coupling techniques between the elements. The single antenna overall size is 38 × 28 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The achieved results confirm that the antenna has reflection coefficient less than -10 dB at the three frequencies and transmission coefficient less than -20 dB. The obtained results are achieved using circuit modeling and full wave simulations.

articleTitle: Propagation of Low-Frequency Broadband Electromagnetic Field Waveforms in the Atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a physical model that enables a detailed quantitative analysis of propagation of broadband low-frequency electromagnetic field waveforms through the atmosphere. Our analysis reveals broadband atmospheric transparency regions within which the group-velocity of atmospheric air is unusually weak, enabling distortion-free long-distance transmission of broadband low-frequency electromagnetic pulses.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of a Microwave Brain Scanner for Cerebrovascular Diseases Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Brain stroke is one of the most common diseases worldwide. Magnetic resonance imaging and computerized tomography are currently the two most assessed and reliable diagnostic tools, of great support to the clinicians. However, these devices are costly, time consuming and not portable, so that they are not appropriate for bedside monitoring. Hence, there is an increasing worldwide interest to develop complementary techniques to continuously monitor a patient after the stroke onset. In this paper, we report about the experimental testing of a novel device able to monitor cerebrovascular diseases, whose realization is based on microwave imaging technology. A 2-D version of the device has been fully experimentally tested and its 3-D version is under development.

articleTitle: A New Approach to Design High Directivity, Compact Omnidirectional CP Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new approach to design high directivty, compact omnidirectional circularly polarized (OCP) antenna arrays is presented in this paper. An array of collinear electric (E-) and magnetic (M-) radiators is realized by simply cascading copper loops and vertical strips to form an electrically long antenna structure. This array has two identical half sections that is excited in its center. The circumference of each loop and the length of each vertical strip are about a half-wavelength. The configuration facilitates the currents on all of the loop and the strip radiators to achieve the same phase and, hence, the array is a set of in-phase E- and M-radiators. Due to the fact that the phases of the magnetic radiator currents are 90° ahead of the electric ones, the 90° phase difference between the two subsets of radiators required to achieve OCP radiation is realized. An optimized prototype was fabricated and measured. The whole structure is compact and easily fabricated. It covers a 130 MHz bandwidth from 2.34 to 2.47 GHz and produces OCP radiation. The peak measured LHCP realized gain for the four-stage version is 5.1 dBic.

articleTitle: Dualband Multi-Constellation GNSS Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper demonstrates a Dual band Multi-Constellation GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) Antenna solution for automotive applications. In designing a GNSS Antenna to cover global requirements and specifications to be considered in order to support multiple navigation satellite constellations. In addition to GPS, the GLONASS constellation is required to support ERA-GLONASS in Russia, the Galileo constellation is required to support eCall in Europe. Also, there is the BeiDou constellation being deployed by China. These constellations have varying bandwidths and carrier frequencies, it is a challenge to design and integrate an antenna solution to support global coverage. In this paper, a single Dual band multi- constellation patch antenna is designed and result shows some of the potential applications.

Author Keywords: Patch Antenna; Dual band; Higher order mode

articleTitle: Using MIMO to Extend the Operating Band of Over-the-Horizon Radar Transmit Beamformers to Lower Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A MIMO radar approach is used in the lower portion of the frequency band of an over-the-horizon radar transmit beamformer to improve its robustness to calibration errors. By exploiting smaller Doppler frequency shifts at lower frequencies, the MIMO approach can preserve the unambiguous range-Doppler space across the operating frequency band and improve clutter rejection by several orders of magnitude.

articleTitle: Coupling Effects on Polarization-Agile Patch Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents two configurations of four-element polarization-agile patch antenna array: corner-to-corner and side-to-side arrangement of simple stub-loaded elements. By feeding sequentially with 0.4λ element spacing at 1.575 GHz for GNSS applications on 1.6-mm FR4 substrate, both structures are smaller than the common half-wavelength spacing arrays, and have very low axial ratio of sub-0.1 dB, coupling coefficients of less than -22 dB, and realized gain of 5.68 dBic for RHCP and 6.18 dBic for LHCP of corner-to-corner configuration, as well as a CP gain of 6.81 dBic for side-to-side configuration to explore the effects of coupling on array performance.

articleTitle: Theory of Vertical Dipole Over a Dielectric-Coated Impedance Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The space-wave radiation characteristics of the vertical electric dipole antenna placed above a dielectric-coated impedance surface is investigated. The reflection from the dielectric-coated impedance surface is characterized using the generalized reflection approach using the impedance boundary condition. The resultant Sommerfeld integral equation is separated into the particular and homogeneous parts using the method of scattering superposition. The particular term is recast into the Richmond's form while the DCIM with GPOF technique is used to obtain the closed form of the integral corresponding to the homogeneous part. The current distribution on the dipole is thereafter obtained and the radiated far-field evaluated using method of steepest descent. The formulation can be used to evaluate the input-impedance and radiation characteristics of antennas over the sea, a lake under ice-cover or over the earth with a layer of cement or asphalt over the earth-surface.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Base Station Antenna Array for Sub-6 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band dual-polarized basestation antenna is developed for the 5th generation mobile communication system. By using frequency selective surface, the proposed antenna can successfully cover 0.69-0.96 GHz band (B1) and 3.3-5 GHz band (B2) with low-profile characteristics and stable radiation patterns. The total size of the proposed array is 0.82λL × 0.82λL × 0.17λL (λL is the wavelength at the center frequency of B1). Simulated results show that the proposed dual-band dual-polarized array achieves 32.7% bandwidth in the B1 and 40.9% bandwidth in B2. These attractive features make this array an ideal candidate for further 5G massive MIMO base station antenna developments.

articleTitle: A Wideband Endfire Antenna Using SWG-HIS Hybrid Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A surface wave-based planar endfire antenna with wideband performance is presented. Surface waves are excited and supported to propagate in a required direction in a surface-wave guide (SWG)-high impedance surface (HIS) hybrid structure. Four surface-wave modes are excited, and thus the antenna resonates at 4.5 and 5.5 GHz. The proposed antenna supports a operation band from 4.08 to 5.72 GHz and the realized gains in a range of 5.75 ~ 7.05 dBi.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Planar Microwaves Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a sensor design concept for enhancing the electromagnetic energy stored in the sensing volume is presented. The design concept is based on using a three-dimensional capacitor to enhance the stored electric energy in the sensing volume that is exposed to the material under test. For validation, a resonator based on a split-ring resonator (SRR) was utilized to design a sensor. The concept was tested using numerical simulation to characterize dielectric materials.

articleTitle: Codebook Requirements for Estimating Multi-Antenna SAR in Linear Time
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) is an exposure safety measure used by regulatory agencies for determining the compliance of portable wireless transmitting devices. It has been shown that compliance of devices with multiple transmitter chains operating at a single frequency can be determined with measurement time that is linear in the number of antennas per probe location. One known example relies on a specific set of excitation signals that turns on one or two antennas at a time. We provide a general requirement on the excitation signals such that a wide class of signals can be used for SAR compliance in linear time. This general requirement allows a subset of the signal "codebook" of the device to be considered as the excitation signals for SAR compliance. We give an example where the excitation signals turn all of the antennas on simultaneously and show its advantages over the existing method.

articleTitle: Simulation and Experiment of a Loaded Ultra-small Symmetric Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In order to realize the miniaturization design of symmetrical dipole antenna operating at 0.1-1 GHz, folding method is adopted to improve the effective current path of the dipole, and resistance is loaded to improve the impedance matching. A symmetrical dipole antenna with a size of 78 mm × 12 mm × 10 mm is proposed. The antenna was modeled and simulated in the CST Microwave Studio software<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>. The simulation results show that the VSWR of the antenna is less than 2 in the frequency range of 0.1-1 GHz. The antenna has the characteristics of ultra-miniaturization, and its size in the polarization direction is only 0.026 times of the minimum operating wavelength. In addition, it has ultra-wideband characteristics, which can be used in small microwave test systems.

articleTitle: Metasurface based far infrared solar absorber
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metasurface based broadband solar absorber made up of gold and silver using square and rectangular resonators is proposed. This design is first analyzed by the geometrical parameters to study the solar absorption characteristics in the of infrared and visible frequency range of 150THz to 500THz. Results are analyzed in terms of reflectance, transmittance and absorption characteristics and electric field distribution is shown. The proposed design provides high and broadband absorption which can be used as solar absorber of sun irradiance spectrum in solar cell.

articleTitle: Full-duplex Near-infrared Communication via Spatiotemporally-modulated Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We demonstrate the operation of a spatiotemporally-modulated array antenna as a full transceiver in near-infrared frequency regime which enables optical full-duplex communication via rejection of interference between transmitted and received signals. For this purpose, we load plasmonic nanodipoles with indium-tin-oxide whose permittivity can be varied in time via modulation of carrier concentration by applying a radio-frequency biasing signal. The extreme confinement of electric field at the nanogap when operating in the resonant regime leads to enhanced frequency conversion efficiency. Adopting a progressive phase delay in the temporal modulation of an array of transversely polarized nanodipoles supporting backward guided modes enables transmission and reception via frequency up/down conversion through space-time photonic transitions of guided modes into leaky propagating modes and vice versa. Such array antenna offers simultaneous transmission and reception due to isolation between temporal frequencies of transmitted and received signals, while the direction of transmission/reception can be tuned in real-time via modifying the modulation phase delay of nanoantennas. Moreover, the relatively wide bandwidth of antenna allows for multiplexing and multicasting different wavelengths in near-infrared regime. In order to analyze the time-modulated antennas, we extend the framework of discrete dipole approximation method via a multifrequency coupled approach.

articleTitle: Slot Based Frequency Reconfigurable and UWB Sensing MIMO Antennas for CR Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an integrated multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system is presented that consists of 4-element ultra-wide-band (UWB) antenna and 4-element frequency reconfigurable antenna system. Both antenna elements are designed on the same substrate. The frequency reconfigurable communication antenna is a slot-based structure that achieves frequency reconfigurability over wide range from 1.4 to 2.2 GHz using varactor diode tuning. The UWB antenna can be utilized to sense the frequency spectrum as well as operate as a MIMO antenna system over a frequency band from 1.4 to 4.85 GHz. The frequency reconfigurable antenna is loaded with an annular split ring resonator (SRR) for size reduction. The simulated and measured results are in good agreement. The total size of antenna is compact with dimensions of 150 × 200 × 1.52 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The proposed antenna is suitable to be used in tablet PCs and laptops with cognitive radio capabilities.

articleTitle: A WiFi Based Electromagnetic Visual Aid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper details the design of a demonstration device for visualizing electromagnetic wave behavior in educational contexts. The tool uses a grid of WiFi tracking nodes with RGB LEDs to display the field strength over a region.

articleTitle: Monitoring Quality Control of Fruits Using Terahertz Sensing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel application of terahertz (THz) sensing to monitor the quality of fruits by detecting the moisture content (MC) and the transmission response. The preliminary results show that the difference of loss in MC value from day 1 to day 3 is only 15% for pear slice, while that is 62% for apple slice, which causes the significant difference in the transmission response between pear and apple slices in the first 3 days. The results indicate that the relationship between the concentration of inner substances and the path loss of the THz radiation is very close to the absorption characteristics of the samples in the THz region. The application presented here can be extended to analyze the internal dielectric properties of fruits and obtain the spectral signatures of different compositions and the biomass quality control in fruits.

articleTitle: A Circuit-based Approach to the Synthesis of 2-D Omega Materials
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In one dimension, a circuit network equivalence has been established for omega materials. However, 2-D circuit-based or transmission-line metamaterials have previously been restricted to magnetic and electric responses. This paper proposes 2-D circuit-based omega materials using asymmetric circuits. A general formulation is provided in terms of ABCD-parameters and an example is shown using π-networks. These metamaterials could enable the design of compact beamformers, power dividers, and other microwave devices.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Antenna with Improved Bandwidth and Isolation for MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A multi-layer substrate integrated cavity (SIC) backed millimeter-wave antenna is proposed for multi-input multi-output (MIMO) applications.
