Owing to the stacked SIC architecture, the bandwidth and frequency selectivity of the antenna are significantly improved. Moreover, the MIMO antenna exhibits a high isolation between elements due to the constraints placed on the electromagnetic wave. To demonstrate the concept, a two-element MIMO antenna with a close spacing of 4.8 mm (0.44 λ @ 28 GHz) is designed and prototyped. Simulated and measured results show that the antenna has a broad bandwidth ranging from 26.5 to 30.2 GHz, good filtering performance, and a high isolation of over 16 dB.

articleTitle: Slow light at the nanoscale based on active epsilon-near-zero plasmonic waveguides
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Plasmonic waveguides exhibit an effective epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) response at their cut-off frequency. In this work, we demonstrate the formation of an exceptional point (EP) in a nanoscale open and lossy (non-Hermitian) nanophotonic system consisting of an array of periodic nanowaveguides loaded with a very low gain coefficient material. We theoretically analyze the obtained EP, as well as its topological properties, by using a transmission-line model adapted to the plasmonic properties of the proposed device. The dispersion of the active ENZ mode and the group velocity are thoroughly investigated. Reflectionless transmission (perfect loss compensation) and ultraslow group velocity values at the nanoscale are realized at the EP, which coincides with the ENZ cut-off frequency of the proposed plasmonic system. This special spectral degeneracy (EP) is a unique feature of the presented nanoscale symmetric plasmonic ENZ configuration, different from most of the previous works that were mainly focused on asymmetric bulky micron-scale active photonic configurations.

articleTitle: Printed Cactus Monopole Antenna with Enhanced Impedance Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Previously proposed "cactus" designs of wideband printed monopoles reported impedance bandwidths of 1:4. Here, the "cactus" topology is re-designed to enhance the impedance bandwidth to 1:8 with moderately increased electrical size. The proposed antenna is printed on an 18 cm by 15 cm FR-4 substrate. It is designed for an impedance bandwidth from 700 MHz to 5.6 GHz with a return loss better than 10 dB. Simulation and measurement results are presented and compared. Strategies for improving the accuracy of the simulation are discussed. The application is a monostatic surveillance radar utilizing two pairs of identical antennas oriented for co- and cross-polarization.

articleTitle: Modified Floquet Scattering Matrix Method for Solving N-path Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: With advances in semiconductor technology, researchers have begun exploring periodic time-modulation as a route to non-reciprocity. One such device, recently used to achieve non-reciprocity, is a N-path network. However, N-path networks can be difficult to design since the number of unknowns in simulation becomes proportional to the number of paths. By relating the frequency harmonics on the different paths, the problem size is reduced by a factor of N (the number of paths). This dramatically reduces the runtime and memory requirements, and improves the convergence of N-path network simulations. Following a description of the computational method used in this work, a validation of the code and an application example is reported.

articleTitle: Fully-Coherent Electromagnetic Scattering Model for 3D Dense Random Volumes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Physics-based Fully-Coherent Electromagnetic (EM) scattering model from 3D dense random volumes with arbitrary thickness is considered. A fully-coherent EM computation is performed using the Statistical S-Matrix Wave Propagation-in Spectral domain approach (SSWaP-SD) along with a Method of Moments (MoM) code based on the Discrete-Dipole Approximation (DDA). For an arbitrarily thick volume, thin slabs of the medium is analyzed a corresponding polarimetric N-port (representing different directions of scattering) S-matrix is generated. These S-matrices are cascaded using SSWaP-SD method to calculate the total forward and backward bistatic scattered fields in a fully coherent way. The simulation results of the backscattering from an arbitrary thick snow layer are presented.

articleTitle: A Modified Vivaldi Antenna with Low Self-reflectivity for Bone Health Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a modified Vivaldi antenna with low self-reflectivity working at 1-4 GHz is designed to improve the radiation gain by opening rectangular grooves and loading parasitic patches on the surface of the radiating patch. In order to support bone detection and reduce the self-reflectivity of the antenna, the influence of the loading resistance at the end of the antenna on the reflected signal of the antenna is analyzed. The simulation shows that this antenna has a gain of 0.92 dBi. The self-reflection characteristic of the Vivaldi antenna can be effectively reduced by loading resistors.

articleTitle: A Wideband Compact Filtering Array Antenna Using Two Sections L-CRLH Impedance Transformer
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new two-elements wideband circular monopole array antenna is presented. The array is fed by a new compact two-sections wideband impedance transformer. The transformer is comprised of two unit cells of inductor loaded composite right/left handed (L-CRLH) transmission line. The L-CRLH transformer has a size of 9.3×15.3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ≡0.54× 1.07 λg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, at mid frequency; 80% miniaturized compared to conventional design. The simulation results confirm that the transformer has a return loss less than 10 dB and insertion loss less than 0.02 dB within the passband. Consequently, the array antenna has wideband 10 dB return loss bandwidth from 1.6 GHz – 3.3 GHz (70%) with 3 dB out of band at 0.95 GHz and 3.95 GHz.

articleTitle: W band Substrate-integrated Slot Antenna-in-package Using Higher Order Mode
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This study presents the design of substrate-integrated slot antenna based on the TE20 mode. The conductance of a slot is calculated using a TE20 mode rectangular waveguide. A 94 GHz antenna is designed using benzocyclobutene for the package to validate the conductance calculations. Conductance is compared at different substrate-integrated waveguide thicknesses. The 94 GHz slot antenna has a gain of 7.2 dBi. Simulated and measured results have been compared. The antenna in package can be further interconnected and integrated with other active devices to demonstrate a three-dimensional integration.

articleTitle: N-Way Spatial Power Combining in SIW for High Power Generation MMICs – Scalability Bounds
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An N-way transition between an array of amplifiers and a single substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is presented. Its operation principle is based on excitation of the spatially distributed TE10 mode with an array of parallel and strongly coupled microstrip lines (MLs). The paper discusses and evaluates the approximate scalability bounds of such a structure in terms of the number of input channels. The model shows that, by employing a thin substrate, more amplifiers are capable of interfacing a single SIW to increase the output power, which is an important conclusion in regards to a future on-chip implementation of the structure. The model has also been validated by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: A Metafilm Based on Magnetic-Metamaterial-Lined Discs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a highly miniaturized metafilm unit cell based on metallic discs that are coated using μ-positive and large (MPL) liners. The proposed MPL-coated discs resonate at frequencies where they measure λ/9 or smaller in diameter, and exhibit a fano-shape reflection behaviour (i.e., a maximum in reflection followed by a minimum). The proposed metafilm demonstrates a polarization-selective behaviour when illuminated using a plane-wave. In this paper, we present simulation as well as experimental data demonstrating 10-12 dB better shielding at resonance using a compact metafilm measuring 1.3λ by 1.3λ. Furthermore, the proposed design remains transparent outside the shielding band.

articleTitle: A Novel Technique to Reduce Truncation Error in Near-Field Measurements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel technique for the reduction of the truncation error in near-field (NF) antenna measurements is presented. The proposed methodology is based on the generation of an over-compete dictionary to accurately model the radiation of the antenna under test (AUT) and robustly extrapolate the NF pattern outside the measurement region. An illustrative numerical result is shown to assess the performance of the presented technique when dealing with a cylindrical NF set-up.

articleTitle: Spinning Magnets in Electromagnetic Education
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recently, spinning magnets have been used to mechanically generate time-varying electromagnetic fields. While this is inherently an extremely inefficient technique limited to near-field applications, the merit of spinning magnets is the strong practical and educational link between small loop antennas and short magnetic dipoles with fictitious charges. Furthermore, important topics relevant to antennas, propagation and communications are considered when studying the performance of spinning magnets. This paper identifies a discrepancy in a major antenna text that leads to a singularity when determining the electromagnetic fields of a spinning magnet. Comparisons between calculations and published measurements of spinning magnets are also provided.

articleTitle: Gain-Maximization of FPA-fed Reflectors by Means of Linear Regression
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Mutual coupling has a demonstrable impact on the embedded pattern of the focal plane array (FPA). Therefore, it is necessary to optimize the FPA complex weighting to achieve the antenna system maximum gain. A system level model based on a hybrid combination of an in-house developed PO tool, an EM tool (CST). It turns out that the mutual coupling effects on the embedded patterns of the FPA can be can be optimized through the application of a minimum least squares (LS) residual method. Subsequently, the geometry and pattern of the FPA can be further optimized to increase the efficiency of the reflector antenna system.

articleTitle: Advanced Discontinuous Galerkin Time-Domain Methods for Challenging Engineering Problems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The unique properties of the discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method make it a very powerful numerical solver for engineering problems from different disciplines. The use of discontinuous basis functions and numerical fluxes enables many advanced techniques to be developed and implemented for the DGTD method. In this paper, our effort towards a flexible numerical solver based on the DGTD method is reviewed. The development of advanced techniques, such as dynamic h-adaptation based on adaptive Cartesian meshes, dynamic p-adaptation based on tetrahedral meshes, and multirate time integration, makes the DGTD method widely applicable to different problems.

articleTitle: Voronoi Tessellation Optimization : A Local/Global Optimization Hybrid for Electromagnetics Design
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a new hybrid local-global optimizer called the Voronoi Tessellation Optimization (VTO) algorithm which leverages precomputed gradients and a space partitioning technique to improve single objective convergence speed and robustness. VTO has been herein compared with other well-known optimization algorithms used in electromagnetics and optics and has demonstrated commensurate or improved performance on two multimodal test problems.

articleTitle: Ultra-compact wave-based solvers for fractional-calculus equations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In recent years, metamaterial and nanophotonic structures have been proposed as a new platform to perform basic mathematical operations such as integration and differentiation on a propagating wave signal. Based on suitably engineered metamaterial waveguide networks, more complex operations can be performed, for example solving integral and differential equations. In this paper, we first discuss the design of basic fractional-calculus operational elements based on compact Fourier-optics configurations. Then, we show that these basic elements can be combined in a metamaterial waveguide network to act, for example, as an analog wave-based PID controller. Finally, we present a compact optical cavity, the topology of which is equivalent to an optical feedback system, that solves fractional calculus equations. The footprint of the wave-based solver is as small as approximately 4λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>*4λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the free-space wavelength, orders of magnitude smaller than conventional Fourier-optics systems. The proposed analog wave-based equation solvers may be used as a hardware accelerator for existing digital signal and image processors.

articleTitle: Fast Multipole Time Domain Algorithm for the Scalar and Vector Wave Equation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new algorithm, fast multipole time domain (FMTD), to speed up the evaluation of interactions in the boundary integral equation method for wave equations. In FMTD, the bandlimited source signal in the time marching solution is truncated and converted to frequency domain. The static and dynamic (multilevel) fast multipole method are employed to accelerate the evaluation at discrete frequencies. Finally, the results are transformed back to obtain the transient fields. The numerical results demonstrate the accuracy of FMTD.

articleTitle: Auxiliary Space-based Preconditioner for Higher Order Finite Element Method : Performance investigation of a Hybrid CPU/GPU Implementation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a hybrid CPU/GPU multilevel preconditioner for large sparse linear systems that arise from the discretization of Maxwell's equations with higher order hierarchical finite elements. We compare the performance of the proposed approach with direct sparse solvers, and with a multiprocessor-based preconditioned iterative solution available in the commercial Altair Feko solver. This investigation shows significant speed-up with respect to the direct solvers, but moderate gain when compared to an efficient multi-processor-based preconditioner.

articleTitle: VO2-based Active Terahertz Chiral Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate a vanadium dioxide (VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) integrated chiral metamaterial exhibiting tunable chiroptical responses at terahertz frequencies. Simulated results show that a circular dichroism of ~40° and a maximum polarization rotation of ~200°/λ can be achieved around 0.7 THz with VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> in its metallic phase. More importantly, the chiroptical response from the hybrid metamaterial varies dramatically with the phase transition determined by the THz conductivity of VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Our results reveal that the unification of structured metals and phase-change materials provides the foundation to establish a new paradigm for THz chiroptical metadevices.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna Array for Ku-Band Data-Link
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes a design of a circularly polarized patch antenna array for Ku-band (14.45 GHz - 15.65 GHz) data-link for small to medium unmanned aerial vehicles. A multilayer antenna structure including the feeding network is studied in this paper. Compact size, circular polarization and bandwidth are important requirements in designing this system. The required bandwidth and circular polarization are achieved by truncating the corners of patch elements using a power divider and four bent slots to reduce the coupling effects and maintain the polarization purity. The antenna array is analyzed in terms of return loss, radiation pattern, axial ratio and total gain over the complete frequency band.

articleTitle: Polarization Independent, Broad Angle Retro-Reflection with an Optical Meta-Grating
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metasurfaces enable a large degree of manipulation of the impinging electromagnetic wavefront over a thin profile. As an example, retroreflective metasurfaces reflect waves in the opposite half space compared to regular mirrors, a functionality highly desirable for identification tagging, radars and street signaling. While common approaches require bulky configurations, gradient metasurfaces have been recently proposed as thin retroreflectors. However, these designs suffer from inefficiencies and sensitivity to loss. Here, we discuss the design and implementation of an ultrathin grating metasurface realizing polarization-independent retroreflection on the impinging wavefront, with a broad angular response and nearly lossless features. By judiciously engineering the metasurface in space, the incident light can be coupled back to an anomalous diffraction order aligned with the impinging direction. We optimize the surface to provide a robust response in angle and frequency, paving the way towards efficient, easy to engineer and polarization-independent retroreflection using a single, deeply subwavelength metasurface layer.

articleTitle: Augmenting a Patch Antenna with a Hybrid Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an unconventional design for a 2.4 GHz rectangular patch antenna is explored by implementation a Hybrid Particle Swarm Optimization (HPSO) algorithm. The proposed design utilizes multiple non-driven patches scattered around a central, driven patch in order to improve the bandwidth and gain over an identical design without the non-driven patches. Results show a 16% increase in bandwidth with a concurrent improvement to gain between 18% and 22%. Furthermore, the final design was achieved by using a custom Python script to integrate the HPSO algorithm with the full-wave solver.

articleTitle: Search-Based Design of Digital Non-Foster Antenna Match for High-Speed Low-Impedance Converters
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Previous design procedures for low-frequency digital non-Foster circuits are most effective when high input impedance analog-to-digital converters are employed. However, these earlier design methods did not include the effects of potentially low impedances of high-frequency converters that may be required for antenna impedance matching. Therefore, we present a new search-based design procedure for digital non-Foster antenna matching circuits using low-impedance converters. An example of the new design method is presented, with simulation results showing effective impedance matching of a 10 MHz electrically-small antenna using a digital non-Foster circuit and a low-impedance converter.

articleTitle: Comparison of Algorithms and Input Vectors for Sea-Ice Classification with L-band PolSAR Data
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Convolutional neural network (CNN) and fuzzy c-means (FCM) are applied to L-band PolSAR data in advanced-melt and winter phases, respectively, to classify sea-ice type. Several types of input vector are derived from the covariance matrix to improve the accuracy rate of classification. The parameters in algorithms and input vectors are also analyzed.

articleTitle: Dual Frequency Processing of Subsampled Measurements in W-band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Nowadays, mm-waves are targeted for numerous applications, among which security ones. With the increasing threats of attacks all over the world, concealed objects detection has become a major concern. Systems already exist but they need to be improved for the upcoming requirement of imaging a moving crowd. Having a real-time image is one of the serious challenges for system’s completion. Measurement time is an issue that we endeavor to drastically reduce. We image an object with subsampled measurements and the real-time back-propagation algorithm (BPA). The on measurements points compression rate is 95%. BPA intrinsically requires a high number of spatial measurements points to avoid grating lobes in the image, which makes the subsampling impracticable. We make use of a dual frequency processing to overcome this difficulty. The processing was tested on measurements taken at 77 and 94 GHz and results show a good grating lobe suppression. Few years ago, the practical implementation of this dual frequency technique would have been an issue but the increasing developments of systems at mm-Waves makes it easier.

articleTitle: Beamforming Apertures with Wideband Low-Cost Front-Ends
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Low cost beamforming for 5G communication systems is of strong interest. A goal is to reduce complexity and the number of components for the beamforming network. In this paper, we present a novel hardware-reduced radio frequency (RF) front-end of beamforming at 5G bands. To reduce the large number of RF chains in such millimeter-wave (mm-wave) massive arrays, we introduce a frequency independent beamforming concept based on element-to-element mixing (BEEM). BEEM avoids conventional phase shifters and further reduces components by grouping several antenna elements into subarrays. Doing so, more than 96% in hardware and size reduction is achieved. Simulations were conducted to validate our system's performance using 16-quadrature amplitude modulation (16-QAM) schemes. Results show that a near theoretical signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gain is achieved using our topology.

articleTitle: Analysis of Oxygen Absorption at 60 GHz Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, analysis of atmospheric attenuation due to oxygen absorption of 60 GHz band signals is presented. The analysis is based on a time-domain simulation model that incorporates medium dispersion properties. For this purpose, a multi-pole material dispersion model of oxygen absorption is developed based on available experimental data. The simulation algorithm is based on the auxiliary differential equation (ADE) finite difference time domain (FDTD) technique which implements the general polarization formulation and uses the rotating boundary conditions to allow for long propagation distances. The results are useful in the prediction of propagation power loss such that methods for compensation can be devised.

articleTitle: Geometric Improvements on Solar Cells for Reducing Reflections
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present horn-shaped cavities in order to improve the efficiency of energy harvesting in solar cells with traditional materials. Nano-cavities, which are already used for this purpose in the literature, are generally based on the principles of ray optics, while their sizes are in fact comparable to wavelength. Inspired by their effectiveness at radio and microwave frequencies, we design horn-shaped cavities that can effectively trap light and reduce reflections. Based on electromagnetic responses of initial structures, horn geometries are further optimized to minimize reflections and improve absorption efficiency. Numerical results demonstrate excellent performances of the designed cavities, which may even eliminate need for matching layers.

articleTitle: Optimal Thinning Techniques of Antenna Phased Arrays for Dual Band Operation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a comprehensive design method is proposed to construct a dual-band operation antenna array, interleaving two arrays operating at Ku and Ka-band frequencies, on the same real estate with minimal number of elements. This novel approach targets the optimization of directivity and sidelobes level (SLL) for two phased arrays over a wide scan range.

articleTitle: Loss Optimization of Dual-Resonance Phase-Agile Reflectarray Using Equivalent Circuit
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the loss optimization of a reconfigurable dual-resonance reflectarray array element is presented. First an equivalent circuit is developed which models the electrical performance of the array element. The major sources of loss in the array element are then discussed before the equivalent circuit is used to evaluate the external coupling's effect on loss and phase range to minimize the element's loss while maintaining a phase range greater than 360°. Finally, the optimized loss and phase performance of the equivalent circuit is presented.

articleTitle: Optimization of Coplanar Waveguide Structure for Ultra Wideband Integrated Electro-optic Mach Zehnder Modulator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Using numerical tools, coplanar waveguide (CPW) transmition line is optimized to be utilized in ultra-compact traveling wave electro-optic modulators (EOMs). Important factors such as minimization of the radio frequency (RF) loss, impedance mismatch, and velocity mismatch are investigated. Our results reveal that coplanar waveguide can provide conditions for ultracompact Mach-Zehnder modulators (MZM) to operate at frequencies up to terahertz range.

articleTitle: X-Band Reflective Electromagnetic Beam Controlling Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Reflective array metasurface has essential applications in wireless remote communication systems due to their high gain, narrow beamwidth, and simple structure. A reflective beam focusing metasurface and a beam deflecting metasurface are proposed in this paper. The focal length of the focusing metasurface is three and ten times wavelength, respectively. The beam deflecting metasurface can achieve beam deflection at 20°. An experimental prototype is manufactured to validate our design.

articleTitle: A Dual-polarized FSS on a Single Substrate using Highly-coupled Interlayer Inductance
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes a reconfigurable FSS loaded with varactors for manipulating the vertical and horizontal impedance with incrementally configured DC voltage bias. Highly coupled unit cell topology featuring near-zero separation (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>/250 at 2.4 GHz) leads to rapid impedance transition with an extremely low insertion loss in the electrically transparent state and high reflections in the electrically opaque state. Equivalent circuit analysis is introduced and experimental measurement confirms this approach.

articleTitle: Field Sampling Strategies for POD Model Order Reduction of Particle-in-Cell Simulations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Particle-in-Cell (PIC) simulations are an useful tool for the analysis of kinetic collisionless plasmas such as those found in high power microwave devices, vacuum electronics, directed energy devices, among others. However, PIC simulations remain computationally costly, and model order reduction strategies such as the Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) can be instrumental in reducing some of these costs. The efficacy of the reduced-order model resulting from application of POD depends on several factors, among them the strategy employed to sample field values when constructing the reduced order model. In this work we analyze and compare several such field sampling strategies.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Gap Leakage Analysis for the SKA Mid-Frequency Dish
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents electromagnetic analysis as performed on the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) mid-frequency dish in order to estimate the ground leakage caused by gaps in the main reflector. The effects of the ground leakage are shown in terms of conventional performance parameters such as gain and aperture efficiency, as well as the percentage of feed power hitting the ground behind the main reflector. Analysis were performed for SKA Band 1 and 2 with a combined frequency range of 0.4 − 1.8 GHz. It is shown that the gaps in the main reflector reduce the gain between 0.23 and 0.05 dB and could increase the noise temperature by approximately 14 K when pointed at zenith. The transmission percentage of the incident power hitting the ground is below 0.2% across the combined bands.

articleTitle: Diffuse Scattering Characteristics of Rough Materials at mm-Wave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The results of a wideband measurement campaign aimed at investigating the diffuse scattering characteristics of rough materials at 40-50 GHz are shown in this paper. Scattering coefficients are derived based on the Fresnel formula theory and Gaussian rough surface model. The results indicate that the calculated coefficients agree well with the measured data, and the backscattering phenomena and the Fabry-Pérot resonance characteristic are obvious.

articleTitle: An Easily Fabricated 3D Design for Increased Permittivity Range in Artificial Dielectric Layers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel design for artificial dielectric layers which utilizes connectivity between various layers to achieve an increased range of effective permittivity in the unique direction. Like traditional artificial dielectric layers, the new design may be easily fabricated through standard PCB techniques. An experimentally-determined formula for designing unit cells of this type to achieve desired permittivity values is also presented.

articleTitle: Mars Exploration: Wideband Frequency Reconfigurable Electrically Small Multi-Turn Loop Antenna Using MEMS Switch
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Wideband frequency reconfigurable electrically small multi-turn loop antenna is designed for 0.8-10MHz broadband dielectric spectrometer for potential future Mars rover missions to explore water and hydrated minerals present in the Martian subsurface. The novelty of this work is the achievement of reconfigurability and wideband impedance transformation by employing MEMS switch and transmission line transformers. Switch circuit model and ideal transmission line transformer model are used to demonstrate proof of the concept. A prototype of the design is developed, and measurements are performed.

articleTitle: Wideband Vector Antenna using Radiation Pattern Reconfigurability for 3-D Direction Finding
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this communication, direction finding performances of a wideband vector antenna are improved by taking advantage of its radiation pattern reconfigurability. A method is proposed to select the additional radiation pattern diversity that provides an accurate estimation of the direction of arrival of an incident electromagnetic field over a wider frequency bandwidth.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Filtering Antenna Using SRR Without Extra Circuit
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a novel dual-polarized filtering patch antenna without extra circuit. This proposed antenna can achieve four radiation nulls with split ring resonators (SRR) placed inside the antenna aperture. As a demonstration, the antenna is designed to meet the applications for the 5G band (4.8-5 GHz) for S11 <; -10 dB with the total profile of 0.06λL. The implemented antenna achieves an average gain of 5 dBi, a cross-polarization ratio of 23 dB, an isolation of 20 dB within the operating band.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Dual-Circularly Polarized Pyramidal Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A polarizer system based on a cross slot on the broad-wall of a rectangular waveguide is presented. The system can exhibit dual-bands of operation, one at 72 GHz and one at 84 GHz. The polarizer feeds a pyramidal horn antenna with constant gain of 18 dB. The system can achieve dual-circular polarization in both bands of operation when the feeding port is switched. The isolation between the two feeding ports is more than 20 dB at the resonant frequencies.

articleTitle: Linear-Complexity H2-Based Direct Sparse Solver for Electromagnetic and Multiphysics Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A fast nested direct matrix solution is developed for solving the sparse matrices resulting from electromagnetic and multiphysics analysis in linear complexity. In this solver, we accelerate all dense matrix computations underlying the state-of-the-art multifrontal direct solver by developing fast H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-based algorithms. Each computation is performed on small matrices of rank size, which is also the rank of the separator instead of the rank of the original 3-D problem. Direct solution of millions of unknowns arising from a finite-element based analysis is obtained in a few minutes on a single CPU core.

articleTitle: Periodic Leaky-Wave Antenna with Modified Gielis-Shaped Patch Elements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, periodic leaky-wave antenna with modified Gielis-shaped patch elements are proposed. Modified Gielis curve profiles are used for the patch elements to enhance the operating bandwidth of the leaky wave antenna. The antenna has an operating bandwidth from around 4 GHz to 8.5 GHz and its characteristics such as return loss, insertion loss, realized gain and radiation pattern are simulated and are compared with the measured results of the fabricated prototype.

articleTitle: Detection of Scatterers Inside Metal Containers via VLF Signals of Opportunity
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Radio frequencies at or below the VLF range (3-30 kHz) are uniquely capable of penetrating highly conductive materials. This can be exploited to detect objects hidden within metal containers. In this paper, we present observations of VLF scattering in such a situation, using VLF transmitters as signals of opportunity. Scattering is detected in the near field from an object inside an aluminum enclosure, and a gradiometric method is presented to differentiate the scattered signal from the plane wave that is incident onto the system.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study of a Cylindrical Microstrip Metasurface Using the State Space Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work a preliminary study of the state space method applied to the electromagnetic cloaking problem is presented. A dielectric coated circular cylinder cloaked with a metasurface based on a sinusoidally modulated unit cell is considered. The state space method is used to examine the object's scattered field and to analyze its composition in terms of specular, trapped and creeping wave modes around the cloaking working frequency.

articleTitle: Impedance-matched circular polarization selective surfaces with spin-selective phase modulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes an impedance-matched circular polarization selective surface which also allows reshaping of the reflected circularly polarized (CP) field. The required reflection phase discontinuities are realized by leveraging the geometric phase shift (i.e., Pancharatnam-Berry phase). The physical realization of the surface is discussed which utilizes cascaded layers of crossed meander lines. The versatility of the proposed structure is showcased by numerically demonstrating a CPSS that reflects a left-handed CP field at an arbitrary angle, but normally transmits a right-handed CP field.

articleTitle: A Tri-Band Dual-Polarized Slot-Ring Antenna for Array Design
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-polarized shared-aperture slot-ring antenna that can switch among S, C and X band is presented for array applications. By appropriately selecting the states of PIN diode switches, an S-band antenna element can be reconfigured into a 2×2 C-band array or a 4×4 X-band array. The antenna/array can operate at 2.74-4.02GHz, 4.08-6.52GHz or 7.68-8.84GHz. The coaxial lines are utilized to bring the ports to the backside of ground plane for modularity. The diagonal feeding and center feeding methods are used to support dual polarizations.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Bifilar Helical Antenna With Parasitic Parallelogram Loops
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band bifilar helical antenna with two conformal parasitic parallelogram loops is presented. The bifilar helical strips are printed on the outer surface of a Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 board, while two parasitic loops of parallelogram shape are printed on its inner surface. This board is then wrapped around a Teflon tube. The diameter and total length of the antenna are 61 mm and 58 mm, respectively. It has been shown through simulation that this bifilar antenna has not only good return loss at both the 1202 MHz to 1254 MHz and 1550 MHz to 1614 MHz bands, but also circularly polarized radiation patterns. The results show that the antenna is suitable for applications in Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS).

articleTitle: Array Synthesis in the Autocorrelation Domain - Proof and Research Tracks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the synthesis of planar thinned arrays with controlled sidelobes is addressed. A novel multi-step autocorrelation-based approach is presented, in which a stochastic optimization is firstly exploited to determine the binary sequence providing the best matching with a target function in the autocorrelation domain, and then the thinned excitations of the array are defined by selecting the best cyclic solution evaluated in terms of a user-defined figure of merit.

articleTitle: A Rectangular Waveguide Antenna with Filtering and Beam-steering Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, we discuss a convenient technique for designing rectangular waveguide filtering antennas with reconfigurable radiation properties. The basic structure we consider is an open-ended WR-137 rectangular waveguide working in the frequency range 5.85-8.20 GHz, with a stable realized gain around 7 dB. We will show that by placing two electrically small resonators at the end of the waveguide, the bandwidth of the overall structure can be reduced with important advantages in terms of noise/interference rejection. Moreover, by loading each resonator with a varactor diode, the phase shift introduced by the two elements can be controlled and, thus, exploited for steering the radiation pattern of the antenna.

articleTitle: Analysis of Cross- and X-Shaped Spiral Antenna Arrays for Amplitude-Comparison DF Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a performance analysis of cross- and X-shaped arrays of cavity-backed spiral antennas for amplitude-comparison direction finding (ACDF) systems. First, an effective calibration strategy for the ACDF system is proposed, which uses the embedded element patterns to improve the accuracy of the evaluated calibration coefficients. As will be seen, both cross- and X-shaped arrays show calibration residual error values lower than 1° rms. Finally, the ACDF system angular error values are quantified for sources which are not polarization matched to the spiral antennas. Full-wave simulations are run to estimate the arrays radiation performances in the range from 1 to 18 GHz.

articleTitle: VHF notch antenna integrated in an aircraft winglet
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the preliminary design and integration of a notch antenna in an aircraft winglet. The antenna covers bandwidth reserved for VHF air traffic control.

articleTitle: A reconfigurable antenna element for improved physical layer control
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new reconfigurable phased array antenna element is described. This element operates at X-band and provides digital control of the effective antenna structure, and therefore, its far field pattern, frequency response, polarization, etc. This presents an opportunity to improve the performance of software-defined or cognitive radio systems for which improved reconfigurable filtering is needed [1]-[2]. Because this reconfiguration occurs at the antenna and outside the front end, it has the potential to increase the dynamic range available to a system when operating in close proximity to other users.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional Joint Inversion of Acoustic and Electromagnetic Data Based on Contrast Source Inversion
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we study a three-dimensional joint inversion algorithm for acoustic and electromagnetic data based on the contrast source inversion method. Two contrast sources and two contrasts are defined to invert parameters in both acoustics and electromagnetics. The joint inversion is achieved by two interactive regularization operators, in which we use the contrast in acoustics to constrain the contrast in electromagnetics, and vice versa. Through minimizing the cost function of the joint inversion, we can reconstruct compressibility in acoustics and permittivity in electromagnetics. Numerical results show good performance of the 3D joint inversion method.

articleTitle: UWB Impedance Matching by Temporal Switching
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We introduce a novel impedance matching paradigm that is based on transmission lines with characteristic parameters, velocity and impedance, that can, at a certain instant in time, be switched between two states #1 and #2. Since the matching system is time-variant, it is essentially not constrained by the Bode-Fano bound. Thus, as we show theoretically, using this approach it is possible to obtain a linear and passive ultrawideband (UWB) impedance matching that its efficiency is well above traditional matching techniques.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Metamaterials Formed Through a Combination of Nanowire Assemblies with Top-Down Fabricated Nanoantennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we show that reconfigurable metamaterials can be achieved through a combination of nanowire assemblies with top-down lithographically fabricated nanoantennas. Simulation results show that the proposed metamaterials, which consist of assembled nanowire lattices and lithographically fabricated nanoantennas, exhibit strong chiral response in the near-infrared region. More importantly, chiroptical properties including the circular dichroism and handedness of the metamaterials can be controlled by varying the orientation of the assembled lattices. Our study reveals that directed self-assembly of nanoparticles in conjunction with nanostructures obtained from top-down fabrication approaches may open up new avenues for reconfigurable metadevices.

articleTitle: Analysis of Multi-Stage Voltage Doubler for RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The output voltage of the Rectifying Antennas (Rectennas) is known to be very low, so Multi-Stage Voltage-Doubler (MSVD) rectifiers are the most considered solution for raising this voltage level. However, in the rectenna design, it is also necessary to consider the conversion efficiency. This paper proposes an analysis of the MSVD for a compromise between the DC output voltage and the conversion efficiency of the Rectenna. Up to ten stage voltage doubler have been studied in this paper, and their performance have been evaluated through the definition of a Rectifier Figure of Merit (RFoM). The result obtained shows the existence of an optimal number of stages of the MSVD for a given RF input power level. This paper suggests that the search for the optimal number of stages should be integrated into the design issues of an MSVD.

articleTitle: Characterization of Optically Transparent Copper Micro-Wire Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Copper micro-wire patterns are a viable option for generating optically undetectable antenna and other RF devices. The conductivity of the electroless plated copper presented in this paper enables low loss designs, where the losses are predominately due to the increased resistance due to the sparse area coverage and not the fundamental conductivity of the material. In this paper, we will review the process for fabricating these copper micro-wire patterns and compare the measured and theoretical transmission line performance demonstrating the broad applicability of these highly conductive transparent patterns.

articleTitle: Doppler Effect on High-Speed Railway at 465 MHz
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Doppler effect of the radio channel is mainly presented in this paper. This is the first result on the Doppler effect in a high-speed railway (HSR) scenario under long-term evolution for railway (LTE-R) testing network whose center frequency is 465 MHz and bandwidth is 5 MHz. Detailed descriptions of the measurement environment and system are introduced. The Doppler spectrum is shown. Characteristics of Doppler, e.g., Doppler shift, root mean square Doppler spread, coherence time are discussed. This practical and novel research can be used for channel modeling, evaluating and significantly promoting the LTE-R network performance.

articleTitle: Low Profile Tri-Bands Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low-profile compact antenna with triple band operation for wireless security, WIMAX, and WLAN applications is proposed in this paper. The antenna has a simple structure with an overall area of 40 x 40 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Analysis and simulation of the proposed antenna is done by using the full 3D electromagnetic simulation software CST STUDIO SUITE. The performance of the proposed antenna was evaluated by using the reflection coefficient, the radiation pattern, and the gain.

articleTitle: A 60 GHz LTCC Magneto-Electric Dipole Phased Array with Symmetric Hybrid Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 60 GHz magneto-electric dipole phased array antenna in package (AiP) solution with symmetric hybrid feeding network is proposed using low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology. The hybrid substrate integrated waveguide (SIW)/microstrip feeding network is designed to reduce the feeding loss. With the hybrid SIW/microstrip structure, a symmetrical feeding network can be obtained in the phased array design. Benefited from the symmetrical feeding network, the performance of the array element is more identical. The 16-element phased array package size is 20 mm×20 mm×0.97 mm, which consists of 4 2×2 subarrays. The measured results show that the |S11| of each element is less than −10 dB from 56.2 to 65 GHz, and the peak gain of each element is about 6.25 ±0.75 dBi cross all four IEEE 802.15.3c channels.

articleTitle: Sinuous Antenna Design for UWB Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Sinuous antennas are capable of producing ultra-wideband radiation with polarization diversity. This capability makes the sinuous antenna an attractive candidate for UWB polarimetric radar applications. Additionally, the ability of the sinuous antenna to be implemented as a planar structure makes it a good fit for close in sensing applications such as ground penetrating radar. However, recent literature has shown the sinuous antenna to suffer from resonances which degrade performance. Such resonances produce late time ringing which is particularly troubling for pulsed close in sensing applications. The resonances occur in two forms: log-periodic resonances on the arms, and a resonance due to the sharp ends left by the outer truncation. A detailed investigation as to the correlation between the log-periodic resonances and the sinuous antenna design parameters indicates the resonances may be mitigated by selecting appropriate design parameters. In addition, a novel truncation method is proposed to remove the sharp end resonance.

articleTitle: Hybrid Method of FDTD/PO for EM Scattering Simulation of Electrically Large Targets
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: When calculating the scattering field of electrically large targets with conventional full-wave method, such as the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method, huge memory and computing resources are consumed. This paper proposes a FDTD/PO hybrid electromagnetic simulation method to solve this problem. This method can save computing resources greatly while maintaining the accuracy of FDTD calculation. Numerical simulation results are given to verify the hybrid method.

articleTitle: A High Gain Slotted Waveguide Array Filtering Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel design of slotted waveguide array filtering antenna is proposed. By integrating a pair of waveguide bandpass filters with the slotted waveguide array antenna, the integrated design not only exhibits a high gain, but also offer a good filter response. For demonstration, an antenna prototype with a center frequency of 10 GHz is designed and simulated. The simulated results show a fractional bandwidth of 7.4% covering from 9.526 to 10.39 GHz, and a high gain of 17.1 dBi.

articleTitle: A Dual-band Rectenna with Improved RF-DC Sensitivity for Wireless Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A rectenna with improved output DC voltage for dedicated wireless energy harvesting at both of 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz bands is presented. A wideband Vivaldi antenna with coupled feed along with a dual band 2-stage charge pump was designed for dual-band harvesting in the 2.4 and 5.8 GHz bands. Measurements show a DC output voltage of over 1.8V with only 2.14 μW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 2.4 GHz and 18μW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 5.8GHz of incident wireless power.

articleTitle: Effect of Electrolyte on a 2D Surface-Based Reconfigurable Liquid Metal Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper studies a reconfigurable liquid metal antenna on an open 2D surface. The antenna consists of a room temperature liquid metal, eutectic gallium and indium (EGaIn), and an electrolyte. The electrolyte is used to electrochemically modify the surface tension of the EGaIn and cause it to flow and contract on the open surface. By altering the shape of the EGaIn on the surface, its properties can be tuned over a large range, in principle. This paper studies the types of geometries that can be obtained with this electrochemical tuning and the effect of the electrolyte configuration on the antenna. The larger the volume of electrolyte, the lower resonant frequency and radiation efficiency. Moreover, in the case of electrolyte area with 80 mm × 50 mm × 0.5 mm, the operation frequency continuously tunes from 0.71 GHz to 4.03 GHz for a tuning ratio to 5.6 : 1 and the maximum gain is 3.48 dBi.

articleTitle: New potential of a direct printed LoRa antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In order to minimize the PCB (Printed Circuit Board) footprint of an IoT microtracker, we analyse the opportunity of deporting a LoRa antenna on the plastic case of the microtracker. This paper aims to compare an antenna conventionally manufactured on a PCB (FR4) and a printed antenna using jetting technology on a PC+ABS (Polycarbonate and Acrylonitrile Butadiène Styrène) polymeric substrate. The influence of the conductive ink, the antenna design and the substrate are underlined. Computational simulation is carried out. The LoRa antenna design is similar to the one used by [1].

articleTitle: X-Band Reconfigurable Reflectarray Element using Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An X-Band reconfigurable reflectarray (RA) element is designed using a frequency selective surface (FSS). The design consists of two layers. The radiating geometry at the top layer comprises of multiple smaller sized patches which are closely spaced to create strong coupling while a circular slotted patch is used as an FSS at the bottom layer. The element is a square of length 10mm (0.38λ at 11.5 GHz). A surface mount varactor diode is attached at the top layer geometry. To isolate the RF signal from DC, the biasing line is also considered. The proposed FSS-based electronically tunable element results in a phase tuning range of 250° with amplitude loss below 2 dB.

articleTitle: Tunable 3D-Printed Coaxial-Cavity Filters with Mixed Electromagnetic Coupling
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper reports on 3D-printed coaxial-cavity bandpass filters (BPFs) with multiple levels of transfer function tunability. These include: i) center frequency tuning, ii) bandwidth (BW) tuning and iii) intrinsic switching-off. They are based on a new type of mixed electromagnetic coupling that facilitates the realization of a tunable transmission zero (TZ) that is exploited for the tuning of the BPF's BW and its out-of-band isolation. Center frequency adaptivity is obtained by incorporating linear actuators on top of the cavity walls. A proof-of-concept two-pole/one-TZ BPF with tunable frequency between 1.3-2.2 GHz and BW between 59-98 MHz was manufactured and measured.

articleTitle: Cold Plate Design, Fabrication, and Demonstration for High-Power Ka-Band Active Electronically Scanned Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recent developments in mm-Wave Active Electronically Scanned Arrays (AESA) are the primarily focus on 5G applications requiring low transmit power. For some applications where high transmit power is required, the thermal management becomes a serious challenge because of two reasons: poor efficiency of the power amplifiers and closely spaced radiating elements at mm-wave frequencies. In this work we demonstrate the cooling system of a 256-element AESA operating at Ka-Band dissipating about 1kW over an area of less than 3 × 3 inches.

articleTitle: A Compact Probe for EM Side-Channel Attacks on Cryptographic Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A shielded loop probe designed for evaluating EM side-channels attacks on cryptographic systems is described. This probe is compact and is sensitive enough to measure extremely weak signals that usually comprise EM side-channels. Furthermore, this probe can greatly suppress the influence of the electric field on its measurements. At its center frequency, the probe has a sensor factor of -0.17 dB S/m and electric field suppression ratio of 30.18 dB.

articleTitle: Performance of Multi-Arm Sinuous Antenna in Analog and Digital Angle of Arrival Estimation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The angle of arrival (AOA) estimation using a single-aperture, multimode, and dual-polarized eight-arm sinuous antenna is discussed. The AOA accuracy is evaluated for the classical analog amplitude/phase comparison method and for the digital direction finding systems using Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB). Good performance demonstrated by low RMS error (<; 6°) over wide field of view is obtained over 3:1 bandwidth from 1.5 to 4.5 GHz with the considered design.

articleTitle: H-Plane Metallic RWG-to-SIW Transition Using Aperture Coupling
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of transition between H-plane metallic rectangular waveguide (RWG) and substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). It is suitable for efficient RF/microwave and millimeter-wave (mm-wave) circuit and phased array antenna systems. The simulation results of the H-plane RWG-SIW transition and the 3-dB junction power splitter are presented. The transition shows an insertion loss of less than ~ 0.11 dB @ 30 GHz with reflection coefficient less than 10 dB over the frequency band 26.3-30.7 GHz.

articleTitle: Error Estimation and Uncertainty Quantification Based on Adjoint Methods in Computational Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a summary of applications of adjoint-based methods in computational electromagnetics. We highlight the use of adjoint-informed error estimation for targeted, adaptive discretization refinement. Results are based on the higher-order finite element method in one- and three-dimensions.

articleTitle: Deep Convolutional Neural Network Approach for Solving Nonlinear Inverse Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We describe a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) approach for nonlinear electromagnetic (EM) inverse scattering problems. We evaluate the performance of the proposed CNN as a function of the number of layers using different metrics such as structure similarity measure and mean-square error. The results show that the proposed DNN architecture has great potential in tackling nonlinear inverse scattering problems.

articleTitle: A Novel 60-cm Nonsherical 3-D Printed Voxelized Lens Antenna: Design, Fabrication and Measurement
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel 60cm 3D printed, shaped, engineered material, inhomogeneous dielectric lens antenna. Common commercial 3D printers do not have a print bed large enough to directly print the 60cm diameter lens, and thus the lens must be printed in parts and fused together afterward. The presented design was printed in octants and fused together through printed alignment points to obtain the final fabricated product. To the authors knowledge, this lens is the largest 3D printed lens to date. The lens is designed using a novel synthesis tool based on a Geometrical Optics and Particle Swarm Optimization combination. The design is then voxelized for 3D printing fabrication. A unique cylindrical cell geometry is used to allow printing via Fused Deposition Modeling method and thus in a space qualified material. The lens is 3D printed and measured for pattern performance. The measured results agree well with simulations.

articleTitle: One Dual-Polarization 10-40 GHz Planar Array Antenna For Sattellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An ultra-wideband dual-polarization planar array antenna with the operational bandwidth from 10 to 40GHz has been proposed in this paper for satellite communications. In order to eliminate the external wideband baluns and complex feed organizers, this antenna is feeding by the unbalanced feed structures for easily fabrication and overcome the electrical and manufacturing limitations above Ku band. The performance of the proposal antenna is good with the active VSWR below 2.45 covers from 10.34 to 39.61 GHz while scanning to 45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>, and the radiation pattern is stable during all-planes scanning. The total thickness is less than 0.5 wavelengths at the highest operation frequency.

articleTitle: Dual-Band and Dual-Polarized Reconfigurable Beam-Steering Array for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band and dual-polarized reconfigurable beam-steering array is presented. The proposed antenna array consists of eight directional dual-band (2.38-2.52 GHz and 5.2-5.9GHz) dual-polarized (+45°/-45°) one-port elements. The polarization state of these antennas can be changed through PIN diodes. When different ports are excited, a beam switchable array with the characteristic of 360° pattern coverage in azimuth can be achieved. The simulation results show that the proposed array has an acceptable front-to-back ratio (above 15dB) and a high port to port isolation (above 25 dB) in the whole working band. The above-mentioned advantages with respect to the array indicate that the array is suitable for WLAN applications.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Pattern-Reconfigurable Antenna for modern wireless sensor network applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The implementation of a reconfigurable antenna capable of rotating a unidirectional pattern by 360° in the azimuth plane is proposed. The antenna uses the Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) screen with aperture switching components to offers more compact solutions than array. Indeed, the transmission/reflection responses of each planar FSS are carefully delineated to elaborately reshape the screens to a cylindrical form. Then, by precisely controlling the active elements integrated into the cylindrical FSS, the dipole’s pattern at the center of the cylinder is controlled to achieve the desired functionality. Validation for Adaptive Pattern-Reconfigurable Antenna is achieved by comparing the simulated and measured radiation patterns parameters. The measured half-power beam width is 72° while 40° for the simulated. The measured gain is around 10 dBi while the simulated realized gain is around 15.1 dB. The antenna is intended to operate with software define radio in the wireless sensor network at the frequency range of 2.45GHz and offering multiusers pattern reconfiguration within a limited volume at low cost.

articleTitle: Oblique Incidence PML Reflection Analysis for Cylindrical FDTD
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The main objective of this presentation is to apply discrete FDTD theory to the stretched-coordinates PML for cylindrical FDTD and derive the overall numerical reflection coefficient off the PML region with obliquely incident cylindrical waves. Obtained predictive equations avoid the need for actual FDTD experiments which are problematic when the PML layers are within a wavelength from the axis of rotation. Presented work will aid in predicting near-field cylindrical FDTD PML efficiency in applications such as borehole EM analysis.

articleTitle: A Flat Luneberg Lens Antenna for Wide-Angle Beam Scanning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact multi-beam flat Luneberg lens antenna operating at Ka-band is proposed and designed. The lens antenna consists of six dielectric layers and two parallel plates. A linear antenna array with 11 E-shaped patch antenna elements is employed to feed the lens antenna. The aperture size of the lens is 80×5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, while the lens antenna has narrow beams in the azimuth plane and wide beams in the elevation plane, respectively. Thanks to the usage of the transformation optics, the focus-to-diameter (F/D) of the proposed flat lens antenna is small as only 0.375. Simulated results show that the antenna has wide-scanning ability (up to ±60° in the azimuth plane) and high aperture efficiency (over 60% at the axis direction).

articleTitle: 4×4 MIMO Antenna Elements Fed by Microstrip Ridge Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A high gain wideband to cover 57-71 GHz antenna array using microstrip ridge gap waveguide (MRGW) is presented for indoor application. Then a 4×4 MIMO antenna with orthogonal channels is proposed. Each element in the 4×4 is represented by a 2×2 subarray. The performance of the system is evaluated by calculating the correlation coefficient.

articleTitle: Wideband, Wide Angle Radome Design for mm-Wave Automotive Radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a radome design that exhibits higher transmission over a wider field of view for millimeter-wave automotive radars . The radome consists of periodic arrangements of unit cell that are etched into a dielectric slab with notches in the form of inverted square pyramids from both sides. To improve field of view coverage, the depths of the pyramidal exclusions have been gradually decreased as we go away from the array center. The design was 3D printed and tested to demonstrate the improved performance.

articleTitle: Higher Order Plasma-Based Tunable Absorber Using Magneto-Dielectric Substrates
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a multilayer absorber based on the technique previously developed for the design of a thickness customizable high-order bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS). Lossy substrates are used to absorb the electromagnetic energy in the FSS backed by a ground plane. Such technique allows simple integration of the tuning elements, while simultaneously providing the design option to realize the absorber with specific/desired thicknesses. The lossy substrates are perforated to host discrete electrically tunable ceramic gas-encapsulating chambers (plasma-shells). These plasma-shells enable dynamic control of the absorption spectral band. To demonstrate the design flexibility and performance, a second order frequency selective absorber operating at the C-band (center frequency at f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> = 6 GHz with 17% fractional bandwidth) is designed with different thickness configurations. Then the plasma-shells are strategically integrated in the design in order to control the location of both absorption resonant frequencies by applying different plasma frequencies. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations are carried out to validate the proposed concepts.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Triple-Resonance Substrate Integrated Waveguide Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna With Cavity Resonator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A triple-resonance substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-backed slot antenna using two cavity resonators is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna consists of a radiation area and a cavity resonator area. In order to generate triple resonance, two cavity resonators are designed in the cavity resonator area. The working mechanism of the proposed antenna is explained with its electric field distributions.

articleTitle: High-Frequency CubeSat Platform Scattering Using Higher-Order Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a 10 cm offset reflector antenna mounted inside a 6U CubeSat platform and analyze the bare reflector and three reflector + CubeSat platform configurations in W band (86 GHz), where the CubeSat platform is electrically large. Using higher-order MoM/MLFMM techniques, we obtain accurate antenna patterns and quantify the significant impact that any of the CubeSat platforms in this case have on the antenna pattern. In addition, our study demonstrates that details of the CubeSat platform impact the patterns to a lot smaller extent.

articleTitle: Low-Profile, Vehicle Roof-Top Mounted Broadband Antenna for V2X
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a monocone roof-top broadband antenna for V2X (Vehicle to Everything) wireless communication. The proposed antenna consists of four elements - monocone, ground ring, center post, and parasitic disk. The antenna performance is characterized with respect to reflection coefficient and radiation pattern. The simulated and measured data indicate that the proposed antenna can support 0.7 GHz to 6 GHz. Radiation patterns show omnidirectional and high-gain characteristics on the horizontal plane. The simulated magnitude of reflection coefficient is similar to that of the measured data.

articleTitle: Folding-Dependent vs. Folding-Independent Flexible Antennas on E-Textiles
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper explores folding effects upon two classes of antenna designs that exhibit folding-dependent and folding-independent electromagnetic (EM) performance, respectively. Specifically, Finite Element simulations are used to model: a) a monopole antenna that attains multi-band operation with ~44.5% shift in resonance frequency for a 60° fold, and b) a microstrip antenna that maintains a minimal resonance frequency shift of ~3.5% for a 60° fold. These designs bring forward unique opportunities for antennas that reconfigure their EM performance vs. antennas that maintain their EM performance despite changes in their constituent geometry. Notably, flexible and robust prototypes can be embroidered on e-textiles.

articleTitle: A Bandwidth Reconfigurable Multiband Fractal Antenna For Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a CPW crescent-shaped reconfigurable antenna using fractal geometry is proposed and studied. Six pin diodes are used on the surface of the crescent-shape radiating patch iterated to the third order to create frequency reconfigurability. The antenna covers most of the existing wireless and mobile frequency band allocations from 1.52 GHz to 10.95 GHz, with relative impedance bandwidths of around 2.7 and 26.61%. The overall dimension of the proposed antenna is 25×31×1.524 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The proposed antenna is a good candidate for multiband applications due to its advantages of compactness, simple structure, low cost, and ease of fabrication.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles: A Characteristic Mode Analysis Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A simple Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) model is developed to computationally and experimentally quantify its electromagnetic scattering characteristics and its susceptibility to interference. Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA) is evoked to calculate the fundamental modes of the structure. The properties of these calculated modes will allow the prediction of the response of the UAV to various interfering waveforms. Innovative experimental measurements are performed to directly measure the coupled current to the UAV and validate the CMA predictions. The analysis and measurements presented in this work provide the first direct experimental validation of modal behavior and the novel application of CMA to study interference to UAVs and similar systems.

articleTitle: Differentially Fed CDRA Array with Phase Inverter for High Gain and Reduced Cross Polarization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a compact novel 2×2 CDRA array with high gain and reduced cross polarization. By feeding the array elements differentially, the reduction of cross polarization and the enhancement of gain are achieved. The feeding network employs an on-board 180° phase inverter as a balun for differential feeding of array elements. The simulated results show that the proposed array achieves -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 5.78-5.9 GHz with a broadside radiation pattern having a peak realized gain of 11.07 dBi at 5.84 GHz. The cross-polarization levels in the boresight direction are -30.65 dB and -29.5 dB in YZ and XZ plane, respectively at 5.84 GHz. The proposed CDRA array is compact, making it suitable for portable devices.

articleTitle: 4×4 Broadband Butler Matrix and Its Application in Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces the design method of broadband 4×4 Butler matrix feeding network and applies it to broadband antenna array to realize broadband multi-beam antenna. The proposed Butler matrix switches to different forms of Butler matrices when operating in different frequency ranges to achieve broadband performance.
