The broadband 4×4 Butler matrix consists of three kinds of directional couplers: a conventional 3dB directional coupler, a broadband 3dB/90° directional coupler, and a three-section directional coupler. The antenna array is designed by stacking antenna patch and coupling between antennas. The Butler matrix feeding network and patch antenna array designed in this paper operate from 2 to 4 GHz. Four beams are obtained in one frequency octave operating frequency range (2 GHz-4 GHz), and the simulation result achieves the desired result.

articleTitle: Time-Varying Phase Control for Frequency Translation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Frequency conversion is typically achieved by mixing a signal with a local oscillator. However, mixing typically generates an image frequency, in addition to other unwanted harmonics. Here, we achieve X-band frequency translation without image frequency suppression using a device capable of 360° phase modulation. The device is realized in microstrip technology, and varactor diodes are used for phase control in a serrodyne translator topology. The design could be used as a building block for the development of nonreciprocal devices such as isolators and circulators.

articleTitle: Near-field Electrically Small Sensors Array with PCA for Microwave Breast Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we propose the use of an electrically small dipole antenna arrays as a microwave sensor combined with a classification algorithm for near field microwave breast tumor detection. The proposed sensor has high sensitive to detect any changes or abnormality in the dielectric properties of the breast tissues. Detecting the existence of the breast tumors are expected by estimating the variations in the response of the reflection coefficient of the sensor. The Principle Component Analysis (PCA) feature extraction technique is applied to accentuate the variance in the sensor responses for both healthy and tumourous cases. We show that when a numerical realistic breast with and without tumor cells is placed in the near field of the sensor, the sensor is capable of detection tumorous with various sizes placed in single locations at two different stand off 5 mm and 10 mm respectively.

articleTitle: Frequency and Polarization Agile RFID Patch Antenna with Reduced Dimensions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a frequency and polarization reconfigurable UHF RFID patch antenna based on a switchable feeding network. For best integration of the antenna, its size and ground plane are much smaller with respect to the canonical patch antenna design, however the proposed design is able to cover the EU and US frequency bands of the RFID standard. State-of-the-art CMOS switches are employed as key element for selecting the desired polarization and proper matching network. The switches provide also a simple solution for high power applications in contrast to concepts based on PIN diodes or varactors. Simulated results have shown good performance. Considering its flexible and inexpensive structure, the proposed system is a promising alternative to aperture tuning and circular polarized antenna approaches.

articleTitle: Dual-band Phased Array Antenna on Metal for mmWave Mobile Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The demand for faster mobile data traffic has become stronger than ever, and multiple bandwidth antennas architecture at millimeter wave (mm-wave) is considered to be one of the critical breakthrough technologies in the upcoming era of the 5G technology, although plenty of room for improvement still remains. In this paper, a folded "dual-slot" phased array antenna on a metal frame for portable mobile device which can operate at mm-wave of 28 GHz and 39 GHz simultaneously is proposed. The proposed array antenna consists of 4 × 2 folded slot antennas placed at the edge of the metal frame. The measured -10 dB bandwidth is 1.3 GHz (27.2 GHz - 28.5 GHz, gain of 11.3 dBi at 28 GHz) and 6.8 GHz (34.7 GHz - 41.5 GHz, gain of 12.4 dBi at 39 GHz), respectively. Our computational simulations and prototypical measurements demonstrate that the proposed "dual-slot" architecture is an efficient method to optimize the antenna performance of currently available metal body mobile devices.

articleTitle: Fast and Accurate Near-Field to Far-Field Transformation Using an Adaptive Sampling Algorithm and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new approach to enhance the speed and accuracy of the antenna near-field measurements and near-field to far-field (NF-FF) transformation is proposed. First, a uniform measurement is performed using an electronically switched probe array. Then an adaptive algorithm is developed that starts with a small number of samples and gradually focuses on the areas with highly dynamic near-field pattern and increases the number of samples over such regions. Thus, the number of required samples for an accurate result decreases significantly, and consequently the speed of the back projection algorithm increases.

articleTitle: Anisotropic Slab Scattering: A High Frequency Solution
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a heuristic uniform theory of diffraction (UTD) corner and wedge diffraction coefficient for predicting electromagnetic scattering by a thin lossless anisotropic slab is presented. An approach based on modifying UTD corner and wedge diffraction formulations for a half-plane with the reflection and transmission coefficients of an anisotropic media is proposed. Numerical results for various scattering problems showing excellent agreement with reference solutions are provided.

articleTitle: Signal Enhancement for Ferromagnetic Resonance Measurement of Magnetic Nanowire array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) measurement technique to enhance signal detection of magnetic nanowire in array form (MNA) is presented. Two signal enhancement methods were developed for characterizing the MNA sample. The samples were placed on top of a coplanar waveguide (CPW) test circuit and exposed to both AC and DC magnetic fields. The first method indicates that FMR response is stronger for MNA on the slots due to stronger AC field around slots. The second method indicates that the FMR response of MNA with a copper (Cu) back layer is seven times stronger. Thus, to enhance the signal strength of FMR response, the MNA sample should be placed on the slot and/or include a Cu back layer. These methods are useful for identification methods, such as nanolabels used in biosensing applications that use small volume and size samples.

articleTitle: A Thick Origami Four-Patch Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a thick-origami based on a four patch antenna array with a packing efficiency of 50%. The antenna array is differentially fed using the origami structure and creating a symmetric radiation pattern. The array is designed on low-cost FR4 substrate having a thickness of 1.5 mm and an overall dimension of 290 mm × 100 mm. The peak gain is approximately 8.2 dB, at broadside. The ability of the array to compress its size and its fabrication simplicity makes it a very good candidate for applications where space savings are critical.

articleTitle: Channel Characterization and Simulation for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) have been widely applied not only in military but also for public applications in recent years. Wireless communication should be considered as a key technology to guarantee the control and operations of UAVs. The blockage of UAV, the changing flight attitude and the obstacles around the propagation environment result in the complexity of analyzing the channel. Hence, the knowledge of the channel characteristics for UAV is crucial for designing and evaluating the communication technology. In this paper, channel characteristics between UAVs are investigated through Ray-tracing simulation (RT). The considered center frequency is 2.2 GHz and the bandwidth is 20 MHz. The proposed environment is urban environment and the digital map of Xi'an city is used. The UAV models in this work is assumed as unmanned gyroplane and fixed-wing UAV. The path loss (PL) is modeled via CI model in this paper. The shadow fading (SF) and path loss exponents (PLE) of LOS and NLOS cases are provided and compared.

articleTitle: Effect of temperature sensor location and measurement time on Evaluation of the Calibration Factor of the Lead Electromagnetic Model
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: For a helix coax lead at 128 MHz using a set of incident electric fields (E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">tan</sub>) with different profiles we numerically investigate the influence of the temperature sensor location on the evaluation of the calibration factor of the lead electromagnetic model. A shift of the sensor from the electrode tip to the electrode pedestal resulted in a decrease of the linear regression model coefficient from 0.99 to 0.5.

articleTitle: Highly Accurate Liquid Permittivity Measurement using Coaxial Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel complex permittivity measurement system for low-loss and lossy liquids based on the use of multiple frequencies. The system includes a designed coaxial structure that contains the liquid under test and a reconstruction algorithm. Fabrication results show the validity of the method with a higher accuracy level compared to the commonly used open-ended coaxial technique, which makes the proposed method an attractive candidate for highly precise and cheap liquid permittivity identification.

articleTitle: Modeling of Sub-Millimeter Wave Coplanar Waveguide Graphene Switches
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a theoretical study on the performance of graphene-loaded coplanar waveguide switches for 5G and beyond applications. Therefore, we exploit the tunable properties of graphene to device cost-effective, large-scale, broadband sub-millimeter-wave switches. Given the sheet impedance of biased and unbiased graphene monolayers, the model provides the optimum switching ratio with respect to insertion loss, characteristic impedance of transmission line, and graphene geometry. Using measured graphene sheet resistance, we compute the optimum switching performance for series and shunt single- pole-single-though sub-millimeter-wave (220-330 GHz) switches.

articleTitle: X-Band Archimedean Spiral Antenna Array with Sloped-Wall Backing Cavity
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An Archimedean Spiral Antenna Array with Sloped-Wall Backing Cavity was designed to achieve the broad bandwidth with high gain, circular polarization, and low-profile configuration for X-band (8-12 GHz) Deep Space communications for CubeSats. The designed 2 by 2 array showed good impedance matching and a low axial ratio (<; 3 dB) from 8 to 12 GHz. The addition of the slope-wall backing cavity increases the realized gain of the Archimedean Spiral Antenna by greater than 3.2 dBiC across the frequency band without the drop in gain experienced by conventional cavities. The designed array fits on the 1U (100 x 100 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) face of the CubeSat.

articleTitle: Analysis of multistatic vehicle-drone Ground Penetrating Radar configurations for mine detection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, a novel Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) configuration to detect low-contrast buried targets is presented. It is based on combining the advantages of Forward-Looking GPR (FLGPR) and Down-Looking GPR (DLGPR) using a distributed GPR system, with a vehicle-mounted transmitter looking ahead and a drone-mounted receiver looking downwards. This configuration provides good penetration and high resolution, reducing the clutter compared to DLGPR. Several simulations have been performed and the resulting Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images have been compared.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual Polarized Tunable Frequency Selective Surface With Varactors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel dual polarized varactor-tuned frequency selective surface with embedded bias-network is presented. The proposed FSS is composed of a dielectric slab and a metallic layer. Symmetric meandered square loop geometry is chosen as an FSS geometry in order to achieve miniaturization and insensitivity for polarization. Tuning is realized by loading four varactor diodes around the meandered loop slot. Analyzes of the FSS are carried out in CST. The simulation results shown that the resonant frequency can be adjusted from 3.8 GHz to 5.76 GHz by changing the loaded varactors.

articleTitle: Ringing Effects Due to Non-ideal Components in Direct Antenna Modulation Transmitters
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Direct antenna modulation (DAM) is a method used to transmit broadband signals through a narrowband antenna by switching the antenna or matching network at precise moments during the carrier cycle. In this paper, we study the effects of parasitics in the antenna and matching network and their effects on the DAM system. We demonstrate that parasitics introduce significant ringing after the switching instant that degrades the ability of DAM to store energy and effectively transmit broadband signals in practice. The parasitic effect is predicted by circuit model simulation and is validated with measurements with an equivalent antenna circuit model.

articleTitle: RCS Enhancement Using Topology Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Radar cross section (RCS) reduction has been a topic of interest for a long time; on the other hand, RCS enhancement has gained significant interest recently in the automotive industry to improve road safety. This paper introduces an efficient way to improve/enhance the RCS of an object using topology optimization. A planar metal sheet is used as an example to demonstrate the concept. Global response surface method (GRSM) for double objectives topology optimization is used. Numerical results show a promising use of topology optimization for RCS enhancement. The optimized structure shows around 10 dB improvement of the RCS.

articleTitle: 3D-printable Perforated Dielectric Reflectarray in Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, some preliminary results on a 3D-printable dielectric Reflectarray antenna are presented. The unit-cell consists of a single-layer dielectric element perforated with a square hole, whose side is used to control the phase response. It has been adopted to design a 32×32 offset Reflectarray working in Ka-band. The antenna shown a maximum gain of 24.8 dB at 30 GHz and good radiation performances. Moreover, the Reflectarray can be easily printed using Additive Manufacturing techniques.

articleTitle: Online Diagnostic Ultra-Wideband Antenna System in High Voltage Polymeric Insulator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna system is proposed for fault inspection and online diagnoses on high voltage polymeric insulators. This technique makes use of the multimode transferring theory on dielectric waveguides, where the transmission signal level difference can be employed to detect internal defects in the core rod. An investigation by simulation is performed with regard to the interfacial mm-ordered cracks in transverse and longitudinal orientations, and roughly 30~50 dB and 20~40 dB differences have been observed over the same band 3~10 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Lossy Antenna Arrays with Frequency-Independent Beamwidth
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna feeds for lens and reflector systems require uniform and customizable beamwidths. Here, an antenna array fed with a resistively loaded a transmission line network is considered. Theoretical calculations show that it is possible for the array to radiate a Gaussian beam with frequency-independent far field over an arbitrary bandwidth. A prototype array fed with resistively loaded microstrip lines is then designed. The 16x16 Vivaldi element array radiates a Gaussian beam with a 35° 10 dB full beamwidth and 20 dB directivity from 6.5 GHz to 19 GHz. The design flexibility does come at the expense of a low radiation efficiency though, which is 1%. Therefore, the architecture is intended for test and measurement applications where beam purity and wide bandwidth are of utmost importance, while low radiation efficiency can be tolerated.

articleTitle: 28 GHz Side-Edge Loop Antenna with End-Fire Radiation Polarized Vertically to Substrate
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact and simple side-edge loop antenna structure with the end-fire radiation polarized vertically to a substrate is proposed as an antenna element for phased array antennas. The single and the 4-element array antenna fabricated in the 1.8mm thickness substrate are demonstrated by showing the measured 28GHz characteristics in comparison with the calculated values.

articleTitle: An Ultrathin Flexible Metasurface for Half Mirror and QWP Operation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel metasurface with half-mirror (1:1 beam-splitter) and quarter-wave plate operation is being presented in this paper. The design consists of a square-shaped slot resonator with a slit and a split ring resonator inside it. The proposed metasurface exhibits simultaneous half-mirror and quarter-wave plate (QWP) operation over two broad frequency bands between 7.025-7.385 and 19.1-20.33 GHz, while only half-mirror operation is achieved over other two frequency bands centered at 14.6-16 and 27.7-29 GHz.

articleTitle: Broadband Array Antennas For Curved Geometries
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Employing a Generalized theoretical broadbanding algorithm developed for curved surfaces, this paper utilizes new improved radiator models to develop, test and assess broadband Conformal open-Waveguide arrays realized on Curved Surfaces.

articleTitle: Wideband Omnidirectional Circularly Polarized Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Applications Using Printed Artificial Anisotropic Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband omnidirectional circularly polarized (CP) antenna using printed artificial anisotropic polarizer is presented for millimeter-wave applications. The spherical linearly polarized (LP) wavefront radiated from a bicone is regulated into cylindrical wavefront by a rounding hyperbolic lens before entering the conformal CP polarizer. The polarizer is made of 3D printed artificial anisotropic material with curved laminates being configured 45 degrees to the incident electric field. Measurement results show that the antenna has a wide operating bandwidth of 34.5% from 24 to 32 GHz, which completely convers potential 5G frequency bands at 28-GHz millimeter-wave range.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Beam-Switching Antenna Using Square Active Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-band beam-switching antenna using active square frequency selective surfaces (ASFSS) is presented. The proposed design consists of a dual-band monopole antenna as a source of electromagnetic waves (EM Waves), and two ASFSS. The ASFSS are used to convert the omnidirectional radiation pattern of the source into a directional one, forming a reconfigurable radiation pattern antenna. By applying different combinations of pin-diodes, a beam steering with 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> angular beamwidth has been achieved at 2.45 GHz and 5.8GHz.

articleTitle: Propagation Modeling for Air-Ground Channel over Rough Sea Surface in Low Altitudes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel multipath propagation model is presented for air-ground (AG) channel over sea surface whose roughness is determined by different wind speeds. The path loss is deduced and verified using the measurement data. The results show that our model is applicable to describe the multipath behavior and is generic for the design and optimization of low-altitude wireless communications over the sea environment.

articleTitle: Band Structures and Modal Fields in Topological Acoustics: An Integral Equation Formulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Topological states in photonics were initially proposed by Haldane in analogy to the quantum Hall (QH) effect in electronic system. Topological acoustics has also been demonstrated recently. In this paper, an integral formulation is developed to study the band structure and the band modal field distribution within a phononic crystal that supports acoustic topological edge states through rotations of the ambient fluid. The governing acoustic wave equation includes a vector potential term that originates from the rotation and lifts the degeneracy at the Dirac points and induces topological wave phenomena. This wave equation resembles that governs the wave function of a nonrelativistic particle in a periodic vector potential and can be mapped to a QH system. We have converted this modified inhomogeneous Helmholtz equation into a volume/surface integral equation using the periodic lattice Green's function of the stationary ambient fluid. We represent the lattice Green's function using a novel hybrid representation that includes fast converging spatial series evaluated at a given imaginary wavenumber and a fast converging spectral series in terms of Floquet plane waves that is suitable for broadband evaluations. The volume integral equation is solved using the method of moments and converted into a nonlinear eigenvalue problem. We illustrate solutions of this eigenvalue problem that represent band diagrams and band modal field distributions of the phononic crystal that vary with the magnitude and direction of the ambient fluid rotation. Topologically protected eigenmodes are revealed at K point in the Brillouin zone.

articleTitle: Design of a Miniature Reactive Beam Forming Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper outlines the design and testing of a new highly optimized reactive beam forming network. The optimization technique produces beam forming networks that are smaller than traditional printed circuit lenses has more sidelobe and beam control than a Butler Matrix based lens.

articleTitle: Two-Port, Common Aperture, High-Isolation, Dual-Polarized Sub-Millimeterwave Antenna System Based on Spatial Power Divider
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A two-port antenna system is proposed that uses a polarization-independent spatial power divider to align the beams from two orthogonally oriented dual-polarized feeds. Such an antenna system will provide a common aperture for transmit and receive, and high port isolation, while minimizing radar parallax and maintaining compatibility with fully polarimetric radar. The spatial power divider is designed using an all-dielectric metasurface approach, and is fabricated on a silicon wafer using the standard micromachining technology. The simulated device exhibits at most 0.1 dB of difference between reflection and transmission for both TE and TM incident waves at 45-degree incidence, over a band from 227 GHz to 239 GHz.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STAR): Circulators Versus Nonreciprocal Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Desired antenna and front-end for simultaneous transmit and receive systems in addition to nonlinear and/or time variant nonreciprocal antennas are reviewed. The STAR system requirements in terms of antennas and front-end are investigated. Then, the properties of some proposed techniques for nonreciprocal antennas and circulator-based systems are investigated.

articleTitle: Efficient and accurate electromagnetic scattering analysis of perfectly conducting thick plates
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The scattering analysis with the Electric-Field Integral Equation by the Method of Moments of perfectly conducting plates is normally carried out through the thin-plate approximation, which models the closed surface as an open surface and discards the influence of the plate rim. The resulting accuracy is accepted in many practical applications as long as the thickness of the plate is small enough. However, in the scattering analysis of plates with grazing incidences, the thin-plate approximation gives rise to severe inaccuracies. In this paper, we present a new numerical approach, which we name thick-plate formulation, for the accurate computation of the current and the RCS for a plate with nonzero thickness. Our scheme provides similar accuracy as the solution obtained with the full modelling of the plate and with less computational time.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Compressive Processing for Inverse Scattering within the Contrast Source Formulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an effective microwave imaging method based on the Compressive Processing (CP) paradigm combined with an Iterative Multi-Scaling (IMS) approach within the contrast source formulation is presented. For each step of the IMS procedure, a customized relevance vector machine (RVM) is employed to retrieve the unknowns contrast source coefficients of a suitable sparsification basis and driven to search for the solution within a restricted domain defined according to the information progressively acquired on the scatterer features.

articleTitle: A Simple Technique for EBG Design for Monopole Antenna Isolation Improvement
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The stopband frequencies of a single column mushroom EBG structure between two vertical wire monopole antennas were determined using HFSS, an existing model and a proposed new model. The results show that the stop band frequencies calculated using the proposed new model is more accurate compared to those obtained from the existing model especially for larger patch width to height ratios (w/h>2.1).

articleTitle: Low-Profile Electronically Tunable Low-Loss Single Layer Reflectarray Element
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new design of a single-layer low-profile, and low-loss reconfigurable reflectarray (RA) element is presented in the X-Band. The design consists of multiple smaller sized patches connected in a square ring. The element is a square of length 10mm (0.33λ at 10 GHz). A surface mount varactor diode is attached in the ring. A biasing line is also considered to isolate the RF signal from DC. The proposed element provides amplitude losses under -1.5 dB for applied voltages varying from 0 to 15 volts. A phase tuning range of 290° is achieved from a single varactor diode @ 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Rapidly Deployable Portable System for Real-Time Antenna Diagnostics and Characterization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a portable system, based on off-the-shelf components, to perform in-situ fast antenna diagnostics and characterization is presented. In order to perform the antenna evaluation, the operator holds a probe antenna, which is moved in front of the antenna under test (AUT) to acquire the near-field (NF) on an arbitrary surface. During the NF acquisition, an equivalent currents distribution on the aperture of the AUT is continuously reconstructed based on the available samples. Moreover, the far-field (FF) radiation pattern is also computed. In addition to the probe, the system comprises a commercial real-time position tracking system capable of providing the Cartesian coordinates and the rotation angles of the probe, which can be deployed and calibrated in a few minutes. The NF acquisition is accomplished by means of a vector network analyzer (VNA). The obtained results of a test characterizing a horn antenna are discussed, showing good performance.

articleTitle: Accelerated Antenna Optimization Using Gradient Search with Selective Broyden Updates
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The paper addresses design optimization of antennas using accelerated gradient-based search. In our approach, finite differentiation conventionally used to estimate the antenna response Jacobian is replaced, for selected variables, by rank-one Broyden updates. Variable selection depends on the alignment between direction of the recent design relocation and the coordinate system axes. Comprehensive numerical validation indicates significant computational savings that can be achieved without compromising the design quality.

articleTitle: GPR Bowtie Antennas with Reduced Induction Footprints for Dual-Modality Detectors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Dual-modality detector systems often require ground-penetrating radar antennas to be placed in close proximity to electro-magnetic induction (EMI) sensors. Traditional bowtie antennas have large copper areas in which eddy-currents can flow, leading to a big response from the EMI sensor. New antenna designs, based on removing specific copper areas to reduce the area of the eddy-currents, are introduced and evaluated here. It was found that the magnitude of the response from the EMI sensor can be reduced by over 91% without substantially altering the time-domain signal transmitted by the antennas.

articleTitle: Towards Decreasing Side Lobes Produced by Near-Field Phase Gradient Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: When steering or tilting the beam of a planar high-gain antenna using a near-field phase gradient metasurface, undesirable side lobes are often noted. These side lobes can be predicted reasonably well by exciting the metasurface with a normally incident uniform plane wave but direct optimisation of such an electrically large metasurface to reduce strongest undesirable side lobes is computationally very expensive. Here we have applied a more efficient approach to reduce the levels of all side lobes below -20 dB.

articleTitle: On the design of metamaterial radar absorber applying AMC by controlling surface resistance
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel methodology for designing and applying artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) through controlling pattern's surface impedance instead of shape is proposed and analyzed. A wideband metamaterial radar absorber applying this methodology is designed and verified numerically. Simulation results indicate this methodology can be used to widen absorption bandwidth for metamaterial radar absorbers.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel Triple Band Antenna for WLAN Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized triple band antenna is proposed. The antenna is simulated by high-frequency structure simulator (HFSS) software. It is designed on a FR4 substrate whose size is 35 mm × 21 mm × 1.5 mm. This triple band antenna is composed of a rectangular ring, a concave ring and a rectangular branch. By adjusting their shapes and sizes, three working frequency bands can be obtained. The antenna operates at 2.4 GHz, 3.5 GHz and 5.8 GHz and it is suitable for wireless local area network (WLAN) applications, World Interoperability for Microwave Access (WIMAX) applications and Bluetooth services.

articleTitle: Four Year Cloud Attenuation Study in a Tropical Station
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The paper present four year results of Cloud attenuation measurements carried out at Covenant University, Ota, Nigeria. The links operate at frequency of 12.245 GHz and the cumulative distribution function for monthly Cloud attenuation have been estimated from the 4-year measured spectrum analyser data. The result of the visually measured Cloud and Satellite Cloud cover data are presented. The monthly variability shows that the highest cloud attenuation at the station occur in August, reaching a maximum of 3.96 dB for 0.01% of time; which corresponding to an average cloud cover of 89.86% and 75.36% by ground and satellite data respectively of which Nimbostratus (Ns) is average of 29.1%. The lowest cloud attenuation at the station occur in September, with a value of 2.5 dB for 0.01% of time; corresponding to an average cloud cover of 90.3% and 77.26% by ground and satellite data respectively, of which Nimbostratus (Ns) is average of 28.9%.

articleTitle: Effect of Antenna Array Element Separation on Capacity of MIMO Systems Including Mutual Coupling
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we study the effect of element separation in a base station array (BSA) on the downlink line-of-sight achievable sum-rate of MIMO systems in the presence of mutual coupling at the BSA. The channel matrix H is modeled using the embedded field patterns of the BSA and is used to analyze the outage performance for two single-element user equipments assuming no inter-user coupling.

articleTitle: A Shared-Aperture Broadband Circularly Polarized Antenna for Satellite Communications and Navigation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A shared-aperture broadband circularly polarized antenna for satellite communications and navigation is presented in this paper. This developed antenna deploys a 2×2 crossed- dipole antenna array and a 4×4 microstrip antenna phased array sharing a common aperture. With this compact scheme, the high aperture reuse efficiency can be achieved. The 2×2 crossed-dipole antenna array is designed to cover B1~B3 bands of Beidou satellite navigation system (BDS) while the 4×4 microstrip antenna phased array is designed to operate in S-band for satellite communications. The broadband phase-shift network with dual-probe feeding and four-probe feeding are employed to broaden the circularly polarized band respectively. The simulated results show that the relative operating bandwidth of the presented antenna is 34.5% in L-band and 38.1% in S-band.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Polarized Dual-Band Unit-Cell for Wideband FSS in Ku Band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-polarized frequency selective surface (FSS), designed in Ku and K bands which can be used as passband multilayer spatial filter. This design consists of double-sided unit-cells comprising a cross-dipole and a stubbed square loop, arranged in a square lattice. The three-layer broadband (35% to 45%) dual-polarized FSS is realized using this unit-cell with low transmission coefficient (better than -0.2 dB) and excellent ripple-free bandpass which corresponds to Butterworth filter response. Full-wave analysis demonstrated a dual-polarized, dual-band capability with an independent stable frequency response control in the aforementioned band in x- and y-polarizations, making it a good candidate for broadband dual-polarized microwave and optic applications.

articleTitle: Eight-element MIMO Antenna with Tightly-arranged Pairs for 5G Mobile Terminal
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact eight-element MIMO antenna is presented for 5G mobile terminal applications. The proposed antenna structure consists of four blocks, and each block has two tightly arranged inverted F antennas (IFAs). The edge-to-edge distance between the two IFAs is only 1 mm. Inductor is used to improve the port isolation in each block. The size of the block is 27.4 mm × 4.5 mm. There is no ground clearance between the antenna and the platform. The simulated results show that the bandwidth of the proposed MIMO antenna is 260 MHz, which is sufficient for the 3400-3600 MHz band.

articleTitle: The Huygens’ Box Antenna: Metasurface-Based Directive Antenna Beam-Steering with Dramatically Reduced Elements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate the Huygens' box antenna. We show that we can synthesize waves in a region enclosed by an active metasurface, and that by allowing the wave synthesized in such a cavity to leak out through an aperture a highly directive antenna can be formed. We present simulation results and compare these results to those obtainable from a microstrip patch array of the same aperture size as our Huygens' box antenna. We show that similar radiation patterns can be achieved in both cases, but with the Huygens' box antenna we are able to significantly reduce the number of sources required, which also dramatically reduce the complexity and component cost for the antenna array. We envision the Huygens' box antenna will be a great cost-saving alternative to microstrip patch arrays for mm-wave regime.

articleTitle: A Broadside Three-Port Antenna for 5G Massive MIMO Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a broadside antenna with three ports operating at the same frequency. The TM030 and TM003 modes of a patch are excited by two coaxial cables to generate two orthogonal linear polarizations. The patch can be transformed into a slotted SIW cavity whose TE201 and TE102 modes are jointly excited by the third cable. A matching cavity and a matching patch are introduced to broaden the impedance bandwidth of the third port. The simulated results show that the isolations between these three ports are higher than 18 dB, even though the radiation patterns of the three ports are all broadside. The proposed three-port antenna can provide a solution to increase the number of the ports per unit area in outdoor massive MIMO antennas.

articleTitle: An Efficient FB-based Underground Channel Estimation for MIMO Mm-Wave Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel algorithm based on the concept of Forward-Backward (FB) compressing sensing principle for underground mm-wave channel estimation. The efficiency of FB approach is successfully verified in the context of MIMO orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) system. To reach that, the approach relies on the channel support forward selection and backward removal, which iteratively expands and compresses the support estimate, hence improving the ability to cover up for the errors made in the conventional orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm. The superiority of the FB-based channel algorithm in reconstructing the original sparse channel, over the OMP alternative, is highlighted by evaluating the estimation accuracy, when applied on underground mm-Wave channel measurements.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Differentially-Fed Multi-Band Dual-Polarized Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Two differentially-fed multi-band dual-polarized antennas backed by substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavities are proposed. One is a dual-band antenna and the other is a tri-band antenna. Both antennas consist of a symmetric radiating slot and a SIW cavity. The radiating slot for each SIW cavity-backed antenna is differentially driven by two orthogonally crossed microstrip feedlines. The dual-band antenna covers the frequency bands of 2.4-2.5 GHz and 4.97-5.96 GHz for differential reflection coefficient <; -10 dB with an isolation better than 40 dB. The tri-band antenna achieves 10-dB differential impedance bandwidths for 2.4-2.49 GHz, 3.29-3.6 GHz and 4.8-5.05 GHz with isolation better than 30 dB. Both antennas has a low profile of lower than 0.054λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.4GHz</sub> (where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.4GHz</sub> is the free-space wavelength at 2.4 GHz), suitable for WiFi and 5G mobile communication systems.

articleTitle: Compact Microstrip Patch Antenna Utilizing Low Cost Solution Cast Nanomagnetic Thin Film
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact integrated microstrip patch antenna with low cost magnetic nanoparticle thin film loaded in the air substrate has been designed, fabricated and characterized. First, a microstrip patch antenna patterned on a thin Liquid Crystal Polymer was mounted on a partially 3D printed air substrate through a lego-like process to have the measured resonance at 8.3 GHz and 6.5 dBi of realized gain. To achieve the compactness, MnFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> magnetic nanoparticles were deposited within the air substrate to have a magnetic film thickness of 30 μm, which shifted the measured resonant frequency down to 7.8 GHz while the realized gain was increased to 7.0 dBi. Detailed comparison of the simulation and measurement results are provided. This work demonstrates a low cost and compact microstrip patch antenna utilizing the magnetic nanoparticle film which could find many applications in the RF and microwave circuits and devices.

articleTitle: A tunable ferroelectric unit cell for wideband beam-steering reflectarray antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a tunable ferroelectric unit cell for wideband beam-steering reflectarray antennas is proposed. The proposed element is composed of three parts, i.e., a shorted parallel plate waveguide, a bifurcated ferroelectric phase shifter and two symmetric four-section stepped impedance transformers. Employing the DC bias voltage to vary the permittivity of ferroelectric material, the reflection phase of proposed unit cell can be continuously tuned. Full-wave simulated results show that the reflectarray element can achieve more than 360° linear phase tunability from 5.0 GHz to 6.5 GHz. The impact of ferroelectric loss on the performance of unit cell is also investigated. The proposed ferroelectric unit cell can be used to implement wideband beam-steering reflectarray antennas, providing an alternative of complicated phased array antennas.

articleTitle: Machine-Learning-Assisted Two-Step Antenna Modelling Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An efficient machine-learning-assisted two-step antenna modelling method (TSAMM) is proposed based on multi-output Gaussian process regression (MOGPR) methods. Variable-fidelity electromagnetic (EM) models are calculated with their responses trained to build two separate MOGPR models. By using asymmetric and symmetric MOGPR methods, mappings between the same and the different responses of the EM models with variable-fidelity are learned. Using the training set with sufficient coarse data and only a few fine data, fine responses can be accurately predicted. The frequency responses of the reflection coefficient and the gain of a quad-resonance substrate integrated waveguide cavity backed slot antenna are modelled to validate the superior of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Graphene-based Textile Ultra Wideband Antennas for Integrated and Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an ultra wideband antenna using graphene as a conductive patch. In order to provide flexibility, the cotton fabric is used as a substrate. The proposed antenna covers a bandwidth of 2-8 GHz. Simulated antenna efficiency is approximately 60% in overall bandwidth. The attractive features of conformity, lower design complexity and fabrication ease as well as integration of an environment friendly and low cost graphene have suggested the proposed antenna well-suited for body-centric, biomedical and wearable applications.

articleTitle: Full D-band Coplanar to Rectangular Waveguide Transition for UTC-PD Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a broadband coplanar waveguide (CPW) to rectangular waveguide transition for unitraveling carrier photodiode (UTC-PD) THz source application. The four step Chebyshev ridge waveguide is used to transform the quasi-TEM mode of the CPW to the TE10 mode of the rectangular waveguide, and to widen the transition bandwidth. Simulated results demonstrate that the proposed CPW to waveguide transition covers the whole D band (110-170 GHz), and achieves a wider fractional bandwidth of 43% and lower insertion loss of 0.5 dB.

articleTitle: Fast Algorithms for Converting an FMM-Based Representation of Electrically Large Integral Operators to a Minimal-Rank ℋ2-Matrix
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we develop fast algorithms to convert an FMM-based representation to a new ℋ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-matrix whose rank is minimized based on accuracy. We then apply these algorithms to solve electrically large surface electric field integral equations for scattering analysis. The resultant new ℋ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-matrix is found to have a much reduced rank without sacrificing prescribed accuracy.

articleTitle: Nature-Inspired Optimization of Aperiodic Metasurfaces for Antenna Beam-shaping
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Partially Reflective Surfaces (PRS) are highly reflective metasurfaces that are well-suited in the design of antennas for beamforming and high gain wireless applications, particularly in the mm-wave regime. Periodic PRS, made of uniformly spaced elements, however, limits the design of the antenna with regard to the trade-off between gain, sidelobe level, or achieving a prescribed arbitrary pattern. Aperiodic PRS, made of non-uniformly spaced inclusions provide more degrees of freedom in antenna synthesis and design. In this work we investigate optimal design of aperiodic PRS for various antenna functionality using several nature inspired global optimization techniques. Numerical examples and experimental verification of a prototype for achieving a shaped beam pattern is given.

articleTitle: Wide-Band Series-Fed Patch Antenna Array with Low Side Lobes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 2-D tapered microstrip series-fed patch antenna array with wide bandwidth is presented. First, a series-fed antenna sub-array consisting 10 patch antenna elements with tapered width is demonstrated to obtain -20 dB SLL in the E-plane. Then, multiple slots are used in the patch design to enhance operational bandwidth. Finally, an 8×10 antenna array fed by three-stage T-junction power divider with Taylor distribution is presented. The antenna array realizes a pencil beam with 5.1% fractional bandwidth, less than -20 dB side lobe level in E and H planes.

articleTitle: An Innovative UWB Connected Array for Multifunctional Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work describes the design procedures and prototype measurements of an innovative ultra wideband (UWB) antenna for Multifunctional Active Electronically Scanned Array (M-AESA) systems. The proposed antenna is a Connected Array composed by 24 Connected Vivaldi elements in vertical polarization, displaced in 3 rows and 8 columns. The array is completely metallic (aluminum), ensuring a high total efficiency. One of the key aspects of this architecture is that it takes advantage of electrical connections between each element of the array in order to improve the antenna matching over a wide frequency band. The strength points of the presented Connected Vivaldi array are: wideband functionality, high efficiency, high gain, wide scanning capabilities, low manufacturing costs and simple assembly. The comparison between simulations and measurements shows very close correspondence.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Polygonal Discone Antenna for Simplified Fabrication and Reconfigurability
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The antenna presented herein is formed as a hexagonal approximation of the traditional discone geometry. This design eliminates the curved surfaces of both the disk and the cone of the typical design, replacing them with flat trapezoidal panels. This greatly reduces the fabrication complexity, while maintaining the high bandwidth and symmetric radiation pattern of the canonical structure. The polygonal discone also introduces the possibility of post-fabrication reconfigurability, through articulation of the six panels.

articleTitle: The Dual Weighted Residual and Error Estimation in Double Higher-Order FEM
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We summarize the application of the dual weighted residual for error estimation for a double higher-order finite element method solution in frequency-domain computational electromagnetics. These error estimates facilitate intelligent refinement strategies, allowing an automated targeting of potential problems in a discretization, both in terms of accuracy and efficiency. We outline the construction of the dual weighted residual for three-dimensional scattering problems, and demonstrate error contribution estimates for two examples.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Silicon Substrates for IC-Waveguide Integration based on a Contactless Transition at mm-Wave frequencies
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a comparison between different silicon (Si) substrates used in Si-based IC technologies at E-Band (71–86 GHz). A unique low-loss and compact contactless transition from a silicon IC (p-doped substrate) to a metal waveguide is used. The proposed transition incorporates a spatial power combiner to enable direct electromagnetic coupling from an array of patches on the IC to a metal waveguide. This design enables a high-power transition from an IC to a waveguide and/or antenna at millimeter-wave (mm-wave) frequencies, where a galvanic contact between the two parts is avoided.

articleTitle: Elevation Imaging Based on Vortex Electromagnetic Wave
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A method of elevation imaging based on vortex electromagnetic wave generated by concentric uniform circular array (UCA) is proposed. The dual relationship between the elevation angle of target and the locations of the UCA elements is used. Subsequently, the compressed sensing strategy is utilized to determine the elevation angle of target. Simulation results show high accuracy of this method. The work can benefit the research on orbital angular momentum (OAM) based information-rich radar.

articleTitle: Efficient Delay and AoA Estimation Using Vector Antenna for Radio Propagation Measurements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Channel parameter estimation is an essential part for radio propagation measurements. An electromagnetic vector antenna (EMVA) based method is proposed to estimate delay and angle of arrival (AoA). The parallel factor (PARAFAC) decomposition is used to obtain the AoA and the delay of each ray. The proposed method can extract more rays than the antenna number even with only one snapshot. The simulation results verify the proposed method.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction in Wideband Electromagnetic Medical Imaging Antenna Array Using Compact Electromagnetic Band Gap
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact, low profile, and wideband electromagnetic band gap (EBG) unit cell for mutual coupling reduction between antennas of electromagnetic medical imaging is proposed. The EBG unit cell is designed on a 3-mm thick polymer RTV6166 substrate and consists of a square patch (14×14 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) with four symmetrically L-slot. The EBG unit cell is characterized using suspended transmission line method. It achieves fractional stopband bandwidth of 101.3%, which covers the low microwave frequency band from 1.18 GHz to 2.7 GHz. This usually requires large size, and high profile if conventional EBG structures are used. To further assess the proposed EBG cell and its effect on suppressing the coupling between antenna arrays, two CPW circular monopole antennas are designed and investigated with the presence of EBG unit cells. The simulation results show that the EBG unit cells are able to reduce the coupling in an array system that encloses an average human head model by 7 dB over the operational frequency range.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Filtering Reflectarray for High-Gain Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a new concept of high-gain filtering reflectarray antenna operating at millimeter-wave (mmW) frequencies. Two-section metal waveguide element is used as the reflectarray unit cell. Taking advantage of the high-pass filter nature of the waveguide structure, the reflectarray elements can provide desired reflection coefficients in the targeted band of interest yet deteriorating reflection phase and amplitude responses at lower and upper out-of-band frequencies, respectively. Therefore, the proposed reflectarray can realize filter-like frequency response by controlling the aperture amplitude and phase distributions. The antenna has been fabricated by low-cost 3-dimentional (3-D) printing technique followed by metal coating. Both simulated and measured results are presented to verify its radiating and filtering functions.

articleTitle: Compact, Multi-Band, Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel multi-band slot antenna. The antenna's different dimensions can be easily calculated for obtaining the desired resonance frequencies. The antenna presents a very good efficiency in the different resonant bands. Also, each resonance could be reconfigured independently from others. Simulations in frequency domain using HFSS and in time domain with CST provide almost the same results confirming the design approach and performances.

articleTitle: Dual beam end-fire antenna using cantilever-enabled Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an end-fire antenna with multi-beam switching capability using cantilever-based frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) is presented. The single and dual-beam configurations in the E-plane radiation of the antenna is obtained by the integration of seven layers of the 3 × 1 array of proposed reconfigurable FSS. The simulated results of the antenna system show single beam and dual beams having a tilt of ±45 in the E-plane without much degradation in the antenna gain at 10 GHz frequency.

articleTitle: Resonance Tuning Cost in Radiation Efficiency of Electrically Small Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Numerical tools are used to predict the upper-bounds on radiation efficiency with and without a constraint on self-resonance. It is demonstrated that the assumption of lossless external tuning produces unrealistic results. The main result of this contribution is that, when realistic (e.g., finite conductivity) materials are used, the cost of resonance tuning in the radiation efficiency of small antenna systems is high and is manifested by a dissipation factor which scales as a fourth power of electrical size.

articleTitle: Polarization-Independent and Broadband THz Coherent Perfect Absorber based on Black Phosphorus Bifacial Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work reports a novel black phosphorus (BP)-based metasurface exhibiting broadband and polarization-insensitive coherent perfect absorption (CPA) at THz frequencies. The proposed design is composed of a thin dielectric layer sandwiched between two BP monolayers patterned in patches. An equivalent microwave circuit model is developed to accurately model and analyze this design. It is shown that CPA can be achieved over a broad bandwidth of 1.5 THz for both TM and TE waves. The broadband and polarization-independent CPA response is achieved due to the ultrathin thickness of the proposed design and the anisotropic dispersive properties of BP. The presented ultrathin and broadband CPA devices can be used as tunable planar THz modulators, detectors, and signal processors.

articleTitle: The Effect of Antenna in the Forward Model of Near Field Microwave Imaging Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A fast and accurate forward problem solver for near-field microwave imaging systems is developed by considering the electric field intensity as the measured quantity. Since the antenna port voltage values will be the real measured quantity in practical applications, the effects of transmitting/receiving antennas in the forward problem model is investigated.

articleTitle: Observed Q and Gravitationally-Small Antenna Behavior of a Binary Black Hole Radiator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recent theoretical advances have provided an analytical expression for the Q of gravitationally-small sources of gravitational radiation, along lines similar to the Wheeler-Chu limit for electrically-small antennas. This paper presents the first published results using this new theory to analyze the Q of a black-hole inspiral, using observed transient gravitational wave data from the GW170608 black-hole merger. Despite the astronomical scale of a radiation source comprised of two black holes having upwards of 7 solar masses each, the GW170608 binary black hole is shown to be a gravitationally-small high-Q radiator at the very low frequencies of the gravitational waves.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Based First-Order Sea Clutter Region Extraction Method for HFSWR
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The first-order sea-clutter region extraction method is one of the key technologies for high frequency surface wave radar (HFSWR) for sea state remote sensing. However, the first-order sea clutter in the Range-Doppler (RD) map is hard to extract, especially in the presence of targets and splitting Bragg peaks. This paper presents a method to extract sea clutter based on machine learning with discriminative features from different aspects. The performance of the proposed method is verified and results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Data Acquisition Circuit for Identification of RF Signals’ Direction of Arrival
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design, manufacture and tests of a front-end circuit for a Direction Finding (DF) system. The front-end circuit is composed of low noise amplifiers (LNA), multiplexers for selection of the signals received from an antenna array, and a microwave comparator responsible for determining the relative voltage on the antennas’ terminals. A successful testing of the prototype combined with a four-element microstrip antenna array and a software based on the MUSIC (Multiple Signal Classification) validate the proposed front-end circuit.

articleTitle: Generalized Tensor FDTD Method for Sloped Plasmonic Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A tensor finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method for sloped interfaces is generalized to dispersive media and applied to the study of plasmonic periodic structures formed by silver nanorods. Conventional staircased FDTD exhibits poor convergence properties in this situation, as plasmonic fields are strongly localized right where staircasing errors occur, namely at the air-silver interface. Alternative methods that have been proposed for this problem include the use of a triangular mesh or effective permittivity models that lead to a fourth-order auxiliary differential equation (ADE) connecting D and E at the interface. The proposed approach offers high accuracy, still employing a rectangular FDTD mesh, thus striking a very appealing balance between accuracy and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: The Dawn of Spacetime Metamaterials : (Invited Paper)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper is a subset of a full-length paper that will be published in a special issue on metamaterials of the transactions at the end of this year. It presents the current authors' perspective on the emerging field of spacetime metamaterials. Emphasis is placed on the definition, contextualization and fundamentals of the concept. In addition, a few new physical effects are described and a number of applications are enumerated.

articleTitle: Design of a Quasi-Optical Si/GaAs W-Band Beam-Forming Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a Si/GaAs metasurface antenna at W-band frequencies. The antenna operates in a holographic manner; leveraging the guided-mode launched by the input ports and synthesizing a desired radiation wave-front by modulating the guided-mode using a metasurface layer - similar to a hologram. We show the beam-steering capability of the metasurface antenna by switching between the input ports. The simulated reflection coefficient of the antenna is greater than -15 dB with a maximum directivity of 31.9 dBi at 94 GHz.

articleTitle: Microstrip-Fed Endfire Antennas with High Gain and Stable Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, three endfire antennas with a large ground plane are proposed. Fed by an air-substrate microstrip line, the endfire antennas have the merits of high gain and stable radiation pattern. In addition, the first antenna has a narrow structure, the second antenna achieves a wide endfire gain bandwidth, and the third antenna could be embedded into a metallic platform.

articleTitle: A Substrate Integrated Waveguide Filtering Slot Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A fully integrated 1×4 filtering linear antenna array is presented in this work. The filtering array is designed in substrate integrated waveguide technology and consists of 5 coupled cavities with a 6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-order filtering function. The antenna array is formed with a linear arrangement of four slot antennas in the final cavities which excite two modes in the radiating cavity. The array operates at a center frequency of 6.75 GHz with a fractional bandwidth of 5.0% and with a gain of 7.44 dBi.

Author Keywords: cavity resonators; linear antenna arrays; slot antennas

articleTitle: A Tightly Coupled Array Loaded On a Miura-Ori Pattern
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper the electromagnetic performance of an array of tightly coupled dipoles is investigated when it is loaded on a modified Miura-ori pattern. The ability of the Miura-ori structure to change its shape is used to adjust the scanning capabilities of the array. Based on our results, as the structure is deformed from 0° to 45°, the arrays' reception is improved compared to the unfolded/flat state for both the E and H planes.

articleTitle: Partition Waveguide Slotted Array With Shaped Patterns
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a large partition waveguide slotted array (WSA) is summarized. Genetic Algorithms (GAs) is employed to synthesis the fan beam shaped pattern waveguide slotted array. Waveguide phase shifters are used to compensate the definite phases for each waveguide. The whole array is divided into eight partitions to broaden the bandwidth. Full wave simulations confirm the design of the shaped pattern antenna.

articleTitle: Wideband Two-Beam Antenna array Fed by Modified Butler Matrix
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel beam-forming network operating in an octave frequency band by using a modified Butler matrix. The Butler matrix contains two different types of couplers which can switch the signal between the radiating elements at different frequencies. At f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, the selected radiating elements spacing 2d are excited, whereas at 2f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> the radiating elements spacing d are excited, ensuring the stable radiation pattern in the wide frequency range. This work has been verified by simulations, fabrications and measurements of broadband antenna array fed by a 2×4 beam-forming network operating in 2-4 GHz.

articleTitle: A Compact Tri-Band Antenna for Vehicle Communication and Navigation Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact design of an integrated Tri-band antenna with different polarizations and radiation patterns is proposed in this paper. The antenna structure is composed of two stacked boards that the upper board is a monopolar wire patch with two symmetrical slots and the lower board is a square patch with four rectangular slots. The monopolar wire patch can provide stable conical radiation patterns with vertical polarization within the GSM 850/900, and DCS1800/PCS1900 bands while the side length of the monopolar wire patch is 46mm and the antenna height is 10mm. Also, the square patch shows good circular polarization characteristic for GPS application at L1 bands and provide broadside radiation pattern. The isolation between communication and navigation ports is well above 25 dB within the working frequency bands.

articleTitle: L-Probe and U-Slot Microstrip Circular Antenna for Application in the Detection of Partial Discharges in Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, the applicability of a circular microstrip antenna with U-slot and L probe in the detection of partial discharges in power transformers was analyzed. Dimensional parametric analyzes were carried out for the design of an antenna with optimized performance. The joint application of both bandwidth enhancement techniques proved to be more efficient in terms of bandwidth and gain than their respective individual applications. In addition, the values of bandwidth, size, gain and directivity obtained allow to classify the designed antenna as applicable in the detection of partial discharges in power transformers.

articleTitle: Tunable Hybrid Terahertz Metamaterials Based on VO2 Phase Transition
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a series of proof-of-concept designs for highly tunable hybrid THz metamaterials based on the phase transition of vanadium dioxide (VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) are presented. In particular, we verify by full-wave simulations the tunable properties of the hybrid metamaterials including Fano resonances, perfect absorption bands and THz magnetism. Our results indicate that an integration of VO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> structures and conventional metallic resonating components can be used to create THz metamaterials with properties that can be dynamically tuned over a large scale.

articleTitle: A Compact Platform-Based Antenna for an Unmanned Ground Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a design strategy for covert platform-based antennas that operate on electrically-small platforms such as compact unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs). Specifically, we report the design of platform-based antennas operating at the lower end of the very high frequency (VHF) band for a small UGV having electrical dimensions of 0.13λ × 0.09λ × 0.05λ at 40 MHz. To do this without increasing the size or visual signature of the platform, the bottom of the UGV is modified in a nondestructive fashion. Specifically, a quarter-wavelength slot antenna is created in the bottom of the vehicle by placing a false bottom in the undercarriage area. The proposed antenna generates a vertically-polarized, monopole-like radiation pattern as verified through simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: A Two-Dimensional LC-Network Metamaterial on an Irregular Grid
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A planar network of reactive elements on an irregular grid for realizing an effective two-dimensional medium is presented. In an elemental cell that occupies a cylindrical volume having an irregular polygonal cross section, one shunt element and multiple series elements are connected at a node. The effective medium parameters are found in terms of the shunt and series element values. A numerical example of a 2-D Luneburg lens design in TE polarization is presented for validation.

articleTitle: Antenna Pattern Evaluation of 28GHz band Massive MIMO Antenna RF Frontend Module for 5G
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In the 5th generation mobile communication system, large system capacity, low latency and massive connection will be provided for novel and various applications. In order to realize these features, we are developing high SHF band massive MIMO system which can secure wide system bandwidth and high spectral efficiency. In particular, the combination of analog beamforming and digital MIMO signal processing for the multi-beam multiplexing is a promising approach in order to reduce the computational complexity and power consumption. In this paper, hybrid beamforming configuration for 28GHz band Massive MIMO system and some antenna patterns measured in the anechoic chamber are shown.

articleTitle: Leaky-Wave Antenna on Holey EBG Based Gap-Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a quasi-uniform leaky-wave antenna on a gap-waveguide with a holey EBG structure at 39 GHz. Arrays of 20 and 40 slots are presented, that show good matching, and 12.6 dB and 15.6 dB gain, respectively. In addition, two 2-columns arrays of 40 and 80 slots are presented, with good matching, isolation higher than 45 dB, and gains of 21 and 23 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Design Reusing for Expedited Design Optimization of Antenna Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The paper presents a simple approach to expedited design optimization of antenna structures. Reduction of the design cost is achieved by reusing already existing designs, e.g., obtained for different substrates or operating frequencies. The existing data is employed to identify a good initial design as well as to extract estimated response sensitivities, which speeds up the optimization process itself. The proposed approach is illustrated through the design of a unidirectional quasi-Yagi antenna optimized for a wide range of operating frequencies (3.0 to 6.0 GHz) and substrate permittivity (2.5 to 4.5).

articleTitle: A Stabilized Marching-on-in-Degree Solution of Time Domain Combined Field Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The instability problem of time domain integral equation (TDIE) remains one of the key obstacles to improve the quality of the TDIE solvers over the past decades. In this paper, the stabilized marching-on-in-degree (MOD) method of time-domain combined field integral equation (TD-CFIE-SMOD) is presented in solution of transient scattering problems. The instability problem of TDIE-MOD is primarily caused by the oscillatory nature of the Laguerre functions. Therefore, the Filon-type quadrature for excitation integrals and the Filon-type radial integration method on triangular domains is adopted in the TD-CFIE-SMOD solver. Some numerical results are presented to show the validity of the proposed solution of TD-CFIE using the current methodology.

articleTitle: UWB Millimeter-Wave 180° Hybid Couplers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A myriad of ultra-wide-band (UWB) 180° hybrids have been reported that operate at frequencies below 20 GHz. However, printed circuit board (PCB) parasitics become significantly more problematic as the frequency is extended to mm-wave frequencies and beyond. Here, two different UWB mm-wave hybrid couplers are investigated for operation at 18-67 GHz. First, an asymmetric, coupled transmission line hybrid is reported. The junction parasitics are compensated by a heterogenous multi-layer PCB stackup. Next, a splitter-balun hybrid is considered, which combines a wideband Marchand balun and a tee power splitter at a single junction. This hybrid's symmetry ensures near-perfect amplitude and phase balance over an ultra-wide bandwidth in simulation. However, it is more challenging to fabricate.
