articleTitle: Determining the Maximum Local Specific Absorption Rate of a Multiple-Antenna Transmitter Using K-Order Electric Field Models
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new estimation technique using K-order electric field models for evaluating the maximum local specific absorption rate (SAR) of a multiple-antenna transmitter. Details of the K-order models, estimation methods, and validations are presented and discussed. Thanks to the proposed K-order models, the estimation errors can be reduced significantly, compared to those of conventional techniques. For example, the maximum error in conventional SAR estimations of a three-antenna configuration is about 9%, which is decreased to 0.1% or 0.01% in the 2- and 3-order estimations, respectively.

articleTitle: A non-iterative time-domain sidelobe suppression in doppler shifted LFM waveforms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A time-domain block filtering technique is applied to a pulse of Doppler-shifted linear frequency modulated (LFM) signals and the improvement of sidelobe suppression is investigated in this paper. A brief theoretical methodology of Doppler shift LFM signal and the filtering technique is reviewed. Numerical Simulation and Experimental results are reported. Suppression of 8dB in Integrated Side Lobe Ratio (ISLR) is observed for a signal with 20dB SNR.

articleTitle: A Fundamental Study of Folded Monopole Antenna with Robustness to Metal
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In order to achieve an antenna with robustness to metal for closed space wireless communications, the impedance characteristics of folded monopole antennas (FMA) have been investigated in detail. This paper investigates the antenna characteristics when the antenna approaches metal plates in multiple directions to replicate an actual use environment. The simulation results show that the proposed higher impedance antenna has more robustness to metal than the conventional middle impedance antenna.

articleTitle: Transmit Beamforming Based on 4D Antenna Arrays with Pseudo-Random Orthogonal Time Sequences
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel transmit beamforming approach based on 4D antenna arrays with pseudo-random orthogonal time modulation. The technique shows most advantages of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) arrays and phased arrays with excellent detection and low probability of interception (LPI) performance. Substantial system improvements achieved by the proposed approach are demonstrated through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of the corresponding beampatterns in comparison with those of basic MIMO arrays.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Quad-Polarization Reconfigurable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A quad-polarization reconfigurable antenna with high gain is proposed in this paper. The high-gain antenna is a short backfire antenna (SBA) which is excited by two reconfigurable crossed slots. Eight PIN diodes are mounted across the slots. By changing the on/off states of the PIN diodes, the antenna can switch its polarization modes among horizontal polarization (HP), vertical polarization (VP), left-handed circular polarization (LHCP), and right-handed circular polarization (RHCP). Two probes are utilized to feed the crossed slots. An antenna prototype is fabricated. Experimental results show that the reconfigurable antenna exhibits an overlapped impedance bandwidth of 22.5% for return loss >10 dB and a high gain of about 10.5 dBi for all polarization states.

articleTitle: Simulation Design of Beam-scanning Self-phase-shift Dipole Array Based on Liquid-metal Materials
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a liquid-metal self-phase-shift dipole array with beam scanning capability is proposed. The main part of this design is a two-element dipole array. The arms of two dipoles are made of liquid eutectic gallium indium (EGaIn) that can be shortened and lengthened in the capillaries by applying DC voltages. With the varying lengths, the self-impedance characteristics of dipoles are changed achieving the beam-scanning property. In order to enhance the directivity, two movable EGaIn parasitic elements which are served as director and reflector are loaded in two separated microfluidic channels. In addition, the electromagnetic band gap structures are employed between the two dipoles to reduced mutual coupling. The simulated results by CST Microwave Studio<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sup> indicate that the radiation patterns can attain the scan angle from -21° to 21°.The simulated gains are stable at 7-8 dBi, and the isolation are better than 20 dB.

articleTitle: Optimization of an Adaptive Antenna Array Excitations Employing Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In an adaptive antenna array system, the most favourable solution to the problem of obtaining a certain null or maximum at a specific location may take a long processing time, such that the spatial situation could have been changed before the optimization process ends. In this work, an algorithm employing the schelkunoff nulling theory to achieve specific null or maximum at some desired directions is presented. The optimization of the array excitations is performed using genetic algorithm (GA) method to achieve null and maxima at the desired directions, the proposed technique holds for any adaptive array geometry. It is evidenced that the proposed technique based on reducing the number of array coefficients to be optimized reduces the processing time of the optimization process by about 92% without influencing other parameters such as the side-lobes level or the beam width.

articleTitle: Microwave performance measurement of InP powder under light irradiation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a coaxial cavity for investigating the effect of light irradiation on the microwave performance of semiconductor material is proposed. The photosensitive material used is indium phosphide (InP) powder and the light source is a power tunable signal source with a working wavelength of 808nm. In this experiment, we study the microwave characteristics of InP powder under light irradiation power of 10mW, 50mW, 100mW, and 250mW, respectively. The measurement results show that the microwave properties of InP powder have a manifest offset behavior under different irradiation. According to effective experimental method and theoretical analysis, we conclude that the change of the microwave properties is caused by the electron energy level transition in InP material.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of a Smart Antenna Based on Hybrid Beam-forming Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we have proposed a mathematical model for the design of a hybrid beam-forming antenna. Antenna beam is steered by the hybrid of switched parasitic array and phased array approach, this technique is based on our recently awarded patent. Our design consists of two circular arrays of parasitic elements, each array has six parasitic / passive elements around an active element. Phased shift between the excitation currents is introduced by adding a phase shifter. Antenna beam is steered by the switching (opening / shorting) of the parasitic elements as well as by regulating phase shift. In conventional switched parasitic array antennas beam-steering is not continuous. However, by using our approach continuous beam-steering (0°-360°) is achieved in the azimuth plane. Moreover our antenna gain is 4 dB higher than the conventional switched parasitic array and electronically steerable parasitic array radiator (ESPAR) antennas, typical gain of such antennas is 6.5 dBi.

articleTitle: Matching Considerations for Wireless, Batteryless Brain Implants to High Impedance Electrodes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Having previously proposed a novel wireless, batteryless neurosensing system able to detect deep brain signals down to 20 μVpp during in vitro testing, we now seek to maintain this high sensitivity under in vivo conditions as well. The latter implies recording of deep brain activity via clinical neural electrodes which have inherently high impedances. In this paper, we report a link budget analysis that illuminates the significance of matching the brain implant to its associated electrode. Potentiostatic measurements of clinical microelectrodes are also provided, showing impedances in the tens of kΩ to MΩ range. In the future, these studies can be leveraged to maintain the wireless, passive, batteryless operation while matching implant impedance to the high impedance of clinical electrodes.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Stacked Equilateral Triangular DRA for Wide Band Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Stacked dielectric resonator antenna of equilateral triangular shape is designed and fabricated in this paper for wide band application in C band. Wide bandwidth obtained ranges from 4.65 GHz to 6.8 GHz with broadside radiation patterns throughout the entire range. The wide band is a result of merging TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">101</sub>, TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">103</sub>, TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">105</sub> mode frequencies of the stack. Moreover, the stack is analyzed to find a closed form equation for resonant frequencies of TM mode.

articleTitle: Wideband Near-Zone Radiative Signal Collector System for Detection of Electromagnetic Emission From Distributed Sources
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work reports on a wideband near-zone radiative signal collector system operating from 1 to 50 GHz for capturing electromagnetic emission from a community of bacteria in a petri dish or any other distributed sources confined in a small focusing area. The system includes a dual-polarized signal collector, broadband Low Noise Amplifiers (LNAs) and a precision spectrum analyzer. The signal collector is composed of a quad-ridged horn-type structure of dimensions λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> × λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> × 1.6 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> (where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</sub> is the wavelength at the lowest frequency) having two orthogonal probes. The provision of a dielectric cone along the horn central axis allows for collimating the waves in the focusing area over the entire bandwidth. The signal collector acts as a field concentrator to provide a uniform field distribution across the focusing area (source location) over the entire band. The structure is EM-shielded to exclude outside radiation. The collector is also designed to be resonance-free for uniform collection of the electromagnetic spectrum.

articleTitle: Theory of Horizontal Dipole Over a Dielectric-Coated Impedance Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A horizontal electric dipole antenna located above a dielectric-coated impedance surface is characterized. The generalized reflection coefficient is evaluated using the impedance boundary condition. The Sommerfeld integral equation is dissociated into particular and homogeneous parts using the method of scattering superposition. The particular term is recast into the Richmond's form and the DCIM with GPOF technique is used to obtain the closed form of the homogeneous Green's function. The variation in the dipole current distribution with change in the real and imaginary parts of the surface impedance is thereafter obtained. The reflection coefficient and the radiation pattern are also evaluated.

articleTitle: Gauge Transformations for Recasting Potential Representations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Conversion of a field representation such as TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub> to a different representation such as a TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> by means of general gauge transformations is demonstrated by considering radiation from a dipole.

articleTitle: Full Sparsity in Compressive Processing for Non-Linear Inverse Scattering
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents an innovative full sparse inverse scattering method for non-linear inverse scattering problems. The retrieval of the total field configuration inside a non accessible domain is solved using an efficient Compressive Processing inversion. Accordingly, an over-complete dictionary is built and optimized using a dictionary learning algorithm, in order to assure the sparse representation of the unknowns.

articleTitle: Closely-Spaced Resonant Cavity Antennas For Meeting ETSI Class-2 Specifications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Dense, wideband and high-gain Resonant Cavity Antenna Arrays (RCAAs) are presented in this paper. Two array topologies (comprising square & radial configurations) made out of a Transverse Permittivity Gradient Superstrate (TPGS) are specifically investigated for meeting ETSI Class-2 specifications. Their boresight performance is characterized on the basis of peak directivity, 3dB directivity bandwidth, and most importantly the far-field radiation pattern envelope (RPE) masks. In comparison to a 9 × 9 square array, a radial array (having 91 elements) is shown to achieve the peak directivity of 37 dBi with a 3dB directivity bandwidth of more than 20%. In addition, the radial array demonstrated the potential of satisfying minimum ETSI Class-2 antenna requirements with appropriate RPEs up to 50° and SLLs as low as -17 dBi.

articleTitle: Near Field Focusing using a Circularly Polarized Reconfigurable Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A C-band circularly polarized reconfigurable reflectarray using electromechanical actuators is presented. Circular rings as unit cell elements enable full 360 degree phase adjustment using variable rotation technique. The performance of the reflectarray in near field focusing is evaluated. A near field focusing gain of 18.5dB and depth of focus (DoF) of 1.76λ is obtained. Also a locally plane wavefront is observed around the focal point region.

articleTitle: Towards Generalized Transistor-based Magnetless Nonreciprocal Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a transmission-type transistor-based magnetless nonreciprocal metasurface that can properly be characterizable by bianisotropic surface susceptibilities. This work represents a first step towards generalized magnetless nonreciprocal metasurfaces with the potential inclusion of extra electromagnetic properties.

articleTitle: Evaporation Duct Refractivity Inversions from Fixed Transmitter-Fixed Receiver UWB Measurements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper explores the point-to-point ultra wideband fixed link atmospheric refractivity estimation. The Lower Atmospheric Propagation Ultrawideband (LATPROP-UWB) measurement system was deployed during CASPER-West. A multifrequency objective function is used to invert for the M-profile for a range-independent case. Monte Carlo analysis is performed to obtain estimator variances for increasing SNR and varying numbers of frequencies. A couple of CASPER-West data with evaporation duct are investigated and used to test the algorithm.

articleTitle: A Compact EBG for High Isolation Between Two Very Closeby Wire-Antennas for RFID Tags
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we show a new scheme to tackle the problems of high electromagnetic-coupling, poor impedance-matching and degraded radiation-characteristics of two UHF-band RFID tag antennas, when they are very close. Using an inverted H-shaped EBG as a novel and compact structure, we insert it between the two antennas and prevent the unwanted interference and match the input impedance of both of the tag antennas. Also, the antenna gain of the two tags is -1.23 dBi which is larger than that of ordinary UHF-band tag antennas.

articleTitle: Comparison Between Deterministic and Stochastic Methods for the Synthesis of Aperiodic Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The optimization problem addressed in this paper is that of minimizing the maximum sidelobe level of linear aperiodic antenna arrays radiating a pencil beam directed at broadside and having an assigned beamwidth and (eventually) desired nulls. A uniform amplitude distribution is assumed for the array elements. A deterministic approach is proposed, and its performance is compared with that of a stochastic method of recent literature.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Thin Compact Highly Efficient Π-Section CRLH–EBG Based Antenna for ISM Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An ultra-thin, compact, highly efficient, antenna based on the Π-section Composite Right/ Left-Handed (CRLH) methodology backed with a 2 × 2 Electromagnetic Band-Gap (EBG) array is presented in this paper. The integrated design operates at 2.45 GHz of the ISM Band with simulated gain and total efficiency of 7.63 dBi and 94.6 %, respectively. Moreover, the antenna is printed over 100 μm flexible substrate while the EBG is printed on 0.8 mm substrate which makes the whole structure low profile. With such results, the integrated design is highly recommended for wearable applications. Results are achieved through circuit model and full wave electromagnetic simulations.

articleTitle: Analysis of Multi-Antenna Proximity on Performance of Electrically Small Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Of great interest in the many fields of communication is the requirement to place many small antenna elements in close proximity for diversity or muti-band usage. This work aims to describe in detail the effects of such adjacency in terms of physical distance and operating frequencies as a function of the volume overlap of circumscribing Wheeler-Chu spheres. We investigate any potential bandwidth advantage due to this shared near-field space and define trade-offs between space minimization and acceptable degradation.

articleTitle: A 5G Antenna Array Placed Close to a 4G Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel antenna array for the mobile handset is proposed for the upcoming 5G systems. The antenna element of the array consists of one radiator and two reflectors on the same plane. Based on the antenna element, an antenna array that has four radiators and five reflectors was designed. The proposed array was placed close to a 4G antenna element. The radiation properties of the array and the 4G antenna were investigated. The antenna array exhibited good performance without deteriorating 4G antenna efficiency. The proposed antenna design is expected to be applied to the next-generation mobile handsets.

articleTitle: Acceleration of Finite Periodic Structures Analysis through Full-Domain Basis for Matrix Compression
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Approaching large finite periodic structures with the surface integral equation-method of moments (SIE-MoM) framework is a challenging kind of problems in terms of memory and computing time. Slotting the MoM matrix with slotFFT techniques has proven to be an efficient approach to reduce both metrics through the application of FFT. In this work we propose the integration of a matrix compression method with a controlled impact on the precision based on full-domain distributed basis to improve the acceleration given by the slotFFT method.

articleTitle: End-Fire CP Millimeter-Wave Antenna Loaded with Perforated Dielectric Slab
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An end-fire CP (Circularly-Polarized) antenna is presented in this paper for millimeter-wave applications. It is composed of a VP (Vertically-Polarized) magnetic dipole and a HP (Horizontally-Polarized) printed dipole. The open end of the feeding SIW (Substrate Integrated Waveguide) is employed to work as the VP magnetic dipole. Besides, the electric dipole is realized by a pair of bow-tie dipole. In order to enhance the 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth of the proposed antenna, a perforated dielectric slab is loaded in front of the SIW structure and the bow-tie dipole is constructed on the top and the bottom of this slab. It is shown that the 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth is about 10.6% (the center frequency is 47 GHz), from the simulation results.

articleTitle: Investigation on Resolution of Thermoacoustic Imaging Based on Compressive Sensing: A Simulation Study
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Microwave-induced thermoacoustic imaging (MITAI) has witnessed tremendous development in the past three decades and numerous related applications have been explored. Compressive sensing (CS) based MITAI is a newly emerging modality that can greatly reduce the number of measurements for obtaining acceptable imaging quality. This work investigates spatial resolution of CS based MITAI by using realistic frequency response of two transducers. Simulation results show that a transducer working at a higher frequency is able to image an object with smaller features. This finding agrees with the established theory of MITAI. This work is useful for potential applications and further improvement of the CS based MITAI technique.

articleTitle: Integrated Water Vapor Estimation through Microwave Propagation Measurements: First Experiment on a Ground-To-Ground Radio Link
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The estimation of water vapor (WV) content in the lowest part of the troposphere is a critical issue which, up to now, cannot be obtained from space measurements with sufficient accuracy. A new technique, which is based on Ku-K band microwave measurements of the differential attenuation of two signals transmitted at closely spaced frequencies, has been recently proposed. In order to prove the effectiveness of this technique a prototype instrumentation was designed and tested on a ground-to-ground link.

articleTitle: Accurate Solution of Electromagnetic Scattering by Conducting Objects Based on Nyström Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper mainly addresses the accurate solution of electromagnetic scattering by 3D conducting objects based on Nyström method. The surface integral equation model of the conductor is constructed by surface triangles. The singularity of the near-field points is corrected by replacing the original source points with new points in the triangles and combining the Duffy's transform and Gauss-Legendre quadrature rule. The accuracy of numerical solutions is demonstrated with an example.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Inhomogeneous Microwave Lense of an Arbitrary Shape
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We outline the design and manufacturing approach employed to construct microwave lenses with arbitrary outlines. The lens is fabricated using multi-jet fusion which is suitable for mass production and allows inhomogeneous variation in dielectric constants. The technique is illustrated by making a microwave lens that provides the same performance as a reflector antenna but has the appearance of a birdhouse.

articleTitle: Study of a Method for Increasing Isolation Between Closely Spaced Elements integrated in Multi-Standard Multi-Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the study of a method used for decoupling radiating elements in the case of a multiband structure dedicated to small LTE Smart Cells. This method consists in using a power splitter and a phase shifter connected between the feeds of the two groups of radiating elements. The study begins with a monoband structure made up of printed monopoles and a wired standing one. The impact on the validity of the method, due to the introduction of two additional bands through the addition of parasitic elements was then studied. A prototype was realized and tested and he measurements are discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Tuning Range Enhancement of a Frequency-Agile Tri-band Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low-profile tri-band slot antenna with enhanced tuning range is presented in this paper. Tri-band frequency agility is obtained using three varactor-loaded slots on a planar structure. The tuning range of the proposed antenna is enhanced by suppressing the higher-order resonance modes, especially by controlling the surface currents and creating a fictitious ground on the antenna. Following full-wave simulations, a prototype was developed and measured to validate the concept. Results show a tuning range from 600MHz to 3300MHz, which is a 600 MHz increase in the overall tuning range than previously reported.

articleTitle: Non-Destructive Dielectric Constant Measurement of Low-Loss Dielectric Slabs Using Wideband Autocorrelation Radiometry
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel technique for measuring the dielectric constant of a low-loss layer without the need for sample preparation is presented. This technique inspired by a passive microwave remote sensing method, known as wideband autocorrelation radiometry (WiBAR), which remotely measures the microwave propagation time difference of multipath microwave emission from low-loss layered surfaces such as dry snowpack and freshwater icepack. This time delay is dependent on the incident angle. Using the measured time delay at two different incident angles, the real part of the dielectric constant and the thickness of the loss-less slab can be directly measured. An X-band instrument fabricated from commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) components are used to characterize the freshwater lake ice at the University of Michigan Biological Station. The measurements were performed in H-pol configuration for a lake icepack of about 36 cm from nadir to 59°.

articleTitle: Modeling Large and Complex Objects with Fine Geometrical Details by using the Massively Parallel Computer Codes JEMS-FDTD
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The embedded thin-layer technique and the field-to-wire coupling technique have been developed and integrated into the massively parallel computer codes JEMS-FDTD, enabling us to efficiently model the electrically-large complex objects with fine details. JEMS-FDTD has been applied to model the coupling effects of a real aircraft with the skin partly comprised of carbon fiber composite materials, and the induced currents on cables inside the aircraft have also been investigated.

articleTitle: An Offset-Fed Wideband 3D Printed Aperture Coupled Trapezoidal Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An offset-fed aperture coupled trapezoid shaped dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is presented and investigated for wideband operation. In the first step, a square DRA is studied and then modified to a trapezoidal shape resonator, which achieves a wideband impedance bandwidth of 500 MHz. For potential operation as a dual-polarized antenna, an offset-feed system is implemented in the next stage. The offset-fed DRA achieves a bandwidth of 440 MHz centered at 2.45 GHz.

articleTitle: A comparison of spatial interpolation methods to determine the coverage area of a wireless system
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a study of the coverage area of a wireless system in oil fields located in the city of Mossoró, Brazil. With the measurement campaigns, the necessary data for the application of the spatial interpolation methods that provide contour maps with the distribution of the RSSI (Received Signal Strength Indicator) levels in the study scenario were collected. Cross-validation was used to compare and evaluate the methods, as it establishes the precision criterion for estimation errors. The results showed that the spline method showed the smallest deviations between the measured and calculated values.

articleTitle: Acceleration of Laser-Driven Light Sails with Size Comparable to the Beam
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper derives exact formulas for the force exerted on light sails by lasers and for the resulting acceleration in the presence of spillover, which occurs when the size of the sail is comparable or smaller than that of the gaussian beam. Moreover, it compares these quantities for different sail sizes. This study is of a paramount interest for light/solar sail technology, since it allows one to minimize the size of the sail and the power of the laser for a given desired acceleration.

articleTitle: Full Wave Analysis for Estimating Wave Attenuation In a Random Volume of Metallic Wires Using Monte Carlo Simulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a model for electromagnetic waves propagating through a volume of metallic wires. These wires are assumed to be randomly distributed, perfectly conducting, and electrically large. The mean field propagating through such a medium resembles a field propagating through an effective homogeneous medium with complex permittivity and permeability. The mean field is calculated by coherently averaging the field scattered by many statistically relevant configurations of this random medium. The scattered field is calculated using the Method of Moments (MoM). The average scattered field is then compared to the field scattered by a homogeneous medium. The effective medium is defined as the medium for which the greatest amount of matching exists between the average scattered field and the effective medium scattered field. The propagation parameters of this effective medium are then given for a medium composed of half wavelength long wires occupying a varying volume fraction of the medium.

articleTitle: Zero-Forward Scattering for Omnidirectional Incidence using non-Hermitian Particles
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we derive the formulism for zero forward scattering for an electrical dipole dimer with arbitrary directions of the incident wave, showing that zero forward scattering can be realized by introducing active elements. We analyze a realistic nanosphere dimer and verify the analysis by analytical and numerical results. In order to realize zero forward scattering for omnidirectional incident waves, we present the required topology of the array and calculate the required permittivity of the gain elements. The numerical results validate our design. Finally, we discuss the possibility of multidirectional zero scattering by adding more particles.

articleTitle: Analysis of Rotated Corrugated Parallel Plate Waveguide Using Asymptotic Corrugation Boundary Conditions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Parallel plate waveguides with rotated corrugated surfaces are discussed and analyzed using a simplified, rapid, yet accurate analytical approach: the asymptotic corrugation boundary conditions (ACBC). Surface-wave dispersion diagrams for various rotation cases are also presented, discussed, and verified with a commercial full-wave EM solver.

articleTitle: Analysis of Phase Discretization Influence on the Monochromatic Aberrations of Focusing Metasurface Based on Generalized Rayleigh-Sommerfeld Diffraction Theory
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the effect of phase discretization on the monochromatic aberrations of a planar focusing metasurface. A series of focusing metasurfaces with constant aperture and different numerical aperture (NA) are synthesized by availably discrete phase distributions instead of the ideally continuous phase maps. Under normal and oblique illumination of a Gaussian plane-wave, their diffraction field patterns are computed by the generalized Rayleigh-Sommerfeld diffraction integral. The focusing parameters describing the beam shape and the Strehl ratio quantifying the aberrations are then extracted from numerical results and comparatively analyzed. It is demonstrated that the flat metasurface with increasing phase levels can obtain better focus yet miserably more Strehl ratio decrement for increasing incident angles and NA implying worse Comatic aberrations.

articleTitle: A Novel Conformal Travelling-Wave Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A conformal series-fed microstrip array antenna design for pointing the circularly polarized major lobe broadside is presented. By utilizing the proposed analytical model, the spacings of the array elements within the conformal aperture are computed for a cylindrical surface of a particular radius, and the element-specific spacings of the patch radiators within each element are computed as well. Both sets of spacings are critical to produce a broadside circularly polarized major lobe at the design frequency. An in-line quarter wave matching section is added to each array element. Electromagnetic simulations of the X-band conformal array antenna verify the proposed design approach.

articleTitle: Measured versus Simulated Results of a Dual Band, Hybrid Substrate, and Shared Aperture Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a dual band and dual polarization antenna that shares a common aperture. The low frequency element is an annular ring antenna with a shorting wall to suppress surface waves and increase isolation between excitation ports. The high frequency element is a concentric patch. Both elements use orthogonal feeds to allow either horizontal or vertical polarization. Our results show performance of the annular ring at 3.2 GHz and the concentric patch at 11.1 GHz. We reduce the footprint of the annular ring by loading with a dielectric of ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>=6.15 and loading the concentric patch with a dielectric of ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>=2.33.

articleTitle: Prediction of Impulse Response of a Flexible Wide-band Antenna for WBAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a study of impulse response in time domain is introduced for wide-band antenna. The proposed monopole antenna which was fabricated on flexible substrate has compact area that makes it suitable for wearable applications. Transmission coefficient is measured between two identical antennas. Experimental results are performed while the antennas were in both straight/bent configuration setups in multi-reflections environment. Received pulses in order of ns are calculated for all antenna setups. Cross correlation is applied between input and received pulses in order to comprehend and compare the impulse response for every antenna configuration scenario.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Wideband Connected Slot Array for Wide-Angle Scanning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile wideband connected slot array is proposed for wide-angle scanning applications. By introducing a parasitic parallel slot, the input impedance of the element is reduced. A metasurface loaded over the array is utilized to achieve a wide-angle impedance matching. The proposed array can achieve 69.2% (1.35-2.78 GHz) bandwidth with active VSWR ≤3 when scanning up to ±60° in both E- and H- planes, and the profile is only 0.09<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λL</sub> at the lowest operating frequency. The low cross-polarization, simple structure and the light-weight are also advantages of the proposed array.

articleTitle: Novel Reconfigurable Circularly Polarized Square Slot Antenna for underground mine
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a reconfigurable low profile circular polarized square slot antenna is proposed. The antenna ground plane has four parallel resonator, with six switches embedded over the resonators to alter their lengths. By controlling and combining different states of the switches (ON/OFF), three different frequency bands and three stop bands are obtained. Simulated results of the antenna system showed a good performance in terms of bandwidth control.

articleTitle: Design and Measurements of a 1m Ka-Band Mesh Deployable Reflector Antenna for CubeSats
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: CubeSats offer innumerable possibilities for affordable space missions since they can be piggybacked with conventional satellites during launch and can be built from Commercial Off The Shelf (COTS) components. The small size, however, precludes the use of high gain antennas which are a necessity for advanced space missions requiring high data rates and/or resolution. This work looks to empower future CubeSats by the development of a 1m Ka-band mesh deployable reflector antenna that stows in a volume of just 3U (10x10x30 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>). We detail the mechanical design, deployment strategy and measured results of our antenna. The fabricated antenna demonstrates a measured efficiency of 60% with a half power beamwidth of 0.60° at 35.75GHz, which satisfies the demands of the Radar In CubeSat (RainCube) project envisioned by NASA.

articleTitle: A Wideband High-Gain Conical Short Horn based on a Metasurface-corrected Lens
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband high-gain conical short horn with a wide flare angle is developed by loading a ultrathin planar metasurface lens on the aperture. The lens that exhibits wideband high-efficiency transmission and phase changes is composed of two identical dielectric layers, a metallic cross-dipole in the middle and two identical orthogonally-oriented gratings on the two sides. By placing the metasurface lens on the horn aperture, the linearly-polarized spherical wavefront inside the horn can be converted to be a planar one, resulting in high gain. An example compact horn operating at 30 GHz is given. Simulations show an impedance bandwidth of over 30.5%, a peak gain of 28.9 dBi and an aperture efficiency of 49.4%.

articleTitle: Beam Pattern Analysis of 1:5-D Sparse Array for Millimeter-Wave Imaging Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we analysis the beam pattern of a millimeter-wave 1.5-D sparse array with orthogonal element locations, which its general concept was introduced in [1]. We show that the side-lobe level (SLL) is related to the sparsity of the array. Moreover to improve the quality of reconstruction, the side-lobe level must be low. Measured results at 30 GHz show that the quality of reconstruction is improved by controlling the SLL.

articleTitle: Enhanced Axial-Ratio Bandwidth Single-Point-Fed CP Antenna Using Slot Structure Modification
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact single-point-fed circularly polarized antenna with enhanced axial ratio (AR) bandwidth is investigated. A combination of parasitic strips and modified geometry of the wide-slot is used to improve circular polarization (CP) performance of the antenna. The total footprint of the antenna is only 25×25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. With the proposed technique, an impedance bandwidth |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| ≤ -10 dB of ~70-percent (4.2 GHz- 9.05 GHz), and AR bandwidth ≤ 3 dB of 48-percent (5.4 GHz to 8.65 GHz) has been achieved with the average realized gain of 3.1 dBi through the CP operating band. A stable bidirectional radiation pattern with left- hand CP and right-hand CP in the ±z-direction is observed.

articleTitle: Rotational Doppler Effect of Spinning Metasurface in Radar System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate through the use of a spinning polarization-independent metasurface, the ability to detect the rotational Doppler effect from a radar system. The proposed metasurface with ring shape unit cells is polarization independent and can generate an OAM beam by reflecting an arbitrary polarized incident wave. In our demonstration, a radar transmits a normal electromagnetic wave illuminating on the proposed spinning metasurface, the wave interacts with the proposed metasurface and returns as an OAM wave with rotational Doppler shift. As shown from spectrograms based on measured data, the frequency shift is determined by the angular velocity and OAM mode of the proposed metasurface, the measured spinning speed errors are less than 3.6%.

articleTitle: Capacity-Driven Design of Clustered Array Architectures for New Generation 5G MU-MiMo Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of clustered array architectures for next generation 5G Base Stations (BS) is here addressed. An innovative capacity-driven design methodology is formulated to design BS with clustered architectures achieving optimal capacity performances. To validate the effectiveness and to provide some insight on its potentialities, the proposed capacity-driven design approach has been applied in a real-application scenario and compared with a "classical" design methodology.

articleTitle: Mapping Lung Water Signal Distribution on Human Chest and Predition of Lung Water Content
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Measuring lung water change is invaluable for monitoring patients with heart failure and pulmonary diseases and assessing their responses to the treatment. Sensors for such measurement have been developed in Hawaii Advanced Wireless Technologies Institute (HAWTI) and clinical trials have been carried out. In this paper, we use numerical simulations to obtain the signals received by the sensors as a function of lung water content and sensor locations on the human torso. The data are interpolated to obtain a finer distribution of signals on the chest. The higher resolution data are used to train the support vector regression (SVR) machine to establish a prediction model for lung water content as a function of received signal and location of the sensors. The interpolation and SVR methods can save significant simulation time and will be used for building a database for lung water prediction for various human torsos.

articleTitle: Phase-Controlled Beam-Scanning of Arbitrary Antenna Arrays with Far-Field Fixed Nulls
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a synthesis algorithm for the beam-scanning of antenna arrays having fixed null directions in the far-field pattern. The proposed algorithm performs the beam-scanning by phase-only control. Hence, the amplitudes of the array elements are kept constant, while only their excitations are modified. This allows one to maintain a simpler and less expensive feeding network. The algorithm is suitable for arrays of arbitrary geometry. Numerical examples are provided to show the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Antenna Arrays with Beam Steering for 5G Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In 5G cellular communication systems, millimeter-wave (mm-wave) technology will be applied. To compensate the path loss, beam steerable antenna arrays with high gain has to be utilized in both base stations and mobile terminals. This paper will address some challenges of the mm-wave array designs in mobile handsets, which is mainly due to the user's mobility. As examples, some recent researches on solving these challenges are introduced in this paper as well.

articleTitle: Measurement of Dielectric Constants of Liquid Crystals Using Double-Ridged Waveguide Cavity
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Liquid crystals (LCs) are widely used in reconfigurable microwave devices for their voltage tunable dielectric constant and loss. For the design of materials and devices, accurate measurements of the complex permittivity of LCs are required. This paper presents a method of performing microwave characterizations of LCs using a double ridged waveguide cavity and the perturbation method. To realize the broadband test and make operating frequency points distribute uniformly, the multi-mode technique is introduced and 6 modes (TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,0,2n-1</sub>,n= 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6) are chosen as operating modes to work at 5-22 GHz by one cavity. Besides, the sample loading area in the double-ridged waveguide cavity is much smaller and the sample volume required is only about 0.02 ml. Several LCs are measured: a certain commercial mixture MM (Merck), and M1~M3, as developed LC compositions with large dielectric anisotropy and low microwave losses.

articleTitle: Analysis of Lossy SIW Patch Antenna for Near-Field Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A lossy substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) patch antenna with one radiating edge is proposed for near-field communications. The antenna is designed to be as immune as possible to the effects of surrounding objects that are near the antenna, which would detune an ordinary patch antenna and degrade the performance.

articleTitle: A Broadband Mutimode Antenna Based on the Theory of Characteristic Mode
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a four-port multimode antenna designed by the theory of characteristic mode. The antenna is fed by four SMA ports through a feeding network and works at a broadband of 3~6 GHz. Each port of the antenna excites one or more characteristic mode(s) which do not correlate with other ports, resulting in high port-to-port isolation over the operating band. To improve the port reflection, a capacitive mode is added and compensates the imaginary part of the port admittance. The fabricated antenna has been measured, which shows good agreement with simulation.

articleTitle: X-Band Waveguide Coupler with Low Ripple and Losses
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel wideband coupler operating in the frequency bandwidth from 10.7 GHz to 12.8 GHz is presented. The coupler consists of two crossed rectangular waveguides coupled through four circular apertures with different diameters. In order to improve the operating bandwidth and reduce the coupling ripple across the frequency bandwidth, a Chebyshev distribution is used to determine the radius and distance between the apertures. The coupling coefficient in the operating bandwidth is below -30 dB with less than 0.6 dB ripple. The return loss of all the ports is under -15 dB, and the maximum isolation between ports is below -60 dB. The proposed coupler has the advantage of having small size and low losses, which make it appropriate for high-power applications. The whole structure is simulated and optimized using CST microwave studio software and then fabricated and measured. Excellent agreement between measured and simulated results was achieved.

articleTitle: Balanced-Diplexer Frequency Division Duplex Subarray for X-band Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact dual-circularly polarized magneto-electric dipole subarray is proposed as a unit cell of a phased array for geostationary satellites. A balanced-diplexer is fully integrated with the array to enable frequency division duplex at X-band. The proposed architecture allows to have high rejection between transmit and receive bands without increasing the complexity of diplexers. Isolation > 50 dB, gain > 15 dBic, symmetric patterns, and axial ratio <; 2 dB are demonstrated computationally and experimentally.

articleTitle: Statistical Bayesian Inversion of Ultra-deep Electromagnetic LWD Data: Trans-dimensional Markov Chain Monte Carlo with Parallel Tempering
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Solving the inversion of ultra-deep electromagnetic measurements is a challenging task in directional resistivity logging while drilling (LWD) service. The target is to reconstruct the subsurface formation structure around the borehole in the real-time drilling job. Due to the complexity of ultra-deep measurements, the inverse modeling is highly nonlinear and ill-posed. Hence, the conventional methods are insufficient to resolve this problem. In this paper, a statistical data-driven approach is proposed, which combines Bayesian inference and parallel tempering techniques.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison between Single and Multiple Implanted Receivers in a Hybrid Power/Data Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a multiple implanted hybrid system consisting of a high-frequency coil (13.56 MHz) to transfer power, and an ultra-high frequency antenna (905 MHz) for data communication. This hybrid system was compared with a single implanted hybrid design under lateral misalignment condition. We numerically simulated both systems and studied their performance in terms of power and data transfer. The implanted single and multiple receivers are assumed to be buried inside a layered body tissue model at 30 mm distance. Insertion loss (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>) and transmission efficiency (η) in the range of lateral misalignment of -60 mm to 60 mm in step of 10 mm were evaluated. The simulation results show that multiple implanted antenna/coil pair is more stable and efficient than single one. The effeciencies have been increased to reach 250% and 234% for both antenna and coil respectively at aligned condition.

articleTitle: 2D Physical Optics Analysis of the Focal Region of Parallel-Plate Waveguide Lenses
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A physical optics (PO) method for computing the focal-region fields of a parallel-plate waveguide (PPW) lens is presented. A simplified delay line model is used to represent the delay section between inner and outer lens profile. The lens is analyzed by assuming a plane wave incident on the outer contour. For a given lens geometry, the resulting maximum field loci at different angles of incidence are reported. The close agreement with full-wave results by a commercial simulator validates the applicability of the underlying two-dimensional (2D) lens model. The developed tool is several orders of magnitude faster than the general purpose full-wave simulation and therefore presents an efficient auxiliary tool for the design of lens feed networks.

articleTitle: Eigenmode Analysis of Printed-Ridge-Gap-Waveguide Cavity and Its Application to Antenna design
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The resonant characteristics of a printed ridge gap waveguide cavity are analyzed using the eigenmode method. The field distributions of typical modes and the relevant eigen frequencies are presented. One cavity-backed slot antenna based on the eigenmode results is proposed with the desirable input matching and radiation performance. That could demonstrate the feasibility of antenna design using printed ridge gap waveguide as a resonant cavity.

articleTitle: Analysis of Circular Polarization Properties of 4x4 Arrays at Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper investigates polarization properties of circularly polarized 4x4 patch arrays at Ka-band for classical arrangement and sequential rotation of elements. The investigations are performed for various values of axial ratio of array elements and different steering angles. The simulated results are validated by measurements of fabricated arrays.

articleTitle: K-factor and Correlation Analysis of a 2×2 MIMO Off-body Channel Inside a Mine
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the experimental characterization of a 2 × 2 MIMO channel at a frequency 2.4 GHz in a mine environment. The performed study includes the analysis of the spatial correlation between the MIMO system subchannels for both Line-Of-Sight (LOS) and Non-Line-Of-Sight (NLOS). Moreover, the Rician K-factor was directly estimated from the PDP results. The correlation and K-factor results were used to explain previously published Capacity results.

articleTitle: 3D Multiscale Unconditionally Stable Time-Domain Modeling of Nonlinear RF Thin Film Magnetic Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An unconditionally stable three-dimensional (3D) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithm has been proposed to solve simultaneously Maxwell's equations and the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation with full nonlinear effects. The proposed algorithm can predict the dynamic interaction between magnetic spins and EM fields. The accuracy of the modeling has been validated by 1. Small signal simulation of a linear ferrite isolator and 2. Large signal simulation of the dispersive permeability of a continuous ferrite film. The simulations agree with the theoretical and experimental predictions, under both linear and nonlinear circumstances. Specifically, the algorithm has fully revealed that sufficiently large RF power can decrease the ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) frequency and suppress the permeability.

articleTitle: Low-Cost MoM-Solution of Blood Tube Scattering
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an efficient low-computation numerical solution of the problem of two-dimensional mm-wave scattering of EM waves by test tubes in lossy blood. This is achieved through an efficient use of the moment method along with approximate impedance boundary conditions. Both exact and approximate solutions are consistent with the results obtained using full-wave EM solvers, but with only a fraction of the computation cost.

articleTitle: A Dodecahedron Sequential Rotation Antenna Array for Space Division Multiple Access
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a three-dimensional switched beam antenna suitable for the Space Division Multiple Access paradigm. The antenna is arranged on an half-dodecahedron and its elements operates in circular polarization, hence it is suitable for indoor operation. When hanging from the ceiling, the proposed antenna is the key-component for MIMO system and for position estimation in indoor scenarios. The paper describes the antenna design and the corresponding simulated results.

articleTitle: Accurate Solution of Electromagnetic Scattering by Penetrable Objects with Changeable Shapes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Traditional electromagnetic (EM) analysis assumes that the objects or structures are unchanged in shape and geometric discretization is fixed in numerical solutions. As flexible electronic materials appear and could be applied more widely in the design of electronic devices and systems, such assumptions may not be valid anymore. When the shapes or boundaries of objects change, their geometries should be remeshed and the process is very tedious. We propose a different approach to solve the problem by transforming a domain integral into a boundary integral based on the Green-Gauss theorem so that the domain discretization can be removed and remeshing is not necessary when the shapes change. A numerical example is shown to demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach.

articleTitle: Topological Metasurfaces for Robust One-dimensional Waves
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The discovery of topological condensed matter systems has rapidly been followed by the advent of their photonic analogues, motivated by the prospect of backscattering-immune light propagation. So far, however, photonic topological phases have mainly relied on engineering bulk modes in photonic crystals and waveguide arrays in two-dimensional systems. Here, we present symmetry protected topological states akin to quantum spin/valley Hall effect by engineering surface modes over metasurfaces of infinitesimal thickness. As a result, the proposed structures support robust gapless edge states, which are highly confined and guided virtually along a one-dimensional line rather than a surface interface. In order to generate the modal degeneracies required for emulating the spin degree of freedom, we exploit the internal symmetry of the electromagnetic field by overlapping hexagonal unit cells of complementary metasurfaces. Conversely, we emulate the valley degree of freedom by reducing the C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6υ</sub> lattice symmetry of a hexagonal cell-based metasurface of either inductive or capacitive electromagnetic response into C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> point symmetry. The simplicity of the proposed structures makes them attractive as a tabletop platform for the study of photonic topological phases, as well as for applications benefiting the compactness of metasurfaces and the potential of topological insulators.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Bull’s-eye Antennas for Dual-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact dual-band bull's-eye antenna is presented using a multi-layer substrate. Both the corrugations and antenna feed are designed to provide dual-band operation. The antenna is designed on printed circuit boards (PCBs) to lower the cost and weight, in addition to allowing for ease of integration of active and passive circuit components. The measurement and simulation results agree very well and it is shown that an antenna realized gain of more than 16 dBi can be achieved for both bands of interest.

articleTitle: Inkjet Printed Lange Coupler for Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a novel application for inkjet printing for the use in lange coupler designs and in antenna integration. Lange couplers is a subclass of quadrature couplers where the coupled and through ports have a wideband input match, 3 dB split and 90 degree phase shift relative to branchline couplers. However, traditional lange couplers need crossover paths which requires the need for multilayer structures with vias or bondwires, which adds manufacturing complexity. With inkjet printing, the manufacturing complexity is drastically decreased by utilizing single process fabrication using only one machine, the inkjet printer. This work demonstrates, for the first time, a fully inkjet printed lange coupler structure and the easy of integrating this process into designing and fabricating antenna systems.

articleTitle: 1D Slotted Waveguide Antenna with Controlled Beamwidth and Sidelobe Level Ratio
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Slotted waveguide antennas (SWAs) are widely used in high power microwave applications. In this paper, the slots displacements in broadwall SWAs, previously used to control the SWA sidelobe level ratio (SLR), are further investigated to also adjust the beamwidth of the SWA. A modified Taylor array design method is used to estimate the excitations of the SWA slots leading to independently controllable SLR and first-null beamwidth (FNBW). The slots displacements are then calculated from these excitations. An example is presented where the SWA has 7 slots and the proposed method is employed to find the displacements required for desired SLR and FNBW.

articleTitle: Application of Dielectric and Magnetic Layered Substrate in Antenna Gain Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we propose a method to improve antenna gain using magnetic and dielectric layers. The use of Artificial Magnetic Conductors (AMC) and Magneto-Dielectric (MD) for increasing gain was proposed before. The method we are proposing has similar effect on gain with a simpler structure. We suggest using layers of dielectric and magnetic materials in sequence as the antenna substrate. This method offers less complexity and easier fabrication than AMC and MD methods. For proof of concept, different monopole antenna configurations are investigated and their performances are evaluated at the resonance frequency. The proposed monopole antennas based on dielectric/magnetic materials layered substrate have showed a superior radiation performance compared to previously studied monopole on dielectric or MD substrate. The sequence of the materials can be optimized in terms of materials' properties and physical dimensions in order to achieve the desired operating frequency band and antenna radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: Split Ring Loaded Dual-polarized Dielectric Resonator Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, dual-polarized dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs) with split rings are proposed and investigated. The antennas are designed to operate at the center frequency of 1.25 GHz. The effect of the DRA length to height ratio on cross-polarization is studied. The validity of two cross-polarization reduction techniques, i.e. short probe-stripline differential feeding and SRR gap width reduction, are verified. A bandwidth of 76.6 MHz and below -25 dB cross-polarizations are achieved from an antenna with electrical dimensions of 0.122λ * 0.054λ * 0. 001λ for X-polarization and 0.137λ * 0.046λ * 0.001λ for Y-polarization.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Low-Profile Feeds for UWB Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 5-21 GHz fixed beam array system based on a novel radial LTCC feed and a PUMA array is presented. Through simulations it was found that total efficiency (antenna and feed) is >70%, with VSWR mostly less than 3 even for very small (18 element) arrays. The overall profile of the 4:1 bandwidth feed is less than 0.3 wavelengths at the highest frequency.

articleTitle: Double Layer Hard Surface for Dual-Polarization applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new type of dual-polarized double layer hard surface is introduced. The structure consists of two stacked dielectric substrates. The bottom substrate act as high impedance electromagnetic bandgap structure and the top one is loaded with longitudinal strips, which transfer the upper surface to a GO characteristic of a hard surface. To show the validity of the proposed structure, transmission between dipoles and monopoles is tested. The structure is supposed to provide flexibility to the nature of the hard surface in terms of bending and realization of a relatively thin (<; λ/2) dually polarized guiding structure.

articleTitle: Propagation Characteristics of a Reconfigurable Plasmonic Rectangular Groove Grating Waveguide Using Periodically Photoinduced Plasma
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents theoretical investigations on propagation characteristics of an infinite subwavelength rectangular groove grating with the effectively variable array period and the effectively variable groove depth using periodically photo-induced plasma semiconductor. Using mode matching technique, it is theoretically discussed about the effect of the interaction between surface-plasmon-like waves on the parts of the structured metal surface with effectively different depth on the propagation characteristics.

articleTitle: Manipulation of Microstrip Antenna Directivity and Radiation Pattern using Negative Index Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metamaterials designed to generate multi- negative low-loss passbands are placed at various distances from an X-band patch antenna to examine their effects on the antenna directivity and radiation pattern. The metamaterials being placed half a wavelength away from the antenna, not only improve directivity, but also lower side lobe levels.

articleTitle: Wearable Electromagnetic Head Imaging Using Magnetic-based Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wearable electromagnetic head imaging system for brain bleeding detection using a flexible magnetic-based antenna array is presented. The antenna arrays in a wearable strap-like structure are designed on a polymer magnetic composite substrate with a dielectric permittivity of 5.5, and magnetic permeability of 4. The antenna consists of a conventional rectangular patch with row of shorting pins. The combination of the remarkable magnetic properties material and the shorting pins results in a compact, unidirectional and wideband (0.72 GHz- 1.58 GHz) antenna that satisfies the requirement of the electromagnetic imaging system. A 24-array of antenna is embedded inside the substrate in the form of a wearable strap that can fit an average human head. The antenna arrays are preliminarily evaluated on an average head model using CST software. The simulation-based constructed images of bleeding emulating target using a confocal image algorithm indicate the possibility of using such approach as a wearable system to detect bleeding inside the brain.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Compact and High-Performance Two-Dimensional Grid Array for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design and evaluation of a high gain, wideband, compact antenna grid array at millimeter-wave (mm-wave) band for the 5th generation (5G) applications. The designed microstrip-fed antenna array offers an operating bandwidth of 5.5 GHz in the range of 27.5-33 GHz. The realized gain in the proposed range of operation is above 9 dBi with a peak gain of 11.34 dBi at 32.5 GHz. The numerically calculated efficiency is above 80% in the whole band of 5.5 GHz. The proposed antenna array is a potential candidate for the 5G cellular handheld devices as well as in the indoor base-stations.

articleTitle: Development of Higher-Order DG-FETD Tool for Efficient Modeling of Complex Electromagnetic Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Discontinuous Galerkin finite-element time-domain (DG-FETD) method is one of the most attractive time domain techniques. It is a good combination of DG approach and FETD technique together with special features. Temasek Laboratories at National University of Singapore (TL@NUS) has put a lot of efforts to develop DG-FETD tool for efficient modeling of complex electromagnetic (EM) structures. This paper summarizes main techniques implemented in process of developing our DG-FETD tool that has been verified through the simulation of many EM structures.

Author Keywords: higher order tetrahedral elements; discontinuous Galerkin (DG) approach

articleTitle: A Modified Magnetoelectric Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposed an antenna for microwave imaging application, which is based on the concept of a kind of magnetoelectric (ME) dipole antenna. The working band is 1.13-4.91 GHz, with dimension of 64mm×60mm×46mm and good directivity, which is suitable for use in the application of microwave imaging. The proposed antenna is fabricated and its performance is measured in the anechoic chamber. The measured results meet well with the corresponding simulated results.

articleTitle: A K-band SIW High Gain Planar Antenna with Parabolic Metalized Via-holes Reflector
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a high gain planar antenna with parabolic reflector made by metalized via-holes is proposed. An H-plane horn antenna based on the substrate integrated waveguide is used as a feed on offset focus position of the parabolic shaped metalized via-holes. Reflection coefficient of the antenna is below -10dB from 20 GHz to 30 GHz. The gain of the planar antenna is 17 dB at the frequency of 25 GHz, which is 8.5 dB higher than the gain of the feed of H-plane horn antenna.

articleTitle: 2D Periodic Leaky-Wave Antennas in the Microwave and Optical Regimes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 2D periodic leaky wave antenna produces a narrow and highly directive beam at broadside. This structure is optimized and implemented in the microwave regime and also the optical regime. The antenna radiation characteristics as well as the modal properties of the 2D periodic leaky wave structure have been studied. The 2D periodic leaky wave antenna (LWA) for microwave frequencies is then further optimized in the shape of a cross to eliminate grating lobes.

articleTitle: Automotive RADAR Front-End with Added Target Estimation in Elevation Plane
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work design of antenna front-end is presented for automotive RADAR applications. The antenna is designed to operate from 76-81 GHz. The unit element consists of two coupled stack patches. Four 8×1 element arrays are designed and fabricated, the measured results are in accordance with the simulated results. A robust technique is also proposed for measuring the target elevation. These type of sensors are useful for high vehicles, which have greater space from ground to floor of the vehicle and are difficult to detect through conventional sensors.

articleTitle: Steerable Spiral Slot Reflectarray at 66 GHz Using Micromachined Movable Silicon Slab
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A reconfigurable reflectarray element operating in the V-band (50-75 GHz) is proposed in this paper. The element consists of a previously designed metal-only element made of varying slot sizes. The design was able to achieve 360<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> of phase coverage by a change in length of the element's L-shaped slots. In this work, the L-slots slots are fixed while a deeply etched silicon structure slab is used to tune the reflected phase. The slab moves between the L-shape slots at points where the element's electric field is at its maximum. This architecture results in 328<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> of phase coverage with a maximum loss of 0.9 dB at 66 GHz.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Models and Prony’s Analysis of Electromagnetic Designs Using Genetic Programing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Prior electromagnetic designs using Genetic Programing (GP) showed that GP based designs are competitive and often exceed those based on human expertise. Resulting topologies, however, are unconventional and are less understood. In this paper we propose equivalent circuit models and use Prony's method analysis to explain the high-performance characteristics of the GP designs. Simulation and example analysis are focused on Artificial Magnetic Conductors (AMCs) designed using GP. Ansys Q3D Extractor is used to help determine the RLC component values of the complex computer designed pattern. The equivalent model and multiple resonant results from Prony's method show that complex computer designed AMCs can be explained with electromagnetic and circuit theories.

articleTitle: Modular Phased Array Design Through a Tile-Dimension Tapering Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work proposes a novel synthesis method for tiled rectangular shaped arrays, partitioned using two types of square tiles, controlled in phase by a single phase shifter. In order to maximize the efficiency of the amplifiers, an isophoric feeding network is proposed while the aperture tapering is achieved by means of a module sizes tapering strategy. A multi-objective optimization is used to find the optimal tiling configuration, minimizing the side lobes level, and the number of modules.

articleTitle: Off-Body Dipole Antenna with Dogbone-Shaped AMC Bending on the Human Arm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An off-body dipole antenna with a dogbone AMC structure is introduced for 5.2-GHz body-worn wireless applications. The design consists of a dual-dipole element and an AMC structure that produces a broadside radiation pattern. The AMC structure is used to shield the human body from radiation resulting in very low specific absorption rate (SAR) of 0.356 W/Kg.
