Finally, a way to compromise performance between bending and no-bending conditions was presented. This antenna is a good candidate for wearable applications.

articleTitle: Optimal Synthesis of Maximally Robust Antenna Arrays by Means of Circular Interval Arithmetics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a novel method for the optimal synthesis of linear arrays, maximally robust with respect to calibration and mutual coupling errors. Exploiting the theory of the Circular Interval Arithmetics, analytic and reliable power pattern bounds are used within the optimization, in order to assure the robustness of the designed array with respect to calibration and mutual coupling errors. The synthesis is formulated as a convex problem, providing optimal solutions subject to arbitrary upper bound constraints on the power pattern side-lobes.

articleTitle: A Physical Optics Simulator for Dielectric Bodies Characterization Using a Multistatic Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a Physical Optics simulator able to predict the electromagnetic response of dielectric materials on top of metallic bodies is presented. The simulator is being used for the validation of a prototype of multistatic radar able to detect and identify hidden items carried under clothing in security checkpoints.

articleTitle: Coupling Reduction of Printed Yagi Antenna Arrays for Millimeter-wave Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, methods for reduction of coupling between receiving and transmitting antenna arrays are proposed and tested. Coupling between RX and TX causes saturation and a higher noise level in IF. So, coupling reduction improves image quality of system. Antenna element of arrays are printed antipodal Yagi-Uda antenna with greater than 8 dBi gain and higher than 4 GHz bandwidth. Frequency bandwidth of this imaging system is 27 to 30.5 GHz. Half power beamwidth of this antenna element is larger than 90 dB. Front to back ratio of this antenna is improved in this paper to 30 dB at 29 GHz.

articleTitle: RF Channel Propagation Modeling for Wireless Sensor Networks in Intelligent Transportation Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: One of the most relevant challenge of Smart Cities is an effective transport service in terms of safety, mobility, environment and data. In this sense, it is important to investigate the vehicular propagation by means of 3D deterministic tools in urban scenarios, for Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) applications. In this work, the vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) radio wave propagation for an urban infrastructure wireless communication system has been assessed for 5.9 Ghz. A realistic urban scenario has been implemented in an in-house 3D Ray Launching algorithm and Large-Scale and Small-Scale analysis are presented and discussed. Results and analysis provide useful information for optimal node location in the planning phase of radio communication deployment.

articleTitle: Novel High-Performance, Dual-Polarized, Crossed-Vertically-Fed Microstrip Antenna Array for Multifunction Phased Array Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design and fabrication of a novel dual-polarized crossed-vertically-fed microstrip patch antenna are presented. Differential feeding method has been meticulously evolved to form a unique excitation technique. The proposed method exhibits extremely high isolation of better than 52 dB between horizontal and vertical polarizations in the entire frequency band (2.7 - 2.9 GHz) while scanning up to 45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>. The proposed antenna has the advantage of utilizing low-cost printed circuit board fabrication technology while presenting high-performance electromagnetic characteristics. Additionally, this technique mitigates the surface wave issues associated with conventional microstrip antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Multiple Scattering Solution of Passive Radiative Transfer Equations Applied to Forests
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In microwave remote sensing of soil moisture, vegetation and forests, the optical thickness of can be significantly larger than unity. Thus the effects of multiple scattering should be considered. In this paper, radiative transfer equations are solved by a numerical iterative approach under passive remote sensing configuration. This approach allows to consider higher order scattering which represents the effects of multiple scattering. This approach is applied for tree trunks in forest fields in order to calculate the brightness temperatures. The deviation between zero-th order brightness temperatures, i.e., the tau-omega model results, and the high order results for forest with VWC of 18 kg/m2, shows the effect of multiple scattering.

articleTitle: Measurement of Hybrid Genetic Programming Synthesized Artificial Magnetic Conductors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The fabrication and measurement of previously proposed artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) designs are presented in this paper. The AMC ground planes were synthesized by a hybrid genetic program (HGP) and were compared with AMC designs found in the literature. The HGP designed AMCs outperformed those in the literature. The performance was determined from full-wave electromagnetic simulations. We also validate the performance of the HGP designed AMCs through fabrication and measurement.

articleTitle: Harmonic-Modulated Nonlinear Metasurface Based on Generalized Phase Conjugation Principle
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a generalized phase conjugation (PC) principle is derived through both the wave interpretation and the quantum interpretation. A harmonic-modulated nonlinear metasurface (HM-NMS) is proposed accordingly. Based on the generalized PC principle, it is demonstrated that the proposed HM-NMS could perform as a phase conjugation mirror (PCM), an optically-controlled beam steering (OCBS) array, and could even transform the plane wave excitations into surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) under optical frequencies.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling and Failure analysis in Phased Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The mutual coupling between the radiating elements in an array environment is discussed. The relation between the mutual coupling and the radiation Characteristic (gain and side lobe level) of the subarrays is presented. Then a model to analyze and design the failure of the phased array system including the mutual coupling between the elements is introduced.

articleTitle: Airborne Measurement of Instrument Landing System Signals using a UAV
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A feasibility study to replaced manned-aircraft in-situ measurement of instrument landing system (ILS) signal strengths at commercial airports with an unmanned aerial vehicle platform was conducted. A ground station was erected to radiate the test ILS signals and measurement equipment, including receiving antennas and a spectrum anayzer, were mounted on a large octocopter UAV. Flight testing shows that measured signal uncertainty is significantly lower than that reported for manned-aircraft measurement. Residual uncertainty appears to be associated with pitch and roll changes of the UAV. Correction of the uncertainties using anechoic-chamber-measured radiation patterns of the UAV-mounted antennas is currently being investigated.

articleTitle: Joint Stripmap/Spotlight Synthetic Aperture Radar enabled by Element-Level Digital Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a concept for a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) enabled by element-level digital arrays (EDAs). SARs with arrays which employ analog beamforming for azimuth processing gain are required to trade cross-range resolution for total swath. An EDA mitigates this trade through multiple receive beams, enabling simultaneous spotlight and stripmap SAR. An algorithm is presented along with a demonstration of the realized wide-swath and narrow cross-range resolution.

articleTitle: PCB Bowing Effects on 60 GHz Switched-Beam Antenna Modules
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a method to incorporate the bowing curvature on the 3-D models of 60 GHz switched-beam multilayer antenna modules. This allows such manufacturing effects on the fabricated prototypes to be taken into account in the post-fabrication simulation. The curvature is introduced on the flat 3-D model by intersecting the raised metal patterns with curve solid layers. The method is general and can be applied on any layered structure even if vias are present. The full-wave simulations of the model, with and without the bow, are performed. The reflection coefficients (both measured and simulated) and radiation patterns are compared and analyzed to determine the effects of bowing.

articleTitle: Planar Vertically Polarized Quasi-Yagi Antennas Using Magnetic Current Loops
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel quasi-Yagi antenna based on a magnetic-current-loop-induced electric dipole is presented in this paper. The design emulates the conventional quasi-Yagi antenna by introducing multiple parasitic planar dipole elements that function as directors. However, unlike conventional designs, the proposed antenna radiates a vertically polarized wave by employing virtual dipoles oriented perpendicular to the plane. This eliminates the restriction of positioning the antenna at the edge of the board, providing increased flexibility of integration with microstrip circuitry. The proposed topology is verified through full wave simulation using ANSYS HFSS for antennas consisting of one, two, and five dipole elements.

articleTitle: A convenient rewriting to the 2D inverse scattering problem based on the reduced scattered field
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new model for two-dimensional electromagnetic inverse scattering is introduced by means of a convenient rewriting of the pertinent integral equation and by exploiting the ‘reduced scattered field’, which is underlying a recently introduced qualitative method. The proposed inverse scattering model exhibits a lower degree of nonlinearity with respect to parameters embedding dielectric characteristics as compared to the traditional model, thus suggesting its exploitation in the solution of the inverse problem.

articleTitle: A High Gain Broadband Quasi-Yagi Dielectric Lens Antenna for 5G and Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A high gain wideband microstrip-fed Quasi-Yagi antenna is designed for 5G and millimeter-wave applications. The gain of the proposed Quasi-Yagi antenna is enhanced by a planer perforated dielectric lens resulting in (11-13) dBi realized gain over the frequency band from 28 to 38 GHz with a cross-polarization level better than -25 dB. Furthermore, the presented antenna has radiation and aperture efficiency better than 90% at 30 GHz. The proposed antenna is scaled for different millimeter frequencies and exhibits a competitive performance that makes it suitable for a wide range of mm-wave applications include imaging, high data-rate communication systems (5G backhaul) and automotive radars.

articleTitle: An Efficient Basis-Free Loop-Star Preconditioner Using Sparse Direct Solvers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: When projectors are used to formulate the loop-star preconditioning, a sparse but singular graph-Laplacian matrix must be inverted. In this article, the charge neutrality condition is enforced to remove the zero singular value of this matrix and a sparse direct solver is used to invert the result. While the formulation is low-frequency stabilized and requires few extra operations per iteration, the number of iterations remains high. The iteration count is improved by combining it with an elementdiagonal sparse preconditioner.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Planar 2×2 Dipole Array Antenna Fed by a Modified 4-way Gysel Power Divider
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized high gain planar 2×2 dipole array antenna for WLAN, RFID, radar, and satellite communication applications is proposed. The proposed array antenna consists of four planar dipole antennas and a modified 4-way Gysel power divider. The antenna uses 3 stacked metal layers and a metal reflector under the antenna boosts overall antenna gain. The size of the designed antenna on FR4 substrate was 150 mm × 150 mm × 20 mm (1.25λ0 × 1.25λ0 × 0.17λ0) including the reflector. The designed antenna had left hand circular polarization (LHCP), and its measured circular gain value was 8.7 ~ 9.62 dBic at 2.4 ~ 2.6 GHz. The measured axial ratio (AR) was 0.3 ~ 2.2 dB at the same frequency band of interest.

articleTitle: Modern Approaches and Self-Evaluation Tools for Teaching Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents novel educational approaches and tools for training and motivating students in the field of Electromagnetism and EM Engineering science. The proposed training program and examination tool have been experimentally validated within Bachelor and Master courses by the ELEDIA Research Center.

articleTitle: Utilization of Symmetries in Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The utilization of symmetries on operators within method of moments is presented. Three examples are presented and commented upon - (i) the separation of the problem into a set of smaller sub-problems solved independently making significant reduction in computational time, (ii) effective modal tracking where a decision on modal crossing is made in a deterministic manner, and (iii) a design of feeding schemes to obtain orthogonal channels to be used in multiple-input and multiple-output systems.

articleTitle: Band-notched Reconfigurable Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Parasitic Elements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel band-notched reconfigurable rectangular dielectric resonator antenna is presented. It is fed by step-impedance transform microstrip line with truncated ground plate. By the incorporation of two p-i-n diode switches and parasitic square ring elements surrounding the dielectric resonator, tunable rejection bands are achieved. Depending on the location of the switches, the square ring resonator exhibits different band-notched frequency, corresponding to different resonant length.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Cross-Correlation Green’s Function for MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate the possibility of analytically evaluating the frequency-domain Cross-correlation Green's functions (CGFs), which helps in estimation of far-field correlation in MIMO systems from the antenna current distribution. We propose a robust truncated series-approximation formula to calculate the CGF tensor components, thereby eliminating the requirement of numerically integrating complex exponential functions. Using examples involving vertical dipole pairs, we highlight the inter-connection between the number of terms required in the truncated series-approximation and the normalized inter-element spacing. The proposed analytical evaluation scheme will facilitate integration of these CGFs into optimal synthesis of MIMO antenna systems.

articleTitle: A Side-Edge Frame Printed Eight-Element Antenna Array for Quad-Band MIMO Operations in the 5G Smartphone
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this article, an eight-element antenna array operating in the 2.6/3.5/4.9/5.2-GHz quad-band for 8×8 multi- input multi-output (MIMO) operation in the 5G (fifth-generation) smartphone is presented. The proposed antenna array is formed by eight identical antenna elements printed on the inner surface of the side-edge frame of the smartphone casing. Simulated results show that the impedance bandwidth of each antenna element can fully cover quad-band of 2496-2690/3400-3600/4800- 5000/5150-5350 MHz for reflection coefficient less than -6 dB (3:1 VSWR). Besides, desired gain, 3-D radiation patterns, total efficiency (more than 40%) are simulated and presented. In addition, good ECC (Envelope Correlation Coefficient) of less than 0.2 for any two antenna elements and acceptable isolation (better than 10.8-dB) are also obtained.

articleTitle: Elliptical Disk Cavity Backed Antenna for UWB Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new Ultra-Wideband (UWB) antenna is presented. The proposed antenna has been designed from a circular metallic ring fed by a capacitive elliptical shaped monopole. A cavity is included at the bottom of the structure in order to generate a unidirectional radiation pattern. Simulation result shows an impedance bandwidth ranging from 3.2 GHz to 8.37 GHz (89.36%) for S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> <; -10 dB and gains upper to 7.75 dBi in the wide bandwidth available, respectively. The proposed antenna has overall dimensions of 0.68λ × 0.68λ × 0.16λ, where λ is the wavelength at the minimum frequency.

articleTitle: A New Design Tool for Shaping the Radiation Pattern of Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recently, we have presented several configurations of microstrip antenna, which exhibit peculiar radiation characteristics due to the topological properties of the vortex modes radiated by the antenna itself. In particular, the performances of these structures are all related to the proper superposition of two different circular polarized modes of patch antennas, radiated by two concentric radiating elements. In this contribution, we show that the proposed configurations are particular cases of a more general design tool, which can be exploited for shaping the radiation pattern of patch antennas in many other different forms. In particular, being the pattern shaping capabilities related to the positions of phase singularity points in the overall radiated beam, we determine the equations that relate the singularity locations to the structural and feeding properties of the radiating structure. Moreover, as a practical example, we show the conditions that allow designing a single radiating structure with a multi-beam radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Reduced Active Impedance Variation By Using Time Modulated Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we investigate the active impedance of Time Modulated Array (TMA) as a low-cost and simple beamforming architecture. Since the antenna elements in TMA are periodically turned on and off, the active impedance of this structure has less variation compared to a phased array architecture. In this paper, we have compared the active impedance of a TMA structure and that of the phased array for different cases. The active reflection coefficient of the TMA is always below -10 dB, while the impedance of the phased array becomes unmatched for certain scan angles.

articleTitle: Design of a High-Gain, Wideband, Circularly Polarized Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband microstrip patch antenna with a hexagonal wide-slot is proposed for circular polarization. In simulation, the achieved operational -10-dB impedance bandwidth is between 1.49 GHz and 3.75 GHz (86%) and 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth is between 2.05 GHz and 3.10 GHz (41%). The 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth is fully included in the -10-dB impedance bandwidth. The realized gain in average of the antenna is 7.5 dBic in the common bandwidth between the -10-dB impedance bandwidth and 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth. The total volume of the antenna is 0.35λ×0.35λ×0.19λ and the electrical size is a kr of 1.31.

articleTitle: Analysis of Multiple Objective Cost Functions for Free Space Material Characterization with Genetic Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work continues the research of implementing a genetic algorithm (GA) to perform electromagnetic characterization of RF magnetic materials. Four independent measurements of the Fresnel reflection coefficient are used to compute the multiple objective cost function. Characterization results using synthetic data are presented for a conductor-backed magnetic test sample.

articleTitle: Special Functions for Radiation from Sources Close to an Electrically Large Conducting Convex Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Acoustic hard and soft Fock functions and their variations have been used as special functions in asymptotic methods to compute electric fields pertaining to direct and surface-diffracted rays due to sources on or slightly off an electrically large conducting convex surface. Numerical evaluation of these functions have been studied and reported well. Hence, formulations are available for accurate evaluation of these functions in different intervals of their variable. However, they do not yield accurate and continuous results for the derivatives of these functions. In this paper, the existing formulations are modified to evaluate the Fock functions, and their derivatives. The modified formulations provide accurate results for the functions and their derivatives, and their continuity at the boundaries between adjacent intervals in both magnitude and phase.

articleTitle: Frequency-Selective Rasorber with Tri-resonant Absorption Band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a rasorber with broadband absorption response is presented. The absorption band is located below the transmission window, and a good absorptivity is achieved. Cross-frame and cross-slot FSSs are employed to fulfill the desired rasorber performance. Tri-resonant behavior is obtained by the lossy cross-frame array and used to consume the wide-band incident power. Furthermore, a stable absorption performance is achieved until 50° incident angle. The current distribution and simulated results are given to illustrate the operating mechanism of the presented design.

articleTitle: Beam Steering Using Active Superstrate Antenna for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an active FSS superstrate antenna operating at 5.25 GHz for beam steering applications. The superstrate antenna consists of metallic patches on its one side and metallic grids on its other side. The variation in the reflection phase is created by gradating the mesh grid array, which results in the phase delay of the radiated fields. The tilted radiation beam is produced due to the phase delay of the radiated fields. The proposed structure also helps in making the antenna more directive which enhances the gain while maintaining the cavity height of λ/4.

articleTitle: On the Decoupling Robustness of Distributed Magnetic Traps in Biological Loaded Dual Tuned MR coils
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The robustness of Distributed Magnetic Traps (DMTs) for Magnetic Resonance (MR) coils decoupling in the presence of a biological load is analyzed with numerical analysis. A DMT realized as printed spiral resonators (SRs) has been already presented by the authors along with an accurate equivalent circuit which predicts their resonance frequencies, achieving an excellent agreement with simulations. Here, SRs' peculiar decoupling effect at the desired Larmor's frequency has been numerically analyzed in presence of a phantom mimicking biological tissue properties.

articleTitle: RCS Reduction of a Microstrip Antennas Using Cross Polarization Conversion Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, polarization conversion metasurface for both in-band and out-of-band radar cross section reduction and gain improvement of a microstrip patch antenna is presented. The polarization converter metasurface is realized using anisotropic unit cell has a polarization conversion ratio (PCR) of more than 98% and 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>±26<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> reflection phase deference between its diagonal axes. A chessboard-like metasurface is realized using this unit cell and its mirrored one to achieve the required phase cancellation. The patch antenna is placed at the center of the chessboard and surrounded by the anisotropic unit cell. RCS of the antenna is significantly reduced while its radiation characteristics are preserved and its gain is improved by about 2dB. The proposed design is being fabricated now and the measured results will be presented and discussed at the symposium.

articleTitle: Liquid Waveguide Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel concept of liquid waveguide antenna (LWA) is proposed in this paper. An X-band liquid rectangular waveguide is demonstrated as an example for concept verification. A hollow-wall dielectric rectangular waveguide with standard aperture size is firstly designed and realized by 3-D printing technique. Subsequently, two rectangular metal rings are employed to seal the two waveguide ports so as to constrain liquid inside the waveguide. Conductive fluidic material is therafter filled into the hollow-wall rectangular waveguide to form the LWA. Simulation results verified that the proposed liquid rectangular waveguide has similar electromagnetic properties compared with traditional solid metal rectangular waveguides. Eventually, a Bull's eye waveguide antenna is designed to further demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed LWA.

articleTitle: Design Consideration of Synthetic Phased-Array Antenna Systems for 5-G Mobile Wireless Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Active Synthetic Phased-Array Antenna Sensors will significantly enhance the wireless performance for 5-G Mobile-Network application. It is built on the concept of integrating and interfacing optimized MIMO network systems with primary focus on achieving high spectral efficiency, link reliability, and optimum power operation. The design for these sensors is flexible and can be reconfigured easily for brand range 5-G applications. These systems are especially adaptable to mobile structures such as Robotics and the like operating at extreme environments. The main concerns are channel fading, blind spots, various forms of radiation interferences, cyber security related issues, power consumption efficiency, latency, and effective-maintenance/logistics.When deploying such advanced phased-array sensors on mobile 5-G platforms, it is essential for one to understand the RADHAZ (radiation hazards) impact for operations at various level of radiation. Important concerns are the "hot-spots" generations, these are very crucial for the mobile wireless network community.

articleTitle: Analysis of a U-slot Patch Using Characteristic Mode Analysis and Coupled Mode Theory
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Patch antennas incorporating a U-shaped slot are well-known to have relatively large (about 30%) impedance bandwidths. This paper uses Characteristic Mode Analysis to show a classic U-slot patch geometry supports in-phase and anti-phase coupled modes that occur within Coupled Mode Theory.

articleTitle: Frontiers in Reflectarray Design
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of wide reflectarray antennas (RA) featuring complex unit cells through a scalable, efficient, and effective approach based on the System-by-Design (SbD) paradigm is investigated in this work. Towards this end, the customization of the SbD loop to the RA synthesis problem is described, and the integration of advanced micro-scale modeling techniques based on learning-by-example strategies with macro-scale task-oriented optimization strategies is discussed. A set of preliminary results is illustrated to validate the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Diffraction by a Truncated Slab Filled by Dielectric Material
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper concerns the diffraction of a plane wave by a semi-infinite dielectric slab. A semi analytical solution is derived using the Wiener-Hopf technique through the Fredholm factorization. With this work we present a general methodology capable to deal with angular regions and planar regions filled with arbitrary material.

articleTitle: Modular, Reconfigurable Block Cell Antenna Concept for Millimeter-wave 5G
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A reconfigurable block cell antenna (BCA) concept is proposed for millimeter-wave (mmWave) 5G applications. The 4×4 BCA is exemplified using a low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) process. All ports of the proposed BCA achieve a reflection coefficient below - 10 dB in 28.5 GHz. The proposed BCA features a maximum gain of 7.6 dBi and 15 different modes that can support multiple polarizations and a half of the spherical beamsteering angle.

articleTitle: Dual-band Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact dual-band microstrip line fed rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with defected partial ground plane structure operating at X and Ku-band application is presented. The optimized design resonates at 10.4 GHz and 12.8 GHz. The performance of the antenna with respect to design parameters is studied by carrying out the parametric study using simulation software HFSS and the design is validated experimentally. The prototype designed shows that the X-band resonance has impedance bandwidth of 700MHz, gain of 5 dB, reflection coefficient of -16.9dB and Ku-band resonance has impedance bandwidth of 500MHz, gain of 3.25 dB, reflection coefficient of -18.9 dB. The simulated and measured results show good agreement. The proposed design would be suitable for radar detectors and satellite communication applications.

articleTitle: A Wideband High-Gain Horn Antenna for 140GHz Short-Range Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A horn antenna fabricated by low-cost wire cutting is designed towards short-range beamforming at 140GHz. This antenna connects with a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) transmission line on its bottom, and is excited by a slot etched on the SIW. The measured results of this horn antenna without SIW indicate an impedance bandwidth of over 30GHz centered at 140GHz with a mean gain of 14.7 dBi. When integrating with SIW feed line, the measured mean gain maintains at 14.4 dBi with a fluctuation lower than 2dB.

articleTitle: A Wideband Frequency Beam Scanning Antenna Based on the Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a wideband frequency beam scanning antenna based on the spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) is proposed. The proposed design is employed by a standard 50 ohm coplanar waveguide (CPW) line with periodic holes etched on its middle line to generate a wideband frequency scanning wave. Both numerical simulations and measured results demonstrate the good performance of the proposed structure. Simulation results show that the bandwidth of the proposed antenna is about 63.87% (from 13-25.2 GHz for |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>|<; -10 dB). Moreover, the scanning angle can reach 70° with an average peak gain level of 11.55 dB. The proposed SSPP-based frequency scanning antenna is of great value in planar integrated communication systems.

articleTitle: Experimental Imaging Results of a UAV-mounted Downward-Looking mm-wave Radar
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Optical and thermal sensors mounted on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have been successfully used to image difficult-to-access regions. Nevertheless, none of these sensors provide range information about the scene; and, therefore, their fusion with high-resolution mm-wave radars has the potential to improve the performance of the imaging system. This paper presents our preliminary experimental results of a downward-looking UAV system equipped with a passive optical video camera and an active Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) mm-wave radar sensor. The 3D imaging of the mm-wave radar is enabled by collecting data through the line of motion, thus producing a synthetic aperture, and by using a co-linear MIMO array perpendicular to the motion trajectory. Our preliminary results shows that the fused optical and mm-wave image provides shape and range information, that ultimately results in an enhanced imaging capability of the UAV system.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Dual-Polarized 60 GHz Patch Antenna Array in PCB Process
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 2 × 2 dual-polarized patch antenna array operating at 60 GHz is proposed. Based on the conventional low-cost standard PCB process, for the reliable antenna design a five- laminates stack-up structure is used to reduce the complexity of the manufacturing and cost. To improve the antenna bandwidth and gain performance, a stacked patch is adopted and two probe-fed structures are realized to support both horizontal and vertical polarizations. A 2 × 2 prototype is designed, fabricated, and measured for demonstration. For both polarizations, measurements show that their -10 dB impedance bandwidth can cover the entire 60 GHz band, and their isolation is lower than -22 dB. Moreover, their gain is higher than 10 dBi with a peak gain of about 11 dBi.

articleTitle: Patch Antenna Array With Continuous Frequency and Polarization Tuning For 5G Mid-Band Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A frequency- and polarization-reconfigurable 2×2 patch antenna array is presented for 5G mid-band communications at 3.7 GHz. In this design, patches are alternatively arranged in horizontal and vertical configurations. The reconfigurability is achieved using one short-circuited varactor diode connected with each patch element. Frequency tuning is achieved when all varactors have same capacitance values and provide 45° linear polarization, while right hand or left hand circular polarization is obtained when horizontal and vertical patches have slightly different associated varactor capacitances that leads to 90° radiating phase difference. The proposed design is optimized to cover 3.71-4.15 GHz band with a tuning range of 12.7%.

articleTitle: A Method for Detection of Walls and Large Flat Surfaces in Through-the-Wall SAR Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Through-the-wall imaging using synthetic aperture radar (SAR) provides high-resolution images of hidden objects behind the walls which has many applications in military, security, and rescue operations. Besides imaging of hidden objects, detection of walls provides complete map of buildings' interiors features such as rooms, corridors, and hidden pathways which is required for path planning and threat assessment in rescue and military operations. Unlike targets with small surface size, each point on flat walls provide reflection at certain directions. In this case, forming the image using the entire large aperture has a destructive effect on the image of some points on the wall surface. As a result, in high resolution SAR, the walls are imaged as few discrete points instead of solid lines which may be interpreted as few discrete closely spaced targets. In this paper, a method is presented to discriminate walls and objects with large flat surfaces from limited size objects and determine the existing walls locations and orientations inside the imaged area.

articleTitle: Potentialities of Reduced Beamforming Antennas using Magneto-Electric Dipoles
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose an architecture of array based on parasitic element antennas with multiple excitations. The objective is to improve the directivity of these antenna arrays using Magneto-Electric Dipoles (MED). In this contribution, we consider a 49 (7 X 7) element array with only 8% of the elements directly fed. The others are only fed by couplings and they are loaded on reactive values. The proposed radiating element is compared to a stacked patch in the same reduced array configuration. A maximum directivity of 20 dBi is obtained.

articleTitle: Fast Evaluation of Retarded Electromagnetic Potentials for Quantum Calculations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A fast evaluation of retarded electromagnetic potentials is presented for quantum calculations on a uniform Cartesian grid. The induced potentials are incorporated into the quantum Hamiltonian of the time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) in real space. Both Lorentz and Coulomb gauge-fixed Hamiltonians are implemented using a real-time propagation scheme. The efficiency of the resulting formalism and implementation enables the evaluation of retardation effects on long carbon chains.

articleTitle: A 3D Printed Compact PIFA for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, two compact planar inverted-F antennas (PIFA); (i) a single - band (s-PIFA), and (ii) a dual-band (d-PIFA) planar inverted F-antennas are fabricated using Additive Manufacturing (AM, 3D Printing). The antennas are printed as two separate pieces and snapped together using a LEGO-like assembly process. The simulated reflection coefficient and radiation pattern is shown in the paper. The results of the printed antennas will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: A Ferromagnetic Resonance Measurement System for Small Volume Magnetic Nanowires
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) characterization system for magnetic nanowires on short-circuited coplanar waveguide (CPW) structure. The FMR frequency of cobalt (Co) nanowire chips, with three different volumes-small, medium and large, were measured and compared with Kittel equation. The FMR response of the large chip agrees well with Kittel equation with the mean difference of 0.865GHz. The small and medium chips have higher mean difference values of 1.855GHz and 2.205GHz, respectively. From the FMR response, the signal to noise ratio is reduced as the material volume decreased and resulted in less accurate FMR frequency extraction. Since the lowest detectable signal strength of VNA (Anritsu 37369D) is 0.0002, to detect FMR response accurately for this system, the volume of Co should be greater than 2. 2 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>mm3 and the magnetization should be larger than 317μemu. This paper provides a framework for building identification systems such as nanolabels for low volume biosensing application.

articleTitle: Band-Notched Filtering Crossed Dipole Antenna Without Extra Circuit
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-band dual-polarized (DBDP) filtering antenna for WLAN applications is realized by introducing a band-notch within a wide frequency band. The band-notch (3.4-3.6 GHz) is introduced by modifying the dipole arms into C-shaped split rings without extra filtering circuit. As a result, the proposed antenna covers 2.39-2.69 GHz and 4.98-6.36 GHz for VSWR <; 2. The proposed antenna can realize high gain of 7.5 dBi for the lower band and 9.7 dBi for the higher band. The wideband antenna and the proposed filtering antenna are designed and fabricated, and the simulated and measured results meet well.

articleTitle: A Novel Coding Metasurface Unit for Reconfigurable Reflectors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metasurfaces based merely on passive units present limited functionalities on account of their unchangeable properties. Achieving multifunctional control of EM waves simultaneously in one design has been very challenging to designers. In this paper, we propose a novel active metasurface unit embedded with varactor diodes in microwave band. Through varying the bias voltage, the proposed metasurface units can dynamically change its phase distribution to cover 270 degrees in the frequency range from 4.3 to 5.3GHz. Besides, each metasurface unit can be tuned separately in real time by using metal holes to connect the metallic pattern with the divided floor. Therefore, the metasurface can generate multiple function, such as beam steering, beam shape reconfigurable, and abnormal scatter.

articleTitle: A SIW Leaky-Wave Beam Scanning Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new type of Butler matrix-fed two-dimensional (2-D) beam scanning antenna array using composite right/left-handed (CRLH) substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) technique is proposed. It consists of 4 CRLH SIW LWAs and a wideband feeding Butler matrix as the beam forming network. The proposed array can scan its beams in two dimensions by changing the operating frequency and the input port of the Butler matrix (BM), respectively. The array is fabricated and measured. The main beams can scan in one plane from -60° to 66° continuously by sweeping frequency from 3.7 GHz to 4.7 GHz. In the orthogonal plane, it can point to 4 discrete angles (-36°, -12°, 16°, 36°) by feeding in the different input port of the BM. With a wider coverage of the upper half-space, the low cost, and the low profile, this proposed antenna array is very attractive for a variety of phased array applications, particularly those that require a flush-mounted structure.

articleTitle: Configuration of Network Level Algorithms for Wireless Train Control Systems using Physics-Based Propagation Models
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In communication-based train control (CBTC) systems, as a train travels along a track, it changes its association from one access point (AP) to another, which is referred to as a handoff. Control parameters for handoff algorithms are often set based on desired system requirements, such as outage probability, without considering the effect of the underlying propagation characteristics of the channel on the system performance. Therefore, for typical CBTC systems, conservative safety margins are introduced in order to ensure safe operations leading to potentially sub-optimal system performance. In this paper, we propose a systematic procedure for selecting a control parameter, namely the threshold value, which determines when handoffs are triggered for received signal strength (RSS) based handoff algorithms. The proposed scheme leads to the selection of threshold values that increase the safety margin in addition to reducing the number of handoffs incurred, thereby enhancing the overall CBTC system performance. These enhancements are made possible with the integration of physics-based propagation models and network design that harnesses the propagation characteristics of the underlying wireless channels.

articleTitle: CPW-fed Compact Polarization Diversity UWB MIMO Cup-Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a CPW-fed (coplanar waveguide) compact ultra wide-band (UWB) cup-antenna is designed to operate from 3 GHz to 12 GHz with good matching. The antenna is a semi-elliptical patch and the partial CPW ground is used with two triangular to enhancement the bandwidth. Quadelements from this presented antenna are used to form a MIMO (Multi-Input Multi-Output) system for modern wireless communications. A MIMO arrangement is designed in a square FR-4 substrate with length 55 mm. There is proper isolation among the elements where the isolation coefficient is less than -20 dB. These antennas are designed by two basically different techniques. These are HFSS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> from Ansoft and CST STUDIO SUITE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">™</sup> 2018. The two software packages are basically different; therefore the second has been confirmed the results determined using the first. Good agreement is obtained.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of On-Chip Antennas Using Miniaturized-Element Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A method for improving on-chip antenna with high gain and stable radiation patterns is presented. In this approach, a miniaturized-element frequency selective surface (MEFSS) cover is used over the chip antenna exciter to enhance the radiation and gain. Due to the limitations on the metallic thicknesses in chip, substrate losses, and limitations in real estate, the performance of on-chip antennas is poor. However, the proposed technique solves many of several issues in on-chip antennas. As a proof of concept, a MEFSS cover integrated with an antenna is designed at 10 GHz. The measurement results show a gain improvement of 9 dBi.

articleTitle: Numerical Stability Analysis of M1-D LOD-FDTD Method for Inhomogeneous Coupled Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the numerical stability analysis of multiple one-dimensional locally one-dimensional finite-difference time-domain (M1-D LOD-FDTD) method for inhomogeneous coupled transmission lines. The stability analysis is first performed using the von Neumann method based on Fourier amplification matrix for homogeneous coupled transmission lines. The transition matrix for whole computational domain is next analyzed, which takes into consideration inhomogeneous media. While the M1-D LOD-FDTD method for homogeneous coupled transmission lines is stable based on the von Neumann method, the eigenvalues of transition matrix for inhomogeneous coupled transmission lines may indicate instability. Results show that the stability analysis based on von Neumann Fourier modes alone may not be sufficient to prove stability as it generally assumes homogeneous media.

articleTitle: A 3-D Printed Circularly Polarized Filtering Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel circularly polarized filtering antenna is designed and fabricated. It consists of five resonators and four of them have radiation apertures in the end. Each radiation aperture is truncated to implement left-hand circular polarization. Moreover, high gain can be achieved with the four radiation apertures. The proposed antenna is characterized with a second-order Chebyshev bandpass response with center frequency of 32 GHz and impedance bandwidth of 450 MHz. In order to minimize its size, weight and cost, the antenna is fabricated using 3D-printing technology with ceramic filled resin.

articleTitle: Parametric Analysis of a Dual Band Polarized Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A non-symmetrical single-layer frequency selective surface (FSS), which exhibits a highly stable response to incidence up to 45° is proposed for filtering applications. The structure consists of a set of three dipoles grouped in an "U"-like shape on the same side of an FR4 substrate. A parametric analysis concerning the frequency response in function of the angle of incidence is reported. The structure exhibits a dual band-stop response dependent on the polarization of the incident wave, so it can be tailored to achieve a polarizer.

articleTitle: Image Reconstruction of Freshly Excised Human Breast Tumors using Terahertz Electrical Properties
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work proposes the use of single point pulsed terahertz (THz) transmission spectroscopy implemented on human breast cancer tissues over the frequency range from 0.1 to 3.5 THz. In addition, THz reflection imaging is performed and the data obtained is used to calculate the refractive index and absorption coefficient at each pixel on the tissue. The calculated data at each pixel is then used to construct the THz tomographic images, which demonstrate reasonable differentiation between different tissue types in the excised tumor.

articleTitle: Primary Beams of the Meer KAT Radio Telescope: Measurements and Simulations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A comparison of measured and simulated primary beam patterns of the MeerKAT radio telescope is presented. It is shown that the measured data, after removing noise through aperture projection, displays some asymmetry across the apparent symmetry plane of the offset Gregorian reflector structure. This is absent in the simulated results, but the residual between the simulations and measurements is slowly varying, and mainly due to systematic errors in the geometry of the antenna. This effect will be exploited to estimate the beam patterns of the different reflectors in frequency channels where radio frequency interference has corrupted the measured data.

articleTitle: Multi-user Communication by Electromagnetic Vortex Based on Time Modulated Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel method for multi-user communication based on time modulated array (TMA) has been proposed. The system generates vortex waves with different modes by periodical switching in a uniform circular array (UCA). Information from different users is sent and received through different modes. This method can improve the frequency efficiency in the future 5G communication. Simulation proves that different modes of vortex waves can be generated by periodically switching.

articleTitle: Half Ellipse Magnetic Dipole Antenna for Wide Beam-Width and Low Cross-Polarization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A magnetic dipole antenna in the shape of a half ellipse at 5.8GHz has been proposed here for the first time. The drawback of elliptical micro-strip patch antenna as a linearly polarized antenna is poor polarization purity. Narrow half power beam-width(HPBW) is a traditional shortcoming of micro-strip patch antenna. The proposed antenna has wide half power beam-width and a low cross-polarization characteristic. By parameter study with various sizes of half ellipse magnetic dipole antennas, fractional bandwidth also has been improved.

articleTitle: SIW-Backed Array with Compensated Mutual Coupling for Wide-Angle Scanning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An ultralow-profile (about 0.017 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>) phased array based on substrate integrated waveguides (SIWs) is proposed for wide-angle scanning. The bandwidth is improved by etching unequal slots on the SIW of the array element. To mitigate impedance mismatch of the active element during the scanning process, an effective mutual coupling compensation network is connected to the feeding lines of the array. With the improved bandwidth and compensated mutual coupling, the phased array scans from -65° to +65° in the azimuth plane from 9.8 GHz to 10.2 GHz with realized gain fluctuating less than 2.5 dB.

articleTitle: High Gain Broadband Antenna for Point to Point Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband and high gain antenna, which operates at (3.2-4.2) GHz band and achieves maximum ~12.3 dB realized gain, has been presented. The antenna architecture consists of a driven aperture coupled stacked patch antenna on top of which parasitic radiators are placed. A prototype antenna has been fabricated and characterized. The main advantage of the presented antenna is its high gain which is maintained over a wide bandwidth. This property is very important to improve the signal to noise ratio (SNR) of point to point communication systems.

articleTitle: Single Antenna Changeover Switch for UHF RFID Communications and RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: With the increasing development of low power technologies, particularly wireless, RF energy harvesting to power such devices has become possible. UHF RFID is a versatile platform offering both an RF signal to harvest and a data communications link. A challenge is to efficiently share a single tag antenna for both harvesting and data communication duties. This paper demonstrates a practical design for efficiently switching and sharing a single UHF RFID tag antenna.

articleTitle: Coaxial Marchand Balun - Design and Fabrication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This article presents the design of an ultra-wideband coaxial Marchand balun for the pyramidal sinuous antenna. The focus of the design is related to the fabrication process and the nuances involved. Closed-form equations are used to determine the element values of the balun, which are then tuned to provide a desired equi-ripple response. The designed balun, with a 300 Ω load termination, showcases a simulated return loss better than 10 dB from 1.1 − 4.8 GHz. The initial design produced amplitude and phase balance results within ±2.5 dB and 9.8°, respectively. Updated designs achieve an amplitude balance of ± 0.2 dB and a phase balance of 1.5°.

articleTitle: An Entire-Domain Analysis of Very Large 2-D Scatterers in TM mode Using Gegenbauer Polynomials
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We summarize results for using Gegenbauer polynomials as basis functions in the case of the entire-domain 2-D analysis of strips with curvilinear cross section illuminated by a linearly-polarized plane wave. The involved integrals are calculated with 14-digits precision, due to the used singularity-cancellation transformation, for arbitrary cross-section shape. We investigated the error estimate of the surface current approximation due to the defining parameter of the Gegenbauer polynomials and the maximal order of the polynomial for the current approximation. The results for the surface-current approximation with the highest degree of the polynomial basis functions of 7000 are presented. The analyzed curvilinear strip had the total length of the cross section of 2000 wavelengths at the operating frequency in the free space.

articleTitle: AoA Estimation With Practical Antenna Arrays Using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We study the problem of estimating angle-of-arrival (AoA) using practical antenna arrays. In practical antenna arrays, the antenna elements have nonuniform radiation patterns. However, most existing AoA estimation algorithms are developed based on the assumption that antenna elements are isotropic sources with uniform radiation patterns. Hence, the performance of existing algorithms can be significantly degraded when they are deployed on practical antenna arrays. To overcome the difficulty from nonuniform radiation patterns, we propose a fundamentally different approach of AoA estimation, where we train a neural network to learn the mapping from received signals to AoAs. Since we can generate a large amount of training data from propagation models of electromagnetic waves, our neural network can achieve high estimation accuracy (e.g., 10% estimation errors), which greatly improves the performance of state-of-the- art algorithms (e.g., up to 30% estimation errors). Moreover, by training with data generated from different radiation patterns, our neural network is agnostic of the specific radiation patterns of antenna elements. Since most computation is done in the training phrase, our trained neural network can perform AoA estimation in real time and can be used for tracking AoAs of mobile targets.

articleTitle: Double Metaloop Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Inner and outer metaloops backed by a ground plane constitute a double metaloop (D-ML) antenna. The height of the D-ML antenna above the ground plane is small: on the order of lambda/100 at the design frequency. The outer metaloop creates a null within the circularly polarized (CP) beam pattern generated by the inner metaloop. The null is formed through a difference in the excitation voltage sources for the two metaloops. It is revealed that the null is moved in the elevation plane by changing the amplitude/power of the excitation voltages, and that the null is rotated in the azimuth direction by changing the phase of the excitation voltages.

articleTitle: Integration and Evaluation of Antenna Systems for 5G mmWave Mobile Device
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Critical aspects on millimeter wave (mmWave) antenna integration and performance characterization for 5th generation (5G) mobile device have been reviewed in this paper. The influence of the device housing on the antenna performance is presented, and the corresponding performance characterization from 3GPP has been given. A practical example of an antenna system for a mobile device will also be shown at the end of the paper.

articleTitle: High Frequency Diffraction by Thick Loaded Conducting Slits –H Polarization Case–
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: H-polarized plane wave diffraction by a thick and loaded slit has been analyzed by Kirchhoff approximation (KA). The scattering field can be obtained by the radiation integral from the equivalent magnetic currents on the closed apertures of the slit. The reflected and transmission fields in the slit region are expressed first by parallel plane waveguide modes, then these fields are again converted into the equivalent currents to excite again. Comparison with Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (GTD) is made.

articleTitle: An Independently Tunable Uniplanar Dual Band Band-Stop Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a dual band frequency selective surface with independent tunability of the resonance frequencies. The surface is made of interleaved double hexapole elements with intermediate tripoles for confinement of the fields. The resonance frequencies are shown to be tunable by changing a single geometric parameter of the surface. A prototype is manufactured and the match between measured and simulated response is shown. The prototype has stop bands with -20 dB bandwidths of 15.2% at 2.65 GHz and 2.8% at 6.25 GHz.

articleTitle: Highly Accurate 3D EM Modeling Based on Ultra High Order Basis Functions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Proper implementation of max-ortho bases enables effective usage of ultra high order basis functions. Significance of ultra high order bases is demonstrated in the case of p-refinement of 2λ cube scatterer, in which case mean absolute RCS error of 0.001 dB is attained using expansion order of n = 20. In particular, it was shown that taking edge effects into account this level can be further reduced to 0.0001 dB.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Far-Zone Electric Fields Radiated by Thin Elliptical Loop Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Circular loop antennas have been rigorously studied in the past for RF applications and more recently for the case of dispersive materials at optical wavelengths. The elliptical loop is the more general case which has received considerably less attention. This work extends upon a recent derivation of the electric fields radiated by thin elliptical loops. It is shown that elliptical loops possess interesting behaviors such as the ability to increase the field strength at resonance, simply by pinching a circular loop of the same size. This suggests the possibility of many new and exciting applications to be explored in the future, especially in the optical regime.

articleTitle: Analysis of Close Range Evaporation Duct Inversion from LATPROP Radar Data Collected During CASPER West Research Campaign
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Refractive atmospheric conditions at low altitudes can have a significant impact on electromagnetic signals propagating at low grazing angles in many coastal regions. Refractivity from clutter (RFC) is a technique that refers to the estimation of an atmospheric refractivity profile from radar sea clutter returns. The RFC algorithm obtains the simulated clutter pattern that has the best fit to the collected radar data. RFC is traditionally performed with the minimum range not starting before 10 km. This is because there are large fluctuations in the grazing angle of an electromagnetic signal when an evaporation duct is present. This paper proposes using a commercial Koden MDS-63R marine radar architecture converted for increased sea clutter sensitivity and implementing a modified version of the Georgia Institute of Technology (GIT) model to perform RFC inversions starting on the first kilometer of the returned clutter power. Radar data for testing the procedure was collected in Southern California at Pt. Mugu from September to October 2017 as part of the coupled Air-Sea Processes and EM ducting research (CASPER) West Campaign. Validation data was also collected during the campaign and consist of buoy in situ bulk measurements of air temperature, humidity, wind speed, and sea surface temperature.

articleTitle: Analog Beamforming System Using Rotman Lens for 5G Applications at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the design and simulation of a seven input and eight output Rotman Lens switched-beam Quasi-Yagi antenna array are described. The beamforming system is made on Rogers substrate RO6010 which makes the proposed system compatible with standard planar low-cost processing techniques for millimeter wave monolithic integrated circuit (MMIC). The result shows the system capability of 80° beam scanning for different seven angels in range of -39.7°, -26.5°, -13.3°, 0°, +13.3°, +26.5°, and +39.5° at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: Linear Pulse Compansion based on Space-Time Modulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We presents a new approach for pulse compansion, i.e., compression or expansion, based on copropagating spacetime modulation. An engineered asymmetric space-time modulated medium copropagating with a pulse compands the pulse continuously as it propagates. The space-time medium locally modifies the velocity of different sections of the pulse in order to modify its shape as it copropagates with the pulse. The proposed compansion scheme is linear with respect to the input wave and therefore it can be used to compand multiple pulses simultaneously. Moreover, it does not distort the pulse during compansion. Finally, it can also be used for frequency up- or down-conversion of modulated electromagnetic pulses.

articleTitle: Directions-of-Arrival Estimation in Linear Sub-Arrayed Array Through Compressive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The problem of the estimation of the directions-of-arrival (DoAs) in sub-arrayed linear arrays is addressed in this work by means of an innovative strategy based on the Bayesian Compressive Sensing (BCS). The performance on the DoAs estimation for different sub-array configurations is discussed and compared with those of a fully-populated array for different noisy conditions. A set of preliminary numerical results is reported to highlight the behavior of the proposed method by taking into account data measured at a single time snapshot.

articleTitle: Transmissive Suppressed-Order Diffraction Grating (SODG)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a novel type of Suppressed-Order Diffraction Grating (SODG). An SODG is a diffraction grating whose diffraction orders have all been suppressed except one that is selected to provide electromagnetic deflection. The proposed SODG is a transmissive grating that exhibits high-efficiency refraction-like deflection for all angles, including large angles that are generally challenging to achieve, while featuring a deeply subwavelength thickness, as required in the microwave regime. We first present the design rationale and guidelines, and next demonstrate such a 10.5 GHz SODG that reaches an efficiency of 90% at 70°.

articleTitle: On the Distortion of UWB Circularly Polarized Time-Domain Pulses in Presence of Rotation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The paper provides a first theoretical study on the effect of rotational Doppler on circularly polarized pulsed communication. Despite the circularly polarized communication being considered immune to signal fading due to rotary misalignment, such misalignment will cause a frequency-invariant phase-shift. This phase shift will significantly distort the shape of the time-domain pulse. The property can be used for integration of orientation sensing into well establish pulse-based localization. However, it has also the potential to distort communication for some pulse-modulated UWB systems.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual-Polarized End-Fire Antenna Array with A Single-Layer Feed Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a dual linearly polarized end-fire antenna array at the 28-GHz band. By employing crossover structures and phase shifters, two power-splitting networks are integrated together in a single-layer substrate, corresponding to a low profile of 0.12λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>. A prototype is demonstrated experimentally. The overlap impedance bandwidth for the two polarizations is around 28.6% and the port isolation is over 20 dB within the whole operating band.

articleTitle: A Target Recognition-Based NLOS Identification Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we develop a target recognition-based algorithm for line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) identification, which can be used for channel modeling and parameter analysis. The algorithm first extracts angular information by using target recognition algorithms and then builds a classifier by using support vector machines. Based on the realistic channel measurements, the proposed algorithm achieves fairly high accuracy on LOS/NLOS identification.

articleTitle: L-shaped Metasurface for Chiral Surface Waves Propagation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a novel metasurface design that supports chiral surface waves. The chiral surface waves are circularly polarized waves whose spin direction is locked to their momentum. The asymmetry in the complementary L-shaped design allows the chiral surface wave to propagate along its diagonal in which a spin-down (LCP) wave propagates forward and a spin-up (RCP) wave propagates backward. This work provides the possibility of having a laterally confined unidirectional surface wave propagation. Additionally, it can be used for polarization-based beam splitting as well as steering the beam direction.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Band Band-stop Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band band-stop frequency selective surface(FSS) is designed. Structure of the FSS is composed of upper and lower metal patches on a dielectric substrate. The metal patches consist of a square metal strip on one side of the dielectric substrate and a folded ring part on both sides of the dielectric substrate. The dual-band FSS can operate on 1.6 GHz and 2.4 GHz which TE mode bandwidth is 0.1 GHz~0.18GHz and 0.4 GHz~0.68GHz (-15dB stop-band bandwidth), and TM mode bandwidth is 0.04 GHz~0.1GHz and 0.2 GHz~0.4GHz (-15dB stop-band bandwidth), respectively. The whole dimension of miniaturized unit cell of elements is 0.085λ × 0.085λ. The miniaturization element of FSS and stable center frequency is achieved.

articleTitle: Low-Cost and Highly Flexible Antenna for 2.4 GHz IoT applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low-cost and highly flexible patch antenna has been realized to demonstrate feasibility of commercially off-the-shelf (COTS) Silicone Sponge Rubber (SSR) as a flexible RF substrate. The material enables the fabrication of highly flexible conformal antennas. The target application of the antenna is in the field of Internet of Things (IoT) when an antenna for conformal surface is required. Simulation and measurements results are presented for several conformal surfaces.

articleTitle: A 3D Printed UHF Passive RFID tag for Plastic Components
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, 3D printing by additive manufacturing is employed to fabricate a UHF RFID tag compatible with direct integration into 3D printable plastic parts. A standard meandered dipole design is chosen for the transceiver antenna to receive the query signal and respond back with the identification information to the interrogator operating in the FCC approved RFID range (902-928 MHz). The antenna is printed on a plastic substrate with the RFID chip embedded using a face-up embedding process. The printed tag has a read range of 6 m making the performance comparable with conventional UHF RFID tags. The tag can be easily integrated with plastic parts that are 3D printing compatible such as car bumpers, pill bottles, etc.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Modular Origami Inspired Dielectrics for Frequency Tunable Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We explore the impact of origami structure meta-materials on electromagnetic devices. Here two modular origami-inspired dielectric structures were fabricated by 3D printing with the ability to shift the resonant frequency of patch antennas operating at approximately 1 GHz. Tunablity was achieved by deploying different dielectric origami configurations that were actuated to control the degree of folding or compression when placed on top of a standard patch antenna. The measured effects of the dielectric origami structure is to provide a 2% range of tunability of the antenna resonance frequency, with simulations showing a similar trend as experiments. The demonstration of active tuning by actuation of dielectric origami may find application in future antenna and telecommunication systems.

articleTitle: Monitoring Health Status and Quality Assessment of Leaves Using Terahertz Frequency
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new and non-invasive electromagnetic technique that utilizes the terahertz frequency waves to monitor the plant health. To do so, the water content of a plant leaf is obtained using the measured scattering response in the frequency range of 0.75 to 1.1 THz. Leaves of three commonly used herbs were observed for four consecutive days and the electromagnetic material parameters such as the permittivity were extracted using a material characterization algorithm. The decreasing moisture level and in turn the plant health can therefore be directly inferred from the leaf permittivity which approaches to that of free space with the passage of days.

articleTitle: Design of a Planar Wideband Yagi-Uda Antenna for Millimeter Wave SAR Imaging Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a wideband planar Yagi-Uda antenna was designed for millimeter wave synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging application. A series of simulations were performed to investigate the effect of each part of the antenna on its radiation characteristics. The designed antenna can achieve ~16% (~55 - 65 GHz) bandwidth (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub><; -10 dB), ~7 dB gain, and ~85<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> and 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> half-power beam-width (HPBW) in the E- and H-planes, respectively. Subsequently, the antenna was manufactured and tested, showing close agreement between its simulated and measured characteristics. Finally, the imaging performance of the designed antenna was examined through several SAR imaging experiments.

articleTitle: A Capacity Reconfigurable Multimode Origami MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a receconfigurable multimode Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna is proposed. This antenna is composed of seven identical dual band elements each simultaneously operating in two orthogonal modes. The antenna is implemented on an accordion origami support structure which allows the inter-element spacing to be uniformly varied. This spatial reconfigurability results in a 15% and 13% variation in capacity for the first and second modes, respectively.
