With this antenna, the capacity, gain, and physical size can be optimized for real-time operational requirements.

articleTitle: On-chip Slot Ring Antenna Integrated with Voltage Controlled Oscillator at 140 GHz in 40nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design and measurement results of a on-chip slot ring antenna with Si lens and integrated with a voltage controlled oscillator in 40 nm CMOS process. Slot antenna allows easy metal density adjustment to comply with design rule requirement on standard CMOS process. The measured input matching is better than -15dB at 140~180 GHz. Integrated with a high resistivity Si lens at 5mm diameter and active VCO, the overall radiator has measured peak gain at 5.63dB at 143GHz and 3dB beam width of 30° at both E-plane and H-plane.

articleTitle: Ultra-Low-Loss, Binary-State Elements for a Mechanically Actuated Reconfigurable Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes the design of the binary-state elements that comprise a reconfigurable reflectarray. The elements must switch between two states that have a reflection coefficient magnitude as close to 1 as possible and reflection coefficient phases that differ by 180°. To enhance the polarization independence of the cell, the elements were designed to be hexagonal. Changes in the element's state are achieved mechanically rather than electronically to minimize the loss in the elements. The elements presented here exhibit simulated reflection coefficient magnitude of 0.995 and a phase shift of 175° between the two states.

articleTitle: Measurement-Based Propagation Characteristics at 28 GHz and 39 GHz in Suburban Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Millimeter-Wave (mmWave) communication is considered as a key enabling technology for 5G mobile systems. This paper presents a measurement-based analysis of large-scale propagation characteristics in suburban environment at 28 GHz and 39 GHz. Thanks to the utilization of custom-designed channel sounder, directional power delay profiles can be extracted for modeling directional and omnidirectional channels. The comparisons of the path loss in line-of-sight (LoS) and non-LoS (NLoS) scenarios reveals that the penetration loss through dense foliage is close to 20 dB. Combining with the analysis of composite root-mean-square angular spread, the impact of foliage blockage on the mmWave propagation in suburban environments is given, showing that shorter wavelength probably causes richer foliage scattering, corresponding to larger angular spread.

articleTitle: A Novel Class of Super-Elliptical Vivaldi Antennas with Enhanced Radiation Properties
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel class of super-elliptical antipodal Vivaldi antennas (SAVAs) is presented with improved bandwidth as well as peak realized gain and front-to-back ratio characteristics. The proposed antenna is parametrized on basis of the superellipse equation.

articleTitle: Inter- and Intra-Cluster Characteristics of MIMO Industrial Channels
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the measurement based statistical model of the inter- and intra-clusters in an industrial environment for a bandwidth covering 2 GHz to 6 GHz. Measurements were performed using a vector network analyzer (VNA) and virtual arrays mounted at both the transmitter and receiver sides. Different environment conditions were considered, i.e. line- of-sight (LOS), obstructed-line-of-sight (OLOS) and non-line-of- sight (NLOS).

articleTitle: A Miniaturized and Reconfigurable On-chip Slot Antenna for RFID Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 3 mm × 1 mm on-chip quarter wavelength slot antenna is designed on standard 0.18 μm technology 6M1L RF CMOS process to operate at 2.45 GHz by using a MOS varactor in shunt configuration. The MOS varactor is used to increases the capacitive loading of the slot resonator enabling a decreases in its resonating frequency from 3 GHz to 2.45 GHz. A CPW to microstrip line transition is designed to act as the feed for the slot resonator. A tuning range of 425 MHz can be achieved with 2.45 GHz as the center frequency by varying the input control voltage of the MOS varactor from 1.8 V to -1.8 V. Considering the small size and GHz frequency range of operation this antenna is suitable for short range RFID tag and wireless sensor node applications.

articleTitle: Matching of Small Transmitting Antenna using Non-Foster-inspired Two-transmitter System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: One of the most challenging applications of non-Foster elements is matching of a small transmitting antenna. It requires construction of a high-power and stable NIC-antenna system. Here, an alternative idea that employs two coherent transmitters that imitate NIC behavior, is presented and verified analytically. A possible practical realization, based on two standard power amplifier modules, is proposed.

articleTitle: A Dual Band and Dual Circular Polarization Radial Line Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this letter, the design of a dual band and dual circular polarization RLSA (Radial Line Slot Antenna) fed by a broadband feeding network is presented. The antenna consists of the parallel radial line, slot array on the upper plate and feeding network on the underside of the plate. The antenna works at 12GHz and 14GHz. The feeding network is composed of microstrip line to provide the phase excitation for left-handed circular polarization and right-handed circular polarization. The diameter of the antenna is 100mm. At 12 GHz, the right-handed circular polarization sum gain is 18.02dB. the aperture efficiency is 40.18%; at 14GHz, the left-handed circular polarization circular polarization sum gain is 20.56dB, the aperture efficiency is 53.72%. The axial ratio is lower than 3dB in both bands.

articleTitle: Frequency-Reconfigurable mmWave Antenna Loaded with Capacitive Structure Integrated within a Microstrip Line
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes a frequency-reconfigurable mmWave antenna loaded with capacitive structure integrated within a microstrip line. The proposed topology achieves bandwidth of approximately 1 GHz from 27.8 GHz to 28.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Flexible Reconfigurable Antenna Robust to Folding in Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a flexible reconfigurable antenna suitable for wearable applications is presented. Thanks to the reconfiguration mechanism, the antenna is robust in terms of impedance matching to the folding of the structure.

articleTitle: Feed Based Bandwidth Enhancement of U-Slot Microstrip Patch using Theory of Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, characteristic mode analysis (CMA) of feed based bandwidth enhancement of UWB low profile U-Slot microstrip patch is investigated. The application of characteristic modes to antenna bandwidth enhancement serves as a demonstration of the broad utility of the modal technique. The paper investigates the effect of modal excitation due to feed structure on the natural resonant modes. The paper presents the comparative analysis of natural resonant modes and the current modes of U- Slot structure excited due to straight probe and L-probe feed. The modal significance of the three cases gives a physical insight of the modal behavior and the modal VSWR depicts the impedance behavior due to feed excitation. It has been shown that natural resonant modes are the potential participating current modes in impedance bandwidth upon excitation. It has been shown that impedance bandwidth can be enhanced up to 40% (approx) by exciting certain resonant mode by optimizing and changing a feed structure.

articleTitle: Automatic Generalized Quadrilateral Surface Meshing in Computational Electromagnetics by Discrete Surface Ricci Flow
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present methods for the automated generation of high-order generalized quadrilateral surface meshes for computational electromagnetics (CEM) using discrete surface Ricci flow and parametric domain iterative refinement. We offer a brief overview of discrete surface Ricci flow as it pertains to this work and demonstrate its usefulness for higher-order quadrilateral mesh generation. We present extremely-high-order surface meshes, automatically generated by this method using minute numbers of quadrilateral elements with exceptionally high geometrical orders, demonstrating the method's robustness on both simple and complicated surfaces. The examples of the NASA almond, one of the most popular benchmarking examples, and a more complicated fighter jet model, with as few as four elements of up to 50th geometrical order, are first of a kind, showing great promise for higher order CEM.

articleTitle: Misalignment Resilient, Near Field Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) Antennas using Anchor Shape
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a near-field coupled resonator antenna element is presented for power transfer applications. We propose an anchor shaped geometry that represents a combination of electric dipole and magnetic loop to realize stronger coupling over misaligned distances between the source and receiver antenna. The resonator was prototyped on textile substrate for wearable applications. A full-wave simulation of the power transfer efficiency is presented and compared with single-loop of the same size. The lateral misalignments are studied, and it is demonstrated that anchor-shaped resonators offer 80-90 % power transfer efficiency for misalignments as large as 70% of antenna lateral size. Simulation studies and measurement results are presented.

articleTitle: Design of Large-Band Highly Directive Antenna in the Millimeter Waves Range at 80 GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a broadband highly directive antenna developed for point-to-point communications systems in the millimeter-wave band around 80 GHz (E-band domain). High directivity (about 38 dBi) and very few degrees opening angle are required for this application from 81 to 86 GHz. A Fabry-Perot cavity excited by primary source array (NxN standard WR12 waveguides) is coupled to a metamaterial dual-layer partially reflective surfaces (PRS). The designed PRS is used as a transmitting window and optimized in order to achieve a positive gradient phase (PGP) of the reflection coefficient over the entire considered bandwidth (≈5GHz). The goal is to compensate, even partially, the delay due to multiple interference paths in order to maintain the cavity resonance condition. The dimensions of the planar antenna are 100x100 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The full wave numerical results show a positive linear gradient phase (PGP) of about 13 ° and a quasi-unchanged directivity with a peak value of about 38 dBi. The designed antenna is highly directive, ultra-compact and low profile with good performances over the entire E-band 81-86 GHz.

articleTitle: Radiation from a Non-conformal Antenna Array on an Electrically Large Conducting Convex Surface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Asymptotic solutions have been extensively used to predict radiation from conformal antennas and more recently conformal antenna arrays on convex conducting surfaces. However, their applications to non-conformal antenna arrays are not well developed. In this paper, the previous work is extended to predict the radiation from a non-conformal antenna array on an electrically large canonical structure. Numerical results for canonical shapes are presented in comparison with the results based on the multilevel fast multipole method (MLFMM).

articleTitle: Comparison of Propagation Losses in THz and Optical Non-Line-of-Sight Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We investigate the propagation losses in terahertz (THz) non-line-of-sight (NLoS) imaging and compare the performance to the optical counterpart. NLoS imaging exploits the multiple reflections of electromagnetic waves from surrounding surfaces to reconstruct the geometry and location of hidden objects. THz and visible/infrared radiations are attractive for NLoS imaging due to the short wavelengths and practical apertures that can support this non-conventional imaging. However, the scattering mechanisms vary significantly and determine the quality of the reconstructed images. This work compares for the first time the free-space path loss and rough surface scattering losses of a simple THz and optical NLoS imaging topology. Because specular reflections are dominant in THz scattering while optical systems suffer from strong diffuse scattering, THz NLoS imaging systems can receive considerably stronger backscattered signals.

articleTitle: A Unit-Cell Discontinuous Galerkin Scheme for Analyzing Plasmonic Photomixers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A discontinuous Galerkin (DG) framework is developed for efficient analysis of plasmonic photomixers. The proposed framework solves coupled systems of Poisson/diffusion-drift and time-domain Maxwell/diffusion-drift equations to characterize the non-equilibrium steady state and the transient response, respectively. A unit-cell based modeling is adopted to increase the framework's efficiency. Periodic boundary conditions for carrier densities and electromagnetic fields are enforced on the surfaces of the unit cell. Since the potential is not periodic, a "potential-drop" boundary condition is applied across the opposing surfaces the unit cell. Numerical experiments show that this approach significantly increases the efficiency of the DG framework without sacrificing from accuracy.

articleTitle: Robust Method for Synthesizing Low-RCS High-Gain Antennas Using Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Using array theory, a robust method to reduce the Radar Cross Section (RCS, σ) of an existing antenna, without affecting its radiation performance, is demonstrated. The proposed method is validated by reducing the RCS of a microstrip-patch antenna array consists of ten elements in (5×2) arrangement. Both the scattering and the radiation performances are verified using simulation data.

articleTitle: A Two-Component Compact 2-D FDFD Method for Waveguide Structures with ARPACK
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A two-component compact two-dimensional (2-D) finite difference frequency domain (FDFD) method is proposed based on the four-component FDFD method. The new method eliminates the transverse magnetic field components of the four-component method. The 2-D FDFD method can be concluded as a sparse eigenvalue problem. In the new method, the order of the eigenvalue problem is reduced by half, so the new method is more efficient. Moreover, the new eigenvalue problem can be solved by ARPACK directly with the largest real part strategy.

articleTitle: Study of Active VSWR in a Reduced BFN Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we explore the potentiality of a reconfigurable antenna with a particular excitation scheme to reduce the complexity of its Beam forming Networks (BFN). An example based on a 7×7 stacked microstrip patches with 15% of the elements excited has been investigated, to optimize the overall performances, and especially the active reflection coefficient of each radiating element. The non-fed elements are used as parasitic ones and loaded with complex impedances. The results obtained with this original approach are compared to a fully excited array.

articleTitle: Channel Measurement and Modeling in Highway Scenario at 460 MHz
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we investigate the statistical channel characterizations in a highway scenario at 460MHz with 20MHz bandwidth. Based on the measurements, the channel characterizations, such as Ricean K-factor, root mean square (RMS) delay spread and multipath statistics are analyzed and modeled. The results can promote the evaluation and verification of wireless communication system at 460 MHz in a significant way.

articleTitle: A Novel Deployable Compact Lens Antenna Based on Gradient-Index Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: With the advent of small-scale satellite technologies, there has been significant interest in developing deployable antennas for CubeSat and SmallSat projects. This paper introduces a novel concept of deployable lenses based on impedance matching gradient index (GRIN) metamaterials. The three-dimensional lens antenna consists of multi-layer microstrip square-ring units of variable sizes distributed on planar substrates to satisfy the required refractive index distribution. The attractiveness of this new lens is its high performance and low-profile. Developing lenses within this paradigm opens the door for many new applications which require compact and high-gain antennas.

articleTitle: Global Maxwell Tomography using an 8-channel radiofrequency coil: simulation results for a tissue-mimicking phantom at 7T
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We simulated a Global Maxwell Tomography experiment for the estimation of electrical properties in a numerical tissue-mimicking phantom using a decoupled 8 channel radiofrequency coil designed for 7 Tesla magnetic resonance scanners. The goal of this work was to investigate whether the orthogonality of the coil’s transmit fields ($b_1^ + $ measurements) is required to ensure accurate results. We demonstrated a normalized root mean squared error smaller than 0.6% with respect to the true electrical properties distribution. Our results showed that electrical properties reconstruction with Global Maxwell Tomography is accurate and robust.

articleTitle: An Interior Parasitic Patch Antenna with Wide Isolation Bandwidth for Simultaneous Transmit and Receive (STAR)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A microstrip patch antenna with a 180° hybrid coupler and parasitic patches under radiating patches is proposed for STAR applications. The antenna geometry and isolation improving methods are explained. Simulation results of S-parameters, gain, antenna efficiency, and radiation patterns, are presented. The proposed design has a bandwidth of 110 MHz from 2.399 GHz to 2.509 GHz for both transmission and reception. Its gain is about 2.5 dB to 4 dB between 2.4 GHz and 2.5 GHz. Polarization differences about 20 dB to 40 dB are shown in the radiation patterns. The proposed design also possesses -50 dB isolation bandwidth ranges from 2 GHz to 3 GHz. Such isolation allows the antenna to be used for STAR communication.

articleTitle: Study of Bending Effects on a Dual-Band Implantable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the bending effects on a dual-band antenna, operating at two ultra-high frequency bands (1.6GHz/3.6GHz). The antenna is proposed for wireless power transfer for biomedical applications. This antenna is considered to be printed on a flexible substrate and be implanted inside human body tissue at 10 mm depth. The performance of the antenna under various bending conditions is studied.

articleTitle: Multimode Horn for a Monopulse Subsystem
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a multimode feed horn and coupling network of monopulse feed system is summarized. A new combination of higher modes has been given, which will result in a novel structure that is easier to fabricate and more aseismatic. Coupling slots together with the septums are used for the magic-T. The multimode actuator excite the desired high-order modes that is helpful to make trade-off of the antenna patterns difference. Full wave and theoretical analysis of the feed horn are presented, and far-field patterns are computed. Simulations and measurements showed that the gain difference between the sum and difference patterns is less than 0.9dB.

articleTitle: Experimental Microwave Target Identification Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Electromagnetic radiation in the microwave range has been recently used in a wide range of biomedical applications due to the reasonable penetration depth, resolution, and relatively low cost of equipment in this frequency range. This paper summarizes our progress in developing an experimental microwave system that can be utilized for the noncontact biometric identification of different individuals. The microwave system consists of 8 antennas, arranged in a circular array around the target to be identified, and interfaced to a Vector Network Analyzer using a switching network. The scattered data from ten different cylindrical targets, with different cross-sections, where measured and machine learning techniques were employed to identify these targets with high accuracy. Future work will include upgrading the system and the classification algorithms for the biometric classification of human subjects.

articleTitle: Hybrid Beam-forming Smart Antenna for 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we have proposed the design and simulation results of a Ka band smart antenna. Antenna is designed at the center frequency of 28 GHz. At 28 GHz path loss is high due to the atmospheric absorption and high gain antennas are required to mitigate the path loss. Based on our recently awarded patent, we have proposed a simple and cost effective beam-steering approach. We are using a hybrid of phased array and switched parasitic array approach for beamsteering. Antenna design consists of two circular arrays of six parasitic elements and an active element. Phase shifter is used to introduce a phase shift between excitation currents to the antenna element. Designed antenna has a gain of 10 dBi.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable UWB MIMO Antenna for Indoor and Outdoor Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents implementation and analysis of reconfigurable ultra-wideband (UWB) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system in indoor and outdoor communication scenarios. The proposed compact and reconfigurable UWB antenna system has operating frequency range from 440 MHz - 5 GHz. In indoor communication, based on the TGn-B propagation model, the MIMO system can achieve a maximum channel capacity of 26.97 bps/Hz. In outdoor communication, based on the Spatial Channel Model (SCM) - Suburban - Macro non-line of sight (NLOS), the MIMO system achieves a maximum channel capacity of 6.25 bps/Hz. It is demonstrated that orthogonal orientation of the reconfigurable UWB antenna in MIMO exhibits improved polarization diversity.

articleTitle: Finger Blockage Mitigation Method for mmWave Beamforming Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes a novel method to mitigate the shadowing effect due to the finger, using the optically-transparent frequency selective surface at millimeter-wave (mmWave). Analytical method based on the diffraction is proposed for calculating the required frequency response of the n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> zone of the FSS and verified using full-wave simulation which includes the patch antenna, finger and the FSS. The devised FSS demonstrates over 11 dB gain improvement, enabling the antenna to establish reliable propagation channel when encompassed by the finger.

articleTitle: Inline Millimeter Wave Radar Phase Measurements utilizing High Order Waveguide Modes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a new concept for extremely sensitive frequency modulated continuous wave radar measurements within waveguides. Basis for this concept is the millimeter wave radar's outstandingly broad bandwidth that ensures precise detection of targets and its particularly sensitive phase. Moreover, the conversion of the fundamental TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> to the higher TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> mode with a broadband mode converter allows for advanced inline measurement setups. Therefore, simulations concerning the mode behavior are discussed and measurements that confirm the presented theory are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Evaluation of an Inversion Algorithm for Noninvasive Specific Absorption Rate Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: For noninvasive specific absorption rate applications, an electromagnetic inverse source algorithm is developed and evaluated. The algorithm reconstructs the fields tangential to the phantom from external field measurements surrounding the phantom and the device under test. This study considers simulated two-dimensional transverse magnetic field data.

articleTitle: Microstrip Antenna Design for Underground Water Pipeline Monitoring Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dipole microstrip antenna fed through a J-Shaped balun is presented as the electromagnetic front-end of the RF radio for a wireless sensor solution in the 750 MHz frequency band. The designed antenna is meant for the communication between a wireless sensor placed within underground pipelines buried 3 meters, and surface monitoring bases. Additionally, a miniaturized version of the antenna is also proposed based on meanders technique, reducing in more than 47% the area of the antenna's substrate. Both antennas were tested in free-space and working alike scenarios where the measurements and simulation results shows good agreement validating the design and miniaturization process.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable OTA Chamber Design Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The reconfigurable over-the-air chamber has been shown capable of synthesizing the field incident on the device under test in over-the-air testing. However, to date, there has been minimal exploration of the chamber complexity required to achieve a specified accuracy of the synthesized fields. This paper uses an analytic solution for the fields in the chamber based on the modal Green's function along with optimization of the antenna locations for synthesizing the desired fields according to three different cost functions. The results show that different cost functions achieve notably different results, with a traditional optimization based on minimizing error producing solutions that exhibit supergain characteristics.

articleTitle: All-Dielectric Compound Metaoptics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Lossless, reflectionless metasurfaces are generally limited to impressing phase shifts onto incident wavefronts, and can therefore only manipulate their phase profiles. However, two such metasurfaces placed along a common axis form a compound metaoptic, and can convert an incident complex-valued field to a desired complex-valued field. Here, we show that compound metaoptics at optical frequencies can form desired field patterns when the metasurfaces are separated by a few wavelengths, without relying on reflection, absorption, or polarization losses. With these properties, compound metaoptics are likely to find applications in complex-valued holography, camouflage, and forming custom near- and far-field radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Broadband Optimization of a High Power UHF Band Cylindrical Sleeve Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The sleeve dipole radiator [1] has been used in various configurations to extend the impedance bandwidth of the classical dipole antenna by using a transmission radiation mode along with the fundamental dipole radiation mode. The dual mode resonances generate a two null return loss response. The cylindrical sleeve dipole and balun variation has over eight interactive design variables that are less intuitive compared with simpler dipole designs but provide extensive optimization opportunities. The design and bandwidth optimization of a new high power UHF sleeve dipole used in a new four element prime focus phased array feed is investigated

articleTitle: Orientation insensitive UHF RFID Tag Antenna with polarization diversity using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a UHF RFID tag antenna design with polarization diversity using characteristic mode analysis. The proposed tag antenna consists of two meander dipole-like structure and shorting stubs. By analyzing characteristic modes, the diagonal slots are created to scale down the resonating modes. Since the modes are depicting inductive behavior in the frequency band from 902 MHz to 928 MHz, therefore, the small capacitive slots are created to achieve mode resonance in the required RFID band. Moreover, the proposed tag design is low-cost due to the absence of vias and provide a bandwidth of more than 40 MHz with a 3D orientation insensitive read range pattern. Furthermore, the proposed tag design is able to provide a read range of 7.5 m and 4 m on a metal plate and low permittivity dielectric materials.

articleTitle: Perfect Penetrable Cloaking Using Gain-Less and Loss-less Bianisotropic Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a technique, combining Integral Equations (IEs) and Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions (GSTCs) with bianisotropic susceptibility tensors, to compute the wave scattering by cylindrical metasurfaces of arbitrary cross sections. Moreover, it applies this technique to the new concept of penetrable cloaking. Finally, it demonstrates a synthesized gainless and loss-less and reciprocal bianisotropic metasurface that perfectly cloaks cylinders of arbitrary cross sections.

articleTitle: Compact, Dual-Band, Hybrid Monopole-ASA, Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel compact dual-band hybrid monopole- Annular Slot Antenna (ASA) antenna. The antenna's topology is inspired from both the ASA and the wide-band monopole. The antenna presents a very good efficiency and ASA-like radiation pattern in the two resonant bands. The second resonance of the antenna can be easily reconfigured independently from the first one. The antenna's different simulation parameters are presented and thoroughly analyzed.

articleTitle: Design of a Rotman lens antenna array for wide-scan and beam uniformity applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Rotman lens, which have the advantage of broadband and simple design, is one of the most popular multi-beam feed network. Nevertheless, its insertion loss and power uniformity received by array ports worsen with the increasing of incidence angle. In this paper, we design a wide-scan and low loss insertion Rotman lens based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). At the center operating frequency 2.4 GHz, the insertion loss is less than 2.5 dB within the ±40° scanning area and is less than 3.4 dB within the ±50<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> scanning area. After that, the amplitude and phase information outputted by the Rotman lens are fed into the 4×12 patch antenna array. The simulation result has indicated that the beam gain differences within ±50° scanning area are less than 0.9 dB. Hence, this beam uniformity design suit for satellite communications.

articleTitle: A Low Profile Flexible Circularly Polarized Antenna for Wearable and WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low profile, flexible, circularly polarized antenna based on the artificial material methodology is introduced in this paper. The antenna footprint is 20 mm × 15 mm, where it is excited by the Co-Planar Waveguide (CPW) configuration. Flexibility is achieved by incorporating Rogers Ultralam 3850 as the antenna substrate. By protruding an inverted T-shaped slot from the radiator to the extended CPW ground plane, circular polarization was achieved. The design radiates at 5.2 GHz with a -10 dB bandwidth of 29.7 MHz, gain of 0.7 dBic, boresight Axial Ratio (AR) of 0.86 dB, and 3 dB-AR bandwidth of 64.3 MHz. With such characteristics, the antenna is targeting wearable and Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) applications.

articleTitle: The Flipped Classroom Approach to Engineering Electromagnetics: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We report on our experience and results teaching junior-level engineering electromagnetics with a flipped classroom approach at the Georgia Institute of Technology. In a flipped classroom, students are expected to watch videos and/or complete materials that ordinarily are part of an in-class lecture. During class time, students work on problems in small groups that might otherwise have been part of homework assignments. Homeworks and quizzes have individual and team components. The technique is designed to leverage peer-based learning to emphasize conceptual understanding. The two authors have taught a required junior-level electromagnetics course a total of 6 times with the flipped classroom approach. We report on our techniques as well as our efforts to assess learning outcomes compared to a more traditional lecture-based course.

articleTitle: A Circular Polarized Four-Beam Antenna for Direction of Arrival Applications at 2.45 GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a switched beam circular polarized antenna optimized for operation at 2.45 GHz. It comprises two disc-based patches assembled in a concentric structure. The antenna is capable of four beams: a directive beam with maximum in broadside direction, a conical beam with a transmission zero in φ = 0°, and two tilted beams pointing to φ = ±30°.The compact dimension, the single-layer structure, and the beamset with moderate beam correlation confirms the effectiveness of the proposed antenna for Direction of Arrival (DoA) applications.

articleTitle: Microfluidic Switches with Integrated Actuation for Mm-Wave Beam-Steering Arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Selectively metallized plates (SMPs) repositionable within microfluidic channels offer to realize reconfigurable RF devices with compact size, low-loss and high-power handling. Slow actuation speed and external micropumps currently constitute their major drawback. To address these issues, this paper for the first time introduces the concept of piezoelectric disk actuated microfluidically reconfigurable devices and applies it to mm-wave beam-steering applications. Specifically, SPST and SP4T switch designs operating at 30 GHz are summarized and experimentally verified. Subsequently, a compact 4-element 30 GHz antenna array design integrated with the SP4T switch is presented. The stand-alone SP4T switch is characterized to operate with <; 0.9 dB insertion loss and <; 18 dB isolation across 18 GHz of bandwidth. The 4-element antenna array incorporating this SP4T switch is expected to perform with 10.2 dBi realized gain at 30 GHz.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Through-Wall Repeater for the Wireless Reading of Millimeter-Wave Passive Sensors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper reports the reading of passive and chipless millimeter-wave sensors using a dual-polarized through-wall repeater. The reader is here a millimeter-wave frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) Radar, and the batteryless sensor corresponds to a chipless sensing device whose cross-polarized electromagnetic reflectivity depends on the applied pressure. The proposed dual-polarized repeater allows transmitting two different and orthogonal electric field polarizations. The feasibility of through-wall reading of sensors is demonstrated here at 24 GHz from a passive pressure sensing device.

articleTitle: High Efficiency RF Energy Harvester for IoT Embedded Sensor Nodes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a high efficiency, co-planar and low-complexity RF-to-dc rectifier of one diode, which is able to be directly connected, i.e., without a matching network, to a coplanar antenna, e.g., to a dipole or loop antenna. The rectifier was designed to optimally operate at 868 MHz and for low power input. Specifically, it presents 54.82% RF-to-dc efficiency for 20 dBm power input, while for -14.4 dBm the system is able- to supply continuously, i.e., with any boost converter, a backscatter sensor node with power consumption of 20 μW.

articleTitle: Radiation Efficiency Calculation of the Murchison Widefield Array Using a Power Wave Based Framework
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a power wave based framework to compute the radiation efficiency of phased arrays which aims to simplify and minimize the amount of new simulated/measured data required by reusing prior knowledge of embedded element patterns (EEPs). The framework uses EEPs, S-parameters, and knowledge of low-noise amplifier (LNA) impedance to perform the calculation. Based on the previously simulated Murchison Widefield Array (MWA) embedded element pattern and S-parameters, we calculated the radiation efficiency of the MWA to be no less than 94% whereby the lowest efficiency occurs at approximately 242 MHz.

articleTitle: Path Loss Model as a Function of Antenna Height for 300 GHz Chip-to-Chip Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the path loss model of Terahertz (THz) wireless channel inside a desktop size metal enclosure as a function of antenna height. Measurements for line-of-sight (LoS) propagation inside the metal box show that path loss varies with respect to the transceiver's height from the bottom wall, and for some heights, the path loss is lower than the free space value. Analysis based on the cavity modes shows that the first eight TE modes dominate the resonating modes inside the box. Also, the path loss analysis indicates that the resonating modes combined with the reflections inside the box are responsible for the strong ripples in the path loss curve.

articleTitle: Augmented Unit Cells for Realizing TM-Polarized Huygens’ Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a new augmented unit cell topology for realizing TM-polarized Huygens' metasurfaces (HMSs). They exhibit significantly enhanced performance compared to conventional designs. Each cell is isolated from its surroundings through the inclusion of perfect electric conductor walls between adjacent cells. These walls improve the performance of the HMS by enforcing many of the simplifying assumptions often used when designing metasurfaces. As a result, the proposed unit cells may be used to directly construct complex metasurface devices whereas HMSs designed using conventional cells will require laborious tuning and optimization in order to compensate for the aforementioned assumptions.

articleTitle: High Gain Constrained Lens Antenna on BCB Substrate for 300-GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: straight front face constrained lens is used to excite a leaky-wave antenna (array of slots) at 300 GHz. The supporting polymer of the antennas is Benzocyclobutene (BCB). The lens is fabricated using substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology, while the radiating slots are etched on the polymer by photolithography. Numerical results show a reflection coefficient lower than -15 dB and a realized gain larger than 15 dBi over a 20% fractional bandwidth, spanning from 260 GHz to 330 GHz. The antenna efficiency is estimated equal to 25% by taking into account dielectric and conductive losses.

articleTitle: Exploiting Sparsity in Adaptive Relevance Vector Machine for Reconfigurable Soft-Field Tomography
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We exploit the sparsity inherited from traditional Relevance Vector Machine (RVM) method to efficiently perform the exhaustive search involved in Adaptive RVM operation applied to reconfigurable soft-field tomography sensors. To illustrate these ideas, we include examples from adaptive electrical capacitance volume tomography.

articleTitle: A Novel Multi-user Spatial Modulation-based Code Division Multiple Access Scheme
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Multiple-antenna techniques constitute a key technology for modern wireless communications, which establishes a trade-off between the data reliability and the data rate, and which may result in an increased system complexity and cost. Among the many transmission architectures which exploit multiple-antenna at either the transmitter, the receiver, or both, spatial modulation (SM) is a novel and recently proposed multiple-antennas transmission technique which can offer, with a very low system complexity, improved data rates compared to Single Input Single Output (SISO) systems, and robust error performance even in correlated channel environments. This is achieved by adopting a simple but effective coding mechanism that sets a one-to-one mapping between blocks of information bits to be transmitted and the spatial positions of the active antenna in the antenna array. The main goal of this work is to analyse the viability of spatial modulation as a technology to implement and support future 5G systems that are currently being developed. Since these systems will be deployed in frequency selective channels resulting from the targeted high data rates, and in the presence of multiple users, techniques such as orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) and code division multiple access (CDMA) may be involved. Hence, our objective is to investigate the performance of SM-CDMA and SM-OFDM-CDMA architectures in such frequency selective channels.

articleTitle: Inversion-Free Evaluation of Small Geometry Perturbation in Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Topology sensitivity is introduced and defined to be utilized within method of moments. It is based on a series of the smallest perturbations of the investigated structure and, thanks to the application of the Woodbury matrix identity, its evaluation is inversion-free, suitable for vectorization and parallelization, and results in a fast and versatile tool for analyzing antenna optimality.

articleTitle: Field interpolation with generalized barycentric coordinates in conformal FDTD schemes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to interpolate electromagnetic field for conformal FDTD schemes. This method is based on generalized barycentric coordinates (GBC) interpolation in polyhedron. After a short presentation of GBC theory, we explain how it is applied in conformal FDTD cells. This field interpolation method can be useful to extend FDTD models requiring field approximation, to conformal schemes. An example of field interpolation and surface current computation are given for two canonic PEC structures.

articleTitle: Co-design of Conformal 4G LTE and mmWave 5G Antennas for Smartphones
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents conformal design of CPW (coplanar waveguide) fed compact antenna operating at 2.5 GHz which caters to the class 7 4G LTE band. The proposed antenna is electrically compact having dimensions of 23 x 20 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with forward gain of 1.69 dBi. Also, a conformal microstrip fed patch antenna operating at 27-29 GHz with the forward gain of 9 dBi is presented. Both the proposed antennas are integrated electrically close by 0.004 λ for minimal physical footprint post integration in a typical smartphone case. The isolation is less than 35 dB. Simulated and measured results are presented.

articleTitle: Design of Transmitting Nano-Dipole Antenna Using a Subwavelength Laser Excitation Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this study, we propose a new method to excite nano-dipole antenna using a subwavelength laser. A realistic nano-dipole with spherical tips was designed with a 2nm gap and 10nm radius and then excited by a subwavelength laser with a wavelength of 800nm and a spot radius of 200nm. The electric field at the center of the gap has been recorded for different arm length values. The study shows that the nano-dipole exhibits some resonances at specific values of arm length.

articleTitle: A Measurements Based Characterization of Fading in Indoor Millimeter-Wave Distributed Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we empirically investigate the effects of shadowing and multipath fading upon the user equipment (UE) to access point (AP) channels found in indoor distributed antenna systems (DAS) at 60 GHz. Our measurements have considered the signal power simultaneously received at 9 ceiling locations which are likely to be used in future indoor millimeter-wave DAS deployments. During the experiments, a single user imitated making a voice call on a UE, which acted as the transmitter, while walking through an indoor office environment. To characterize the shadowing and multipath fading, we have made use of the lognormal and κ-μ distributions respectively.

articleTitle: Design of Ultra-Broadband RCS-Reduction Checkerboard Surface Using AMC Circuit Model
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A design procedure is introduced where a refined algorithm is developed and employed on single-band AMCs leading to a 10-dB RCS-reduction bandwidth of 80%. The AMC circuit model is utilized cleverly to reduce the substrate thickness while simultaneously increasing the bandwidth of AMC surfaces. Furthermore, dual-band AMC surfaces are synthesized and utilized in combination with single-band AMC surfaces to extend the 10-dB RCS-reduction bandwidth from 80% to about 99%.

articleTitle: Two-Way Phase Shifter with Equal Phase Shift
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel phase shifter working two-way at two different frequencies in order to obtain equal phase shift. The proposed phase shifter consists of two grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) lines and high dielectric constant slab over the GCPW lines. In realization of equal phase shift at two different frequencies, the length of two GCPW lines should be have inverse portion of frequency. Also, the length of BLT assumes to be equal to the length of two GCPW Lines. The simulated results show equal phase shift at 20GHz and 30GHz which is highly desired for many applications such as full duplex array, interleaved array, and multiband array.

articleTitle: A Slot Antenna for Non-invasive Detection of Blood Constituents Concentrations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new slot antenna for non-invasive detection of the concentrations of blood constituents. The designed antenna is composed of multiple slots that are optimized to enhance its sensitivity to the bound medium. To test its performance, the antenna is loaded by a foam container filled with fetal bovine serum (FBS) solution whose glucose concentration levels are varied. Accordingly, the magnitude and phase of the antenna's reflection coefficient (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>) are monitored at multiple frequencies for various glucose levels. A good correlation between the antenna's S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and reference glucose levels, which are measured with an invasive glucometer, is observed.

articleTitle: An Electronically-Steerable Parasitic Array Radiator (ESPAR) Using Microstrip-Line-Fed Cavity-Backed Slot Antennas in the E Plane
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A three-element Electronically-Steerable Parasitic Array Radiator (ESPAR) using a microstrip-line-fed cavity-backed slot in the E plane is presented in this paper. The driven element at the center is fed by an open-ended microstrip line and the two parasitic cavities lying in the E plane are fed by the center driven cavity through coupling irises. The microstrip line coupled to the parasitic cavity is terminated with varactors to provide variable load impedances. By properly designing the load impedance, continuous E-plane beam steering capability can be achieved. Compared to the ESPARs with boresight radiation, the proposed design is able to achieve a 27.2% impedance matching fractional bandwidth. Additionally, the tunable load can be integrated into the same layer as the microstrip line, which reduces the size of the ESPAR. It is shown that the proposed ESPAR can steer its beam from -30 to 30 degrees in the E plane. The return loss is maintained from 5.00 to 6.58 GHz for all scan angles.

articleTitle: Design of a Characteristic-Mode-Based Fully-Planar Antenna for Indoor In-Band Full-Duplex Radios
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: For indoor full-duplex in-band radios, ultra-low profile antennas with simple feed networks are highly sought. In this paper, a fully-planar, characteristic-mode-based, simultaneously transmit and receive (STAR) antenna with high isolation is presented. The proposed antenna utilizes two orthogonal characteristic modes for transmitting and receiving signals to achieve high isolation without a complicated self-cancellation circuit. The simulated and measured -10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidths of the proposed STAR antenna are 3.6% and 0.4%, respectively. The proposed antenna provides a simulated (measured) isolation greater than 48.4 dB (31.6 dB). The simulated peak gain is 4.4 dBi for both the transmit and receive links. The electrical size of the proposed antenna is 0.6λ×0.6λ×0.01λ where λ is the wavelength at 2.35 GHz.

articleTitle: Effective Figure of Merit Definition for MIMO UWB Radar Channels Selection
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new method has been developed to evaluate and indicate channel quality in a Multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) ultra-wide band (UWB) radar system for human activity detection and identification. A figure of merit noted as Mean Micro-Doppler to Noise Ratio (MMNR) based on time-frequency features and Micro-Doppler signature (μDs) characteristics is used to evaluate the signal quality differences among different channels. When compared to the conventional methods utilized in the time domain, the developed method is robust and could be implemented even in a poor SNR environment. It can be used to offer a practical standard or a threshold criterion for selecting or eliminating some MIMO channels with either high or inferior quality respectively. The developed method was successfully used to evaluate human activities using a MIMO system.

articleTitle: A Compact Wideband Dual-polarized Millimeter Wave Antenna for 5G Smartphones
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a compact 28 GHz dual-polarized antenna for future 5G smartphones. The antenna is based on two discrete elements a folded dipole and a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-backed slot antenna, which are responsible for the horizontal and vertical polarizations, respectively. The structure is designed on a four-layer Roger 4003 laminate with a total height of 0.89 mm. A coplanar strip (CPS)-to-coplanar waveguide (CPW) balun is implemented to feed the unbalanced slot antenna so that both elements can be directly connected to a fully-differential IC chip. The antenna features a wideband performance and covers the entire 28 GHz band (26.5-29.5 GHz). The simulated peak gain of the folded dipole (horizontal polarization) and the SIW cavity-backed slot antenna (vertical polarization) is 3 and 4 dBi, respectively. The antenna has overall dimensions of 7.5mm×5mm and can be easily integrated with RFIC chips.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Coupler Design based on the Concept of Balanced Loaded Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a novel design for compact hybrid couplers. The concept of loaded transmission lines is exploited for the synthesis of a 2-stage hybrid coupler which is comparable in size with a canonical 1-stage coupler. The latter result is obtained exploiting the concept of balance between inductive and capacitive loads. Furthermore, a sinuous design for the longer lines is exploited to enhance compactness. Simulation results confirm that the proposed device outperforms the reference 1-stage device in terms of band of operation despite the comparable size.

articleTitle: Does Low Mutual Coupling Imply Low Antenna Correlation?
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems promise high data rate and have been employed ubiquitously in modern telecommunications. However, due to limited space for MIMO antennas and finite angular spread of the propagation channel, antenna mutual coupling and correlations are inevitable, which can degrade the MIMO performance considerably. Since the antenna correlation is a function of antenna patterns and angular distribution of the spatial channel, it is less intuitive than the mutual coupling for antenna engineers. As a result, MIMO antenna designers usually focus on mutual coupling reduction, hoping that the correlation will be improved as well. But, does mutual coupling reduction guarantee low antenna correlation? Unfortunately, this important question has not been well answered in the literature. We try to address this issue in this work.

articleTitle: Novel Electromagnetic Scattering Model for Carbon Nanotube Composites using the Multilayer Green’s Function Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recently, there has been a strong demand for developing effective computational techniques to calculate the electromagnetic response of Carbon Nanotube (CNT) composites based on the underlying CNT distribution and hence predict the overall electromagnetic shielding effectiveness of the composite. The aim of this paper is to develop a novel efficient full-wave electromagnetic model for CNT composites. The Method of Moment (MOM) formulation of Arbitrary Thin Wires (ATW) is evoked to model the CNTs since they typically exhibit high aspect ratios and complex shapes. The solution is based on electric field integral equation (EFIE) that uses a multilayer Green's function to account for the dielectric slab in which the CNTs are embedded. The Sommerfeld integrals are evaluated using a semi-analytic approach, which uses the elliptic contour deformation technique along with closed form evaluation for the asymptotic tails. The accuracy and performance of this new technique are validated using extensive computational experiments and various applications of the model are outlined.

Author Keywords: method of moment for arbitrary thin wire (MOM-ATW)

articleTitle: Design of Waveform-Selective Mantle Cloaks for Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Here, we discuss the design of a cloaking metasurface (MTS) capable to engineer the scattering of an antenna depending on the waveform of the impinging signal. The MTS consists of vertical metallic strips loaded with lumped-element circuits exhibiting a peculiar time-domain response. Depending on the waveform of the impinging signal, the designed MTS behaves either as an invisibility device (when the signal is a pulse) or a perfect electric conductor (for a continuous wave excitation). The proposed configuration paves the way to a new generation of self-tunable and reconfigurable cloaking devices for antenna systems.

articleTitle: Analysis and design of mm-wave phased array antennas for 5G access
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents the design of two 64-element phased array antennas for 5G access, operating at 28 GHz and at 39 GHz frequency bands. The 8x8-element antenna arrays use a multi-layer printed circuit board stack. 16 commercial quad-core TX/RX ICs are used to provide independent control of phase and amplitude for each radiating element. RF power distribution and combining network is integrated on the PCB, with a single RF interface to an external radio transceiver. Analysis and design of the feed network for the antenna elements is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Antenna Modeling on Complex Platforms Via Sparse Constrained Equivalent Distributions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Accurate in situ antenna manifolds are desired for evaluation of many signal processing algorithms. Measurements of the antenna mounted on the platform of interest are the most accurate way to obtain in situ manifolds, but are often impractical or impossible to obtain. Instead, combinations of simulations and measurements are used to estimate in situ manifolds. The antenna under test is measured on a ground plane, and measured data is imported into numerical electromagnetics codes to include platform scattering. We present a new method to represent measured antennas by a weighted sum of far-fields from a simulated equivalent distribution of simple elements. The weights are found through a sparse constrained ℓ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-norm minimization between the measured far-fields and the equivalent distribution far-fields. The trade-off between solution accuracy and sparsity is controlled by a regularization parameter. In this paper, the details of the method, with a focus on the regularization parameter selection, are presented along with an example result.

articleTitle: A Novel Compact High-Gain Filtenna Using Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel compact filtering antenna (Filtenna) using groove gap waveguide (GGW) technology is presented. The use of GGW structures built by defected periodic metallic posts is an attractive way to achieve high-performance and at the same time, low-cost microwave devices and antennas. The proposed antenna consists of a slotted GGW array antenna operating in Ku-band frequencies which is effectively fed through a fourth-order chebyshev bandpass filter. The proposed Filtenna exhibits good out-of-band suppression and high gain radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Focusing Metasurface with arbitrary Focal Point Based on Pancharatnam-Berry Phase Principle
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A deformed cross structure PB unit-cell with ground plate was proposed first. Then, we modified the conventional Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phase principle. Therefore, a metasurface with arbitrary focal point could be designed employing the new phase compensation formula. For demonstration, a metasurface with focal point of θ = 30°, φ = 30° and focal length of 30 mm was simulated and discussed. Finally, constrains on the minimum periodic number of metasurface were derived.

articleTitle: Challenges for Antenna Design at mm-Waves
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: mm-Wave frequency band is poised to be used in 5G as ample bandwidth is available in this band. Beam-steerable antennas are an essential requirement for 5G mm-Wave networks; they mitigate interference by channeling and focusing the antenna signal towards the desired direction. This ability is significant for mm-wave frequency applications such as cellular back-haul links where high path loss, diffraction, attenuation from obstacles, material penetrations and misalignment due to rain and wind storms are dominant. Currently, the design cost of smart beam-steering antennas is high and there is a need to drive the cost down. This paper encompasses challenges, comparative analysis, cost and limitations of various beam-steering techniques at mm-waves.

articleTitle: Generation of Tilted High-Order Bessel Beam in Millimeter Range Using Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metasurface is robust in manipulating features of electromagnetic waves by properly designed subwavelength unit cells. Bessel beams and orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams have been investigated extensively for a bunch of applications. High-order Bessel beams that inherently carry OAM may benefit long-distance high-capacity wireless communications. This work presents a metasurface-based generator for a tilted Bessel beam of order 5 operating in millimeter wave region. Unit cells of the metasurface is designed to provide different phase shifts. Phase engineering approach is applied to design the metasurface. The entire metasurface plate is the superposition of four functions and corresponding four sets of phase shifts are combined together to give the final phase distribution of the metasurface. Simulation results apparently prove the reliable generation of the tilted high-order Bessel beam by showing correct amplitude and phase profiles. This work is meaningful for generating novel multifunctional beams utilizing metasurface.

articleTitle: A Dual-band and Dual-polarized Aperture Antenna for 5G Millmeter-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a compact aperture antenna involving dual-band and dual-polarized operations for multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) applications. The presented antenna comprises a loaded radiating aperture of dual-band resonances and two orthogonal ports for dual polarization operations. The proposed antenna employs a co-located design concept that uses a radiating aperture for both dual-band and dual-polarization operations, resulting in a very compact design. The prototype of the proposed antenna was built for 5G millimeter-wave applications of 28- and 38-GHz bands. The proposed antenna achieved superior port-to-port isolation of less than -20 dB over both operating bands. The proposed antenna were validated by experiment and simulation with very good agreement.

articleTitle: A Fast Macromodeling Approach to Simulate Complex Electromagnetic Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a macromodeling approach to accurately and efficiently simulate complex electromagnetic surfaces like reflectarrays and metasurfaces using the surface integral equation method. In the proposed method, each array element is enclosed by a fictitious box. Electromagnetic effects of each element are modeled compactly with equivalent electric and magnetic current densities on the box. The crux of the technique is to solve for unknowns on the boxes instead of unknowns on complex scatterers. By doing so, we obtain a final system of equations that has fewer unknowns and is better conditioned than the traditional integral equation method. Numerical results show that the proposed method can simulate a reflectarray up to 8 times faster and with 4 times lower memory than FEKO.

articleTitle: Transmit Pattern Analysis for Active Incoherent Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A microwave imaging technique that enables fast image reconstruction without heamforming using low cost receivers has recently been demonstrated by the authors. Using multiple noise transmitters separated by a large number of wavelengths, an incoherent radiation pattern illuminates the scene mimicking the properties of thermal radiation. The receive array takes advantage of the spatial incoherence of the reflections, producing two-dimensional imagery of the scene. In this paper a study to quantify the incoherence of the transmit radiation pattern is presented using the average mutual coherence metric.

articleTitle: Complex Permittivity Estimation for Construction Materials based on PSO Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: To determine propagation characteristics in buildings for fifth-generation (5G) wireless communication, it is necessary to obtain the complex permittivity of the construction materials at millimeter-wave band. Backward reconstruction of complex permittivity of construction materials in free space at millimeter-waves remains a challenging and up to date complex problem. A procedure for the estimation of the complex permittivity of construction materials based on Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) method is presented in this paper. The complex permittivity is extracted from the transmission and reflection coefficients for perpendicular polarization over 40-50 GHz, and verified by reflection coefficients for parallel polarization. This method is relatively precise and fast which gives a good estimation of complex permittivity.

articleTitle: Locating Scattering Centers Using Compressive PSD Estimation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper concerns stepped frequency radar with the focus on using multi-coset sampling thus reducing the number of frequencies needed to get the target impulse response, and then estimating the location of scattering centers. This processes is accomplished using compressive power spectrum estimation techniques. The extracted scattering centers can then be used for target identification. Scattering centers are extracted from both synthetic and real backscatter of commercial aircraft.

articleTitle: Ring Resonator Metamaterials for Radar Cross Section Reduction
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this communication, we present a comparison of different ring resonator absorber structures, and a proof of concept for the application of a thin metamaterial absorber to achieve radar cross section (RCS) reduction. We demonstrate over 10dB of RCS reduction in the S-band frequency range used by Air Traffic Control (ATC) radar.

articleTitle: A Slotted Circular Patch Antenna with Wideband Filtering Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A circular microstrip patch antenna is fed at its center to simultaneously excite the fundamental TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> and higher order TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0n</sub> modes resulting in omni-directional azimuthal coverage. Two annular ring slots are etched on the circular patch to couple the first three resonating modes. A method is described to control the coupling among the modes, which determine the bandwidth of the antenna and provides filtering characteristics. A prototype is fabricated for X-band application. It provides 28% 10 dB impedance bandwidth at 10.2 GHz. Gain variation is within 1% of 7dBi over the entire passband. The out of band suppression is better than 22 dB.

articleTitle: Metasurface Design for Cross-polarization Conversion and Absorption Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a reflective metasurface working as an efficient cross-polarizer as well as absorber in microwave frequency regime is presented. The proposed metasurface is composed of a metallic split-ring resonator (SRR) along with four orthogonally placed stubs with it. The surface transforms linearly-polarized wave into its cross-counterpart over three operating bands; 3.4-3.6 GHz, 5.3-5.4 GHz, and 10.5-10.9 GHz. The achieved polarization conversion ratio (PCR) is above 60% within the operating frequency bands. The surface also acts as an absorber for normally incident wave over another frequency band 16.9-17.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of an Antipodal Bowtie Array MIMO Antenna for 5G Mobile Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel quest for designing a 2×1 linear array of an antipodal bowtie antenna has been investigated herein for developing a compact 4-port MEMO structure. Considerably high inter-element isolation (>30 dB) has been obtained without any additional decoupling mechanism. The configuration works well over 18% impedance bandwidth (27.5 - 31 GHz) with endfire type radiation portraying a peak gain of about 7 dBi and therefore can be potentially deployed for future 5-G mobile communication systems.

articleTitle: Indoor Path Loss Variations with Frequency and Visibility Conditions at 3.5 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Studying the radio wave propagation within indoor environment is necessary previously to deploy wireless networks. Thus, and next to launching 5G systems at 3.5 GHz band, some insights on the behavior of the channel are required. This contribution describes the results of a measurement campaign in three different indoor scenarios, which are representative for a collection of similar environments. A simple path loss exponential decay model, adjusted by the measurement outcomes, indicates the evolution of radio waves as a function of the distance to the transmitter. In line of sight conditions, path loss seems to be just a bit stronger than in open space situations (the exponent is between 2 and 2.5, depending on the frequency, compared to the standard value 2 of open spaces). However, obstructed line of sight condition strengthens this decay rhythm, being over 4.

articleTitle: Susceptibility of Nanoparticles Studied by Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert and Snoek’s Equations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Snoek's law is a well-known theory used to predict magnetic properties of bulk ferromagnetic material. Landau-Lifshitz-Gilber (LLG) equations are differential equations used to describe the precessional motion of magnetization in magnetic materials. In this paper, we focus on magnetic nanoparticles and study the relationship between LLG equations and Snoek's law in seeking high permeability at high frequencies in magnetic materials. The susceptibility/permeability calculations of cobalt nanoparticles with different shapes are carried out analytically. Micromagnetic software package, Object Oriented MicroMagnetic Framework (OOMMF) software package, has been used to validate the results.

articleTitle: Surface Reconstruction of Large Reflector Antennas Based on a Hybrid of CMA-ES and HIO Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: By taking advantages of the global search ability of the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) and the quick local convergence rate of the hybrid input-output (HIO) algorithm, this paper constructs a practical phase retrieval algorithm used in the surface reconstruction for large reflector antennas. The proposed technique, named CMAES-HIO, is a hybrid two-steps global optimization algorithm which only requires one far-field intensity pattern as the input. Numerical simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is effective to avoid the local stagnation of the conventional iterative phase retrieval algorithms.

articleTitle: EM Measurements of Glucose-Aqueous Solutions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper demonstrates the use of a newly-developed commercial coaxial kit (DAK-TL) to investigate the dielectric properties of controlled binary glucose-water solutions prepared at concentrations (70-120 mg/dL), similar to type 2 diabetes patients, in a broad range of frequencies (0.3-67 GHz) using two different probes. The relative permittivity of glucose-loaded samples are then modeled in the mm-wave range from 50-67 GHz using a single-pole Debye equation of independent coefficients.

articleTitle: 2 × 2 and 4 × 4 MIMO Antennas for 5G mm-Wave Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a design of 2 × 2 and 4 × 4 MIMO antenna arrays for 5G wireless communication. The proposed two MIMO operate on the 28 GHz mm-wave band and they have wide operation bandwidth of 5 GHz with high gain performance over the entire band. The single element antenna that is used in the design of both MIMO antennas consists of two layers where the first layer is the feeding layer and the second layer is the radiating layer. The radiating layer comprises of a 3D printed slot surrounded by cavity and corrugations to improve the gain of the antenna.

articleTitle: Field Performance of A Novel Wideband Optically Transparent GNSS Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper provides and discusses the field test results on the performance of an optically transparent Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) antenna embedded in the lamination of the windshield. It has been shown that the location accuracy by way of transparent antenna is on par with the existing rooftop production antenna in various environments for the current applications and use cases.
