articleTitle: Three-dimensional Nanoantenna Inverse-design
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Realizing a diverse set of high-performance nanoantennas for phase-gradient applications can be extremely challenging without the aid of formal inverse-design techniques. To this end, an inverse-design procedure based on the Multi-Objective Lazy Ant Colony Optimization (MOLACO) algorithm is proposed for the synthesis of three-dimensional nanoantenna geometries that achieve high transmission performance and a wide range of phase options. A unit cell geometry suitable for a Membrane Projection Lithography fabrication technique is presented and explored by MOLACO in order to discover a set of highly transmissive nanoantennas that achieve a full 2π phase range. Finally, future research directions and applications are briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Chiral Helix Metamaterial Using Eigenmode Expansion Method and Characteristic Mode Theory
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Metamaterials are commonly associated to antennas and other microwave devices due to their unique ability to manipulate electromagnetic waves. In general, the approach used to select metamaterials for a given application is based on a classical approach by extracting the scattering parameters to evaluate the material effective properties. In this paper, we address the problem of evaluation and analysis of a specific metamaterial, a chiral helix metamaterial through the use of two modal analysis Expansion Eigenmode Method and the Characteristic Mode Theory. An interaction of the chiral helix with Circular Polarized electromagnetic plane waves is studied. The modal net stored energy of the metamaterial is also calculated. A good agreement is obtained between the net stored energy calculated by the two methods for the chiral metamaterial. The effect of polarisation on the metamaterial is also highlighted by the modal analysis. These modal approaches applied to chiral metamaterials can be of interest for the design of circularly polarised metamaterial antennas.

articleTitle: A Passive Beam Reconfigurable Antenna System for Millimeter-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the performance of a pathfinder beam reconfigurable antenna system for mm-wave applications. The system is completely passive and can provide continuous three-dimensional beam scanning in a conical region of ±40° from boresight direction. It uses a pair of near-field dielectric structures, inspired from optical prisms, introducing a pre-calculated phase gradient to the incoming wave front from a source antenna, and redirecting the radiated beam to an arbitrary direction with in a conical region with an apex angle of 80°. The proposed system can provide a peak gain of 20.7 dBi and does not require expensive phase shifters and a power distribution network.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Wideband Fabry-Pérot Cavity Antenna at 60 GHz using Grid Impedance Approximation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Wide band planar Fabry-Pérot cavity (FPC) antennas formed by an electrically thick partially reflective surface (PRS) composed of multiple metal/dielectric layers are investigated. These multiple metal and dielectric layers have been optimized to satisfy the FPC resonance condition at multiple frequencies, and hence, a larger antenna gain-bandwidth is achieved. The periodic metallic screen impedance is approximated based on its geometrical parameters and implemented as a shunt admittance in the transverse equivalent network (TEN). Two wideband FPC antennas with a single and double dielectric layers with metallic grids patterned at the bottom are designed and verified with a full-wave simulation result, with the double layer PRS leading to a wider band than the single layer one. In addition, the dispersion relation of the leaky-waves shows a quasi-oscillatory behavior versus frequency around the maximum radiated power bands.

articleTitle: Study of interconnecting switch currents in reconfigurable parasitic layer antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents an approach for calculating the currents across the switches of a reconfigurable parasitic layer intended to add beam-steering capabilities to a reference antenna. The method of analysis is based on the port loading technique in which only one Full-Wave Electromagnetic (FWEM) simulation is required to evaluate the behavior of the reference antenna and its interaction with the reconfigurable layer across all its states. Results show that the currents on the switches are at least one order of magnitude lower than the currents on the feed port of the driven radiator, proving the effectiveness of the reconfigurable parasitic layer approach in implementing Reconfigurable Antenna (RA).

articleTitle: Negative Group Delay Folded Circuit with Distributed Broadside Parallel Line
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper addresses the design, analysis, and experimental validation of a Negative Group Delay Folded Circuit (NGDFC) built on flexible substrate. The broadside coupling is exploited on a multi-layer coupled line system. The validation of this approach is performed by the analysis of structures with one element. Some characteristics of transmission lines was analyzed for the frequency range of 2 GHz - 5 GHz. The NGDFC is implemented on a Rogers Ultralam 3850 flexible substrate with a permittivity of <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 2.9 and thickness h = 0.1 mm. The NGDFC with one-element has a total area 133 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The NGDFC analysis shows that the electromagnetic modeling agrees with the experiments performed. Based on the measured and simulated results, was shown that this structure can be increased with more elements.

articleTitle: A 1×4 power divider capable of implementing any phase difference output based on a slow-wave substrate integrated waveguide
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a 1 × 4 power divider capable of implementing any phase difference output based on a slow-wave substrate integrated waveguide is designed at X-band. The upper surface of the output port of the SIW power divider is loaded with microstrip multi-segment line unit periodically. The current distribution on the surface of different ports and the electromagnetic field distribution in the dielectric substrate are changed, so that each port has different phase velocities, thus achieving different phase outputs. For four output power divider consecutive ports have the phase shift of 30 ± 1°, The S11 is below - 10dB and the S21 is 6 ± 0.2dB over the frequency band of 9.9 to 13.1 GHz with the percentage bandwidth of 26.7% is obtained.

articleTitle: Design and Test of 3-D Printed Spherical Ground Planes for Monopole Antennae
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design and test of 3-D printed spherically-shaped ground planes for monopole antennae used in space probe applications. Two monopole antennae with spherical ground planes operating at 880 MHz and 1.33 GHz were designed and fabricated using additive manufacturing. Results were compared to a conventional ground plane antenna as well as alternative spherical ground plane antennae using copper-wrapped incandescent light bulbs. The simulated and measured results were in good agreement. The radiation patterns of the spherical ground monopoles are similar to that of a standard monopole antenna provided the sphere radius is set to less than 0.15λ. The use of 3-D printing allows the antenna designer ample flexibility in accurately modeling arbitrarily-shaped ground planes at low cost.

articleTitle: Modulating Surface Impdances of Surface Plasmon Polaritons for Leaky Wave Plasmonic Nanoantennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Plasmonic nanoantennas offer unusual optical properties and constitute a fundamental building block for plasmonic devices. In this paper, we propose to modulate the surface impedances of surface plasmon polaritons for directional leaky wave emission from hybrid plasmonic waveguides. Simulation results indicate that the proposed nanoantenna presents a wide-angle beam scanning of over 90° with a peak directivity of 19 dBi.

articleTitle: Investigations of Wideband Microstrip Unit Cell Topologies at 28 GHz for Flat Lens Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an investigation into three different types of unit cells based on slot-coupled staked patch with resonant convex and non-resonant concave elements for flat lens antenna at 28GHz. The unit cell is designed to achieve an improved transmission phase-shift. Then, a wideband unit cell is proposed. The implementation consists of two octagonal-shaped patches with cross slot on the ground plane that are displaced exactly 0.46λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. This displacement produces two effects. It generates a transmission phase-shift of 340° with insertion loss of better than 0.2dB, and utilizes less layers, resulting in a compact profile. The proposed unit cell lens employs a simple and less fabrication complexity mechanism for phase-shift correction.

articleTitle: Numerical Cherenkov Instabilities in Kinetic Plasma Particle-in-Cell Simulations based on Structured and Unstructured Meshes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Particle-in-cell simulations are widely utilized for the analysis and design of state-of-the-art plasma-based devices. However, detrimental artifacts present in relativistic PIC simulations exist, called numerical Cherenkov instabilities. These instabilities are caused by grid dispersion and beam aliasing effects. Here, we analyze Numerical Cherenkov instabilities in finite-element-based PIC algorithms on unstructured grids and compare against results from conventional finite-difference-based PIC algorithms on structured grids. We assess the conditions for the onset of numerical Cherenkov instabilities by performing a complete grid dispersion analysis of finite-element field-solvers for various mesh layouts. The analytic predictions are validated against PIC simulations of relativistic plasma beams. We observe that highly irregular meshes alter the beam physics the least among different mesh layouts, preventing coherent spurious wave-particle interactions.

articleTitle: Open Multi-Slot Wideband MIMO Antennas with Microstrip Feed Line for 4G LTE
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A pair of microstrip line-fed open multi-slot antennas are presented for operation in 4G LTE bands. Two open slots are used for forming this open multi-slot configuration: one circular slot open at one side and one rectangular slot terminated in the circular slot with other end open. The open multi-slot antenna is excited by a microstrip line loaded with circular tuning stubs on the underside of the dielectric substrate. Two antennas operate independently for Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) communications and cover a frequency range from 800 MHz to 4.25 GHz. The antenna demonstrates 137% fractional bandwidth with good diversity performance.

articleTitle: Geometrically Stochastic Finite Difference Time Domain Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a geometrically stochastic finite difference time domain (GS-FDTD) method which inserts the geometrical uncertainty directly into the FDTD method by using the delta method approximation. 1D GS-FDTD equations are derived and used to assess the impact of tissue size variation in a layered biological tissue as a bioelectromagnetic simulation example. The results are compared to the Monte Carlo results as a benchmark, and show very good agreement.

articleTitle: Measurement of dispersion characteristic of slow-wave system by microwave network cascade method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the microwave network cascade method is proposed for the measurement of dispersion of slow-wave system. Different from the traditional resonance methods, the new method mainly includes three networks, which are the coaxial line to slow-wave system network A, the slow-wave system network B, and the large reflection terminal network C. Theoretical analysis shows that it is easier to measure the dispersion characteristic using the method given in this paper than the traditional resonance method. Moreover, the cold attenuation of slow-wave system can be measured at the same time. The test system is also built in this paper.

articleTitle: Explicit Unconditionally Stable Symmetric Positive Semi-Definite FDTD Subgridding Algorithm with Analytical Removal of Unstable Modes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An explicit and symmetric positive semi-definite FDTD subgridding algorithm is made unconditionally stable for fast FDTD simulations. The root cause of instability in a subgridding algorithm is found to be the eigenmodes of the subgrid whose eigenvalues are too high to be accurately simulated by a given time step. These unstable modes are then identified analytically and removed from the numerical system based on prescribed accuracy. The resultant explicit subgridding algorithm not only permits a local time stepping in the base grid and the subgrid, but also is unconditionally stable regardless of space step in the fine subgrid. Numerical experiments have validated the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis on Multipactor Effects in Coaxial Cables via Particle-in-Cell Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a numerical analysis on multipactor effects in coaxial cables using an electromagnetic particle-in-cell (EM-PIC) algorithm on unstructured grids. The analysis combines a 2.5-D axisymmetric EM-PIC algorithm and the Furman-Pivi probabilistic model for the realistic description of secondary electron emission (SEE) process. Employing a local and explicit finite-element time-domain (FETD) scheme, the present algorithm yields an energy- and charge-conservation from first principles on unstructured grids. We numerically investigate single- and double-sided multipactor effects confirming that the former originates from the higher-order multipactors (in parallel plates) in conjunction with ponderomotive (inhomogeneous) forces. This analysis can be instrumental in devising multipactor mitigation techniques.

articleTitle: Near-Field Measurement Study for Over-the-Horizon Radar Transmit Beamformers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Two error types related to near-field measurements in over-the-horizon radar transmit beamformers are studied. The first concerns the use of measured array manifolds for beamformer calibration purposes and the second concerns performance verification using the measured beamformer output gain pattern. It is determined through theoretical analysis that important clutter rejection and performance verification accurary degradations will occur if measurements are performed at practical distances including 500 meters.

articleTitle: Selection of Incident Electric fields for Estimating the Calibration Factor of the Lead Electromagnetic Model
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Using several sets of incident electric fields (Etan) with different profiles we estimated the calibration factors of the lead electromagnetic model for two helical coax leads at 128 MHz. The proposed quantities for E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">tan</sub> selection are (i) the unitless ratio of the RF-induced power deposition (P) with the lead in place to P without the lead in place (P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">backgnd</sub>) and (ii) the percentage of P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">backgnd</sub> for the selected E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">tan</sub> to that P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">backgnd</sub> generated by a homogeneous E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">tan</sub>.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Electrically Small Antennas Operating Below 400 MHz
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we study the performance of an electrically small slot antenna without ground plane and an electrically small patch antenna with ground plane, both operating below 400MHz. The comparison of performance with the fundamental Chu-Harrington's limit shows that the slot antenna has a better bandwidth-efficiency product than the patch antenna. Furthermore, we show how the performance of the patch antenna is degraded by the electromagnetic energy stored between the two metal planes and indicate how the performance can be alleviated by studying the reflection phase of the substrate.

articleTitle: Cadaver Measurement Results Using Ultra-flexible Electro-textile MRI RF Coil
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Current surface Radio Frequency (RF) coils used for neck Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) have two major issues: uncomfortable patients experience and low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR). An ultra-flexible 4-channel receive-only RF coil array for neck imaging was designed and tested in this work using electro-textile material. The flexibility of the material is similar to normal clothes thus leading to considerable ergonomic benefit. The SNR at 3 cm is 5.5 times higher than a standard surface array coil. Cadaver images acquired using the new ultra-flexible coil had good depiction of anatomical features of arteries and muscles with high SNR and the resolution of 1mm × 1mm.

articleTitle: Opportunistic Equivalent Sources for Field Synthesis - Potentialities and Future Trends
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An innovative paradigm for the synthesis of feasible sources radiating arbitrary field distributions is introduced. Towards this end, the design problem is formulated in terms of an inverse scattering (IS) one aimed at determining the electromagnetic (EM) properties of an isotropic/non-magnetic field-manipulating device able to modify the radiation features of an assigned source such that it is able to match a desired target field distribution in a given domain. An illustrative numerical example is provided to preliminarily assess the proposed innovative antenna design framework.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Scattering from Random Rough Surfaces with Multiple Elevations for GNSS-R Land Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Global Navigation Satellite System Reflectometry (GNSS-R) for remote sensing has attracted lots of attentions. In this paper, a scattering model by combining numerical Kirchhoff simulator (KA) and numerical solutions of Maxwell equations in 3D (NMM3D) is developed for GNSS-R land applications. The significant difference with past scattering models is that microwave rough surfaces (cm scale) are superimposed on multiple elevations (meter scale) of land. The elevation information are provided by DEM (digital elevation models) data. In the model, exact coherent and incoherent field of rough surface on each elevation (DEM patch) is obtained from NMM3D. With NMM3D outputs, KA simulator is used to calculate phase variations caused by elevations and then get total power received. The combined algorithm considers both coherent and incoherent contributions. It is applicable for simulations of land surface with dozens of kilometers, which is important for analysis of GNSS-R signals. Results of combined algorithm are many dB different with existing coherent and incoherent model, and also larger than KA simulator.

articleTitle: On a Unified Apporach Towards the Modeling of Nonlocal Hydrodynamic Non-classical Response from Plasmonic Nanotopologies
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we present a unified approach to model the optical response from a classical local and a nonclassical nonlocal hydrodynamic interface. The modeling is based on a boundary integral equation (BIE) representation. This representation is general for both 2D and 3D problems and can be numerically solved by the Method of Moments (MoM) algorithm. An example is then demonstrated for the 2D and 3D case. A very good agreement with the generalized Mie theory has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Coupling Analysis of Printed Circuit Board Traces using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the characteristic mode analysis (CMA) has been used to quantify external electromagnetic (EM) field coupling to a realistic printed circuit board (PCB) and to its traces. In our analysis, we show how the location of a trace on a PCB is important in determining the EM field coupling and we illustrate how CMA can be used to optimize the location of a PCB trace for interference control.

articleTitle: Array of stacked leaky wave antennas based on gap waveguide technology
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An array of leaky wave antennas is presented. To create the array, leaky wave antennas in gap waveguide technology are stacked. The distance between the array elements, and the feeding network are studied to achieve maximum directivity and to avoid side effects that reduce the efficiency of the design. The aiming band is that of 92-96 GHz, and the directivity enhancement using an array of four stacked leaky wave antennas is 5 dB, reaching 25 dB, in comparison to the single antenna directivity of 19.9 dB.

articleTitle: Finite Element Domain Decomposition Method for Rough Sea Surface Scattering
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Full-wave solution of electromagnetic wave scattering from rough sea surfaces is achieved by the Finite Element Domain Decomposition (FEDD) method. The method is implemented in a non-iterative manner by dividing the computational domain into overlapping subdomains, and solving the problem in each subdomain by attaching Locally-Conformal Perfectly Matched Layer (LC-PML) at the truncation boundaries. Statistical behavior of the Radar Cross Section (RCS) is investigated by Monte Carlo simulations. The results are compared with those obtained by the standard FEM, analytical models and measurements for different polarizations, frequencies, grazing angles and wind speeds.

articleTitle: Permittivity depth profile measurements of the Antarctic firn layer in the 0.4-2 GHz band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A microwave sensor aimed to characterize the complex permittivity depth profile of the Antarctic firn layer is presented. It is based on the open-coaxial re-entrant cavity method. Preliminary results of the measured permittivity depth profile on the Antarctic firn is also presented showing a very good agreement to expected values.

articleTitle: Implications of Recompression for Grid-Based Low-Rank Approximation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Low-rank compression of moment matrix blocks, representing interactions between clusters of vector basis/testing functions, is often done by a rank-revealing analysis of a simplified grid-to-grid interaction matrix, followed by inter/anterpolation and recompression. While this can provide a close estimate of the rank, it can lead to large errors in the compressed representation due to misrepresentation by grids of the underlying relative orientations of the vector functions. The potential hazard is demonstrated via a simplified example for the dyadic formulation.

articleTitle: A Novel Ultra-wideband Communication System Using an Analog Time-reversal Module
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel time-reversal ultra-wideband (TR-UWB) communication system using an analog time-reversal module was proposed and preliminarily implemented. The experimental platform verified the feasibility of the TR-UWB communication system based on the analog TR module.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Antenna With High Isolation Using Hybrid Balun Circuit
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid balun circuit for the crossed dipole antenna to achieve compact size (43 × 43 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and high isolation (48 dB). The hybrid balun is composed of a tapered balun and a Marchand balun. The tapered balun transforms the microstrip line to the parallel transmission line. The Marchand balun transforms the stripline transmission line to two out-of-phase ports. As a result, the proposed antenna has the bandwidth of 1.7-2.8 GHz for S11 > -15 dB. The hybrid balun and the proposed antenna are implemented, and the simulated and measured results meet well.

articleTitle: Oblique Thin wire for nonuniform FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The oblique thin wire model based on Holland and Simpson's formalism has already been developed for uniform FDTD grid. We propose here to revisit this approach for nonuniform grid with the same benefits, i.e. to freely incline and to shift wires into the FDTD without regard to the mesh scaling. The reciprocal field coupling between the wire and the FDTD grid is established with new bilinear weighting coefficients. Moreover self-consistency of this approach is verified with the current trace continuity condition.

articleTitle: Design of Polarizing Cells for Broadband Reflectors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the topology of two cells that can be used to conceive periodic polarizing reflectors. These reflectors are capable to convert a linearly polarized incident wave to a circularly polarized reflected one. Two polarizer designs are presented and their performance is validated through simulated results.

articleTitle: Optimal Number of Coils for Wireless Power Transfer through Cascaded Resonator Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we show that there exists an optimal number of coils for maximum wireless power transfer efficiency through systems of identical cascaded resonators. We apply convex optimization to determine the ideal spacing of a system in which only the direct coupling between adjacent resonators is considered. We then model the high-order coupling as a perturbation to this system and solve for the optimal spacing. We show that as the number of coils in a system increases, the efficiency for a given source-to-load distance reaches a peak and then starts to drop. Beyond this point, the losses introduced by each additional resonator begin to outweigh the high efficiency achieved by increasingly tight resonator coupling.

articleTitle: Mechanical Tension Effects on Cylindrical Truncated-Corner Microstrip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The experimental characterization of the mechanical tension effects on a 2.25-GHz probe-fed rectangular truncated-corner microstrip antenna conformed on a cylindrical surface is presented in this work. Two prototypes were designed and built for a metallic cylinder with a diameter of 12.55 centimeters. The first antenna was used to characterize the effects of mechanical tension considering the manufacture after etch stress relief effect. A comparison between simulated and experimental results for the first prototype showed that the conformed patch is elongated along the curvature of the metallic cylinder by 0.56 millimeters. The patch elongation was then compensated on the second prototype. Experimental data proved that the elongation was characterized correctly.

articleTitle: Performance Parameter Optimization of Graphene Enhanced Surface Plasmon Resonance Biosensors
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we perform a theoretical study in order to optimize the sensitivity S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> and detection accuracy DA performance parameters of a proposed Silver-based and Graphene enhanced Fiber Optic Surface Plasmon Resonance (FO-SPR) biosensor. Upon simulation utilizing the 4-layer model, it was found that the physical and geometrical parameters of this biosensor such as the metal layer type, addition of a Graphene coating, sensing region length L, core diameter D and thickness of the metal layer d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> have an effect on the sensor performance parameters and thus need to be optimized. The optimal design was found to be a Silver-based and Graphene enhanced FO-SPR biosensor with L = 10 mm, D = 100 mm and d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> = 40 nm.

articleTitle: Underwater Deployment and Performance of Curved Spiral Antennas in Mussel Backpacks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Freshwater mussels are bio-indicators of pollution in rivers because their periodic opening and closing of valves is correlated with the nitrogen content of the water. Our previous work developed noninvasive electronic sensors that are mounted on mussels to measure the valve movement. The backpacks are equipped with a broadband curved spiral antenna that communicates with a surface station through a very low frequency (VLF) radio in freshwater environment. Compared to the conventional flat spiral antennas, their curved counterparts are geometrically suited for deployment on the rounded shell surface. In this work, we present results from measurement and characterization experiments while deploying these such antennas in freshwater. Our experiments indicate relatively constant reflection coefficient of curved spiral antenna in freshwater at 300 MHz with values comparable with the flat spiral geometry.

articleTitle: Robert C. Hansen – Managing Antenna Expectations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Robert (Bob) Hansen took a "big picture" view of the world of antennas. He wanted to get a reasonable understanding of most, if not all, of the various types of antennas, arrays of antennas, electromagnetic materials, etc. Whenever a new antenna concept appeared, Bob would investigate the fundamentals and report to the community on the "true" capability limits for that concept.

articleTitle: On the Performance of Polarimetric Subtraction Technique for the Detection of Bunkers in the Presence of Surface Clutter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An in-depth analysis of the performance of an imaging-domain, polarimetric subtraction-based clutter-suppression technique is carried out as pertinent to the detection of bunkers located under a slightly rough ground surface. The technique exploits the distinctive scattering behaviors of the ground surface and the target of interest for discrimination in cases in which the target may not even be discernible in the conventional synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images. It is seen that the approach is effective at all practical elevation incidence angles, including in the regions close to normal incidence and beyond the Brewster angle. Consequently, provided that a training clutter scene is available for the derivation of the appropriate cancellation coefficient, the target-to-clutter ratio can be significantly improved.

articleTitle: Solving Realistic Multiscale and Composite Problems using an Integral Equation Domain Decomposition Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work investigates the application of a tear-and-interconnect surface integral equation (SIE) domain decomposition (DD) preconditioner to the electromagnetic solution of realistic large-scale composite problems, including multiple materials and multiscale features. The paper especially considers complex, realistic composite penetrable objects, such as those found in the field of nanoplasmonic applications. The capability and benefits for solving real electromagnetic compatibility problems including multiscale components and multiple materials are exploited and illustrated through several real-world application.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional Triple-Band Printed Dipole Antenna Based on a Dual Frequency SRRs
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a compact triple-band planar antenna. The prototype is based on a printed dipole which is excited with Split Ring Resonators (SRRs) as resonant elements to get three frequency bands. To validate the proposed design, an experimental prototype has been manufactured and measured. Good agreement is achieved between simulation and measurements showing that the proposed antenna has three distinct bands that cover the entire WLAN bands at 2.40 GHz and 5.8 GHz and future PMSE access for video link applications at 7.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Dispersion Division Multiple Access Technique Based on Electromagnetic Time Reversal
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The dispersion division multiple access technique based on electromagnetic time reversal (TR-DDMA) is analyzed and demonstrated using a model with a common channel and three dispersive microstrip lines. Three different messages are transmitted to a receiver simultaneously with the same carrier wave. By using the time reversal technique and three dispersive lines, the three messages can be independently output to three ports through a common channel, which demonstrates the effectiveness of the TR-DDMA technique.

articleTitle: Ultra-Low Power Pulse Width Detector for RF Wake-Up Receivers
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-low power address detector is designed and implemented within a Radio Frequency (RF) wake-up receiver (WuRx) operating at Wi-Fi 802.11b/g bands. The address detector aims to wake-up a sensor from sleep mode to active mode. The WuRx receives a wake-up call (WuC) as a pulse with a specific width that determines the address of the targeted sensor. Once this pulsed WuC is received by the antenna front-end, it is driven into a rectifier circuit that is lodged within the WuRx. The signal is then forwarded into a designed address detector that identifies the address of the sensor based on the width of the received pulse. The designed system relies on ultra-low power components for a selective RF wake-up of a targeted sensor without using a microcontroller or an active processor.

articleTitle: Dual-Band WiFi Applique Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a dual-band Wi-Fi applique antenna using the 5-mm thick automotive windshield glass as the substrate. In order to mitigate the strong surface-wave supported by the substrate at 5.8 GHz, a segmented ring was proposed to help the antenna radiate out of the substrate at 5.8 GHz while not degrading the performance at 2.4 GHz. Simulation and measurement results of the antenna were presented demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed surface-wave mitigating approach.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of Engineered Reflector for Wideband Linear-to-Circular Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the design of reflective engineered surface for wideband linear-to-circular polarization (LP-to-CP) conversion is presented. The proposed LP-to-CP polarizer is composed of symmetric anisotropic unit cell have 90° reflection phase difference between its orthogonal reflection components. A LP-to-CP engineered reflector is composed by 14 × 14 unit cells. When illuminated by an x- or y-polarized incident wave, the proposed engineered reflector converts the incident LP wave to a CP reflected wave. The axial ratio (AR) is less than 3dB from 6.9 GHz to 14.1 GHz and LP-to-CP conversion bandwidth is about 66.6%. The proposed LP-to-CP engineered surface design has been fabricated and it's being measured now to validate its polarization conversion characteristics at microwave band. The measured results will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: High Bandwidth Perovskite based Antenna for High-Resolution Biomedical Imaging at Terahertz
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper suggests the prospective utilization of a hybrid perovskite, with a chemical name of Methylammonium Lead Iodide (CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>PbI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>), in the design of a Terahertz (THz) antenna. A newly developed perovskite material has been used for the antenna design which can replace the conventional metallic patches. The proposed antenna operates in two THz bands, i.e. 3.6-7.4 THz and 8.25-10.0 THz. The realized gain of the antenna is above 4 dBi and efficiency is above 70% in overall operating bandwidth. The reported performance of the antenna design provides the proof of the concept for the possible utilization of non-metallic advanced materials such as perovskite in manufacturing antennas for THz based biomedical applications.

articleTitle: High gain circularly polarized stacked circular patches loaded with a circular sector notches and vertical ground ring for UHF RFID universal reader
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper the design and results of circularly polarized broad band antenna covering the universal UHF RFID band (840-960 MHz) is presented. The antenna is constructed from two layers of circular patches above a circular ground plane. Each patch has two rounded circular sector notches on opposite sides. The lower circular patch is coaxially fed, and in turn is feeding a parasitic top patch. The resultant axial ratio is below 2.5 dB across the whole band with gain reaching 9 dBi. The size of the ground plane was reduced by adding a vertical ring at edge of the circular ground plane.

articleTitle: Wideband Millimeter-Wave Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel technique is presented to enhance the gain of a rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) over a wideband. The antenna structure achieves a 16 GHz bandwidth of relative bandwidth of 27.5 % in the 60 GHz band. The peak realized gain is 12.6 dBi with a total antenna radiation efficiency of 96 %. Printed Electromagnetic Band Gap (EBG) technology has been used to feed the antenna and eliminate any parasitic radiation from the feed line. The antenna is suitable for high data rate short-range personal area networks applications at millimeter wave frequencies.

articleTitle: Research on Kernel Functions of SVM for Line-of-sight Identification in Vehicle-to-Vehicle MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Generally, propagation channels show significantly different characteristics for line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions. Due to their good performance in classification problems, support vector machines (SVM) have been widely used for NLOS identification of propagation channels. In this paper, we investigate the impact of different kernel functions on the accuracy of SVM-based NLOS identification and validate the performance based on measured channel data. We find that a Gaussian kernel reduces the mis-identification rate by a factor 4 compared to a linear kernel, and also outperforms polynomial and sigmoid kernels.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Coaxial Collinear Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a wideband high-gain coaxial collinear antenna with a stable radiation pattern. Based on the fat dipole idea, the configuration of the classical coaxial collinear antenna is modified and an 8-section coaxial collinear antenna is designed. The -10dB impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna reaches 36.5 MHz at a center frequency of 450 MHz, which is three times more than the bandwidth of the classical antenna, while it maintains 9 dB gain.

articleTitle: On the Integration of Antennas With Touch Sensor Panels
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Next generation personal electronic devices have optically transparent (OT) touch sensor as an indispensable component of the user interface and rely extensively on high-speed wireless connectivity. Since the real estate for these compact devices is limited, the integration of miniaturized antennas is very challenging. This paper discusses several strategies on integrated antennas in this regard, and presents a flexible OT touch sensor panel with a coplanar antenna element operating at 2.4 GHz for Bluetooth and Wi-Fi applications. The designed touch sensor panel has been characterized for its touch performance. Investigations have also been carried out on the antenna element and little to no change in its radiation performance has been observed upon touch.

articleTitle: A Dual Band UWB antenna for WCE Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna is designed for Wireless Capsule Endoscopy (WCE) systems by applying several miniaturization and bandwidth enhancement techniques. The antenna is designed on Roger RT5880 as a substrate having ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 2.2 and thickness of 0.254 mm. The volume of the optimized antenna is only 28.9 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The performances of the antenna are investigated inside a homogeneous human muscle layer. The -10 dB S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> bandwidth for the first band is from 5.72 GHz to 6.26 GHz and for the second band is from 8.12 GHz to 8.58 GHz. It shows omnidirectional radiation patterns. Maximum power of 24 mW can be set as input to the proposed antenna in order to comply with the IEEE C95.1-2005 safety standards.

articleTitle: A High Gain Rectenna For Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a high gain rectenna for energy harvesting applications. The antenna is based on a multilayer substrate structure fed by aperture coupled and operates at 5.8 GHz with a gain of 10.2 dBi. A single diode rectifier design with good output DC voltage and efficiency at low input power for 5.8 GHz Wifi band is also designed and described. The simulated results including reflection coefficient, output DC voltage and efficiency are provided.

articleTitle: Miniaturized SIW-CBS Planar TX/RX Antenna Arrays For Microwave CW/FMCW Doppler Radars
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Miniaturized Substrate Integrated Waveguide Cavity-Backed Slot (SIW-CBS) planar transmit and receive (TX/RX) antenna arrays are presented. A composite right/left handed (CRLH) structure is used as an interdigital slot on the topside of the SIW cavity to achieve the miniaturization. A two-layer substrate structure is used to isolate the antenna from the potential radar electronics. The resonance frequency and bandwidth are set to be 5.8 GHz and 50 MHz. The array miniaturization ratio achieved by the antenna element employing the CRLH structure is ~60% and ~20% compared to a rectangular slot SIW-CBS antenna array and a patch antenna array, respectively. Each array shows a pure radiation pattern with the gain of ~15 dB and 12 dB of front-to-back ratio.

articleTitle: A Modified Beckmann-Kirchhoff Scattering Model for Slightly Rough Surfaces at Terahertz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The diffuse reflection of electromagnetic waves is merely dependent on the surface roughness, incident angles, complex refractive index of materials and wavelength at hand. At terahertz frequencies, diffuse reflection tends to be particularly strong due to the increased surface roughness and this causes an additional attenuation even in the specular direction of reflection. In this paper, we examine the terahertz (THz) channel from 300 GHz (0.3 THz) to 310 GHz (0.31 THz) in the presence of slightly rough surfaces (0 <; g ≪ 1) by using the approximate solutions from Rayleigh-Rice (R-R) and Beckmann-Kirchhoff (B-K) scattering theories. However, the classical Beckmann-Kirchhoff theory contains a small-angle limitation (i.e., it fails at large angles of incidence and wide scattering angles). Thus, we also endeavor to demonstrate the modified Beckmann-Kirchhoff scattering theory, an approach by Verold and Harvey, using multipath channel transfer function (CTF) dynamics for line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) conditions in a simple office environment.

articleTitle: MIMO Antenna for Indoor Low-Band 5G Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband high efficiency cavity-backed antenna with independent beams is presented. The design is milled in a metallic box and capacitively fed by 4 coaxial cables. Matching is accomplished with the use of an impedance transformer created by the extension of the coaxial inner conductor. This antenna is a compact, and low-cost solution which can be easily manufactured to be mounted as a 5G indoor base station antenna providing MIMO behaviour due to its four independent beams. The operating frequency band ranges from 3 GHz to 5 GHz (50%), covering the early deployment 5G low band. The results of the simulations show a total efficiency greater than 67%. By properly feeding the ports, the antenna can be configured to radiate with horizontal polarization, vertical polarization or circular polarization. The overall dimensions of the antenna are λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>×λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>×0.25λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> the wavelength at the central frequency (4 GHz).

articleTitle: Waveguide-Fed Lens Based Beam-Steering Antenna For 5G Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a two-dimensional cylindrical Lens antenna based on the parallel plate technique is designed. It supports beam-steering capability of 58° at 28 GHz. The antenna is composed of low loss rectangular waveguide antennas, which are positioned around a homogeneous cylindrical Teflon lens in the air region of two conducting parallel plates. The Beam scanning can be achieved by switching between the antenna elements. The main advantages of our design include its relative simplicity, ease of fabrication, and high-power handling capability. Compared to previous works including a curvature optimization for the plate separation of the parallel plates, the proposed antenna has a constant distance between plates. At the 28 GHz, the maximum simulated gain value is about 19 dB. Furthermore, the designed antenna only deviates about 0.4 dB over the 58° scan range.

articleTitle: 5G MIMO Antenna System for Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband 4-antenna array system that can cover the 5G new radio band N77 (3.3-4.2GHz) is proposed for the 5G operation in mobile terminals. The antenna system is based on the self-isolated antenna element and thus quite high isolation (better than -17.9 dB) within the entire band is achieved for the proposed antenna system. The envelope correlation coefficient and the channel capacity of the MIMO antenna system are also studied. The results such as antenna S-parameter, current distribution, radiation pattern and efficiency are also presented.

articleTitle: Conformal Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna With Parasitic Elements For 5G Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a conformal antipodal Vivaldi antenna design on a Liquid Crystal Polymer (LCP) substrate that operates in the 5G millimeter frequency range. A double exponentially tapered Vivaldi antenna is used to achieve wide bandwidth, and the planar directors in front of the slot aperture help to increase the antenna directivity, also the elliptic substrate at the front end serves as a dielectric lens to further enhance the gain. The conformal nature of the LCP substrate allows the antenna to be flexibly integrated into vehicle radome and hand held mobile devices, while maintaining stable radiation characteristics. Moreover, such antenna can be used in a large quantity in the active incoherent millimeter wave imaging system due to its low cost, light-weight, and compact features. The simulated -10 dB impedance bandwidth is 8.2 GHz (37.3 GHz to 45.5 GHz) with the maximum simulated realized gain of 9.7 dBi at 40 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a 1×4 CPW Microstrip Antenna Array on PET substrate for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a single layer Coplanar Waveguide-fed microstrip patch antenna array is presented for biomedical applications. The proposed antenna array is realized on a transparent and flexible Polyethylene Terephthalate substrate. The design has 4 radiating elements with single CPW feed and measures only 280 × 192 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The antenna array resonates at 2.68 GHz and has a peak gain of 10 dBi. A prototype is fabricated using cost effective adhesive copper foils instead of conventional copper or silver nanoparticle ink. The corresponding measured results agree well with the simulated results. The proposed low-profile and cost-efficient transmit antenna array has the potential for wearable applications, including wireless powering of implantable medical devices.

articleTitle: Physical Optics Modeling of Scattering by Checkerboard Structure for RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Physical optics (PO) is utilized to analyze scattering by checkerboard-patterned structures. It is observed that it can predict the RCS along non-specular directions. The locations of the scattered major lobes using PO and array theory are compared with finite elements method (FEM). Moreover, closed-form solutions developed using PO are used to design nonuniform checkerboard surfaces to enhance the RCS-reduction bandwidth. The PO-based results compare well with data obtained by measurements.

articleTitle: Categorizing Metamaterials by using Equivalent Dielectric Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new approach for categorizing metamaterials and metasurfaces, which is based on their equivalent dielectric representation, is presented in this paper. The first step in this process is to replace the unit cell of the metasurfaces by a permittivity tensor by using a procedure described in the paper. The procedure is general and is applicable to both isotropic and anisotropic metasurfaces. An important attribute of the present is that it enables one to reduce the simulation time significantly, by replacing the original metasurface, which typically has fine and/or multiscale features, with homogeneous equivalent dielectric materials that are much easier to deal with numerically than is the original metasurface.

articleTitle: Applicability of SSTDR Analysis of Complex Loads
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Spread spectrum time domain reflectometry (SSTDR) can be used to measure complex impedances in live electrical systems by evaluating the shape and magnitude of the reflected signature. A range of capacitors or inductors can be identified, but above and below this range, they cannot be distinguished from open or short circuits. This range depends on the frequency band of the reflectometry system and characteristic impedance of the transmission line. This can be used to characterize changes in complex impedance for the purpose of fault detection in complex loads, such as PV panels and systems.

articleTitle: Massively Parallel Simulation of Antenna Array Using Domain Decomposition Method and a High-Performance Computing Scheme
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A massively parallel electromagnetic field solver is developed for simulating large antenna array based on supercomputer using domain decomposition method (DDM) together with an in-house massively parallel computing scheme. The proposed solver is validated by comparing the simulated results with that obtained by commercial software. In particular, its speedup, scalability and efficiency are examined in the simulation of some typical large antenna arrays operating at different frequencies. It is numerically demonstrated that our parallel solver can reach a speedup of 7.149 and strong scalability efficiency of 89.36% on 512 CPU cores of 32 computing nodes. Further, a more challenging model is tested by using 1024 CPU cores of 64 computing nodes.

articleTitle: Origami-Enabled Frequency Reconfigurable Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we present a dipole antenna which demonstrates resonance-frequency reconfiguration enabled by the application of Origami folding methods. The antenna resembles a regular dipole antenna at the unfolded state and mimics a bow tie antenna when is completely folded. The simulated results show a frequency reconfiguration over a bandwidth of 2.41 GHz. To enable the design-process, an in house toolset is developed which generates 3-D origami substrates in ANSYS HFSS utilizing origami math algorithms linked with Mathematica.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact High-Gain Slotted Trapezoidal Antenna at 2.45 GHz For Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact, high gain, simple design, and high efficient single layer slotted dipole antenna is presented. The proposed antenna is fabricated on a low-cost commercial FR4 substrate and is suitable for RF energy harvesting applications. The antenna design relying on a simple modified trapezoidal dipole antenna patterned with a rectangular slot to minimize the inductive loading on the input impedance. A four-arms of a trapezoidal structure are arranged on a half-circle configuration. The performance of the antenna is studied using the simulation and experimental measurements. The antenna offers the main lobe in the z-plane direction with more than 6.5 dBi gain. The input reflection coefficient is measured at 2.45 GHz with a bandwidth extending from 2.4 to 2.5 GHz. The antenna has a small footprint and its dimensions are 32 × 34 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Series Chained Patch Phased Array Antenna for mmWave 5G Mobile in Metal Bezel Design
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a series chained patch phased array antenna for metal bezel design mobile application operating millimeter-wave (mmWave) 5G communication at 28GHz. The proposed antenna is 2 × 4 series chained patch antenna array implemented on the corner of metal bezel of mobile device. Also it is designed for beam steering in xy-plane and yz-plane. The metal chain is added and implemented between patch element for its robustness and metal fabrication. The maximum gains of the proposed antenna in xy-plane are 12.8 dBi, 12.9 dBi and 13 dBi. Beam steering angle is ± 45 degrees at xy-plane and ± 30 degrees at yz-plane. The detail of the design methodologies, simulation and measurement results are presented and discussed in relation to the targeted mmWave 5G mobile application.

articleTitle: On Modal Excitation Using Capacitive Coupling Elements and Matching Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A resonant characteristic mode (CM) is useful for antenna design if it is properly excited and well matched to the source. In this paper, we consider the feed design for the excitation of the fundamental CM of a rectangular chassis. The tradeoff between the required number of capacitive coupling elements (CCE) and matching elements used for achieving a given antenna bandwidth is studied. The results reveal that in order to attain the modal bandwidth of the fundamental mode, the use of multiple CCEs with optimal placement and phase simplifies the required matching network.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of Multiband Antenna Based on Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: With the development of the fifth generation (5G) mobile communication, the demands of the multiband antenna are on the increase [1]. In this paper, we proposed a design of multiband antenna using a pixel patch as a unit which elements are optimized by non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II). The measured and simulation results presented contain three bands, which highlights the benefits of the antenna design with multiband for use in 5G applications.

articleTitle: Design of a Terahertz Reconfigurable Reflectarray with Individually Controlled 1-bit Phasing Elements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Terahertz (THz) high gain antennas with electronic beam-scanning capability have been long required in various modern applications. In this paper, a novel reconfigurable reflectarray antenna (RRA) at 0.3 THz with 16×16 individually controlled 1-bit phasing elements is proposed. The element consists of a shorted bow-tie microstrip patch and a double-channel heterostructure HEMT in the middle. Electronic 1-bit phase control can be achieved by switching the state of HEMT. The element simulation verifies its wideband and low cross-polarization performance. Design and analysis of a RRA with 16×16 elements and practical biasing circuits are presented. The high gain beam scanning capability of the proposed RRA is validated by theoretical calculations.

articleTitle: Phased Array Bandwidth Defined by Beam Squint and Pulse Dispersion
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Antenna arrays were originally designed for a single frequency. The term phased array implies a narrow band approach to beam steering and adaptive nulling. This paper takes a look at the beam squint and dispersion problems associated with high data rate phased array antennas. This paper is a tribute to R.C. Hansen who spent a career investigating antenna effects on wide band signals. He advocated the use of time delay in addition to phase shifters in a high data rate antenna array.

articleTitle: Enabling High Efficiency Bandwidth Electrically Small Antennas through Direct Antenna Modulation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: High-bandwidth communications in electrically small antennas (ESA's) are often limited by the inherent narrowband performance physically defined by Chu's limit for these types of emitters. With the advent of compact platforms in unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV's) which may have electrically small volumes yet utilized in systems such as Internet of Things (IoT), supporting such technologies require high-performance antennas capable of radiating high-bandwidth signals. We propose a novel capacitively loaded loop antenna (CLLA), comprised of two complementary and symmetrical high-power high figure-of-merit (FoM) GaN transistors. The antenna utilizes Direct Antenna Modulation (DAM) which, through the transistors, carefully modulate the input RF signal. This allows the transmission of high-bandwidth signals, despite the high radiation Q-factor of the CLLA. The DAM antenna was prototyped, measured, and compared to a conventional CLLA without transistors. The antenna radiates high-bandwidth signals and shows significant efficiency-bandwidth product improvement over traditional ESA's.

articleTitle: Broad Band and Wide Scan SIW Cavity-backed Phased Arrays for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel wideband cavity backed planar antenna and its arrays for fifth-generation (5G) wireless cellular networks is proposed. The proposed element is composed of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity, hollow cavity, and stacked patches. It presents the advantages of compact size, simple feed structure, and low profile. The design has been constructed with a 8×8 (64 element) array. Results show that the infinite array unit cell achieves about 19% bandwidth (26.2-31.7 GHz) with active VSWR ≤ 2 when scanning up to ±40°, and nearly 16.6% bandwidth (26-30.7 GHz) with VSWR ≤ 3.6 when scanning up to ±65° in all azimuth planes. Numerical Results of full-wave simulation by virtue of HFSS demonstrate the design.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Anti-Interference Slot Antenna Using Metamaterial Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a waveguide slot filtering antenna with dual-band anti-interference performance is presented. First, a filtering waveguide is described. It is comprised of a common rectangular waveguide and a metamaterial surface embedded at the bottom of the waveguide cavity. The meta-surface is comprised of two kinds of alternatively distributed metal nails. Under proper design, dual bandgaps can be arrived by the meta-surface at specified frequency ranges, in which the propagation of electromagnetic wave is stopped. As a result, a dual-band bandstop filter function is obtained by the waveguide. Then, a filtering antenna is achieved by cutting radiating slots at the top of the filtering waveguide. A proposed filtering antenna prototype is designed with working band at S-band while two stopbands at C-band and X-band, respectively. The simulated results show that the proposed antenna has good radiating performance as the common waveguide slot antenna. At the same time, strong suppression levels more than 40dB and 50dB are obtained by the proposed antenna within the two stopbands, respectively.

articleTitle: UWB Modified Elliptical Antipodal Vivaldi antenna array fed with four stage Wilkinson Power Divider
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an UWB array that is constructed from two elements of a newly modified broadband Elliptical Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna (EAVA) is presented and four-stage Wilkinson power divider as the feeding network. The array is developed to provide a high gain array that can be used in reflection measurement characterization of dielectric materials over a wide frequency range. In order to achieve an acceptable array performance across the wide band frequency (0.7-10 GHz), a fixture was designed to manually adjust physical spacing between the elements. The performances of the array element, the power divider and the antenna array system are measured and have proven an acceptable performance in the desired band.

Author Keywords: Vivaldi Antenna Elliptical Tapered Slot Edge

articleTitle: Microstrip-fed Scanned Dipole Antenna Array for 5G Applictions
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes a novel millimeter wave (mm-Wave) microstrip-fed antenna array, designed for beam-scanning, for fifth generation (5G) applications. Unlike microstrip patches or waveguide slots, the array element chosen in the present design is a 3D-dipole, which is excited by using either a single or a balanced microstrip line. The performance characteristics of the proposed design are investigated in the frequency range of 25-30 GHz, and are shown to be very good. The issue of scanning the array without the use of lossy and expensive phase shifters is addressed, and a switcher with one input and 5 outputs (SP5T) based configuration is proposed to achieve the beam scan.

articleTitle: Magnetic Induction-based Human Activity Recognition (MI-HAR)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) is a growing research area with applications in a variety of domains, such as healthcare, rehabilitation, daily life-logging, personal fitness, senior care, and assistance for people with cognitive disorders. Detection of human movements using body sensor networks is one of the most popular yet challenging approaches. There are critical challenges inherent in the sensor-based activity recognition method, such as power management, security, and coverage. Lossy mediums, such as the human body can significantly affect the electromagnetic wave propagating systems. In this paper, we introduce a novel wireless system based on magnetic induction (MI) and deep learning for human activity recognition to address the main challenges and constraints. The generated synthetic MI motion signals are also presented. The proposed MI system is integrated with machine learning techniques to model and detect human activities.

articleTitle: A Yagi-Uda Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna for WiMAX Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a pattern reconfigurable array antenna with linear polarization is presented. It comprises three parts that include a driving element centered between two other parasitic elements. To achieve pattern reconfiguration, the approach of Yagi-Uda configuration is employed, where the positions of the reflector and director are to be interchanged using DC-controlled electronic switches. Five scanning angles at the same operating frequency of 3.65 GHz are obtained with an acceptable input impedance matching in all switching schemes.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized V-Shaped Patch Antenna for RFID Application
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A circularly polarized (CP) V-shaped patch antenna is proposed. Different from normal patch antennas, the suggested antenna employs a 3-dimentional V-shaped patch as the radiator. Two wings of the V-shaped patch gradually change antenna height and provide the impedance taper, therefore increases the bandwidth. The bottom of the "V" avoid large inductive reactance introduced by long feed probes. And a metal screw shorted to the ground has been added to significantly improve the impedance matching and CP performance. Good agreement has been observed between simulation and measurement. Measured results show that this antenna has an impedance bandwidth (|S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <; -10 dB) of 22 %, and a 3 dB AR bandwidth of 4.4 %, gain is around 8 dBi with a 915 MHz center frequency. Overall, the proposed antenna is very suitable for RFID applications.

articleTitle: Wideband Metasurface for Microwave Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband metasurface based absorber is proposed for microwave electromagnetic energy harvesting. A unit cell of the metasurface consists of dodecagon shape with two vias to allow for ultrawideband reception response. The vias are connected to resistive loads to channel and dissipate the absorbed energy. Numerical simulation results show that the metasurface is capable of capturing the incoming microwave energy with a bandwidth of 10.7 GHz and efficiencies higher than 50%.

articleTitle: Toward Large-Scale Dynamically Reconfigurable Apertures Using Graphene
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a novel fabrication technique for large-scale, on-wafer graphene devices. With the proposed technique, large-area graphene apertures can be fabricated, enabling the proliferation of graphene-based reconfigurable devices, including metasurfaces. Such topologies require large-area high yield fabrication processes. To avoid graphene delamination during the chemical processes of the fabrication, we use a titanium sacrificial layer to protect the graphene monolayer. To evaluate the fabrication method, we present broadband in-plane graphene measurements in the 220-330 GHz band for the first time and compare the measured resistance sheet with previous works.

articleTitle: A Multi-Level Reconstruction Algorithm for Electrical Capacitance Tomography Based on Modular Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Electrical capacitance tomography (ECT) enables the imaging of multiphase flow systems in industrial processes. Recovering flow profiles from measured capacitance data in ECT is an inverse problem that is traditionally solved using numerical algorithms such as the Landweber and Tikhonov regularization (TV) methods. This paper, however, proposes a machine learning-based approach to the ECT inverse problem through the use of modular deep neural networks (MDNNs) in a multi-level image reconstruction scheme. The basis behind the method put forth is, instead of having a single neural network take in the capacitance measurements and perform the inverse imaging task on its own, the reconstruction is delegated to separate sub-neural networks that each only recovers the image on a particular subsection of the imaging domain. Our proposed approach has demonstrated improvement upon the Landweber and TV algorithms in terms of reconstruction accuracy, suggesting that MDNNs are suitable candidates for tackling inverse imaging problems.

articleTitle: 4-40 GHz Permittivity Measurements of Indoor Building Materials
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The transmission properties of common building materials, such as glass and red brick, are measured at normal incidence over a range of 4-40 GHz in a modular anechoic chamber using a vector network analyzer. Complex permittivity values are estimated using only transmission S-parameters of the material under test and an air reference measurement. Results suggest that the method provides reasonable estimates of complex permittivity at high microwave and lower mm-wave frequencies.

articleTitle: Nonreciprocal Radiation Pattern Metasurface Transformer
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the concept of nonreciprocal radiation pattern metasurface transformer. The metasurface is placed on top of a source antenna, transforms the radiation pattern of the source antenna, introducing different radiation patterns for transmit and receive states. The metasurface is composed of an array of unit cells, each of which consist of receive and transmit antenna elements and a nonreciprocal phase shifter. The priliminary analytical results proves the operation and functionality of the metasurface transformer. The proposed metasurface transformer may presenst different interesting properties including radiation pattern tunability, angular sector and gain.

articleTitle: High Gain Millimeter-Wave Slot Antenna with Symmetric Radiation Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a new generic design perspective to boost the gain and provide symmetric radiation characteristics of electric or magnetic current elements. The symmetric radiation characteristic is similar to a magneto-electric dipole, but with higher gain and narrower bandwidth. The antenna is realized by an excited wide slot surrounded by a rectangular dielectric ring. The antenna achieves 11.5-dBi gain and 13% relative matching bandwidth centered at 60 GHz.

articleTitle: Antenna-on-Display (AoD) for Millimeter-wave 5G Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a novel concept of an optically invisible antenna-on-display (AoD) realized using photolithography that can be integrated in active display panels such as OLEDs and LCDs. The proposed approach is exemplified for future millimeter-wave 5G mobile devices. A multi-layer structure with AoD is proposed and designed for potential beam-steering applications. The designed and fabricated 1×8 AoD exhibits 9.16 dBi boresight gain at 28 GHz while maintaining 88% optical transparency.

articleTitle: Broadband Linear Antenna Arrays with Frequency-Invariant Half-Power Beamwidth
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper reports on the design of broadband four-element antenna arrays with frequency-invariant half-power beamwidth (HPBW) within a bandwidth (BW) of 3:1. They are based on frequency-selective feed networks that gradually shift the power from the outer elements to the inner ones as frequency increases. The operating principles of the proposed concept are presented through a four-element array of isotropic radiators.
