For practical validation, a 3:1 elliptical monopole antenna array fed by a feednetwork that comprises two second order low-pass and two fifth-order high-pass filters was developed. It exhibited HPBW variation of ±26.5% in the frequency range 2-6 GHz.

articleTitle: Gesture Recognition Using A Portable and Flexible Meta-Atom Panel and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present here a gesture recognition technique based on a flexible and portable meta-atom tag (e.g. split-ring resonator or SRR). By inject printing of nano-silver conductive film on PET substrate, we demonstrate that a compact meta-atom array can behave as an RFID tag for cyber-physical applications. The experimental and theoretical analysis on radar cross section (RCS) response as functions of the meta-atom geometry show the capability of the proposed system in the robust and accurate gesture recognition. Moreover, we propose an error auto-correction readout technique based on the neural network to make this system feasible for a widen spectral range and large number of binary combinations.

articleTitle: Design of a Transverse Slot Array in Groove Gap Waveguide using Horns at 28 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We design an array of transverse slots cut out from the broad wall of a groove-gap waveguide, with periodic spacing between slots of a guided wavelength at 28 GHz that is centered about an important millimeter-wave band. External horns are brought upon to address the problem of grating lobes. The simulations have been carried out for operation in the designed frequency band from 27.676 to 28.652 GHz while preserving the conditions for port matching. This antenna solution lends itself to many applications within this millimeter-wave band.

articleTitle: A Tri-Band Shared-Aperture Antenna for Wi-Fi MIMO and Beam-Scanning Wi-Gig Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A tri-band shared-aperture antenna (2.4, 5.2 and 60 GHz) is proposed in this paper. It is the first time to put these three bands of antennas within the same radiator, and then realize the operation of both 2.4/5.2 GHz Wi-Fi application combined with the multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology and 60 GHz wireless gigabit (Wi-Gig) application simultaneously. By using the structure-reused technology, the spiraled dual-band inverted-F antenna (PIFA) at the Wi-Fi frequency band and the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) leaky-wave antenna at the Wi-Gig frequency band can share the same radiator without adding extra aperture area. Thus, the radiation aperture utilization ratio can increase from 0 to 92.4%. What's more, the MIMO technology is also applied to the Wi-Fi antenna design. The calculated ECC are all lower than 0.04, and the radiation efficiencies are 85-95% and 87-97% at these two bands respectively. Thanks to the MIMO design for the Wi-Fi operation, Wi-Gig antennas can obtain the high gain (a peak gain of 12.29 dBi) and the wide range of beam coverage (±36° from 57 to 64 GHz) at the same time. The antenna design has been validated by the experimental results.

articleTitle: An Aperture-Coupled Dual-Polarized Stacked Patch Antenna for Multi-Layer Organic Package Integration
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an aperture-coupled dual-polarized stacked patch antenna integrated in an RFIC package environment for Ka-band applications. The package is based on multilayer organic technology, so it can be fabricated by PCB manufacturers. The antenna has a measured peak gain > 5 dBi and supports a 4 GHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Development of High Aperture Efficiency Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Fabry-Perot cavity antenna (FPCA) system with high efficiency is proposed. The design consists of a source antenna with a frequency selective surface (FSS). The source antenna is an aperture coupled microstrip slot antenna with cavity backing. The FSS is a square aperture with rectangular unit cells. The E-field in the near and far field is compared for the FPCA system and the source antenna without the FSS (i.e. source antenna only). The FPCA has low phase variation of approximately 10° in the E-plane compared to high sinusoidal phase variation of 90° of the source antenna. The far-field gain of the FPCA system is 11.3 dB, which is a 4.5 dB improvement of the source antenna gain. The aperture efficiency of the FPCA system is 84% compared to the source antenna efficiency of 30%.

articleTitle: An Ultra-thin Triple-band Smartwatch Antenna with Support of Several Wireless Application Bands
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact planar ultra-thin triple band antenna is introduced. The proposed antenna with three bands can cover the Galileo, GPS, Glonass, DCS, PCS, UMTS, LTE2400, LTE2500, WiMAX, and WLAN bands. The suggested antenna has a simple configuration, consisting of a monopole radiating element on top of the substrate, and a small ground at the bottom of the substrate. The triple band of the antenna is achieved by using complementary split-ring resonators and cutting some slots to optimize and widen the operating bands of the antenna. The antenna has a simple and compact configuration, and so it is cost effective. With the small total size of 35mm ×30mm×0.5 mm, it can be a good choice for portable ultra-thin wireless handsets, like smartwatches.

articleTitle: Design of Compact UWB Coplanar Waveguide-Fed Modified Sierpinski Carpet Fractal Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact coplanar waveguide-fed planar fractal antenna for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications is designed. The proposed approach consists of two iterations modified Sierpinski hexagonal slots with hexagonal radiation patch and CPW feeding. It has a simple structure with compact size of 16.5×14.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. An impedance bandwidth of 112.2% (3.03-10.77 GHz) is achieved, with a maximum peak gain of 3.74dBi at 8.15 GHz. With these promising features, this antenna is suitable for UWB communication applications.

articleTitle: Spatial characterization of the ambient backscatter communication performance in line-of-sight
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An ambient backscatter device, or Radio Frequency (RF) tag, transmits information to an RF reader simply by modulating the propagation channel between an ambient RF source such as TV broadcast and a reader. Here, the tag switches between two scattering states (e.g., scattering or transparency to RF waves) and influences the reader received power. A basic power-detector is sufficient, as long as the contrast between the two levels of received power is sufficiently large compared to the noise floor. This low complexity communication technology is therefore promising for Internet-Of-Things (IoT) applications. We characterize theoretically, numerically and experimentally, the power contrast (PC) and the bit error rate, as a function of the relative positions of the source, reader and tag. Surprisingly, even in line-of-sight, PC is subject to deep fades. Indeed, the scattered path added by the tag does not always modify the reader received power. Our experiments and simulations at 2.4, 3.5 and 5.2 GHz, show that the tag is indeed well detected on regularly spaced ellipses with the source and the reader at foci locations.

articleTitle: A Vanadium Dioxide Microbolometer in the Transition Region for Millimeter Wave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a new class of microbolometer that exhibits high responsivity for passive imaging arrays (camera) at millimeter wave (mmW) band. The main objective is to exploit the non-linear behavior of phase-change material (PCM) vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) by biasing the sensor at the transition cliff (~68 °C). Simulated results together with calculations show high responsivity of 7.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> V/W and low noise equivalent power (NEP) of 6.1 pW/√Hz. The corresponding response time of the proposed microbolometer is 376 µs. Two orders of magnitude improvement in device performance as compared with the state-of-the-art sensors is the direct result of both suspension in air by micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) microfabrication processing as well as the sharp change in resistivity of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in its transition region.

articleTitle: Design of 2-bit Programmable Reflective Metasurface in K-band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Programmable metasurface has enabled real-time manipulation of electromagnetic (EM) waves to achieve diverse applications by the spatial distribution of digital bits. In this paper, we present a 2-bit programmable reflective metasurface for dynamic control of electromagnetic wave in K-band. Each unit cell of proposed metasurface contains two PIN diodes which can produce phase responses of 0, π/2, π and 3π/2 by changing the states of PIN diode. A phase difference of 90° degree is realized between adjacent states and total phase shift range of 360° is achieved. The proposed metasurface can be used for beam manipulation, beam diffusion and realized different far-field patterns by designing different coding sequence for PIN diodes.

articleTitle: The Square Kilometre Array Observatory
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: When constructed, the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) will be the World's largest Radio Observatory. Its observations at unprecedented sensitivity will help to solve some of the biggest questions in the field of astronomy and give astronomers insight into the formation and evolution of the first stars and galaxies after the Big Bang, the role of cosmic magnetism, the nature of gravity, and possibly even life beyond Earth. This paper provides a description of the SKA Observatory and its main sub-systems.

articleTitle: A Characteristic Mode Based Decoupling Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel and compact decoupling structure has been introduced in this work to improve the mutual coupling of a two element microstrip antenna array. A systematic blending of electric and magnetic dipoles lead to the construction of the isolating element whose working principle has been explained using the theory of characteristic modes.

articleTitle: Simulation Design of Dual Band Metamaterial Absorber Based on the Fractal Structure
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new dual band metamaterial absorber based on sun fractal structure is presented. The proposed metamaterial absorber unit cell is printed on FR-4 substrate with thickness 1.6 mm and it has compact size 37×37 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed metamaterial absorber structure exhibits two distinct absorption peaks at 2.24 and 7 GHz with peak absorption values of 97.2 and 98 % respectively. All simulation results are performed using the Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Microwave Studio 2018 software.

articleTitle: 3:1 Bandwidth Dual Polarized Feeds for Compact Range and Near-Field Probes
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The authors have developed a new family of dual-polarized compact range feeds with a bandwidth ratio of 3:1. These feeds are also suitable for use as near-field probes.

articleTitle: Bending Analysis of Switchable Frequency Selective Surface Based on Flexible Composite Substrate
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper presents a switchable frequency selective surface (FSS) based on composite flexible substrate has been investigated. To make the FSS switchable, various combinations of switches are used. The design is bent E-field and H-field directions over various bending curvatures and the corresponding behavior is analyzed. It is observed that design has less variation when bending is applied along H-field direction. Whereas, slight variations are observed when bending is applied along the E-field direction. It is noted that the design exhibits stop band and pass band characteristics. Furthermore, in pass band it provides single wideband and dual band operations. These characteristics are preserved when bending is applied, thus making it suitable for wearable applications and modern communication systems.

articleTitle: Compact Broadband Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna With a Cross-slotted Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a compact circularly polarized (CP) antenna fed by microstrip line is proposed to work at millimeter wave band. The single series feeding line coupling with cross-slots in the ground plane creates a phase difference and excites orthogonal modes for circular polarization. Sequential rotation of current excited on the surface of radiating patch broadens the axial ratio bandwidth compared with the traditional CP patch antenna. The proposed antenna covers an impedance bandwidth (|S11|<; -10 dB) from 25 to 36.58 GHz (37.61%) and a 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth from 30.8 to 36.13 GHz (15.92%). The gain is greater than 5 dBi over the band. The proposed antenna has the merits of low profile, wide axial ratio bandwidth, and high gain.

articleTitle: Characterization of Microchamber Arrays for Targeted Drug Delivery
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Drug delivery devices have been recently emerged as a significant facet of therapeutic treatment. Most of the devices comprises of tiny reservoir based structures for carrying and delivering drugs to a targeted location in human body. In this paper, the material characterization of microchamber arrays is presented. The microchamber arrays were prepared in the thin layer of Graphene Oxide deposited on a glass substrate. In the next step, the complementary split ring resonator (CSRR) sensor was used to characterize the tiny reservoirs of microchamber arrays. It was observed that the permittivity of microchamber arrays have an impact on the resonant frequency of CSRR.

articleTitle: Dual Functional MIMO Antenna System for mm-Wave 5G and 2 GHz 4G Communications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual feed tapered slot antenna with multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) configurations is presented for 4G/5G mobile applications. The proposed MIMO antenna system covers 1.9-2.6 GHz band for 4G and 27-40 GHz band 5G. At 4G band, the structure operates as an open-ended slot antenna (X/4 long at 2.6 GHz) and gives omnidirectional radiation patterns. At the 5G band, it works as a tapered slot antenna (3k long at 28 GHz) and gives a directive beam with end-fire radiation patterns. This dualfunctionality of the tapered slot is unique and attractive to cover multi-bands for dual wireless standards. For geometry modelling of the proposed design, the substrate Rogers RT/duroid 5880 is used with an overall size of 158×77×0.38 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> which matches the size of the latest mobile handheld devices.

articleTitle: Wideband Propagation Channel Measurements in an Indoor Office Environment at 26 GHz
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, useful measurement results of the propagation channel characteristics in an indoor office environment at 26 GHz are presented. The parameters of both the floating-intercept (FI) and close-in (CI) free space reference distance path loss models have been derived from channel measurements. The time dispersion characteristics have been analyzed in terms of both the root-mean-square (rms) delay spread and the coherence bandwidth. These results allow us to have a better knowledge of the propagation channel characteristics and can be also used to evaluate the performance of fifth generation (5G) networks in indoor office scenarios.

articleTitle: A Compact 2 by 2 Printed Yagi-Uda Antenna Array with Enhanced Isolation and Gain
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design and experimental evaluation of a compact 2 by 2 printed Yagi antenna array at 5.8 GHz. The planar array has a rectangular grid with d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>=0.5λ and d<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sub>=0.2λ. To alleviate performance degradation due to the reduced element spacing of 0.2λ, parasitic dipoles are placed in the closely- spaced stacked Yagi array. The designed parasitic elements improve the isolation between the stacked Yagis by over 15 dB and increase the gain of 2×2 array from 7.76 dB to 9.343 dB. Measurements of the fabricated prototype confirm the simulated predictions. The proposed technique is a low-cost solution for improving the achievable gain of a planar printed Yagi array in constrained form factor designs.

articleTitle: Solving Cybersecurity Problem by Symmetric Dual-Space Formulation—Physical and Cybernetic
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: To address cybersecurity, this author proposed recently the approach of formulating it in symmetric dual-space and dual-system. This paper further explains this concept, beginning with symmetric Maxwell Equation (ME) and Fourier Transform (FT). The approach appears to be a powerful solution, with wide applications ranging from Electronic Warfare (EW) to 5G Mobile, etc.

articleTitle: Consideration of Poynting Localized Energy Around Radiators: An FDTD-based Investigation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the Poynting Localized energy around arbitrary radiating systems, which is fundamentally different from the antenna reactive energy. By utilizing the FDTD-computed near-zone electric/magnetic fields around any antenna (multi-band/wide-band, not necessarily electrically small), it is possible to evaluate the Poynting localized energy density for various temporal excitations (Gaussian pulse/gated sinusoidal signals). Using the proposed FDTD-based scheme, we analyze the localized energy behaviour around microstrip-fed slot-loaded printed dipoles. We re-examine the impedance matching issues and redistribution of localized energy, caused by perturbation of antenna parameters, and obtain insights not available from the traditional circuit-theoretic Q-factor approach.

articleTitle: SIW-to-Mini-Coaxial Vertical Transition for Low Profile MM-Wave PCB-to-PCB Assembly
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A vertical transition between substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) and super mini-coaxial connector for millimeter-wave (mm-wave) is presented. It consists of via-pad/anti-pad structure embedded in the SIW printed circuit board (PCB) to match the SIW's TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>-like mode and the connector's TEM mode with low loss over the operating frequency band. The transition is designed and used to construct back-to-back test structures at 20 GHz and 30 GHz bands for evaluation. Both the simulation and measurement results are presented.

articleTitle: Metasurface Design Using Electromagnetic Inversion
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper summarizes and synthetically evaluates a method proposed for metasurface design. The method takes as input a set of desired far-field (FF) performance specifications and produces an effective susceptibility distribution that, when illuminated with a known incident field, produces a FF radiation pattern exhibiting the desired specifications. To this end, electromagnetic inversion (inverse source) is used to solve for the desired tangential fields on the output side of the metasurface. A finite-difference frequency-domain solver, recently developed for simulation of metasurfaces, is used to synthetically evaluate the proposed method using a two-dimensional (2D) example. It should be noted that microscopic metasurface design (i.e., the design of the physical metasurface implementation) is beyond the scope of this paper.

articleTitle: A Broadband H-Plane Patch Antenna Decoupling Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel method for decoupling the elements in a phased-array antenna is proposed. The antenna elements are decoupled by embedding non-radiating coupled resonators between the elements. The coupling through the resonators cancels the coupling through the air and substrate. By properly designing the resonance frequency of the resonators, proper transmission zeros can be created within the operating bandwidth and wide bandwidth of isolation can be created. A mutual coupling reduction of more than 10 dB is achieved over the entire operating bandwidth.

articleTitle: Generation of dual-beam orbital angular momentum vortex beam using transmit arrays
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new dual-beam orbital angular momentum (OAM) vortex wave generation method based on the integration of circular antenna array (CAA) with a transmit-array antenna. The transmit unit cell consists of two-layer rings and three-layer patches for independent phase adjustability. A 310° phase coverage with high transmission coefficient is obtained for the transmit unit at the designed frequency of 10 GHz. A fabricated prototype is measured to validate the numerical simulation and theoretical analysis of the proposed design for dual-beam OAM generation. The present design provide a new method to generate dual-beam OAM vortex waves in flexible designed directions for microwave wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: Coding Programmable Metasurfaces Based on Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a coding scheme based on deep learning techniques for complex beam forming with programmable metasurfaces. A fully convolutional neural network is carefully designed that can "learn" the physics of beam forming from computed data, and make online prediction of the coding matrices. Both numerical and experimental results show that the network can compute coding matrices fulfilling the input requirement in less than one millisecond. This scheme may open a door for real-time complex beam steering with programmable metasurfaces and digital phased arrays.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband, Glass Package-Integrated Power Dividers for 5G and mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband, glass package-integrated, equal-split power divider with footprint smaller than the unit free-space wavelength corresponding to the operating frequency of 28 GHz 5G band. The utilization of precision low-loss redistribution layers (RDL) on ultra-thin glass substrates with stable electrical properties at mm-wave frequencies enable the ultra-wideband power dividing networks to have a small footprint in x-y-z dimensions along with excellent performance. This approach aggregates the benefits of ceramic, low-loss polymers and silicon: electrical performance of the ceramic, processability of polymers and the dimensional stability of silicon, simulated in glass substrate to realize fine features for the power dividers. The power divider exhibits low added insertion loss, minimal phase shift between its output ports and has a height less than 150-μm.

articleTitle: Design of Ultra-Wideband Circularly Polarized CPW-Fed Antenna with a Metasurafce Substrate
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes the novel design of coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed quadrilateral-shaped compact planar antenna for ultra-wideband (UWB) application. The fractional axial ratio (ARBW) bandwidth of the antenna for circular polarization (CP) is 56.64% (5.91-10.58GHz) and its fractional impedance matching bandwidth (IMBW) is 137.1% (3.1-17.5GHz). The proposed antenna structure is simple and compact; hence its design is efficient. The gain of the antenna varies between 3.33 to 8.9dBi. The gain further improves by placing a metasurface below the antenna up to 4.8dBi, without affecting its axial ratio bandwidth, while its IMBW reduces to 118.2% (4.5-17.5GHz). Simulated and measured results are shown to be in good agreement.

articleTitle: Reflection-Cancelling Dielectric Huygens’ Metasurface Pair for Wideband Millimeter-Wave Beam-Forming
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel all-dielectric metasurface based on reflection cancelling Huygens' source pair is proposed for mm-wave beam-forming applications, and demonstrated using full-wave simulations. The metasurface is realized using an elliptical resonator connected with its neighbor using four dielectric bridges to provide mechanical stability. The quarter-wavelength spaced resonator pair is next used to achieve reflection cancelling, thereby matching the structure over a large bandwidth. By exploiting resonator ellipticities, transmission phase is engineered. Its application in beam-forming is next illustrated by realizing a monopulse pattern as an example.

articleTitle: Direction of Arrival Estimation using Root-Transformation Matrix Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a preliminary study of a novel polynomial-solving Direction of Arrival (DOA) estimator called Root-Transformation Matrix (root-T) technique which includes an investigation of its performance against current DOA algorithms such as root-MUSIC and improved-MUSIC. The main objective of this work is to conserve the performance of improved-MUSIC which achieves high DOA estimation accuracy and resolution while reducing the cost of computational complexity. It's shown that the Root-T performs better in low SNR with performance improvement of 86.7% and with closely-spaced signal condition with performance improvement of 96.8% as compared to root-MUSIC without degrading improved-MUSIC performance while reducing mean computational time by 49.5%.

articleTitle: Broadband MST sensor probes based on a SP3T MEMs switch
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Modulated scattering techniques (MST) wireless sensors have recently proven their capabilities in different application scenarios. In particular, when the MST sensor antenna is loaded with three different resistive loads by using a suitable electronic switch, it is possible to retrieve the electric characteristics of the surrounding media. The main drawback of MST sensors is the RF switch, because of its cost and narrowband behaviour. The adoption of suitable RF-MEMS microwave switches is a good opportunity to overcome this problem. This work proposes the design and application of an SP3T MEMs switchable to provide good performances up to 20 GHz with reduced dimensions and complexity. An MST sensor prototype able to retrieve the dielectric permittivity of the surrounding media has been designed, fabricated and experimentally assessed. The obtained results were quite promising.

articleTitle: Geometry Optimization of a Phased Array Feed on the Arecibo Telescope for Maximum Survey Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wide-field receiver for the Arecibo Telescope is currently in development, the Advanced L band Phased Array Camera for Arecibo (ALPACA). The Arecibo optical system provides a new challenge for design optimization of phased array feeds. We report on results from a simulation and design optimization study aimed at determining the element layout and geometry that maximizes the receiver sensitivity, field of view, and survey speed.

articleTitle: Role of Classical Time Domain CEM Methods for Quantum Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: As quantum theory matures, quantum applications that significantly depend on electromagnetic effects are becoming increasingly of interest to engineers. We discuss a number of diverse computations that are needed in the engineering design of various devices leveraging these quantum effects. In each case, the broadband knowledge of the classical dyadic Green's function of the problem being analyzed plays an important role. As a result, many of these applications require the extremely broadband solution of classical electromagnetic scattering problems in complex geometries to evaluate components of the dyadic Green's functions. This suggests that classical time domain computational electromagnetics methods will play an important role in the future of quantum applications.

articleTitle: Massive MIMO Beamforming on a Chip
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An LTCC passive beamformer package with 10-30GHz instantaneous bandwidth, 9 simultaneous beams in a 90 degree sector capable of driving a 13 element stick array is proposed. Full-wave simulations show 30%-50% beamforming efficiency, with excellent impedance match and beam fidelity.

articleTitle: Cross Dipole FSS Bandwidth Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a parametric study of conventional cross dipole frequency selective surface (FSS) on the bandwidth performance is investigated. The study analyses the effect of the unit cell metal width on the bandwidth characteristic. A prototype with central frequency of 10 GHz was designed, fabricated and measured.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Antenna For Automotive Radar System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable antenna for automotive radar with smaller size and longer detecting range. The size is reduced by reusing antenna for different work patterns. The detecting range is increased by more output power added at antenna. The work patterns are transferred by switches on chip. The proposed antenna is based on planar microstrip array which can be easily realized by using transmission line model. When radar works at near-range, middle-range and long-range patterns, the reconfigurable antenna can provide maximum gain 17.4 dBi, 19 dBi and 23 dBi correspondingly.

articleTitle: Structural Effect on Image Quality Degradation in Ground-Penetrating Radar Array
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper examines the additional clutter generated from the inclusion of a reflective backplate on a multi-static ground-penetrating radar array. Clutter is shown to be introduced via a ringing cavity and multipath propagation. This clutter is target-dependent and difficult to process. Experimental radar images show inclusion of a reflective backplate has a dramatic negative effect on image quality and we present potential clutter mitigation with the inclusion of absorbing material.

articleTitle: A 1-bit Reconfigurable Reflectarray Element with Independent Dual-band Phase Controlling Capability
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 1-bit reconfigurable reflectarray (RRA) element with independent dual-band phase controlling capability is designed and analyzed. Two PIN diodes are placed at the orthogonal sides of the rectangular microstrip patch. By switching them ON or OFF individually, the resonant property of the patch is tuned, and thus, independent 180° phase difference at 12.5 GHz and 14.25 GHz is achieved. Two sets of biasing circuits that are able to isolate DC/RF signals effectively at both frequencies are elaborately designed. Element simulations demonstrate good 1-bit phase controlling performance with optimized isolation between two frequencies, laying a solid foundation for the practical realization of functional 1-bit dual-band RRA in the future.

articleTitle: Improvement in FSS-Based Sensor Sensitivity by Miniaturization Technique
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Frequency selective surfaces are a planar array of elements (or unit cells) that, when illuminated externally, have a frequency response that depends on element geometry and spacing, and the dielectric properties and thickness of the substrate. Thus, FSSs are good candidates for wireless sensing for numerous nondestructive testing applications. As sensitivity is an important sensing issue, detection sensitivity of FSS-based sensors can be improved by increasing the number of unit cells within a given (physical) space. This is a result of the fact that more unit cells will contribute to the frequency response within a given physical area (i.e., the illuminating footprint upon the sensor) in addition to smaller inter-element spacing (e.g., higher mutual coupling). Both of these aspects increase the sensitivity of the sensor to geometrical changes, and can be physically realized through implementation of FSS miniaturization techniques. To this end, in this work, two FSS-based sensors have been designed; one of which is the miniaturized version of the other. Measurement results indicate that the miniaturized FSS sensor is more sensitive to geometrical variations.

articleTitle: Fluidically Beam-Steering Metasurfaced Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a fluidically beam-steering metasurfaced antenna. The proposed antenna consists of a source antenna and a bi-layered metasurface which acts as partially reflecting surface (PRS) as a superstrate. The top-layer metasurface composed of 4×4 conductive squared ring element array on the top side of thin dielectric substrate and a 3-D printed bottom-layer for fluid movement. Radiation beam has been steered by means of water as a fluid flow in the different channels inside the bottom layer of metasurface. A 2-D beam-steering of ±15° in theta axis with 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 2.54-2.68 GHz has been achieved. Stable radiation gain of more than 5-dBi has been demonstrated across the operating bandwidth. The proposed antenna is low cost, low profile and can be used in systems for radiation diverse applications where the periodic metasurface structures are needed.

articleTitle: A MIMO Antenna Array for 5G Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a MIMO antenna array for 5G mobile terminals was proposed. The defected ground structure (DGS) was used between the array elements to increase the antenna element isolation and the antenna bandwidth at the same time, which was also analyzed by the theory of characteristic mode. The parameter of the designed antenna array was simulated and optimized by CST software. The bandwidth of the antenna is 3.3GHz-3.6GHz and 4.8GHz-5GHz. The performance of the simulation shows that the proposed antenna array can be used in 5G mobile terminals.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Scanning Dielectric Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a beam steering flat dielectric lens antenna working at 60 GHz. The lens antenna is manufactured with a rapid prototyping 3D printer using low-loss ABS material. The antenna is excited through a single element patch antenna for innovative low-cost applications. The beam steering will be achieved through the integration of innovative Plastic-MEMS magnetic actuator that was recently developed at CIARS at the University of Waterloo. The new structure has potential in applications that requires beam steering, low-cost, and less complexity of current phased array antenna systems. The simulation results showed high gain of 18 dB and scanning angles ± 10 degrees in all directions.

articleTitle: Empty Substrate Integrated Waveguide Planar Slot Antenna Array for 5G Wireless Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a planar 4 × 4 slot antenna array based on Empty Substrate Integrated Waveguide at 28 GHz. The proposed antenna offers reduced weight and fabrication cost as well as relatively feasible integration with planar electronic components. The proposed antenna suggests an operating bandwidth of 7.8% (i.e. 27.1-29.3 GHz) suitable to fulfill demands of 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> Generation (5G) networks with high gain performance of 17.2 dBi and with reduced sidelobes level in the H-plan.

articleTitle: Fabric Antenna for Temperature Sensing over ISM Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a microstrip patch antenna on a fabric substrate with temperature sensing function at ISM band. The antenna is designed to operate around 2.45 GHz, the selected frequency band was the unlicensed 2.4-2.4835 GHz ISM band<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>. The resonant frequencies of a microstrip patch antenna are dependent on the physical dimensions of the antenna and the dielectric constant of its substrate. Both characteristics are affected by temperature changes. In this paper, we omitted the variations on the physical dimensions and we focused on the shift in frequency due to the dielectric constant. It can be a low-cost solution for heat sensitive items and it can be modified for the narrow range of temperature changes of the human body.

articleTitle: Wide-Angle Scanning Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A cross-shaped wide angle scanning array antenna is studied and presented. High impedance periodic structure (HIPS) is applied to ameliorate radiation pattern of the antenna element in an array. The HIPS could improve the beam-width of an active antenna element in the array. Then the wide-angle scanning performance of the phased array is extended. The gain of the array antenna is improved when the main beam scans at ± 60° both in the H-plane and E-plane. By the comparison to the metal ground plane, the gain of the array antenna with HIPS is 4dB higher in H-plane when the main beams are at ± 60°. And the gain of the array antenna with HIPS is 2.6dB higher in E-plane when the main beams are at - 60°. The main beams are more symmetrical when they are at ± 60° in E-plane. The cross-shaped wide scanning array antenna with periodic structure is fabricated and measured. The main beam of the array antenna scans up to ± 60° with high gain is achieved in the H-plane and E-plane respectively. The measured results of the array are in good agreement with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Electronically Reconfigurable Dipole Antenna Using Integrated Passive Non-Volatile Solid-State Metal-Insulator-Metal Switches
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this article, we present for the first time, the design and experimental results of an electronically reconfigurable dipole antenna using passive and non-volatile solid state Metal-Insulator-Metal (MIM) switches. MIM switch is integrated and fabricated inclusively with the antenna, in an ambient lab environment and notably without the use of any `clean room' facilities. Radiation pattern of the antenna could be configured electronically using DC pulses applied to the MIM switch. A 180° steering of the E and H plane radiation patterns from positive to negative end-fire direction and vice versa is achieved by choosing Set(ON)/Reset(OFF) state of the switch. The antenna shows good return loss characteristics for all switch states around 2.23GHz and has a usable -10dB band width of 54MHz in common for both switch states.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Dual-Polarized SIW Filtering Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band dual-polarized filtering antenna in SIW technology. An annular ring slot is etched on top of a SIW cavity for radiation. A vertical corner pin is introduced inside the cavity to control coupling between the first two higher order modes, TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">210</sub> and TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">120</sub>. The coupling controls the radiation frequencies. The antenna provides orthogonal linear polarization at the two frequencies. A prototype filtering antenna is fabricated for radiation at 10.47 GHz and 11.87 GHz with 10 dB input matching bandwidth of 1%. Measured peak gain is at least 6.8 dBi for both the pass bands with 0.1 dB variation over the entire passband.

articleTitle: Low Angle Scanning Phased Arrays With Greater Than 50:1 Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An Extremely Wideband (EWB) antenna array is presented that covers the entire UHF to C bands (0.13-7.63 GHz). The array has dual-linear polarization and is capable of wide-angle scanning. This array achieves an impressive 58:1 contiguous bandwidth at broadside and 42:1 bandwidth when scanning down to 60° in both E and H planes using a VSWR <; 3 metric. In addition to building on the tightly coupled dipole array concept, the enabling novelty of this extremely wide bandwidth array is the use of a Frequency Selective Surface within the substrate that acts as a multistage narrowband notch filter to suppress periodic ground plane interference. Also, a highly improved impedance matching feed is employed. A 12×12 array prototype was fabricated and tested to verify the bandwidth and gain performance. The overall radiation efficiency was demonstrated to be 73% on average.

articleTitle: Beam Probability Metric for 5G OTA Testing in Multi-Probe Anechoic Chamber Setups
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Over-the-air (OTA) testing for 5G antenna systems has become a strong need because conducted testing is no longer applicable. New OTA testing metrics are required to evaluate new performance of 5G antenna systems. This paper investigates the recently proposed metric, e.g. beam probability for 5G OTA testing in multi-probe anechoic chamber (MPAC) OTA setups.

articleTitle: 32-GHz Outdoor-to-Indoor Channel Measurement of Propagation Losses and Delay Spread
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents millimeter-wave (mmWave) propagation losses and delay spread characteristics, based on outdoor-to-indoor (O2I) channel measurements. The measurements were conducted in an office building at 32 GHz. Although the results of the propagation loss measurement are similar to the ITU-R and the 3GPP model, the delay spread result is quite different from the 3GPP model. It should be noted that delay spread models for O2I scenarios in the 3GPP are identical to both above 6 GHz and below 6 GHz. We also considered the propagation characteristics in terms of indoor propagation environments in that typical O2I propagation is affected not only by the building penetration but also by the indoor propagation. We believe that these mmWave O2I characteristics will be useful for 5G system design and evaluations.

articleTitle: Sparse Recovery with Predictable Accuracy in Noisy Spherical Antenna Near-Field Measurements
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The influence of noise on the minimum number of measurement samples for a sparse recovery in a spherical antenna near-field to far-field transformation (NFFFT) is investigated. To this end, several modified phase transition diagrams are determined. These diagrams show the minimum number of samples required to achieve a certain accuracy in the reconstructed far-field. With this approach, the reconstruction by the basis pursuit algorithm and its quadratically constrained version are shown to be sufficiently robust against measurement noise for actual measurements. In consequence, sparse recovery can be applied to the spherical NFFFT with predictable accuracy.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable K/Ka Band Filtenna Using a Double Arm Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work introduces a right hand circularly polarized (RHCP) 16-element antenna array, able to operate at multi K/Ka-band regions using a modified ring resonator. The filtenna has a stack topology where the radiating elements are separated from the feeding network suppressing any possible interferences with the antenna radiation pattern. The frequency tuning is achieved by integrating two pin diodes on two stub arms loading the ring resonator and converting it to a frequency selective filter. By controlling the pin diodes, four different resonant frequencies can be selected. This design method yields a high gain circularly polarized frequency reconfigurable antenna at the K/Ka-bands.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of a Compact Rectenna for Structural Health Monitoring Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper addresses the design and characterization of a compact rectenna for structural health monitoring applications. The size of a rectenna is only 66 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, of that is, 0.057 of square wavelength at the operating frequency (868 MHz). By adding a small metallic reflector plate (15 x 9 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) positioned at 5 cm behind the rectenna, a dc power greater than 100μW (dc voltage greater than 1V) can be harvested from illuminating radiofrequency power densities greater than 0.78μW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Eight-Antenna MIMO Array for 5G Smartphone
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact dual-band antenna array for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system in the smartphone is presented. Antenna elements in the array are set at the long side edge frame of the smartphone. The antenna has a planar structure with a compact size of 13.8 × 7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (0.161λ × 0.082λ, λ is the wavelength at 3500 MHz) for operating at fifth-generation (5G) band (3400-3600 and 4800-5000 MHz). The total array consists of two symmetric four-antenna arrays, along two long side edge frame of the smartphone. A 2 mm (0.023λ) distance is achieved between adjacent antennas in each four-antenna array. The antennas have an acceptable isolation and thereof their envelope correlation coefficients (ECC) are less than 0.1 in the operating band.
